10.label: The world made
10.recap: God speaks light, sky, sea, land and living creatures into being across six days.

10.label: The garden and the serpent
10.recap: A talking serpent persuades the woman in the garden to reconsider the one tree she was told to leave alone.

10.label: The ark
10.recap: God warns Noah of a coming flood and gives him the exact measurements for a wooden ark.

10.label: The coat of many colours
10.recap: A favoured young son's fine coat and his boastful dreams turn his older brothers against him.

10.label: The sea divided
10.recap: With Pharaoh's chariots behind them, the fleeing Israelites cross the seabed on dry ground.

10.label: The champion of Gath
10.recap: An enormous Philistine steps out between the armies each day and dares Israel to send one man against him.

10.label: A wager over Job
10.recap: A blameless and prosperous man becomes the subject of a conversation held about him in heaven.

10.label: Writing on the wall
10.recap: At a Babylonian banquet a disembodied hand writes on the plaster, and none of the king's wise men can read it.

10.label: A birth in Bethlehem
10.recap: A child is born in a stable, and shepherds keeping watch nearby are told where to find him.

10.label: Sermon on the mount
10.recap: Jesus climbs a hillside and begins teaching the gathered crowd with a series of blessings.

10.label: The road to Damascus
10.recap: A man travelling to arrest believers is struck to the ground by a light and left without sight for three days.

10.label: A new heaven and earth
10.recap: The visionary watches the old order pass away and a city come down, and the book closes on its final promise.

11.label: Down the Rabbit-Hole
11.recap: Bored by the riverbank, Alice follows a waistcoated White Rabbit down a hole and lands in a hall of locked doors.

11.label: The Pool of Tears
11.recap: After shooting up tall and shrinking small, Alice weeps a whole pool of tears and swims off through it.

11.label: A Caucus-Race and a Long Tale
11.recap: A soggy crowd of birds and animals dries off with a muddled Caucus-Race, then drifts away one by one.

11.label: The Rabbit Sends in a Little Bill
11.recap: Mistaken for the Rabbit's maid, Alice grows enormous inside his house before nibbling her way back out and fleeing.

11.label: Advice from a Caterpillar
11.recap: A hookah-smoking Caterpillar quizzes Alice on who she is, then leaves her a mushroom that changes her size.

11.label: Pig and Pepper
11.recap: In a pepper-filled kitchen Alice meets the Duchess, finds the grinning Cheshire Cat, and rescues a baby that turns into a pig.

11.label: A Mad Tea-Party
11.recap: The Hatter, the March Hare, and a drowsy Dormouse pull Alice into a riddling, never-ending tea-party.

11.label: The Queen's Croquet-Ground
11.recap: Gardeners frantically paint white roses red as the fierce Queen of Hearts sweeps Alice into a chaotic croquet match.

11.label: The Mock Turtle's Story
11.recap: The Duchess waxes on about morals, then a wistful Mock Turtle and a Gryphon recount their odd schooling by the sea.

11.label: The Lobster Quadrille
11.recap: The Mock Turtle and Gryphon dance the Lobster Quadrille and coax Alice through some thoroughly muddled recitations.

11.label: Who Stole the Tarts?
11.recap: At the trial of the Knave of Hearts, witnesses give nonsense testimony while Alice quietly begins to grow again.

11.label: Alice's Evidence
11.recap: Alice towers over the court, scatters the Queen's nonsense, and wakes on the riverbank to find it was all a dream.

12.label: By the drawing-room fire
12.recap: Alice scolds a kitten over a tangled ball of worsted and begins wondering aloud about the house on the other side of the mirror.

12.label: The garden of live flowers
12.recap: Alice finds a flower bed where the blooms speak their minds, and learns that the paths here refuse to take her where she wants to go.

12.label: Insects and a train
12.recap: Alice surveys a country laid out in squares, then finds herself in a railway carriage without a ticket and among very odd passengers.

12.label: Two brothers in the wood
12.recap: A pair of identical little men contradict everything, recite a long poem to Alice, and then fall out over a broken rattle.

12.label: The White Queen's shawl
12.recap: Alice tidies a flustered queen who lives backwards, remembers forwards and recommends believing impossible things before breakfast.

12.label: On the narrow wall
12.recap: A large egg perched on a wall lectures Alice about names, un-birthdays and who gets to decide what a word means.

12.label: Soldiers and messengers
12.recap: Stumbling soldiers and horses pour past Alice to a king who is counting them in his memorandum-book and waiting on news from the town.

12.label: Two knights claim her
12.recap: A red knight and a white knight each declare Alice their prisoner and agree to settle the matter by the rules of battle.

12.label: Queen Alice examined
12.recap: Newly crowned and practising dignity, Alice is set upon by two queens who insist she must pass an examination first.

12.label: The banquet goes wrong
12.recap: At her own feast the candles, bottles and guests all misbehave at once, until Alice loses patience and seizes the tablecloth.

12.label: Back on the hearth-rug
12.recap: Alice talks the whole adventure over with her kittens and puzzles about whose dream it was in the first place.

16.label: Growing up at number 14
16.recap: Wendy discovers at two that she must grow up, and the Darling household is introduced in full.

16.label: A shadow in the drawer
16.recap: A strange boy escapes through the nursery window, leaving his shadow behind to be rolled up and hidden away.

16.label: Boy on the nursery floor
16.recap: Wendy wakes to find a boy sitting on the floor crying, and politely offers to help him.

16.label: Second to the right
16.recap: The children fly for days over open sea and learn that falling asleep in the air is dangerous.

16.label: The island wakes
16.recap: The Neverland stirs at Peter's return, with boys, pirates, natives and beasts circling one another endlessly.

16.label: Home under the ground
16.recap: The newcomers are fitted to hollow trees and settle into the underground house, where Wendy takes charge.

16.label: The mermaids' lagoon
16.recap: Long summer days pass at the lagoon, where the mermaids play with bubbles but never speak to the children.

16.label: Taken from the trees
16.recap: The children are hauled one at a time out of their hollow trees and bound by waiting pirates.

16.label: Aboard the Jolly Roger
16.recap: Night settles on the pirate brig, where Hook paces the deck brooding instead of enjoying his triumph.

16.label: Homeward under sail
16.recap: A crew of boys works a ship toward the mainland under a captain who allows no slackness at all.

16.label: Six boys in a row
16.recap: The lost boys line up hopefully before Mrs. Darling while Mr. Darling wrestles with his wounded pride.

16.label: Spring cleaning time
16.recap: Years slide by and the story closes on Peter coming back, generation after generation, at spring cleaning time.

20.label: Waking in the fiery gulf
20.recap: The beaten rebel angels lie stunned on a burning lake, and their leader lifts his head and speaks to the companion nearest him.

20.label: The council in Hell
20.recap: Enthroned before his whole fallen host, Satan opens a great debate on what the defeated should do next.

20.label: At the gates of Hell
20.recap: Reaching the barred gates, Satan finds two monstrous shapes on guard and refuses to give way to either.

20.label: Seen from Heaven
20.recap: The poet turns to praise light, and the view shifts to Heaven, where the Father looks down on the garden and on the enemy already on his way.

20.label: The tempter draws near
20.recap: Approaching the new world, Satan is torn by horror and doubt before he begins the attempt he has come so far to make.

20.label: Morning in the garden
20.recap: Adam wakes at dawn, finds Eve flushed and restless in her sleep, and gently wakes her.

20.label: Armies in Heaven
20.recap: An angel rides all night through Heaven and comes at morning on plains already covered with squadrons drawn up for battle.

20.label: How the world began
20.recap: The poet calls again on his muse, and Adam asks his heavenly guest to tell him how the heavens and earth were first made.

20.label: The notes turn tragic
20.recap: The poet announces a change of key, from friendly conversation with angels to distrust, anger and judgement.

20.label: Word reaches Heaven
20.recap: What happened in the garden becomes known above, and the angelic guards go up silent and sorrowful to give their account.

20.label: Prayers go up
20.recap: The pair stand praying in the lowest plight, and their petitions rise to Heaven where an intercessor presents them before the throne.

20.label: The world before them
20.recap: Led down from the hill and out through the eastern gate, the two look back once and then set out together.

21.label: Who was Aesop
21.recap: A short account of the fabulist himself: born a slave, freed for his wit, and sent on an errand that went badly at Delphi.

21.label: A lion and a mouse
21.recap: A lion spares a mouse who has woken him, and finds out later what the promise was worth.

21.label: Down a well
21.recap: Stuck at the bottom of a well, a fox persuades a thirsty goat to join him and proposes a way out for them both.

21.label: Envying the lapdog
21.recap: A hard-worked ass decides that the household pet has the better life and tries the same tricks himself.

21.label: Crying wolf
21.recap: A shepherd boy amuses himself by calling his neighbours out for nothing, until the day the wolf actually arrives.

21.label: Hiding in the shed
21.recap: A hunted stag takes shelter among the oxen, who warn him that the real danger has not passed through yet.

21.label: Pleasing everybody
21.recap: A miller and his son take the road to market and adjust their arrangements for every passer-by with an opinion.

21.label: A gnat picks a fight
21.recap: A gnat challenges a lion to single combat and celebrates the outcome loudly on his way home.

21.label: Two mice, two tables
21.recap: A country mouse is tempted to town by a friend's account of the food there, and finds the meals interrupted.

21.label: An axe in the pool
21.recap: A woodcutter loses his axe in deep water and is offered a choice of replacements by a god who is watching.

21.label: A contest of imitators
21.recap: A famous joker wins a crowded theatre with an imitation, and a countryman announces he can do better tomorrow.

21.label: The last fable
21.recap: A metalworker's dog sleeps through the hammering and wakes for dinner, and hears exactly what his master thinks of it.

23.label: What he was never told
23.recap: Douglass opens with what he does not know about himself: his age, his father, and the mother he saw only at night.

23.label: The closet door
23.recap: A child newly moved to his master's house witnesses a punishment in the kitchen and hides where he cannot see it.

23.label: The tarred fence
23.recap: A tour of the great plantation: the fruit garden guarded with tar, the fine stables, and the two men who keep the horses.

23.label: Three days of scrubbing
23.recap: Word comes that the boy is to be sent to Baltimore, and he spends three happy days washing himself for the journey.

23.label: The alphabet stopped
23.recap: A kind new mistress starts teaching him his letters until her husband explains, in front of the boy, why she must not.

23.label: Bread for lessons
23.recap: Shut out of lessons at home, he turns errands, spare bread and street friendships into a way of learning to read.

23.label: Ranked with the livestock
23.recap: After a death in the family, everyone owned by the estate is gathered to be appraised and divided along with the animals.

23.label: Sent to the farm
23.recap: Hired out to a farmer with a reputation, the narrator becomes a field hand and learns what the work and the man cost him.

23.label: Monday in the stable
23.recap: Before daylight on a Monday, an ordinary chore in the stable turns into a confrontation neither man expected.

23.label: A Sunday class
23.recap: At a gentler place he quietly starts a Sunday reading class that grows to dozens of eager scholars.

23.label: Riders at the gate
23.recap: The morning of a long planned undertaking arrives, and men on horseback appear at the lane gate.

23.label: First wages
23.recap: Settled in a northern port, he takes his first paid work, meets colour prejudice at the docks, and finds an anti-slavery paper.

26.label: Waking in the fire
26.recap: The defeated rebel angels come to on a burning lake, and their leader takes in the ruined place that is now his.

26.label: The council in Hell
26.recap: The fallen powers hold a formal debate over whether to renew open war or find some quieter way to strike back.

26.label: At the gates
26.recap: Two monstrous shapes guard the way out, and one of them claims a kinship that stops a fight before it starts.

26.label: Seen from above
26.recap: God looks down on the new-made world, foretells what the traveller from below intends, and the Son answers him.

26.label: In sight of the garden
26.recap: Within view of Eden the tempter is ambushed by his own conscience and argues bitterly with himself about repentance.

26.label: A troubled dream
26.recap: Adam wakes early and finds Eve restless, and she tells him of a strange voice that called her out in the night.

26.label: War in Heaven
26.recap: A loyal angel returns to find the plain filled with armed squadrons, and the order to march is given.

26.label: How the world was made
26.recap: The angel turns from warning to wonder, describing how the world itself was called out of the deep.

26.label: Return by night
26.recap: Under cover of darkness the tempter comes back to the garden, changed in method and settled on his purpose.

26.label: News reaches Heaven
26.recap: Word of what happened in the garden arrives above, and the guardian angels are called to account for it.

26.label: Prayers carried up
26.recap: The pair pray in humility, and their wordless petition is presented and pleaded for them before the throne.

26.label: Out of the gate
26.recap: The angel takes them down from the height and leads them out, and they step together into the open world.

35.label: The Machine
35.recap: At his dinner party the Time Traveller shows a small glittering machine and sends it vanishing into time before his startled guests.

35.label: Time Travelling
35.recap: Returning dishevelled a week later, the Traveller tells how he first hurtled forward through the centuries.

35.label: In the Golden Age
35.recap: He arrives in the year 802,701 among the gentle, childlike Eloi in a soft and crumbling paradise.

35.label: The Sunset of Mankind
35.recap: Puzzling over the frail Eloi, the Traveller discovers his time machine has been dragged away and hidden.

35.label: The Morlocks
35.recap: He uncovers the pale, underground Morlocks and the grim truth of how the two races of the future now live.

35.label: The Palace of Green Porcelain
35.recap: Hunting for a weapon, the Traveller and his Eloi friend Weena explore a vast ruined museum of the past.

35.label: The Trap of the White Sphinx
35.recap: Fighting the Morlocks in the dark to reach his machine, the Traveller loses Weena in the chaos.

35.label: The Further Vision
35.recap: Escaping forward in time, he travels on to a dying earth beneath a vast, cold, red sun.

35.label: The Traveller's Return
35.recap: He races home to his laboratory and his waiting guests, exhausted and forever changed by what he has seen.

36.label: Watched from across space
36.recap: The narrator sets out how calmly Earth went about its business while colder, older minds studied it from a neighbouring planet.

36.label: The falling star
36.recap: A meteor comes down near Woking and an astronomer walks out at dawn to look at what has buried itself in the sand.

36.label: The cylinder opens
36.recap: A jostling crowd rings the pit as the lid finally unscrews from within and something begins to climb out.

36.label: A flag of truce
36.recap: A small deputation walks toward the pit carrying a white flag, and an invisible heat sweeps across the common.

36.label: Night drive in the storm
36.recap: After leaving his wife with cousins, the narrator drives home through thunder and hail and sees something striding over the pine woods.

36.label: Leaving Maybury Hill
36.recap: The narrator and a stray artilleryman slip out of the emptied houses and set off across country together.

36.label: London empties
36.recap: Panic breaks the railways and roads as millions of people try to force their way north and east out of the capital.

36.label: Cut off at Halliford
36.recap: Hemmed in by drifting black smoke, the narrator and a frightened curate wait out two long days in an abandoned house.

36.label: The peephole
36.recap: Hidden in a ruined kitchen, the two men quarrel bitterly over the food and over the chance to look out.

36.label: A bed and a reckoning
36.recap: Alone in a looted inn, the narrator eats, sleeps in a real bed for the first time in weeks, and finally lets himself think.

36.label: Walking through dead London
36.recap: He crosses the river and moves through silent, powdered streets where almost nothing is left alive.

36.label: The lost days
36.recap: The narrator's memory fails him entirely for three days, and he comes back to himself in the care of strangers.

41.label: The sleepy glen
41.recap: The narrator describes a quiet Dutch valley off the Hudson where a drowsy, dreaming influence settles on everyone who stays a while.

41.label: The headless rider
41.recap: Fireside legend gives the valley a nightly horseman who lost his head to a cannonball and hurries the roads looking for it before daybreak.

41.label: A schoolmaster arrives
41.recap: Ichabod Crane comes from Connecticut to keep school, boarding a week at a time with the farmers and making himself useful to their wives.

41.label: The farmer's daughter
41.recap: Among his singing pupils is a well-off farmer's only child, and one visit to her father's homestead fixes Ichabod's ambitions.

41.label: A formidable rival
41.recap: The neighbourhood's roistering champion horseman has been courting the same girl, and he is not a man used to being crossed.

41.label: An invitation arrives
41.recap: A messenger clatters up to the schoolhouse door with word of a merry-making at the Van Tassel farm that very evening.

41.label: Riding out on Gunpowder
41.recap: Ichabod borrows a broken-down plough horse and sets off through the golden autumn countryside in the style of a knight-errant.

41.label: The Dutch tea-table
41.recap: At the farmhouse the narrator lingers over the heaped cakes, pies and preserves before the music calls everyone to dance.

41.label: Ghost tales on the piazza
41.recap: The older guests trade war anecdotes and then goblin stories, most of them fixed on the church bridge and its regular visitor.

41.label: The road home at midnight
41.recap: Riding back alone and low in spirits, Ichabod passes the great tulip tree around which every fearful story in the district is set.

41.label: Something by the brook
41.recap: A huge shape stirs in the shadow of the water and falls in beside him, matching his pace however he rides.

41.label: What was found next day
41.recap: The horse comes home alone, tracks are followed to the bridge, and the neighbourhood settles on the explanation that suits it best.

42.label: A Sunday walk
42.recap: A dry, dependable London lawyer is introduced through his habits, his tolerance of others, and the weekly walks he takes with a distant kinsman.

42.label: The neglected door
42.recap: Enfield points out a blistered door in a prosperous street and tells the ugly story he attaches to it.

42.label: The will in the safe
42.recap: Utterson takes a troubling will out of his safe, broods over its terms, and calls on an old friend for information he does not get.

42.label: Mr. Seek
42.recap: The lawyer keeps watch on the by-street night after night until he finally meets the man he has been waiting for.

42.label: After the dinner party
42.recap: Utterson stays behind after a dinner to press Dr. Jekyll about the will, and leaves with a promise he dislikes making.

42.label: A crime by moonlight
42.recap: A maidservant at her window sees a shocking assault in a lane, and the evidence brings the police to Utterson's door.

42.label: The letter
42.recap: Utterson is received in Jekyll's laboratory, is handed a letter to judge, and afterwards has his clerk cast an eye over the handwriting.

42.label: A friend's decline
42.recap: The hunt goes cold and Jekyll returns to society for a season, until Utterson finds Dr. Lanyon terribly changed and unwilling to explain.

42.label: At the window
42.recap: Utterson and Enfield stop in the court and talk to Jekyll at his window, until something cuts the conversation short.

42.label: Poole comes for help
42.recap: The butler arrives in a state of terror and begs the lawyer to come to the house and hear something for himself.

42.label: Breaking the door
42.recap: Utterson and Poole force the cabinet door and then search the whole building for the missing doctor.

42.label: The full statement
42.recap: The book closes with a long confession in the doctor's own hand, setting out the whole affair from its beginning.

43.label: Story of the Door
43.recap: Lawyer Utterson hears how a cold, brutal man named Hyde trampled a child and paid the family off with a cheque signed by the respected Dr Jekyll.

43.label: Search for Mr. Hyde
43.recap: Troubled by Jekyll's will leaving everything to Hyde, Utterson haunts the door until he finally meets the chilling man face to face.

43.label: Dr. Jekyll Was Quite at Ease
43.recap: Over dinner Jekyll airily waves off Utterson's worries, asking only that, whatever should happen, Hyde be looked after.

43.label: The Carew Murder Case
43.recap: Hyde beats a kindly old gentleman to death in the street, and all London turns out in a manhunt for him.

43.label: Incident of the Letter
43.recap: Hyde has vanished. A pale, shaken Jekyll shows Utterson a farewell letter from Hyde, but its handwriting plants a fresh doubt.

43.label: Incident of Dr. Lanyon
43.recap: With Hyde gone Jekyll grows sociable again, then suddenly shuts himself away, while old Dr Lanyon sickens under some secret dread and dies.

43.label: Incident at the Window
43.recap: Chatting up at his window, Jekyll's face twists into such horror that Utterson and Enfield flee the courtyard in silence.

43.label: The Last Night
43.recap: Jekyll's butler Poole comes in terror: a stranger's voice is locked in the cabinet, and the two men resolve to break down the door.

43.label: Dr. Lanyon's Narrative
43.recap: Lanyon's sealed letter reveals what he saw that night: a potion drunk, and a transformation so impossible it shattered him.

43.label: Henry Jekyll's Full Statement
43.recap: In his own hand, Jekyll confesses the whole truth of his double life, and how it finally consumed him.

45.label: A watchful neighbour
45.recap: Mrs Rachel Lynde spots her shy neighbour driving out of Avonlea in his best collar on a working afternoon, and cannot rest until she knows why.

45.label: The wrong child waiting
45.recap: Matthew reaches the station to collect the boy he was promised and finds a small, talkative girl sitting on a pile of shingles.

45.label: A name worth arguing over
45.recap: At Green Gables the child understands she is not the one they sent for, and then negotiates fiercely about what she is to be called.

45.label: A visitor speaks her mind
45.recap: Mrs Rachel comes to inspect the newcomer, says exactly what she thinks of her looks, and gets a scorching answer in return.

45.label: The way to school
45.recap: Anne and her friend take the prettiest route to school through lanes and hollows that Anne has renamed to suit herself.

45.label: Company to tea
45.recap: Left in charge of the house, Anne entertains her friend among the apple trees and then brings out something cool from the pantry.

45.label: The night everyone went to town
45.recap: With the grown-ups away at a political meeting thirty miles off, Anne and Matthew keep house together on a bitter January night.

45.label: A dare too far
45.recap: At a garden party the girls fall to daring each other, and Anne refuses to let Josie Pye have the last word.

45.label: Playing the lily maid
45.recap: Four girls stage a scene from a poem on the pond, and Anne is the only one willing to lie still and float downstream.

45.label: A summer outdoors, then books
45.recap: Ordered into the open air all summer for her health, Anne comes back in September with her ambition and appetite for study restored.

45.label: A folded paper in his hand
45.recap: A sudden shock at the porch door brings neighbours and doctor hurrying to Green Gables, and the house is quiet by nightfall.

45.label: The bend in the road
45.recap: Marilla comes home from town with hard news of her own, and Anne sits alone at her window working out what she owes.

46.label: Marley's Ghost
46.recap: On Christmas Eve the miser Scrooge sneers at the season, until his dead partner Marley's chained ghost warns that three spirits will visit him.

46.label: The First of the Spirits
46.recap: The Ghost of Christmas Past carries Scrooge through his lonely boyhood, a kind old employer, and the sweetheart he lost to greed.

46.label: The Second of the Spirits
46.recap: The Ghost of Christmas Present reveals the warm, poor Cratchit home and frail Tiny Tim, and the world's mingled joy and want.

46.label: The Last of the Spirits
46.recap: A silent, hooded phantom shows Scrooge a death no one mourns, and lets him read his own name upon a neglected grave.

46.label: The End of It
46.recap: Scrooge wakes on Christmas morning overjoyed and made new, and keeps Christmas generously for the rest of his days.

55.label: The Cyclone
55.recap: A cyclone carries Dorothy, her dog Toto, and the whole farmhouse far away from the grey Kansas prairie.

55.label: The Munchkins
55.recap: The house lands on the Wicked Witch of the East; the grateful Munchkins give Dorothy silver shoes and send her to the Wizard for help getting home.

55.label: The Scarecrow
55.recap: On the yellow brick road Dorothy frees a friendly Scarecrow who wishes only for brains.

55.label: The Tin Woodman
55.recap: They free a rusted Tin Woodman who longs above all for a heart.

55.label: The Cowardly Lion
55.recap: A great but timid Lion joins the company, hoping the Wizard can grant him courage.

55.label: The Poppy Field
55.recap: A field of deadly poppies nearly claims Dorothy and the Lion before the others carry them to safety.

55.label: The Emerald City
55.recap: In the dazzling Emerald City the Wizard appears differently to each, and will help only if they destroy the Wicked Witch of the West.

55.label: The Wicked Witch
55.recap: The Witch sets wolves, crows, and winged monkeys on the travelers, then captures Dorothy as a slave.

55.label: The Witch Melts
55.recap: Dorothy melts the Wicked Witch with a bucket of water and frees her friends and the Winged Monkeys.

55.label: The Man Behind the Curtain
55.recap: Back in the city they discover the great and terrible Oz is only an ordinary humbug hiding behind a curtain.

55.label: Wishes Granted
55.recap: The humbug Wizard cleverly gives the Scarecrow, the Woodman, and the Lion the brains, heart, and courage they craved.

55.label: Home Again
55.recap: Glinda reveals the silver shoes can carry Dorothy anywhere, and she returns at last to Kansas and Aunt Em.

62.label: Gold in Arizona
62.recap: A Confederate veteran and his partner strike a rich vein in the hills, and one of them rides out for equipment.

62.label: Paralysed in the cave
62.recap: Sheltering in a mountain cave, he finds he cannot move a muscle while riders close in on him.

62.label: Waking on Mars
62.recap: He wakes on a plain of yellow moss under a strange sun and has to learn how to walk all over again.

62.label: Cornered by white apes
62.recap: Pinned to the floor of a ruined building, he is saved by an unlikely ally and immediately has the chance to repay it.

62.label: Ships over the dead city
62.recap: A fleet of airships drifts in over the ruins, and the green warriors open fire from the windows without warning.

62.label: An understanding with Woola
62.recap: He tests his monstrous guardian at the city's edge and finds affection works where authority would not.

62.label: Frescoes of a lost people
62.recap: Moving to better rooms, he studies wall paintings of a vanished race and begins to piece together the planet's history.

62.label: A quarrel over a mount
62.recap: A warrior picks a fight in front of the whole horde, and the long swords come out.

62.label: Into the jeddak's palace
62.recap: He climbs into a hostile palace by night and looks down from a gallery on a chieftain's crowded audience hall.

62.label: Two weeks in the waste
62.recap: Alone in the wilderness, he walks by night, fights off things that leap from the dark, and finds help from an unexpected quarter.

62.label: Behind the hangings
62.recap: Posted as a palace guard, he watches a royal audience unseen from a passage behind the wall coverings.

62.label: Back in the dark
62.recap: He wakes in a cave among grim relics and steps out onto a ledge under a sky he knows far too well.

64.label: The call of Mars
64.recap: After ten lonely years on Earth the narrator feels the old pull of the red planet and wakes beneath a strange forest canopy.

64.label: The herd in the meadow
64.recap: Hidden behind a tree, he studies a herd of tall, single-eyed creatures grazing between the forest and the sea.

64.label: The chamber of mystery
64.recap: Trapped in a rocky room with his old friend, he learns at last where on Mars he has landed and what the place means to Martian faith.

64.label: Chained in the dark
64.recap: He wakes among chained prisoners and penned beasts, and a young red Martian woman offers to show him the secret of the wall.

64.label: Raiders from the sky
64.recap: Black-skinned raiders drop out of the night in small fliers and fight the temple guards among the gardens and statues.

64.label: Rammed in mid air
64.recap: A stolen flier is run down by a battleship, and the little craft's passengers are quickly overwhelmed and bound.

64.label: A love refused
64.recap: A proud young woman who has offered herself is turned down and lays out an elaborate revenge in reply.

64.label: Mapping the escape
64.recap: In a prison cell two captives scratch maps on the floor and time the pace of the sentries outside.

64.label: Through the pits
64.recap: Pressed against the wall of a side corridor, he shadows guards escorting his chained friend back to a cell.

64.label: Trial in the temple
64.recap: He and his companions are marched down a crowded hall to stand before thirty-one judges and answer for blasphemy.

64.label: The fleet goes south
64.recap: Battleship after battleship lifts from its dock and forms a long thin line running south into the night.

64.label: Fire in the temple
64.recap: With fighting spreading through the halls he is reunited with the woman he crossed worlds for, and must decide where she will be safest; the book ends on a deliberately unresolved note.

68.label: Waiting by the temple
68.recap: Half a Martian year into his vigil beside the Temple of the Sun, the narrator trails a furtive figure through the forest at night.

68.label: The underground river
68.recap: He follows his quarry by boat into a glowing subterranean lake, then loses the trail among three dark branching channels.

68.label: The hidden fortress
68.recap: The trail ends at a mountain stronghold whose triple-barred gate stands invitingly ajar.

68.label: A fall and a flier
68.recap: Saved from a fatal drop by a snagged strap, he steals an aircraft and races northeast in pursuit.

68.label: Ambush on the road
68.recap: He spots a green horde lying in wait for the troops of Kaol and runs to raise the alarm.

68.label: Before three thrones
68.recap: Summoned before the jeddak of Kaol, he faces an accuser who claims to have pierced his disguise.

68.label: North to the ice
68.recap: The chase turns arctic and ends in a crash at the foot of a barrier no flier has ever passed.

68.label: Meeting Talu
68.recap: A yellow-skinned hunter they rescue turns out to be a prince at war with his own uncle, and he offers help.

68.label: The tyrant's court
68.recap: Chained in gold and hauled before the Jeddak of Jeddaks, he hears an announcement made to the assembled nobles.

68.label: Follow the rope
68.recap: A smuggled message points to a hidden way out of the pit, and something worse is lowered in after him.

68.label: Under the palace
68.recap: Pursued through unfamiliar corridors, he slips into an antechamber and finds a ceremony under way beyond the curtains.

68.label: Back across the ice
68.recap: A useless flier is brought down on the arctic waste, and the walk back to the city runs into one last obstacle.

72.label: In the royal gardens
72.recap: A princess of Ptarth is grabbed by an unwanted suitor and rescued by a visiting friend, then has to keep two nations out of war.

72.label: The missing servant
72.recap: A servant drops out of the jeddak's retinue, walks into the city, and presents a token at a foreign embassy.

72.label: Suspicion falls
72.recap: Word of the princess's abduction reaches Helium, and Carthoris is sent to answer for himself at her father's court.

72.label: A change of colours
72.recap: Waking aboard the flier, Thuvia sees that her captors have swapped their insignia, and the ship settles into a dead city.

72.label: Between two banths
72.recap: Carthoris feels his way along a pitch-dark tunnel with a hunting beast ahead of him and another closing from behind.

72.label: Crossing the field
72.recap: The two set out for a walled city across a battlefield whose dead will not stay where they fell.

72.label: Archers out of nowhere
72.recap: A quarrel in the throne room fills the chamber with bowmen, and the jeddak of Lothar takes an interest in his guests.

72.label: Alone with the jeddak
72.recap: Left with Tario, Thuvia is informed that she is somebody else's imagining, and answers him with scorn.

72.label: What waits below
72.recap: Dropped into a lower chamber, the prisoners are told what their host keeps behind the door, and then it comes through.

72.label: The hand that fades
72.recap: Walking through the wood, Carthoris realises the companion at his side is not what he took her for.

72.label: Alone in Aaanthor
72.recap: He wakes wounded among the dead and makes for water through a deserted city where something is watching him.

72.label: The east tower
72.recap: Locked in a tower and waiting for an assassin, Thuvia finds her thoughts running somewhere she did not intend.

73.label: Camp by the river
73.recap: An army sits in muddy winter quarters while a rumor of marching orders runs through the huts and starts arguments.

73.label: The rumor collapses
73.recap: The promised move proves false, and the young soldier is left alone with a private question about what he will do under fire.

73.label: Waiting in the grove
73.recap: Held in reserve at the edge of a wood, the men trade wild reports of the battle while shells begin dropping among the trees.

73.label: The first attack
73.recap: The enemy comes across the smoky field and the youth finds himself firing before he has decided to, swallowed up in the work of the regiment.

73.label: They come again
73.recap: Flush with relief that the trial is over, the men look up to see the enemy re-forming and starting toward them a second time.

73.label: Alone in the woods
73.recap: Away from the guns he builds a long argument in his own defence, then pushes deep into the trees until he reaches a chapel of arching boughs.

73.label: The road of the wounded
73.recap: Drawn back toward the noise, he falls in with a column of bleeding men leaving the fight, and a gentle tattered soldier attaches himself to him.

73.label: A face he knows
73.recap: Slipping back through the procession to escape a question, he recognizes someone in the crowd of wounded and promises to take care of him.

73.label: The line breaks
73.recap: A panicked flood of soldiers bursts out of the woods, and his attempt to stop one of them and ask what has happened ends badly for him.

73.label: Back among his own
73.recap: He stumbles into his regiment's night camp and gives his comrades an account of where he has been.

73.label: The charge
73.recap: Ordered forward over open ground, the regiment runs at a distant clump of trees through heavy fire, leaving a trail of bodies.

73.label: The guns fall quiet
73.recap: The firing thins away, the column turns back toward the river, and the youth finally has room to look over everything he has done.

74.label: Tom in Trouble
74.recap: Mischievous orphan Tom dodges his Aunt Polly, skips school for a swim, and scraps with a newcomer.

74.label: Tom Meets Becky
74.recap: Dreading school, Tom is smitten at first sight by the new girl in town, Becky Thatcher.

74.label: Murder in the Graveyard
74.recap: Sneaking to the graveyard at midnight, Tom and Huck witness Injun Joe murder the doctor and frame poor Muff Potter.

74.label: Off to be Pirates
74.recap: Heartsick over Becky, Tom runs off with Huck and Joe to live as pirates on Jackson's Island.

74.label: Their Own Funeral
74.recap: Given up for drowned, the boys creep back to town and stroll in on their own funeral, to everyone's joy.

74.label: Tom Takes the Blame
74.recap: At school Tom nobly takes Becky's whipping to spare her from disgrace.

74.label: The Trial
74.recap: At Muff Potter's murder trial Tom bravely testifies to the truth, and Injun Joe leaps from the window and escapes.

74.label: Hunting Treasure
74.recap: Tom and Huck go hunting for buried treasure and end up creeping through a haunted house.

74.label: Injun Joe's Gold
74.recap: In the haunted house the boys watch Injun Joe dig up a box of gold and carry it off to a secret hiding place.

74.label: Lost in the Cave
74.recap: Tom and Becky lose their way deep in McDougal's Cave, where Injun Joe is also hiding.

74.label: Injun Joe's End
74.recap: After Tom and Becky's rescue the cave is sealed, and Injun Joe is found dead inside it.

74.label: Rich and Respectable
74.recap: Tom and Huck recover the hidden gold, become the town's heroes, and the Widow Douglas takes Huck in.

76.label: Civilizing Huck
76.recap: Adopted by the Widow Douglas and schooled by Miss Watson, restless Huck slips out for midnight adventures with Tom Sawyer.

76.label: Pap Returns
76.recap: Huck's drunken father reappears to grab his money and shuts Huck away in a lonely riverside cabin.

76.label: The Escape
76.recap: Huck fakes his own murder to be free of Pap and slips away down the river to Jackson's Island.

76.label: Jim on the Island
76.recap: On the island Huck finds Jim, who has run off to escape being sold away from his family.

76.label: Down the River
76.recap: Disguised as a girl, Huck learns men are hunting Jim, and the two push off down the Mississippi on a raft.

76.label: Lost in the Fog
76.recap: A thick fog parts Huck and Jim on the water, and Huck's cruel trick afterward shames him into apologizing to his friend.

76.label: The Feud
76.recap: Taken in by the genteel Grangerfords, Huck is swept into their bloody feud with the Shepherdsons.

76.label: The Duke and the King
76.recap: Two con men styling themselves a duke and a king commandeer the raft and pull Huck and Jim into their swindles.

76.label: The Wilks Fraud
76.recap: The pair pose as the long-lost brothers of the dead Mr Wilks to rob his trusting orphaned daughters.

76.label: Huck's Choice
76.recap: After the con men sell Jim, Huck wrestles with his conscience and resolves to free his friend, whatever it costs his soul.

76.label: At the Phelps Farm
76.recap: Mistaken for Tom Sawyer at the farm where Jim is held, Huck is joined by the real Tom and a wild rescue scheme.

76.label: Setting Jim Free
76.recap: Tom's needlessly elaborate escape goes wrong and he is shot, but the truth that Jim is already free finally comes out.

84.label: Walton's Letters
84.recap: Explorer Robert Walton writes home from the edge of the Arctic, longing for a true friend as his ship pushes north.

84.label: A Stranger on the Ice
84.recap: Walton's crew rescues a wasted, haunted traveller from the ice, Victor Frankenstein, who begins to tell his tale.

84.label: Victor's Childhood
84.recap: Victor recalls a happy Geneva boyhood and his beloved adopted sister Elizabeth.

84.label: The Spark of Life
84.recap: At university Victor masters natural philosophy and grows obsessed with discovering the secret of life itself.

84.label: The Creature Wakes
84.recap: On a dreary November night Victor gives his creation life, then flees in horror at the thing he has made.

84.label: News of a Death
84.recap: A letter from home brings terrible news: Victor's young brother William has been murdered.

84.label: Justine's Trial
84.recap: The gentle servant Justine is tried and condemned for William's death, though Victor dreads who is truly to blame.

84.label: Meeting on the Glacier
84.recap: High on a mountain glacier the creature finds Victor and demands, at last, to be heard.

84.label: The Creature's Tale
84.recap: The creature recounts its lonely awakening and how, unseen, it slowly learned to feel and to survive.

84.label: Rejected by All
84.recap: After secretly learning tenderness from a poor family, the creature is driven off in terror the moment it is seen.

84.label: A Terrible Bargain
84.recap: The creature demands that Victor build him a mate, swearing to vanish from mankind forever in return.

84.label: The Promise Broken
84.recap: Sickened by his task, Victor destroys the half-finished second creature, and his enemy vows a terrible revenge.

84.label: The Pursuit North
84.recap: All he loved now taken from him, Victor chases the creature across the frozen north, back to where Walton found him.

86.label: A knight in the road
86.recap: A Hartford machinist wakes in open country and is claimed as the captive of a man in full armor.

86.label: Into the town
86.recap: He is walked past staring, half-clothed villagers and up through the alleys to a great castle.

86.label: A plan in the dungeon
86.recap: Locked up and sentenced, he notices how completely everyone fears magic and starts working out a use for it.

86.label: The stake and the sky
86.recap: Brought out before the whole court, he stakes his life on what is about to happen overhead.

86.label: Armor on the road
86.recap: Sent off on a quest with a talkative companion, he discovers that a suit of armor is a miserable thing to travel in.

86.label: A royal banquet
86.recap: A guest at a great house, he watches a lavish feast and the offhand cruelty of the people at the high table.

86.label: The holy valley
86.recap: Riding high in a monastery valley, he decides to see how far his new reputation will stretch.

86.label: Going among the people
86.recap: He proposes to walk the country dressed as a commoner, and the king insists on coming too.

86.label: A cabin after dark
86.recap: Leaving a stricken cottage at night, the two travellers hide as footsteps come up the path.

86.label: A notice in the paper
86.recap: Back at Camelot, he opens the newspaper at breakfast and finds a public challenge waiting for him.

86.label: The century revealed
86.recap: He throws open the schools and factories he has been building in secret and surveys what the country has become.

86.label: Waiting underground
86.recap: Barricaded in a cave with a handful of young men, he writes and waits while forces gather outside.

86.label: Another hand takes over
86.recap: A second narrator picks up the manuscript to set down how it all finishes.

98.label: The Period
98.recap: In 1775 England and France teeter on the edge of upheaval as the story opens.

98.label: Recalled to Life
98.recap: At Dover, Mr Lorry of Tellson's Bank gently tells young Lucie Manette that the father she thought dead is alive.

98.label: The Shoemaker
98.recap: In Paris the Defarges lead Lucie to her broken father, kept making shoes in a garret after long years in the Bastille.

98.label: A Disappointment
98.recap: Charles Darnay's London treason trial collapses when the lawyer Sydney Carton points out his uncanny resemblance to the accused.

98.label: Hundreds of People
98.recap: At the Manettes' tranquil Soho home a circle of admirers gathers around the gentle Lucie.

98.label: The Gorgon's Head
98.recap: In France the cruel Marquis is found stabbed in his bed, a note left by the people he has trampled.

98.label: Two Promises
98.recap: Darnay asks Doctor Manette for Lucie's hand, promising to reveal his true name on the wedding morning.

98.label: A Fellow of No Delicacy
98.recap: The wasted Sydney Carton confesses his hopeless love to Lucie and vows he would give his life for anyone she loves.

98.label: Echoing Footsteps
98.recap: As happy years pass for Lucie in London, far off in Paris the storming of the Bastille begins.

98.label: Drawn to the Loadstone Rock
98.recap: A desperate plea draws Darnay back to revolutionary Paris, straight into danger.

98.label: In Secret
98.recap: Darnay reaches Paris only to be seized as an emigrant aristocrat and thrown into prison.

98.label: Triumph
98.recap: Hauled before the Revolutionary Tribunal, Darnay is freed thanks to Doctor Manette, only to be seized again.

98.label: The Game Made
98.recap: Carton uncovers Madame Defarge's deadly designs and quietly begins a plan of his own.

103.label: A new manservant
103.recap: Having dismissed a valet over two degrees of shaving water, Phileas Fogg interviews a cheerful Frenchman and takes him on to the minute.

103.label: The wager signed
103.recap: An argument over newspaper timetables at the Reform Club hardens into an enormous bet, and Fogg proposes to leave that same evening.

103.label: Watching at Suez
103.recap: On the wharves at Suez a twitchy little man questions the British consul about steamers, passports and a robbery in London.

103.label: Shoes at the pagoda
103.recap: Sightseeing in Bombay, the valet wanders into a temple where his boots are very much not welcome, and leaves in a hurry.

103.label: Across India by rail
103.recap: On the train out of Bombay the travellers fall in with a brigadier-general who finds Fogg the strangest man he has ever met.

103.label: A procession in the wood
103.recap: Hidden in a thicket, the party watches a torchlit procession pass with priests, a corpse and a young woman, and learns what is planned for dawn.

103.label: Hong Kong harbour
103.recap: The valet roams the docks of Hong Kong while the detective shadowing the party looks for one last way to delay it.

103.label: A typhoon from the south
103.recap: Aboard a small hired schooner the barometer swings, and her master warns that a typhoon is coming up behind them.

103.label: Long noses wanted
103.recap: Stranded and penniless in Yokohama, the valet presents himself at a showman's cabin and asks for work of any kind.

103.label: Missing on the plains
103.recap: After a running fight on the prairie the train halts at a fort, several passengers cannot be found, and Fogg makes a decision.

103.label: A cell in Liverpool
103.recap: Arrested the moment he sets foot in England, Fogg sits motionless in the Custom House while the hours he needs run out.

103.label: London holds its breath
103.recap: With opinion swinging back in his favour, London bets furiously and his five friends watch the door of the club saloon.

108.label: Murder in Park Lane
108.recap: Watson lays out the baffling shooting of a quiet young aristocrat behind a locked door.

108.label: The bookseller calls
108.recap: A stooped old book collector Watson bumped into that afternoon turns up unexpectedly at his study.

108.label: The empty house
108.recap: Watson is led by a roundabout route into a dark abandoned house facing his old lodgings.

108.label: The Norwood builder
108.recap: A frantic young solicitor bursts into Baker Street convinced he is about to be arrested for murder.

108.label: Little dancing figures
108.recap: After a display of deduction, Holmes hands Watson a sheet covered in absurd stick-figure hieroglyphics.

108.label: The solitary cyclist
108.recap: A young music teacher describes the bearded rider who shadows her along a lonely stretch of country road.

108.label: Collapse at Baker Street
108.recap: A vast and dignified schoolmaster arrives, faints on the hearth-rug, and wakes with an urgent errand.

108.label: The worst man in London
108.recap: A card left on the table announces a visitor whom Holmes regards with pure loathing.

108.label: Six plaster busts
108.recap: Lestrade brings word of a burglar who breaks into houses only to smash cheap Napoleon busts.

108.label: A visitor in the storm
108.recap: Rain hammers Baker Street when a cab pulls up and brings news of a death at Yoxley Old Place.

108.label: Summons before dawn
108.recap: Holmes shakes Watson awake in the dark and hurries him onto a Kentish train on an inspector's urgent note.

108.label: A diplomatic secret
108.recap: A lost document is accounted for and Holmes declines, smiling, to explain how.

113.label: There is no one left
113.recap: A neglected, disagreeable child in India wakes one hot morning to find the household in a panic and then perfectly silent.

113.label: Martha and the moor
113.recap: Mary wakes in a gloomy tapestried room at the manor and meets a Yorkshire housemaid who talks to her as an equal.

113.label: Something in the flower-bed
113.recap: The storm clears, the old gardener talks of spring, and the robin leads Mary to something buried in the turned earth.

113.label: Hunting for the door
113.recap: Mary searches the ivy-covered wall in vain, and Martha comes back from her day out with an unexpected present.

113.label: The boy with the pipe
113.recap: Following a low whistling into the wood, Mary comes upon a moor boy surrounded by creatures that will not run away.

113.label: Crying in the corridor
113.recap: A night of rain and wuthering wind sends Mary down the dark passages with a candle, following a faint crying.

113.label: The night of screams
113.recap: Dreadful sounds wake the whole house, and for once Mary answers a tantrum with a temper of her own.

113.label: Springtime behind the walls
113.recap: An afternoon of blossom and bees in the hidden garden leaves everyone in it quietly astonished.

113.label: A man far away
113.recap: A grieving traveller wandering the fiords and mountains feels, for the first time in ten years, something loosen in him.

113.label: In the garden
113.recap: The whole story is finally told aloud inside the walls where it happened.

120.label: The Old Sea-Dog
120.recap: Young Jim Hawkins recalls the scarred old buccaneer who lodged at his family's inn and dreaded a one-legged man.

120.label: Black Dog Appears
120.recap: A sinister visitor named Black Dog confronts the old captain, and the shock brings on a fit.

120.label: The Black Spot
120.recap: A blind beggar delivers the dreaded black spot, and the terror of it strikes the captain down.

120.label: The Sea-Chest
120.recap: With the captain dead and danger closing in, Jim and his mother open the sea-chest and snatch a packet.

120.label: The Captain's Papers
120.recap: The packet proves to hold a map to Flint's buried treasure, and the squire vows to fit out a ship.

120.label: I Go to Bristol
120.recap: Jim joins the venture and meets the genial one-legged ship's cook, Long John Silver.

120.label: The Voyage
120.recap: The Hispaniola puts to sea, though uneasy currents already run among the crew.

120.label: Council of War
120.recap: As the island is sighted Jim shares what he overheard hidden in the apple barrel: the crew means mutiny.

120.label: My Shore Adventure
120.recap: The ship anchors off the gloomy island and the mutiny breaks into the open.

120.label: The Man of the Island
120.recap: Ashore and alone, Jim meets Ben Gunn, a sailor long marooned and desperate to get home.

120.label: My Sea Adventure
120.recap: Jim slips away from the stockade and paddles out into the dark in Ben Gunn's tiny coracle.

120.label: Israel Hands
120.recap: Alone on the drifting schooner with the treacherous coxswain, Jim fights for his life in the rigging.

120.label: The Fall of a Chieftain
120.recap: At the empty treasure cache the mutineers turn on Silver, and rescue arrives in the nick of time.

121.label: An unlikely heroine
121.recap: Catherine Morland's plain, cricket-loving childhood is set out as the least promising start a heroine could have.

121.label: Off to Bath
121.recap: Catherine leaves home for six weeks in Bath with almost none of the drama a novel would demand.

121.label: A partner at the dance
121.recap: At the Lower Rooms she is introduced to a teasing young man named Tilney and enjoys herself thoroughly.

121.label: A new best friend
121.recap: Catherine and Isabella Thorpe compare notes on horrid novels and swear undying attachment.

121.label: The man with the gig
121.recap: Catherine's brother arrives in Bath with the boastful John Thorpe, whose talk is all horses and mileage.

121.label: Watching the weather
121.recap: Catherine waits out the rain hoping for a promised walk, and a carriage party turns up with other plans.

121.label: A walk on Beechen Cliff
121.recap: On a walk above the town the talk runs from novels to landscape to Catherine's education.

121.label: Setting out for the abbey
121.recap: Catherine leaves Bath with her new friends, and on the drive one of them invents the gothic welcome awaiting her.

121.label: The chest in the recess
121.recap: Her room proves comfortable and ordinary, except for a heavy old chest she cannot resist trying to open.

121.label: A monument in the church
121.recap: A memorial to the late Mrs. Tilney sets Catherine's imagination working hard on her host.

121.label: The house at ease
121.recap: With the General away the household relaxes, and Catherine begins to wonder how long she ought to stay.

121.label: The road home
121.recap: Catherine travels back over the road she came by, passing every landmark of a happier week.

121.label: A question of consent
121.recap: Catherine's parents are applied to on her behalf, and attach one condition to their blessing.

135.label: A stranger reaches the town
135.recap: A footsore traveller walks into a small mountain town where every inn, house and door is shut against him.

135.label: Morning in the garden
135.recap: The bishop's housekeeper finds the silver gone and the garden wall scaled, and the bishop goes on examining a broken plant.

135.label: A hard winter
135.recap: Out of work and hounded by debts, Fantine begins selling what she has to keep money going to the people minding her daughter.

135.label: A conscience on trial
135.recap: The town's respected mayor must decide what to do after learning that another man is about to be tried in his place.

135.label: Help in the dark wood
135.recap: A stranger takes the heavy water bucket from a small girl and walks beside her back toward the village.

135.label: Behind convent walls
135.recap: Having gone over a garden wall in the night, Valjean finds himself inside a convent and must somehow be explained away.

135.label: Searching all Paris
135.recap: Marius loses all trace of the girl he used to watch in the Luxembourg garden and sinks into a black melancholy.

135.label: The boy of the streets
135.recap: We learn how the innkeepers disposed of their youngest sons, and meet the ragged boy who lives loose in Paris.

135.label: The wineshop at Corinthe
135.recap: The history of an old Paris tavern is set out on the very spot where the insurgents will raise their barricade.

135.label: Under the city
135.recap: Valjean drops beneath the streets and gropes his way through the darkness of the Paris sewers.

135.label: Javert walking alone
135.recap: For the first time in his life the inspector walks with his head down and his hands behind his back.

135.label: A plain stone
135.recap: The book closes at a nameless grave in a neglected, weed-grown corner of a Paris cemetery.

139.label: A proposal refused
139.recap: A young reporter finally speaks to the girl he loves, and learns what sort of man she thinks she could love instead.

139.label: Asking for danger
139.recap: He begs his Scottish news editor for any assignment with real risk in it, and is given a suggestion he may regret.

139.label: Calling at Enmore Park
139.recap: He talks his way into the house of a notorious professor under a thin pretence of scientific agreement.

139.label: The night of the lecture
139.recap: Bruised and half-convinced, he returns to the office, and the affair moves towards a public meeting.

139.label: Up the great river
139.recap: The party crosses the Atlantic and works upriver to Manaos, where sealed instructions wait to be opened.

139.label: Beneath the red cliffs
139.recap: They reach the foot of an enormous wall of rock and begin looking for a way to the top.

139.label: Cut off
139.recap: The narrator writes that their way back has failed them and that no rescue can arrive in time.

139.label: First morning above
139.recap: Waking on the plateau, he discovers something feeding on his leg, and the place begins to show its character.

139.label: A walk by moonlight
139.recap: Too pleased with himself to sleep, he slips out of camp alone to see the central lake by night.

139.label: Watched and waiting
139.recap: Hidden in brushwood and half-starved, the party learns how patiently the plateau's other inhabitants can wait.

139.label: Coming home to an uproar
139.recap: Travelling back through Brazil and across the Atlantic, they find the world already in a fever over rumours of what they found.

145.label: Miss Brooke
145.recap: Ardent, high-minded Dorothea Brooke longs to devote her life to some great and worthy purpose.

145.label: An Unequal Match
145.recap: The dry, middle-aged scholar Mr Casaubon courts young Dorothea, who mistakes his pedantry for greatness.

145.label: The Vincys
145.recap: We meet the charming Vincy siblings, idle Fred and vain Rosamond, and their rich old uncle Featherstone.

145.label: Lydgate's Ambitions
145.recap: The story turns to Tertius Lydgate, an idealistic young doctor newly arrived with grand hopes of reform.

145.label: Disenchantment in Rome
145.recap: On her honeymoon in Rome, Dorothea weeps, already sensing how cold and empty her marriage will be.

145.label: Fred's Debt
145.recap: Feckless Fred Vincy's unpaid debt threatens to drag down the humble Garth family who trusted him.

145.label: Waiting for Death
145.recap: As miserly old Featherstone lies dying, he tries to make Mary Garth burn one of his two wills.

145.label: Casaubon's Heart
145.recap: Lydgate gently warns Casaubon that his heart may fail at any moment, deepening the scholar's bitterness.

145.label: The Dead Hand
145.recap: Casaubon's will is found to carry a cruel clause: Dorothea loses everything if she ever marries Will Ladislaw.

145.label: Raffles
145.recap: The shady past of the pious banker Bulstrode resurfaces when the blackmailer Raffles turns up in town.

145.label: A Temptation
145.recap: With Raffles dying and Lydgate sunk in debt, Bulstrode faces a terrible temptation.

145.label: The Scandal
145.recap: An ugly scandal engulfs Bulstrode and drags the innocent Lydgate's good name down with it.

145.label: A Helping Hand
145.recap: Alone among the town, Dorothea refuses to believe the worst and reaches out to the ruined Lydgate.

145.label: Sunset and Sunrise
145.recap: After much heartache and misunderstanding, Dorothea and Will are at last brought together.

155.label: A letter from India
155.recap: An officer explains why he broke with his cousin at the storming of Seringapatam, and sets down the legend of a sacred yellow diamond.

155.label: Betteredge takes the pen
155.recap: An elderly house-steward is asked to write down all he knows about the lost diamond, and grumbles his way into beginning.

155.label: The Shivering Sand
155.recap: Betteredge describes the quicksand bay that the lonely second housemaid haunts, and walks down to fetch her in to dinner.

155.label: Followed from London
155.recap: Franklin Blake tells Betteredge he has been shadowed for days, and asks about three Indian jugglers seen at the house.

155.label: The birthday dinner
155.recap: Twenty-four guests sit down to Rachel's birthday dinner, where she wears the great diamond and the table talk turns awkward.

155.label: Where to keep it tonight
155.recap: After the guests leave, Rachel jokes about where to put the jewel overnight and settles on a cabinet with no lock.

155.label: Sending for the sergeant
155.recap: An odd sighting and a doctor's fever arrive with the morning post, along with word that a famous London detective is on his way.

155.label: The lady and the sergeant
155.recap: Lady Verinder, uneasy about the detective before she has met him, agrees to see him only with her old steward in the room.

155.label: Miss Clack's diary
155.recap: A poor and relentlessly pious cousin takes over the story, and describes her tract-distributing devotion to the family.

155.label: Franklin comes home
155.recap: Franklin Blake returns from years of wandering abroad and resolves to reopen the question of the diamond himself.

155.label: The doctor's assistant
155.recap: An ailing assistant surgeon keeps a journal of the careful preparations for an unusual experiment he has proposed.

155.label: Pilgrims to Somnauth
155.recap: Years later a traveller joins a vast night pilgrimage in India and watches a ceremony held in honour of the moon god.

158.label: A wedding and a quiet house
158.recap: A young woman who has always had her own way loses her governess to marriage and feels the evenings go long.

158.label: The wedding-cake question
158.recap: Her father's nerves are troubled by the existence of cake until the last of it is eaten.

158.label: A friend adopted
158.recap: Emma takes up a pretty, docile boarder of unknown parentage and starts improving her acquaintance.

158.label: Unrepentant
158.recap: A disagreement with an old friend leaves Emma sorry but entirely unconvinced, and a framed portrait arrives.

158.label: An evening party
158.recap: A gentleman in very good spirits arrives late and seats himself, barely invited, beside Emma.

158.label: A note from Bath
158.recap: A ceremonious note announces a sudden departure, and Emma notices exactly whose name is missing from it.

158.label: Calling on the Bateses
158.recap: To escape a subject she is tired of, Emma pays a long-overdue visit to two poor and grateful neighbours.

158.label: Back from London
158.recap: A young man returns from a frivolous errand quite unashamed, and Emma decides that manner excuses folly.

158.label: The new bride
158.recap: A newcomer settles into Highbury convinced she has arrived to improve the neighbourhood.

158.label: The ball at the Crown
158.recap: After repeated delays the ball finally goes forward at the inn.

158.label: The day at Box Hill
158.recap: A fine day and a carefully arranged outing somehow refuse to become a happy one.

158.label: After the storm
158.recap: A change in the weather sends Emma out of doors in search of some calm.

158.label: Everything settled
158.recap: Old anxieties about a friend are quietly resolved, and a long-hidden parentage is at last made known.

160.label: Summer at Grand Isle
160.recap: A caged parrot and a mocking-bird drive Mr. Pontellier off the gallery of a Creole summer colony.

160.label: A midnight on the porch
160.recap: Her husband comes home late in high spirits, scolds her over the children, and falls asleep while she sits outside crying.

160.label: The moonlit swim
160.recap: On a warm August night the whole colony walks down to the beach and Edna discovers she can swim at last.

160.label: A hammock and a will
160.recap: Asked to come indoors, she refuses for the first time and stays out until the moon turns copper.

160.label: News at the dinner table
160.recap: The whole table informs her at once that Robert is leaving for Mexico that very evening.

160.label: Back to Esplanade Street
160.recap: The family resumes its polished New Orleans routine, and one Tuesday Edna simply goes out instead of receiving callers.

160.label: Coffee under the roof
160.recap: Edna visits the prickly little pianist in her smoky attic rooms and learns a letter has arrived from Mexico.

160.label: A birthday dinner
160.recap: Ten guests gather at a gorgeously dressed table for a cocktail composed by the hostess's father.

160.label: Coffee in the parlour
160.recap: Over black coffee an embroidered tobacco pouch prompts careful questions about the months spent away.

160.label: A long night upstairs
160.recap: Edna keeps a promise to sit with her friend Adèle through a hard and frightening confinement.

160.label: The shuttered cottages
160.recap: Out of season at Grand Isle, Victor and Mariequita are startled by an unannounced visitor walking up from the wharf.

160.label: Stories beyond the bayou
160.recap: The collection turns to short Louisiana tales, opening with a woman who has never once crossed the water by her cabin.

161.label: The Dashwoods
161.recap: When Mr Dashwood dies, his selfish son and daughter-in-law leave the widow and her three daughters poor and unwelcome at Norland.

161.label: Elinor and Edward
161.recap: Sensible Elinor grows quietly attached to the shy Edward Ferrars, even as the family must give up their home.

161.label: Barton Cottage
161.recap: The Dashwoods settle into a modest cottage under the hearty Sir John Middleton's wing.

161.label: Willoughby
161.recap: Romantic Marianne is carried home from the rain by the dashing young Willoughby and falls headlong in love.

161.label: Willoughby Leaves
161.recap: Willoughby abruptly leaves for London, giving the heartbroken Marianne no explanation at all.

161.label: Lucy's Secret
161.recap: The sly Lucy Steele confides to Elinor that she is secretly engaged to Edward, a blow Elinor must bear in silence.

161.label: London
161.recap: In London Marianne anxiously seeks Willoughby, only to be coldly cut by him at a party.

161.label: Willoughby's Betrayal
161.recap: Willoughby returns Marianne's letters and reveals his engagement to a rich heiress, leaving her devastated.

161.label: Edward Exposed
161.recap: Edward's secret engagement to Lucy comes to light, and his furious mother disinherits him.

161.label: Willoughby's Confession
161.recap: During Marianne's grave illness a repentant Willoughby appears to pour out his excuses to Elinor.

161.label: Marianne Recovers
161.recap: Marianne recovers and resolves to live more wisely, while word comes that Lucy has married a Ferrars.

161.label: Edward Free
161.recap: It was Edward's brother whom Lucy wed; freed of his promise, Edward hurries to Elinor and proposes.

161.label: Two Marriages
161.recap: Elinor marries Edward, and in time Marianne gives her heart to the steadfast Colonel Brandon.

164.label: A shifting reef
164.recap: Ships of every nation report an enormous, impossibly fast object in the sea, and the world argues about what it can be.

164.label: The hunt fitted out
164.recap: An American frigate sails armed with every device known to whalers, and a reward is posted for the first man to sight the creature.

164.label: Overboard in the dark
164.recap: Thrown into the night sea, the narrator swims for his life with his servant beside him.

164.label: Terms from the commander
164.recap: The master of the vessel finally speaks to his captives and sets out the single condition on which they may live aboard.

164.label: Dressing for the deep
164.recap: Diving suits, leaded boots and air-guns are brought out for an excursion on the floor of the sea.

164.label: Stones from the shore
164.recap: A shore party's lunch is interrupted by islanders with slings and bows, and they run for the boat.

164.label: The pearl in the grotto
164.recap: In a submarine crypt the captain opens a gigantic oyster to show a pearl he has been letting grow for years.

164.label: Open water at the pole
164.recap: Beyond the ice lies clear sea and a solitary island, and the captain waits for noon to fix their position.

164.label: Sealed under the ice
164.recap: Walled in above and below, they measure their remaining air and start cutting at the thinnest part of the ice.

164.label: Caverns for poulps
164.recap: Near the Bahamas the talk turns to giant cuttlefish, which the harpooner flatly refuses to believe in.

164.label: A gunshot at sea
164.recap: Still shaken by the captain's story of a lost ship, the narrator hears a distant gun and sights a warship bearing down.

164.label: A fisherman's hut
164.recap: The narrator wakes ashore in the far north and sits down to revise the record of everything he has seen.

173.label: A late visitor
173.recap: A suburban doctor's quiet evening is interrupted by an old friend back from Burma with a healed wound and a warning.

173.label: The house on the square
173.recap: They arrive at the home of the man they came to warn and find police already on the steps.

173.label: A stranger's message
173.recap: Left alone in the square, the doctor is approached by a beautiful young woman who presses a sealed envelope on him and begs him to leave.

173.label: The river's latest
173.recap: At the Wapping river police station they view a drowned man whose mutilated hands match earlier bodies pulled from the Thames.

173.label: Singapore Charlie's
173.recap: Disguised as seafaring ruffians, the pair bully their way into a riverside opium shop to watch who comes and goes.

173.label: Night at Redmoat
173.recap: At a fortified country rectory a nervous clergyman explains the burglaries and the yellow-faced man his daughter saw on a train.

173.label: The traveller's house
173.recap: A midnight summons brings them to a creeper-smothered house full of curios, where a famous explorer has met disaster.

173.label: The hall of dragons
173.recap: Drugged and half-delirious, the narrator dreams of a vast tapestried hall and the face of the man they have been hunting.

173.label: Racing the midnight bell
173.recap: At midnight they hurry to a great Strand hotel by the tradesmen's entrance to reach a guest who has been marked out.

173.label: Out on the marshes
173.recap: Acting alone on a risky tip and keeping the police out of it, the two cross the flats at night toward a hulk moored off the bend.

173.label: Among the cellars
173.recap: Bound and carried through phosphorescent vaults strewn with monstrous growths, the narrator finds his friends captive too.

173.label: The last unmasking
173.recap: A late-night arrest in a cluttered scholar's room brings the long pursuit to its final confrontation.

174.label: The Portrait
174.recap: Painter Basil completes a portrait of the beautiful young Dorian Gray while his friend Lord Henry preaches a creed of pleasure.

174.label: A Fatal Wish
174.recap: Intoxicated by Lord Henry's words, Dorian wishes the portrait would age in his place while he stays forever young.

174.label: Sibyl Vane
174.recap: Dorian falls headlong for a poor young actress, Sibyl Vane, dazzled by her talent on the stage.

174.label: Prince Charming
174.recap: Sibyl glows with love for the gentleman she calls her Prince Charming, as her brother James swears to protect her.

174.label: A Cruelty
174.recap: When Sibyl acts badly, a disgusted Dorian casts her off, and that night the painted face shows its first cruel change.

174.label: The Secret Hidden
174.recap: Learning Sibyl has died, Dorian hardens his heart and locks the changing portrait away out of sight.

174.label: Basil's Worry
174.recap: Basil pleads to understand Dorian's new coldness, but Dorian guards his terrible secret.

174.label: Years of Excess
174.recap: Dorian sinks into years of secret vice while his face stays unmarked and the hidden portrait grows monstrous.

174.label: Basil's Last Visit
174.recap: Basil corners Dorian about the rumours; Dorian shows him the corrupted portrait, and the night ends in murder.

174.label: The Opium Den
174.recap: Haunted and craving escape, Dorian visits an opium den, where Sibyl's vengeful brother nearly catches him.

174.label: The Portrait's Verdict
174.recap: Hoping to be good, Dorian turns a knife on the hideous portrait, and meets the fate it had borne for him.

175.label: The author's claim
175.recap: A researcher explains how years in the Opera's archives convinced him the ghost was a real man.

175.label: Panic in the dressing room
175.recap: On gala night a crowd of ballet girls bursts into a dancer's dressing room swearing they have seen the ghost.

175.label: A new voice
175.recap: With the star diva absent, an unknown young soprano sings and astonishes the whole house.

175.label: A letter from Perros
175.recap: Christine withdraws from singing in public and writes to Raoul that she is going to her father's grave.

175.label: The ghost's ultimatum
175.recap: The new managers open a letter setting out four demands and a warning about that evening's performance.

175.label: The empty fortnight
175.recap: After the disastrous evening the diva falls ill and Christine vanishes from the Opera entirely.

175.label: The masked ball
175.recap: Raoul goes masked in a white domino into a packed Opera ball to keep an appointment.

175.label: On the Opera roof
175.recap: High above Paris beneath Apollo's bronze lyre, Christine confesses to Raoul what frightens her.

175.label: The house in uproar
175.recap: Backstage dissolves into rumour and argument after a singer disappears in the middle of a performance.

175.label: Into the cellars
175.recap: Raoul and the Persian drop through a hidden trapdoor into the Opera's lower levels with pistols raised.

175.label: Behind the wall
175.recap: Trapped listeners overhear a quarrel about a bag holding two keys and a warning about curiosity.

175.label: What the papers said
175.recap: The narrator gathers his last proofs and describes how the affair faded into theatre gossip.

202.label: Born in Tuckahoe
202.recap: Douglass describes the poor, ague-ridden district where he was born and explains why he cannot say what year it was.

202.label: Sent to old master
202.recap: The boy learns that the feared "old master" is a real man on a great plantation, and that he must go there.

202.label: His mother's night visits
202.recap: He recalls the few nighttime visits his mother made to him, and how little chance slavery left them to know each other.

202.label: Colonel Lloyd's plantation
202.recap: He surveys the isolated home plantation, where no school, no shop and no outside opinion ever reaches the enslaved people.

202.label: A new life in Baltimore
202.recap: Sent to the city, he finds hot pavements, hostile boys and a mistress who treats him as a child rather than property.

202.label: Forbidden the alphabet
202.recap: His master forbids the reading lessons and explains why, and the boy takes the explanation as instruction of another kind.

202.label: Sent to Covey
202.recap: He walks seven miles in the frost to the farm of a man hired out for his reputation at breaking people.

202.label: A night in the woods
202.recap: Turned back to Covey's after seeking protection, he hides in the woods and is found there by a kind stranger.

202.label: The runaway plot
202.recap: Hired to a kinder master, he decides that kindness only gilds the chain and begins quietly planning an escape with others.

202.label: Leaving slavery behind
202.recap: He explains why he will not describe the manner of his escape, then leads up to the day he fixed for going.

202.label: A free man in New York
202.recap: Standing free on Broadway, he tries to describe a joy he says no words reach, and the loneliness that follows it.

202.label: Ink, voice and vote
202.recap: Back from Britain he defies his friends' advice to start his own paper, and closes with a pledge for the years ahead.

203.label: A bargain over wine
203.recap: A Kentucky landowner and a slave trader sit over their glasses, haggling about which of the people on the farm will settle a debt.

203.label: A husband's bitterness
203.recap: Eliza's husband George visits her room and pours out his fury at the master who has taken him from work he was good at.

203.label: A mother sets out
203.recap: Eliza leaves the only home she has ever known and walks through the frosty night with her sleeping son in her arms.

203.label: The river crossing
203.recap: Spotted at a riverside inn with her pursuers at the door, Eliza makes a desperate leap toward the far bank.

203.label: Down the great river
203.recap: Tom is carried south on a steamboat piled with cotton, reading his Bible and watching the plantations slide past.

203.label: A New Orleans household
203.recap: Tom enters the elegant, disordered home of a charming, sceptical master, his ailing wife and their visiting New England cousin.

203.label: An unexpected present
203.recap: St. Clare brings home a wild, badly used little girl and hands her over to his cousin to be educated.

203.label: The rose-coloured room
203.recap: The household keeps watch in a bright, carefully furnished bedroom as a child's long illness draws to its turn.

203.label: Sold separately or in lots
203.recap: The narrator walks the reader through a tidy New Orleans warehouse where husbands, wives and children are arranged for buyers.

203.label: The road to the swamp
203.recap: Tom and two frightened women are carted along a wild pine-and-cypress road toward a remote plantation.

203.label: A new kind of master
203.recap: Tom works steadily in the cotton fields and finds that his quiet competence earns his owner's dislike rather than favour.

203.label: The garret's reputation
203.recap: A dusty attic full of cast-off furniture is described, along with the whispered stories that make everyone on the place avoid it.

203.label: Homecoming in Kentucky
203.recap: The Shelby house is scrubbed and the supper table laid for young George's return, though he could not bring himself to write what he had seen.

204.label: A hunt across London
204.recap: The head of the Paris police lands in England after a legendary thief and starts following a trail of small absurdities.

204.label: The sealed garden
204.recap: A glittering dinner party assembles in a Paris house whose garden is ringed by a smooth, unscalable wall.

204.label: Footsteps in the passage
204.recap: At the annual dinner of a very exclusive club, Father Brown sits alone in a side room and listens to the way a man walks.

204.label: A Boxing Day pantomime
204.recap: A Christmas gathering near Putney admires three famous diamonds, then decides to stage an old-fashioned harlequinade.

204.label: The confectioner's shop
204.recap: A young artist proposes to a shop girl, who answers with the story of two suitors she has never quite shaken off.

204.label: The castle in the glen
204.recap: Father Brown joins an inquiry at a bleak Scottish castle where the last earl vanished and a silent servant kept house.

204.label: The white-and-green house
204.recap: Father Brown and Flambeau leave a strange suburban household shared by a colour-drunk poet, his tired wife and an Indian hermit.

204.label: Rowing to Reed Island
