204.recap: Flambeau takes a boating holiday through the Norfolk rivers and calls on a prince who once sent him an admiring card.

204.label: Two brothers at daybreak
204.recap: In a steep hilltop village, a devout curate meets his hard-drinking elder brother outside the inn at dawn.

204.label: The gilt eye
204.recap: Flambeau shows Father Brown his new London offices, where a self-styled priest of the sun has hung an enormous golden eye.

204.label: A tomb in the frost
204.recap: On a freezing night two figures climb to a famous general's monument, and Father Brown starts questioning the story carved into it.

204.label: The house by the railway
204.recap: Father Brown is knocked up at daybreak with news that a famously cheerful philanthropist has been found dead beside a railway line.

205.label: Two years by the pond
205.recap: He explains that he lived alone in a house he built himself beside Walden Pond and answers his townsmen's questions about how.

205.label: Borrowing an axe
205.recap: He cuts white pines beside the still-frozen pond and begins hewing the timber for his house.

205.label: Choosing a place to live
205.recap: He recounts imagining himself the owner of every farm around Concord, then explains what he went to the woods for.

205.label: Listening instead of reading
205.recap: He puts books aside to attend to the sounds around his house, from birds and bells to the passing railroad.

205.label: Three chairs
205.recap: He describes the visitors his small house received, among them a cheerful woodchopper he admires and cannot quite classify.

205.label: Seven miles of beans
205.recap: He hoes his long bean rows through the summer and reckons up exactly what the crop cost him and earned.

205.label: The ponds around
205.recap: He wanders out to the neighbouring ponds and sets down Walden's colour, depth and shoreline in detail.

205.label: War in the woodpile
205.recap: He finds two races of ants locked in a pitched battle across his woodpile and carries three of them indoors to watch.

205.label: The ice harvest
205.recap: A crowd of men arrives with strange tools and begins cutting the pond's ice into cakes and stacking it in great piles.

205.label: The ice goes out
205.recap: He watches the pond thaw, the sandbank pour out its foliage-like forms, and the season turn.

205.label: Leaving the woods
205.recap: He gives his reasons for leaving the pond and urges the reader to advance in the direction of their own dreams.

205.label: A night in the lock-up
205.recap: Jailed for a tax he refused to pay, he spends one night in the village prison and sees his own town from inside it.

209.label: A tale by the fire
209.recap: On Christmas Eve a guest promises the company a manuscript worse than any ghost story yet told.

209.label: Arriving at Bly
209.recap: The new governess reaches the country house at dusk and is charmed by the little girl waiting at the door.

209.label: A letter from the school
209.recap: A letter about the boy arrives, and the governess decides to answer nobody about it at all.

209.label: A figure on the tower
209.recap: Out walking at the end of a June day, she looks up and finds a man standing where no man should be.

209.label: The face at the window
209.recap: Turning back for a pair of gloves, she finds the same stranger looking in from the terrace.

209.label: By the lake
209.recap: Sitting with the little girl beside the water, she becomes certain the two of them are not alone.

209.label: Telling the housekeeper
209.recap: She pours out to Mrs. Grose what she believes the child noticed and deliberately did not mention.

209.label: The staircase at night
209.recap: Reading late, she takes a candle into the passage and meets something waiting on the stairs.

209.label: On the terrace
209.recap: With the children playing on the lawn below, the two women go back over what happened in the night.

209.label: A candle at his door
209.recap: She listens outside the boy's room and finds him wide awake, cheerful and ready to talk.

209.label: Naming it aloud
209.recap: At the water's edge she finally says a name out loud, and everyone present reacts differently.

209.label: The last hour
209.recap: Alone with the boy, she keeps him with his back to the window and presses him for the truth.

215.label: Into the Primitive
215.recap: Buck, a pampered ranch dog, is stolen and sold north into the brutal world of sled dogs in the Klondike gold rush.

215.label: The Law of Club and Fang
215.recap: Buck learns the harsh law of club and fang and the savagery needed to survive among the sled teams.

215.label: The Dominant Primordial Beast
215.recap: The wild grows strong in Buck as he battles the cruel lead dog Spitz for mastery of the team.

215.label: The Toil of Trace and Trail
215.recap: Sold to greenhorns who cannot manage the trail, Buck and the worn team are driven to the edge of death.

215.label: For the Love of a Man
215.recap: Rescued by the kind John Thornton, Buck loves him fiercely and performs astonishing feats for his sake.

215.label: The Sounding of the Call
215.recap: With Thornton gone, nothing binds Buck to men any longer, and he answers the wild at last to run with the wolves.

219.label: Waiting for the tide
219.recap: Four men sit on a yawl anchored in the Thames estuary at dusk, and one of them begins to talk about old darkness.

219.label: A blank space on the map
219.recap: Marlow explains how a boyhood love of unmapped places drove him to beg relatives for command of a river steamboat.

219.label: The company offices
219.recap: He signs his contract in a hushed European city, passing two knitting women and a doctor with unusual questions.

219.label: The lower station
219.recap: Landing at the coast station, he walks up past abandoned machinery, pointless blasting, and a chained work gang.

219.label: The immaculate accountant
219.recap: Amid general muddle he meets a perfectly dressed bookkeeper, from whom he first hears the name Kurtz.

219.label: Meeting the manager
219.recap: After a long overland tramp Marlow reaches the Central Station to find his steamer sunk and the manager oddly unhurried.

219.label: A painting by candlelight
219.recap: A young agent tries to pump him for information, and a strange painting on the wall turns out to be Kurtz's work.

219.label: Steaming upriver
219.recap: The patched-up steamboat crawls between walls of forest while Marlow guesses at the channel and listens to distant drums.

219.label: Fog on the river
219.recap: A blinding white fog stops the boat a few miles short of the Inner Station, and a great cry rises from the unseen banks.

219.label: Arrows from the bank
219.recap: Steering through a narrow channel, the boat is met by a shower of arrows from the bushes and answering rifle fire.

219.label: The man in patches
219.recap: At the Inner Station a young Russian dressed like a harlequin comes aboard, talking without pause about the man upriver.

219.label: A stretcher in the grass
219.recap: A stretcher is carried down toward the steamer as crowds pour out of the forest and then stand utterly still.

219.label: A call in the sepulchral city
219.recap: Back in Europe, Marlow calls on a woman still in mourning to return a packet of letters, and the room darkens as she talks.

221.label: Murder in Park Lane
221.recap: Watson lays out the killing of a young nobleman shot inside a locked upstairs room, then goes to stare at the house himself and collides with a shabby old bookseller.

221.label: A frantic young solicitor
221.recap: A dishevelled man bursts into the sitting room announcing his own name as though it explains everything, and gets read off in a single sentence instead.

221.label: A chain of small inferences
221.recap: Holmes startles Watson by naming his private financial thoughts, explains the chain link by link, and then hands him a sheet of odd little figures.

221.label: The solitary cyclist
221.recap: Watson sifts eight crowded years of casework and chooses the affair of a young woman whose lonely country ride keeps being shadowed.

221.label: A headmaster collapses
221.recap: A large and very dignified schoolmaster staggers into the room and faints flat on the hearthrug before he can say a word about why he came.

221.label: Breakfast with a harpoon
221.recap: After days of unexplained absences, Holmes strides in at breakfast with a barbed spear under his arm and explains what he has been doing with it.

221.label: The worst man in London
221.recap: A calling card on the table sets Holmes off on the character of a blackmailer he nevertheless has to sit down and bargain with.

221.label: Lestrade drops in
221.recap: An evening of weather talk and cigars ends with the Scotland Yard man admitting there is something distinctly odd on his hands.

221.label: Choosing from a crowded year
221.recap: Watson turns over notes on a dozen famous cases before settling on the episode at Yoxley Old Place as the one that shows his friend best.

221.label: A garbled telegram
221.recap: A wire about a missing right wing three-quarter arrives on a gloomy February morning and gives Holmes a puzzled quarter of an hour.

221.label: Woken before dawn
221.recap: Holmes shakes Watson awake by candlelight and hurries him into a cab through the dark streets toward Charing Cross and an early train.

221.label: The last case
221.recap: Watson explains why he had meant this to be the final published record of his friend's work, and why he is publishing one more.

223.label: The absent Mr Glass
223.recap: A shabby priest interrupts a famous criminologist with what sounds like a trivial domestic problem.

223.label: A poet in Italy
223.recap: A flamboyant Tuscan poet meets an old schoolfellow turned courier and joins a banker's party into the mountains.

223.label: A quarrel in Paris
223.recap: Two French freethinkers are summoned by their idol, a celebrated scientist accused by a furious officer.

223.label: Behind the theatre
223.recap: Two eminent rivals meet in a dark passage outside an actress's private stage door.

223.label: A prison in Chicago
223.recap: Father Brown recalls an American official who trusted a lie-detecting machine above everything else.

223.label: The man with the false nose
223.recap: In a tiny London tavern the priest asks his friend to follow a passing stranger, and a frightened girl listens.

223.label: A newspaper legend
223.recap: A nervous editor opens a contributor's letter about a Devonshire family curse he hopes to expose.

223.label: A Cornish cruise
223.recap: Convalescing on a yacht off Cornwall, the priest listens without much interest to talk of local legends.

223.label: The winter seafront
223.recap: Two friends walking a bleak Essex coast in winter come upon a deserted holiday town.

223.label: A shot in the mist
223.recap: Walking home in fog the priest hears a shot followed by a run of noises he cannot place.

223.label: The American interviewer
223.recap: A brash American reporter is sent out to Oxford to interview a quiet, obscure philosopher.

223.label: A German toy kingdom
223.recap: In a sunlit little German state the priest is told that a man was once shot there without firearms.

224.label: Waiting for the visitor
224.recap: With her father laid up by gout, a sheltered vicar's daughter learns she must receive a stranger from London alone.

224.label: The guest arrives
224.recap: Shown in by the back way, the young visitor meets his hostess, and neither is at all what the other imagined.

224.label: A game of chess
224.recap: An evening's chess reveals something distinctly odd about the way the visitor learned the game.

224.label: A ride to the cliffs
224.recap: An attempt to help Elfride mount goes badly, and the pair make their way by lane and field down to the sea.

224.label: Village news at the vicarage
224.recap: The sexton's cheerful account of an accident at the works lands very differently on one of his listeners.

224.label: Rain on the window
224.recap: Rain beats against the carriage glass as a train carries two young people up to Paddington.

224.label: The reviewer's chambers
224.recap: In a soot-blackened London inn, Stephen calls on the older friend he admires above every other man.

224.label: On the church tower
224.recap: Left alone on the leads of a tower due for demolition, Elfride repeats a giddy trick she performed the year before.

224.label: The cliff without a name
224.recap: A demonstration about air currents above the sea turns dangerous on a slope slicked by sudden rain.

224.label: A confession attempted
224.recap: Walking down to the river, Elfride sets out to tell the whole truth and finds at the last moment that she cannot.

224.label: A knock in the rain
224.recap: Late on a wet London evening, a faint tapping at Knight's chambers brings someone he did not expect.

224.label: The valley walk
224.recap: Two travellers walk inland from the coast to a church, and go down the steps into the family vault.

228.label: The invocation
228.recap: The poet announces his subject: a man expelled from his ruined homeland by fate and a goddess's hatred, and the long labours he bore.

228.label: Juno and the winds
228.recap: Furious that the Trojan ships are sailing on, the queen of heaven goes to the king of the winds and asks him to scatter them.

228.label: A captive Greek
228.recap: Shepherds drag a bound Greek prisoner before the king, and the crowd presses in to hear what he has to say about the huge wooden horse.

228.label: An omen from the sea
228.recap: While a priest is sacrificing at the shore, two serpents come out of the water and make straight for him.

228.label: A ghost at midnight
228.recap: Asleep after a day of celebration, Aeneas is visited by the ghost of the city's fallen champion.

228.label: Building the fleet
228.recap: The survivors cut timber at the foot of the mountain, build ships, and set out to look for the land the gods have promised them.

228.label: The queen confides
228.recap: The queen of Carthage tells her sister what her Trojan guest has stirred in her, and how firmly she had sworn never to love again.

228.label: Weather at sea
228.recap: Sailing away from the African coast, the fleet runs into heavy weather and the pilot urges a turn toward a friendlier shore.

228.label: The ferryman's shore
228.recap: Guided past monstrous shapes, Aeneas reaches the river of the dead and sees the crowds waiting on the bank for the boatman.

228.label: Past the enchanted coast
228.recap: After burying his old nurse, Aeneas sails by night past a dangerous shore loud with the cries of transformed beasts.

228.label: Two friends on watch
228.recap: Two inseparable friends share the night watch at the camp gate, and one of them begins to talk himself into a daring errand.

228.label: The challenge
228.recap: With his allies broken and his honour questioned, Turnus storms in and demands the single combat that will end the war.

236.label: Visitors at the cave
236.recap: A wolf family's evening is interrupted first by a gossiping jackal and then by something small coming uphill.

236.label: The Pack Council
236.recap: The cubs are carried to the meeting rock to be looked over, and one of them needs someone to speak for him.

236.label: Night at the rock
236.recap: The Pack gathers with the leadership open, old grudges surface, and the boy brings something the wolves fear.

236.label: Lessons with Baloo
236.recap: An earlier tale: the old bear drills the boy in the Law and the Master Words, and is argued with about it.

236.label: Carried through the treetops
236.recap: Hands seize the sleeping boy and the Monkey People race him away along their roads in the branches.

236.label: The Cold Lairs
236.recap: Rescuers creep up on the monkeys' ruined city under a clouding moon, and the fight begins in earnest.

236.label: Down to the village
236.recap: The boy walks twenty miles out of the valley and is taken in by villagers who think they recognise him.

236.label: Herding the buffaloes
236.recap: Sent out with the herds each dawn, he keeps a lookout posted on a rock and waits for news.

236.label: Beaches in the Bering Sea
236.recap: A new tale: on crowded northern rookeries the seals fight for room, and one pup is born the wrong colour.

236.label: A mongoose indoors
236.recap: A flood washes a young mongoose into an English family's bungalow, where curiosity keeps him.

236.label: The elephant Kala Nag
236.recap: A veteran government elephant and the small boy of his driver's family are introduced in the Garo hills.

236.label: Camp in the rain
236.recap: A month of rain, a stampede, and a narrator who finds himself listening to the transport animals argue.

244.label: Watson Meets Holmes
244.recap: Invalided home from war, Dr Watson is introduced to the eccentric Sherlock Holmes and they take rooms together at Baker Street.

244.label: The Science of Deduction
244.recap: Watson puzzles over his strange flatmate until Holmes reveals he is the world's first consulting detective.

244.label: The Lauriston Gardens Mystery
244.recap: Holmes is called to an empty house where a man lies dead without a wound, the word RACHE scrawled in blood on the wall.

244.label: What John Rance Had to Tell
244.recap: Holmes questions the constable who found the body and astonishes the police with deductions about the killer.

244.label: An Unexpected Visitor
244.recap: A newspaper advertisement lures someone to Baker Street, but the wily suspect slips through Holmes's fingers.

244.label: Light in the Darkness
244.recap: A second murder shakes the baffled police, and Holmes calmly announces he already has the culprit in hand.

244.label: The Great Alkali Plain
244.recap: The story leaps to the American West, where a man and a little girl, lone survivors in the desert, are rescued by Mormon pioneers.

244.label: The Flower of Utah
244.recap: Years on, the girl Lucy grows up and falls in love with a young hunter, against the elders' rigid wishes.

244.label: Ferrier and the Prophet
244.recap: The Mormon leader demands Lucy marry within the faith, and her adoptive father quietly defies him.

244.label: A Flight for Life
244.recap: Lucy, her father, and her lover flee across the mountains, hunted by the vengeful Avenging Angels.

244.label: The Avenging Angels
244.recap: Tragedy overtakes the fugitives, setting the sole survivor on a lifelong road of revenge.

244.label: The Conclusion
244.recap: Back in London the captured killer tells how the western tragedy drove his hunt, and Holmes lays out the full solution.

245.label: The River and Its Explorers
245.recap: Twain recounts the early explorers of the Mississippi, chief among them La Salle.

245.label: The River Rises
245.recap: As a green cub pilot, young Twain learns the river the hard way during a dangerous high-water rise.

245.label: A Pilot at Last
245.recap: Twain wins his pilot's license, only for the Civil War to close the river to steamboating.

245.label: A Thumb-print
245.recap: On his return journey Twain nears Napoleon, Arkansas, with a curious private errand and a strange tale to tell.

245.label: The Metropolis of the South
245.recap: Twain reaches New Orleans, comparing the city he remembers with the one he now finds.

245.label: Reminiscences
245.recap: Steaming north toward St. Louis, Twain gathers his last reminiscences of the great river.

271.label: A meadow and a mother
271.recap: A black colt grows up in a quiet meadow under a kind master, taking his manners from his mother.

271.label: The hunt goes past
271.recap: The young colts watch a hare hunt sweep across the neighbouring fields, and it ends badly for more than the hare.

271.label: Bit, saddle and shoes
271.recap: At four years old he is broken in gently by his first master, and taught not to fear a passing train.

271.label: The wooden bridge
271.recap: Driving home through a gale and a rising river, he refuses to step onto a bridge and his master learns why.

271.label: Smoke in the stable
271.recap: A pipe carried up into the hayloft leaves the horses shut in a burning stable in the middle of the night.

271.label: The midnight gallop
271.recap: Woken by the stable bell, he is ridden eight miles at full speed to fetch a doctor to the house.

271.label: A new stable, new rules
271.recap: Sold on to a great house, he and Ginger meet a coachman bound to a mistress who insists her horses be reined up tight.

271.label: A loose shoe
271.recap: A clever groom with one weakness is left in charge of the stables and rides him home over freshly stoned roads.

271.label: Bargaining at the fair
271.recap: Standing for sale among sound horses and broken ones, he judges the buyers by their hands and hopes for one particular man.

271.label: An old friend on the rank
271.recap: Waiting with the other cabs, he recognises a worn-out chestnut mare drawn up beside him and they manage a quiet talk.

271.label: The hardest master
271.recap: Sold to an owner who allows no rest, he is worked through the summer heat until an overloaded fare nearly finishes him.

271.label: A quiet house on a lawn
271.recap: Groomed with unusual care, he is driven out to be shown to three ladies who may take him on trial.

345.label: The Journey East
345.recap: Solicitor Jonathan Harker travels deep into the Carpathians to help a mysterious Count with a London property purchase.

345.label: A Prisoner in the Castle
345.recap: Harker realises the castle is a prison and begins to grasp the monstrous nature of his host.

345.label: Mina and Lucy
345.recap: Back in England, Mina exchanges letters with her dear friend Lucy, who is giddy over three marriage proposals.

345.label: Whitby
345.recap: Mina joins Lucy at the seaside town of Whitby, fretting over Jonathan's long silence.

345.label: The Derelict Ship
345.recap: A fierce storm drives a derelict ship ashore at Whitby, its dead captain lashed to the helm and no living soul aboard.

345.label: Sleepwalking
345.recap: Mina rescues the sleepwalking Lucy from the cliff at night and notices two small marks at her throat.

345.label: A Wasting Illness
345.recap: Lucy grows pale and weak from an illness no one can explain, and Dr Seward sends for his old teacher Van Helsing.

345.label: A Turn for the Worse
345.recap: Despite the doctors' desperate efforts, Lucy's strange decline takes a frightening turn.

345.label: Van Helsing's Warning
345.recap: Van Helsing struggles to make the sceptical Seward believe the dreadful truth about what now stalks the night.

345.label: The Churchyard
345.recap: At midnight the men keep a grim vigil at the tomb to face the horror Van Helsing has foretold.

345.label: The Hunters Unite
345.recap: The friends band together under Van Helsing and resolve to hunt their enemy to the end.

345.label: In the Asylum
345.recap: Seward's strange patient Renfield reveals what he has seen as the danger reaches into the asylum itself.

345.label: The Last Pursuit
345.recap: The hunters race across the frozen Carpathians for a final reckoning before the sun goes down.

348.label: Two kinds of Strife
348.recap: The poet calls on the Muses and tells his brother Perses that rivalry comes in two forms, one ruinous and one that spurs honest work.

348.label: The making of Pandora
348.recap: Angered by a theft of fire, Zeus has the gods fashion a lovely maiden and send her down to mortals as a gift.

348.label: The ages of mankind
348.recap: The poet traces a succession of human races from a golden age of ease down to the hard iron present.

348.label: Winter on the farm
348.recap: A long portrait of the cruellest month, with the north wind driving beasts to cover, followed by advice on clothing against it.

348.label: The Muses on Helicon
348.recap: The Theogony opens with the goddesses meeting a shepherd on the mountain and giving him a laurel staff and a voice for song.

348.label: A stone in swaddling clothes
348.recap: Grieving for the children Cronos swallows at birth, Rhea asks Earth and Heaven for a plan to hide her youngest.

348.label: The hundred-handed brothers
348.recap: Three enormous prisoners bound beneath the earth are brought back to the light and fed nectar before their help is asked.

348.label: Alcmena comes to Thebes
348.recap: A woman of great beauty follows her husband into exile at Thebes, where he must first finish a task laid on him.

348.label: A flower in the meadow
348.recap: A girl gathering flowers with her companions reaches for one marvellous bloom, and the plain opens beneath her.

348.label: A newborn thief
348.recap: Born at dawn in a shady cave, Hermes leaves his cradle at once and finds a tortoise feeding at the gate.

348.label: Mouse meets frog king
348.recap: A mouse drinking at a pond is hailed by the king of the frogs, and the two boast about their families and their diets.

348.label: A contest of song
348.recap: Two poets are each asked to recite their finest passage before a king who must decide between war and husbandry.

389.label: An evening on the terrace
389.recap: Two friends walk above a quiet Welsh valley while one argues that a veil hides the real world from human eyes.

389.label: Into the laboratory
389.recap: Raymond takes his witness through a locked door into the room where the operation is to be done.

389.label: Clarke's private memoirs
389.recap: Years afterwards, Clarke sits by his fire with the manuscript in which he collects accounts of the unexplained.

389.label: The girl at the farm
389.recap: A written case describes a strange child boarded at a Welsh farmhouse and her long solitary walks in the forest.

389.label: A beggar in Soho
389.recap: Villiers recognises an old college friend in a beggar and walks him into a quiet street to hear his story.

389.label: Villiers calls on Clarke
389.recap: Villiers brings his puzzle to Clarke, including what he felt inside an empty house in Paul Street.

389.label: A letter of advice
389.recap: Villiers shows a friend the strange reply he received when he asked an older man what to do.

389.label: News from Piccadilly
389.recap: A popular nobleman is found dead in his room, and London soon learns his is not the only such death.

389.label: What Villiers found
389.recap: Villiers spreads out his documents and explains where his search through the city's worst streets has led.

389.label: A doctor's hurried notes
389.recap: A physician's private memorandum records, in guarded language, what he was called in to witness.

389.label: Back to the valley
389.recap: Clarke writes of returning to the Welsh village and wandering for hours in the great wood above it.

389.label: Raymond's reply
389.recap: Raymond answers at last and sets down plainly how much of it he had known all along.

393.label: Below decks, becalmed
393.recap: An old Irish sailor plays his fiddle and spins yarns for the crew of a ship stuck in a dead calm.

393.label: Something burning
393.recap: On the fourth still day the passengers glimpse sharks under the hull, and then the captain smells smoke.

393.label: Away in the dinghy
393.recap: The smallest boat is lowered with the old sailor and the two children aboard, and a fog bank comes on.

393.label: The derelict brig
393.recap: They pull alongside an abandoned timber ship and climb aboard to see what has been left behind.

393.label: The lagoon
393.recap: The boat drifts through a break in the reef into a bright, sheltered lagoon fringed with palms.

393.label: Alone in the dark
393.recap: The two children spend a terrible night huddled in their hut, unable to speak of what they have seen.

393.label: Years later
393.recap: Long afterwards, a girl sits feeding a tame blue bird outside the small house they have built.

393.label: The rock pool
393.recap: Wading in a pool on the reef at low tide, Dick is caught fast by something under the water.

393.label: Marks on the sand
393.recap: Rowing back to the old beach for fruit, Dick finds the sand trampled and the signs of night visitors.

393.label: The storm
393.recap: A leaden stillness gives way to a wind and rain unlike any weather the island has shown them.

393.label: Adrift on the tide
393.recap: Carrying fruit down to the water, Dick looks up to see the boat loose in the middle of the lagoon.

393.label: Sailing south
393.recap: A fast schooner clears the Golden Gate and turns south, carrying a man who will not give up his search.

394.label: The Amazons
394.recap: The genteel ladies who rule the little town of Cranford are scandalised by the plain-spoken newcomer Captain Brown.

394.label: Captain Brown
394.recap: Kindly Captain Brown wins the town's affection before a sudden tragedy on the railway.

394.label: An Old Love
394.recap: We learn of gentle Miss Matty's long-lost romance with the farmer Mr Holbrook.

394.label: Mr Holbrook
394.recap: A visit to Mr Holbrook's farm stirs old feelings the years had never quite stilled.

394.label: Old Letters
394.recap: Miss Matty and the narrator spend a quiet evening reading the family's bundle of old letters.

394.label: Poor Peter
394.recap: We hear how Miss Matty's mischievous brother Peter played one prank too many and ran away to sea.

394.label: Visiting
394.recap: Cranford flutters over the proper etiquette of who may call upon the grand Mrs Jamieson.

394.label: Your Ladyship
394.recap: The ladies are agog at the arrival of the titled but unassuming Lady Glenmire.

394.label: Signor Brunoni
394.recap: A travelling magician dazzles and unsettles the town, setting off a wave of nervous rumours.

394.label: The Panic
394.recap: Fear of robbers throws the timid ladies of Cranford into a delicious panic.

394.label: Old Friends
394.recap: Lady Glenmire surprises everyone, and the mystery of Signor Brunoni is gently solved.

394.label: A Clue
394.recap: A surprising engagement sets tongues wagging, and a clue surfaces about Miss Matty's long-lost brother.

394.label: Stopped Payment
394.recap: The failure of the town bank leaves the trusting Miss Matty suddenly penniless.

394.label: Friends in Need
394.recap: Her friends quietly rally round, and Miss Matty makes a brave new start selling tea.

394.label: A Happy Return
394.recap: A long-awaited return from distant lands brings joy back to Miss Matty's door.

394.label: Peace to Cranford
394.recap: With old wounds healed, gentle peace settles once more over the little town.

408.label: The unasked question
408.recap: The writer describes the question nobody puts to him directly, and the childhood moment when he first felt shut out.

408.label: After the war
408.recap: The rise and collapse of the Freedmen's Bureau is traced from the first fugitives who appeared inside Union lines.

408.label: Weighing a leader
408.recap: Booker T. Washington's programme is described with real admiration and then questioned point by point.

408.label: A school in the hills
408.recap: A student walks the Tennessee back roads hunting a country school, finds one, and meets the families who fill it.

408.label: Atlanta and its hunger
408.recap: Atlanta is drawn as a city racing after money, and the writer warns what that appetite costs both races.

408.label: Into the Black Belt
408.recap: A train journey south turns into a tour of Georgia's cotton country and a census of the people living on it.

408.label: The cotton kingdom
408.recap: Cotton, credit and the crop-lien system are followed from the field into the merchant's ledger.

408.label: A country revival
408.recap: A young teacher walks toward a backwoods church at night and meets a religious frenzy unlike anything he has known.

408.label: A first-born son
408.recap: A telegram brings news of a birth, and a father sets down what the child's first months were like.

408.label: Three temptations
408.recap: The life of a black clergyman is told as a passage through the temptations of hate, despair and doubt.

408.label: The coming of John
408.recap: A good-natured Georgia boy is sent north to school, and the story follows what an education begins to do to him.

408.label: The sorrow songs
408.recap: The book closes with the slave songs, their origins and meaning, and a final question addressed to America.

421.label: Leaving Essendean
421.recap: David takes the key from his father's door for the last time and walks to the ford with the minister, who has a letter to give him.

421.label: Asking the way to Shaws
421.recap: Coming down toward Edinburgh, David asks strangers for directions and finds that the name of his family's house makes every one of them uneasy.

421.label: Porridge and a fly-leaf
421.recap: A quiet day among his uncle's books leaves David puzzling over an inscription in an old chap-book that does not add up.

421.label: The inn at Queen's Ferry
421.recap: David is brought to an overheated upstairs room where a cool, courteous sea captain rises to greet his uncle.

421.label: A boat in the fog
421.recap: After days of foul weather the brig runs something down in the dark, and the single survivor is brought aboard carrying pistols and a sword.

421.label: Behind the barred door
421.recap: David climbs into the berth with an armful of pistols and watches the deck while his companion waits below with sword and dirk.

421.label: Called on deck to pilot
421.recap: The captain fetches both passengers out to look at fountains of white water rising one after another from the moonlit sea.

421.label: Crossing into Appin
421.recap: David is rowed up the loch, sees red coats moving along the shore, and is set down alone in a birch wood above the road.

421.label: Running by night
421.recap: The two travellers pass news from house to house as they hurry, and daybreak catches them in a bare valley of rock and river.

421.label: A nest in the trees
421.recap: High on a wooded hillside they reach a hidden wattled house where a chief has lived for years out of the soldiers' reach.

421.label: Knocking at Shaws
421.recap: Alan hammers at the door of the old house until a window goes up and a frightened voice demands to know who is there.

421.label: Rest-and-be-Thankful
421.recap: Looking down on Edinburgh, the two friends stop at the place where they both know their roads must part.

468.label: A crowd at Passy
468.recap: A traveller stops in a country town where a crowd has gathered around a convoy of chained women, and finds a young gentleman weeping in the corner of the inn.

468.label: The coach from Arras
468.recap: A model student, one day from going home, watches a girl step down from a coach and abandons every plan he had for his life.

468.label: Kept at the door
468.recap: Returning to his Paris lodging earlier than expected, he is left waiting outside and hears something from the frightened maid that he cannot make himself believe.

468.label: After the examination
468.recap: Now a promising young churchman, he shines at a public examination in theology and returns to the seminary covered in congratulations.

468.label: Fire at Chaillot
468.recap: A servant arrives with news of a fire at their country house, and he rushes out to see what has survived it.

468.label: Supper and a charade
468.recap: An elaborate joke is played over supper at a wealthy old admirer's table, with everyone at it acting a part.

468.label: Five minutes down the street
468.recap: Barely clear of the house, a stranger steps out of the dark, recognises one of the party, and vanishes again.

468.label: The visitor and the mirror
468.recap: A foreign admirer is shown upstairs, and Manon receives him in a manner nobody in the room expected.

468.label: The door bursts open
468.recap: An enraged old man arrives at midnight with armed guards, looking for someone else entirely, and finds the two of them instead.

468.label: Beside the wagons
468.recap: He buys minutes of the guards' indulgence so that he can ride alongside the prison carts on the road to the coast.

468.label: Landfall in New Orleans
468.recap: After two months at sea they reach a settlement of mud huts, and the governor takes an interest in the couple's manners.

468.label: A ship on the river
468.recap: Walking beside the water, he watches a vessel come in and recognises a face among the passengers coming ashore.

500.label: The log that talks
500.recap: An old carpenter picks up a common piece of firewood and hears it complain when he raises his hatchet.

500.label: Geppetto carves a son

500.label: The puppet theatre
500.recap: Hauled before the terrifying director of a marionette theatre, the runaway pleads for a friend's life.

500.label: Gold and two strangers
500.recap: Sent home with five gold pieces for his father, he meets a limping fox and a blind cat who take a keen interest in his pockets.

500.label: Night on the road
500.recap: Alone in the dark with coins hidden under his tongue, he is set upon by two figures in black sacks and runs for his life.

500.label: Medicine and lies
500.recap: Nursed back to health by a girl with azure hair, he refuses his medicine and then tells her a string of untruths.

500.label: The Field of Wonders
500.recap: He returns to the buried gold expecting a tree of coins, and a parrot in a nearby branch laughs at him.

500.label: A pigeon and the sea
500.recap: Finding the little white cottage gone, he weeps until a very large pigeon offers him news of his father and a ride.

500.label: Lamp-Wick's invitation
500.recap: His favourite schoolfriend is waiting for a midnight wagon bound for a country where nobody ever studies.

500.label: Donkey fever
500.recap: He wakes with something new on his head, and a fat little dormouse diagnoses him with unwelcome precision.

500.label: A light in the dark
500.recap: Deep inside an enormous fish he follows a faint glow toward a candle, a small table, and someone he has been searching for.

500.label: Fifty pennies
500.recap: On his way to buy himself new clothes, he meets a snail with news that changes what he does with his money.

514.label: Christmas without presents
514.recap: Four sisters grumble by the fire about being poor at Christmas, then talk themselves round to doing without.

514.label: News in the garret
514.recap: Meg climbs to the garret, where Jo hides with apples and a book, to bring her some news.

514.label: Being neighborly
514.recap: Jo sets out into the snow with a broom and a shovel, determined to find an adventure next door.

514.label: A sisters' quarrel
514.recap: Jo discovers what Amy has done in revenge, and her temper gets badly the better of her.

514.label: Meg goes visiting
514.recap: Meg packs for a fortnight of parties at a wealthier friend's house while her sisters help and envy her.

514.label: The family post
514.recap: Beth hands round the day's letters and parcels, and a summer outing takes shape.

514.label: An anxious journey
514.recap: Word arrives that sends the girls' mother away, and they see her off at dawn without crying.

514.label: Amy in exile
514.recap: Sent to stay with her stern great-aunt, Amy discovers how much she is petted at home.

514.label: Something unsettled
514.recap: With their father home again the household fusses over him, but the elders sense a question still hanging over Meg.

514.label: Artistic attempts
514.recap: Amy throws herself at one art form after another with far more audacity than skill.

514.label: Writing for money
514.recap: Living away from home, Jo tries to turn her pen into an income and takes some questionable shortcuts.

514.label: Harvest time
514.recap: An unexpected legacy opens up new possibilities, and the whole family gathers to take stock of what it has.

521.label: Against his father's advice
521.recap: A restless third son ignores his father's careful argument for the safe middle station of life and sets his heart on the sea.

521.label: Trading to Guinea
521.recap: He prospers on one African voyage, then loses everything on the next when a corsair from Sallee takes the ship and makes him a slave.

521.label: Stealing the fishing boat
521.recap: Sent out to catch fish with a man and a boy, he quietly provisions the boat and turns her toward open sea.

521.label: The ship strikes
521.recap: A second storm drives the ship aground on unknown sand and the crew take to a small boat in a heavy sea.

521.label: Salvaging the wreck
521.recap: He swims out to the stranded ship and rafts ashore provisions, tools, arms and everything else he can prise loose.

521.label: Building the castle
521.recap: He chooses a spot under a rock, fortifies it with piles and turf, and begins keeping a journal of his days.

521.label: Surveying the island
521.recap: After ten months he explores inland and finds grapes, melons, tobacco and a green valley he calls his own.

521.label: A print in the sand
521.recap: A single bare footprint on the shore destroys his sense of solitude and drives him back to his fortification in terror.

521.label: Fire on his own shore
521.recap: In his twenty-third year he sees a fire burning on his side of the island and prepares his guns for a siege.

521.label: Teaching a companion
521.recap: He sets about teaching his rescued companion to eat cooked meat, to speak a little English, and to fear a gun.

521.label: A trap on the beach
521.recap: With allies at his back he lays an ambush for the boat crews sent ashore from a ship anchored offshore.

521.label: Homeward at last
521.recap: He sails for England, travels to Lisbon to recover his Brazil fortune, and takes the overland road home through wolves, a bear and the winter Pyrenees.

524.label: Home on the evening train
524.recap: Ann Veronica travels back to her suburb resolved to settle something with her father that very evening.

524.label: The study interview
524.recap: Father and daughter argue across the gas fire about a dance, a college, and who gets to decide.

524.label: Down the staircase
524.recap: Dressed for the ball under an opera cloak, she comes downstairs to find her father waiting in the hall.

524.label: Counting her resources
524.recap: Sleepless, she totals her trinkets and small allowance and decides she must leave in the morning.

524.label: A stream of visitors
524.recap: Installed in a rented room, she receives her tearful aunt and a procession of callers urging her home.

524.label: Answering advertisements
524.recap: She tramps a foggy London hunting work and discovers what the market actually offers a young woman.

524.label: The biology laboratory
524.recap: She takes up advanced comparative anatomy and finds the quiet, single-minded atmosphere of the lab a relief.

524.label: Dinner and an opera box
524.recap: An evening out with her friendly benefactor grows uncomfortable somewhere in the second act.

524.label: Thoughts in a cell
524.recap: On a hard prison bed she keeps arguing, in rhyming couplets, with a man who is not there.

524.label: Spring in the laboratory
524.recap: Warm weather leaves two people alone in an empty laboratory, unable to work and saying very little.

524.label: Across the Channel
524.recap: A journey through Switzerland to blue lakes and high snow, shadowed only by thoughts of home.

524.label: A dinner table, years later
524.recap: Four years on, a flat, a laid table, and guests expected who once seemed lost for good.

537.label: A fragment from the sky
537.recap: An editor presents the torn notebook of an airman who set out to learn what waits in the thin air above forty thousand feet.

537.label: A collector in Paris
537.recap: The narrator describes a wealthy friend whose mildewed Paris house holds a famous library of occult books and some very unwholesome curiosities.

537.label: Two archaeologists in Rome
537.recap: In a stuffy room above the Corso, one antiquary presses another to share the secret of a discovery he has plainly been hiding.

537.label: A surgeon and a scandal
537.recap: London gossip has long linked a brilliant surgeon with a famous married woman, and now reports that both have abruptly vanished from public life.

537.label: A journal from Derbyshire
537.recap: A dead doctor's sealed account opens with his reasons for writing down what he began to suspect about a cave mouth near his convalescent farm.

537.label: An heir with no money
537.recap: A young man explains how his father's faith in a rich uncle left him with grand expectations, mounting debts and no profession at all.

537.label: A train that vanished
537.recap: A reporter assembles the record of a special train chartered out of Liverpool by a foreign gentleman, and the inquest that followed.

537.label: Lodgings in Gower Street
537.recap: A newly qualified doctor with no practice and dwindling savings describes the cheap top room where his luck finally turned.

537.label: The Rugby mystery
537.recap: A writer recalls the strange affair of an evening train out of Euston that filled the papers for weeks and was never explained.

537.label: A post at Thorpe Place
537.recap: A private tutor sets the scene of the grey stone Midlands country where he took, and lost, the best situation he ever had.

537.label: The doctor of Bishop's Crossing
537.recap: A Lancashire village takes in a dark, courteous stranger of unknown origins, whose nickname turns from mockery into a title of honour.

537.label: A curator's inheritance
537.recap: A brilliant young Egyptologist takes charge of a London museum and finds the reputation of the man he replaced hard to live beside.

558.label: Bored in London
558.recap: Richard Hannay, home from Africa and sick of England, gives the old country one more day before he books his passage back.

558.label: The man at the door
558.recap: A neighbour with frightened eyes asks to come inside for a minute and talk.

558.label: Alone in the flat
558.recap: He works out exactly how bad his position is and decides that vanishing beats calling the police.

558.label: Out as the milkman
558.recap: Wearing a borrowed cap and overall he walks whistling past the watchers in the street.

558.label: Driving the moor roads
558.recap: With a borrowed car and a decoded notebook, he learns what is really being planned.

558.label: Hunted from the air
558.recap: On bare green hills with no cover at all, he watches an aeroplane circle and knows he has been seen.

558.label: The roadman's job
558.recap: He meets a badly hungover road-mender and offers to take over his hammer, his spectacles and his name.

558.label: A night in the heather
558.recap: Coatless and starving he sleeps out on the hill, and wakes to men beating the slope below him.

558.label: Sick and on the move
558.recap: Poisoned, bruised and half-blind, he sets off across country to recover his coat and the notebook.

558.label: Breakfast with Sir Walter
558.recap: At last among officials, he hears how carefully a French visitor's journey through London has been arranged.

558.label: Watching the villa
558.recap: From the edge of a golf-course he studies a red-brick seaside house and the mild old man who strolls out of it.

558.label: The last hand
558.recap: Sitting at a card table in a suburban parlour, he finally sees the three men opposite him for what they are.

560.label: New orders, no details
560.recap: Pulled out of his brigade and told to change his name, Hannay travels down to a Cotswold manor with no idea what is wanted of him.

560.label: The garden city
560.recap: He settles into lodgings in a colony of high thinkers, buys a shelf of English classics, and plays the mild South African visitor.

560.label: A Glasgow tenement
560.recap: Hannay climbs two dirty flights in Glasgow to meet a small, grizzled workman with smouldering eyes.

560.label: A cottage on the shore
560.recap: On the run in the western Highlands he finds a fisherman's cottage, a plain supper and long talk of old evictions.

560.label: An old subaltern's favour
560.recap: Hannay works on a cheerful young flying officer to take him south a day early in a machine he is meant to deliver.

560.label: A letter from Peter
560.recap: Low and beaten in his London flat, Hannay reads a long, plodding letter from an old friend about courage.

560.label: Back in uniform
560.recap: He resumes command in France, turning a private puzzle over in his mind through months of hard Flanders fighting.

560.label: A château on the map
560.recap: A crossroads hamlet behind the British front nags at him, so he goes digging through a French clerk's dusty registers.

560.label: A porter in the Alps
560.recap: A shabby Swiss porter steps off a train at a frozen village, having shed several identities on the journey.

560.label: A pass and a car
560.recap: Hannay bluffs a grave, fanatical stranger into handing over a frontier pass and the keys of a motor-car.

560.label: Behind the screen
560.recap: Half dead with fatigue and hidden behind a screen, Hannay watches two men face each other across a game of Patience.

560.label: The last morning
560.recap: After a scrap of sleep he wakes in a broken building, prays for rain, and counts the hours until relief can arrive.

564.label: Waking in a squalid room
564.recap: A man comes to his senses among strangers in a wretched lodging, studies them, and gropes his way out into the morning.

564.label: Talk in the Close
564.recap: Two churchmen linger after service and trade careful gossip about the choirmaster's health.

564.label: The auctioneer's epitaph
564.recap: A magnificently self-satisfied auctioneer entertains a guest and unveils the inscription he has composed for his late wife.

564.label: Daggers drawn
564.recap: Two young men walking home from an evening call needle each other until the evening ends badly.

564.label: A night in the crypt
564.recap: Two companions spend a moonlit night among the tombs and stairways of the cathedral with a bottle between them.

564.label: Christmas Eve
564.recap: Christmas Eve settles over the old city, with shops full, visitors returning, and a storm gathering.

564.label: Breakfast on the road
564.recap: Neville, miles out of town at the start of a walking trip, stops for breakfast at a bleak roadside inn.

564.label: The philanthropist's office
564.recap: Half a year on, Crisparkle waits in a London office for an audience with a bullying professional philanthropist.

564.label: A settler arrives
564.recap: A white-haired stranger takes lodgings in the city and shows a leisurely interest in everyone in it.

564.label: Rosa decides to go
564.recap: Badly frightened, Rosa works out that she must leave at once, and where she can safely turn.

564.label: Two men who never speak
564.recap: Two men who meet daily and never mention the past are each drawn back toward the old question.

564.label: Morning service
564.recap: On a bright morning the cathedral fills for service, and a quiet watcher adds a mark to his private tally.

580.label: The club resolves
580.recap: A learned club votes to send four of its members travelling, at their own expense, to report back on everything they see.

580.label: A day at the review
580.recap: The four travellers wedge themselves into the front of a crowd to watch a military review and are swept up in the manoeuvres.

580.label: The White Hart yard
580.recap: In an old Borough coaching inn a boots cleans shoes and answers the bells, and is about to prove very useful to somebody.

580.label: A morning in Goswell Street
580.recap: Pacing his lodgings before a journey with something important on his mind, Mr. Pickwick raises the subject with his landlady.

580.label: Blues against Buffs
580.recap: The party arrives in a borough where every question down to a new pump is a party question, just in time for an election.

580.label: A day's shooting
580.recap: A shooting party sets out on the first of September with two enormous game bags and two extremely nervous gentlemen.

580.label: A nervous suitor
580.recap: At an Ipswich inn a fellow traveller works himself up to an interview with a lady, and asks Mr. Pickwick for advice.

580.label: Christmas at Dingley Dell
580.recap: The friends load a coach with a cod and barrels of oysters and set off for a country Christmas and a wedding.

580.label: A day in Guildhall
580.recap: On the fourteenth of February the party drives to court, where counsel, jury and judge are waiting on a case of breach of promise.

580.label: Inside the Fleet
580.recap: A turnkey walks a new arrival through the galleries and cellars of a debtors' prison and shows him where he is to sleep.

580.label: Two medical gentlemen
580.recap: Two young surgeons discuss minced veal, a practice that pays nothing, and a sister's thousand pounds.

580.label: Everything concluded
580.recap: After a week of mysterious daily errands, Mr. Pickwick sits his friends down over the decanters and explains what he has been arranging.

583.label: Told by many pens
583.recap: The narrator explains that this account will be given by several witnesses in turn, each speaking only to what they saw themselves.

583.label: A midnight road
583.recap: Walking back to London long after midnight, a young drawing master is stopped by a stranger dressed head to foot in white.

583.label: First morning in Cumberland
583.recap: He wakes to sea and sunlight at his new post and comes down to breakfast to meet the first of his two pupils.

583.label: Asking around the village
583.recap: He and Miss Halcombe question the village for news of the stranger and stop outside the schoolroom window.

583.label: The lawyer takes over
583.recap: The family solicitor picks up the story to describe the business that brought him north to Limmeridge House.

583.label: Marian's diary begins
583.recap: With the lawyer gone, Marian goes upstairs uneasy about what her sister may have let slip, and finds her impatient to speak.

583.label: Arrival at Blackwater Park
583.recap: After half a year apart, Marian installs herself in a flat, tree-smothered Hampshire house to wait for the travellers.

583.label: Portrait of a guest
583.recap: Marian tries to work out why she cannot manage to dislike the enormous, soft-voiced Italian now staying in the house.

583.label: Watching the boathouse
583.recap: Marian arranges the afternoon carefully so that a private meeting can happen without the rest of the household noticing.

583.label: An invalid is disturbed
583.recap: Mr. Fairlie complains his way through an account of the day a servant arrived at Limmeridge wanting his help.

583.label: Hidden in London
583.recap: Walter resumes his story from cheap lodgings in a poor London street, living under a false name with two women.

583.label: A house left empty
583.recap: After a fortnight away on newspaper work, Walter comes home to find nobody there and only a note telling him where to follow.

589.label: Rich and hunted
589.recap: David Balfour walks out of an Edinburgh bank a landed man, with a deadly piece of business still to settle.

589.label: A girl in the close
589.recap: Sheltering from rain, he watches a prisoner marched past and speaks to the Highland girl following him.

589.label: The Lord Advocate
589.recap: After hours forgotten in a dark cabinet, David is at last received by the most powerful lawyer in Scotland.

589.label: An outing to the park
589.recap: Escorted by the Advocate's daughters into fashionable company, David is singled out for a quarrel.

589.label: The road to Dean
589.recap: Against all good sense he walks out to see Catriona, and the two of them talk more freely than before.

589.label: Waiting in the wood
589.recap: He lies all night in a wood outside the city, arguing with his own conscience while he waits for a friend.

589.label: Running for the sands
589.recap: The two of them race across country toward a ship lying at anchor off a lonely stretch of coast.

589.label: A rock in the sea
589.recap: Carried off by boat before dawn, David watches a great sea-crag come clear in the growing light.

589.label: The verdict
589.recap: Hidden from the court, David hears the judgment given and the ballads the young lawyers make of it.

589.label: Sailing from Leith
589.recap: Boarding a merchantman bound for Holland, David discovers who is to be his fellow passenger.

589.label: The last walk
589.recap: Sent out together one more time, David tries to say the thing he has been carrying for months.

589.label: The inn by the dunes
589.recap: At a smugglers' inn among the sandhills everyone is waiting on something, and nobody will say what.

599.label: Leaving the academy
599.recap: Two very different schoolgirls are driven away from a genteel Chiswick boarding school, and one of them leaves without a single tear shed for her.

599.label: A night at Vauxhall
599.recap: A pleasure-garden outing is arranged so that a stout, shy gentleman may finally propose, and a bowl of punch takes charge of the evening instead.

599.label: Arriving at the baronet's
599.recap: The new governess is delivered to a shuttered London house in a dismal street and discovers that the shabby man who carried her trunk is not a servant.

599.label: An unexpected offer
599.recap: A recently widowed baronet calls in Park Lane and, refusing to be put off, makes the governess an offer she never expected to hear.

599.label: A family ruined
599.recap: Napoleon's return from Elba topples the markets, and a comfortable Russell Square household loses everything in a night.

599.label: Brussels before the guns
599.recap: With the army gathering in Brussels, old acquaintances meet again in the park, and the social manoeuvring resumes as if there were no war at all.

599.label: The city in panic
599.recap: Cannon fire rolls in from the countryside, rumours race through Brussels, and civilians scramble for horses and any road out of town.

599.label: Nothing a year
599.recap: The narrator explains, with relish, exactly how a fashionable couple keeps a house in Mayfair on no visible income at all.

599.label: The great doors open
599.recap: A great nobleman's patronage carries one climber into the very highest London houses, and a charade evening becomes her triumph.

599.label: Arrested for debt
599.recap: An officer is taken to a sponging-house over an unpaid bill and writes home for the money that will set him free.

599.label: Home from India
599.recap: After long years abroad, a patient major lands at Southampton and can hardly wait to be on the London road.

599.label: Accounts settled
599.recap: The last of the fortunes and reputations are totted up, and the narrator folds his puppets away.

600.label: The man in the corner
600.recap: A retired clerk of forty introduces himself as sick, spiteful and unattractive, and dares you to make sense of him.

600.label: The mouse and the wall
600.recap: He contrasts the blunt man of action with the over-conscious creature who broods on an insult for decades.

600.label: Against enlightened self-interest
600.recap: He attacks the notion that men would behave well if only they understood their own advantage.

600.label: Ant-heap and arithmetic
600.recap: He argues that people love building more than living in what they build, and dread a world settled by arithmetic.

600.label: Hurrah for underground
600.recap: He declares inertia the better course, then admits he does not believe a word he has written.

600.label: Sixteen years earlier
600.recap: He turns back to his twenties, a friendless clerk who despised his colleagues and dropped his eyes before all of them.

600.label: A plan on the Nevsky
600.recap: After an officer brushes past him without noticing, he spends months preparing an absurdly precise revenge.

600.label: Old schoolfellows
600.recap: Calling on an acquaintance, he finds a farewell dinner being planned and invites himself into it.

600.label: The farewell dinner
600.recap: He arrives an hour early to a dinner that goes badly from the first handshake.

600.label: Into the wet snow
600.recap: He hires a sledge in falling snow and rehearses aloud everything he intends to do when he arrives.

600.label: A stranger's eyes
600.recap: He wakes in a dark unfamiliar room and finds a young woman looking steadily at him.

600.label: The last visit
600.recap: He paces his room, peers through a screen, and does a cruel thing he immediately regrets.

601.label: A crowded sermon
601.recap: All Madrid packs into the Capuchin church, most of them there for anything but devotion, to hear a famous preacher.

601.label: Alone in his cell
601.recap: Left by himself after his triumph, the abbot congratulates himself on a virtue that has never once been tested.

601.label: The novice's confession
601.recap: In the abbey garden a grieving young novice tells the abbot a story about a dead sister, then makes an admission of his own.

601.label: The crimson sheets
601.recap: A traveller sheltering in a woodcutter's cottage acts on a whispered hint and learns what his hosts intend for him.

601.label: The castle of Lindenberg
601.recap: The traveller reaches a German castle, charms its hunting-mad baron, and meets the young niece of the house.

601.label: Shame at daybreak
601.recap: The abbot wakes appalled at his own weakness and is argued out of his remorse before the morning is over.

601.label: A new appetite
601.recap: Back behind the abbey walls, the monk turns his attention on a girl who trusts him, and cools toward the woman beside him.

601.label: No trace of Agnes
601.recap: The marquis falls ill with grief over a woman lost inside a convent, while his devoted page schemes for a way in.

601.label: Impunity
601.recap: Days pass with no suspicion raised, remorse thins out, and fresh advice is offered on how to get what he wants.

601.label: Outside the convent gates
601.recap: Lorenzo waits with armed men in a festival crowd, meaning to seize the prioress the moment the procession passes.

601.label: Into the vaults
601.recap: With the whole city out watching the procession, the abbot lets himself down into the burial vaults beneath the convent.

601.label: The reckoning
601.recap: Held by the Holy Office and abandoned by the city that adored him, the abbot waits for his trial.

674.label: Where fable ends
674.recap: Plutarch explains his plan of paired Greek and Roman lives, and warns that the earliest of them stray into legend.

674.label: Sparta's lawgiver
674.recap: The much-disputed life of Lycurgus opens a long account of how Sparta got its constitution and its severe customs.

674.label: Athens gets laws
674.recap: The origins of the Athenian lawgiver are weighed, along with his reform of debt, property and the courts.

674.label: The rise of Themistocles
674.recap: An obscurely born Athenian pushes his way to the front just as the Persian fleet comes west.

674.label: Athens in its glory
674.recap: Plutarch turns to the statesman who filled Athens with buildings and led it into a long war.

674.label: The charming troublemaker
674.recap: A brilliant, spoiled Athenian dazzles and scandalises his city by turns.

674.label: The king of Epirus
674.recap: The restless Epirot king takes his elephants west and measures himself against Rome.

674.label: Rome turns on itself
674.recap: Sylla's ascent opens the story of Rome's civil wars, marches on the city and proscription lists.

674.label: The richest man in Rome
674.recap: Crassus builds an enormous fortune out of fire and confiscation, then goes looking for military glory.

674.label: Lives, not histories
674.recap: Plutarch explains that a small saying can show a character better than a great battle, then follows the Macedonian from boyhood.

674.label: Antony in the East
674.recap: An open-handed, appetitive soldier-politician is traced from a generous Roman family out towards Egypt.

674.label: A very short reign
674.recap: The book closes in a year of civil war with a new emperor trying to steady a shaken Rome.

696.label: A wedding day set
696.recap: A prince rushes his sickly son's marriage while an old prophecy about the castle unsettles the townspeople.

696.label: Something in the courtyard
696.recap: Manfred goes out to find the cause of the screaming in his court and cannot take his eyes off what lies there.

696.label: A summons by torchlight
696.recap: Manfred sends for his son's betrothed and makes her a proposal that leaves her horrified.

696.label: Down to the vaults
696.recap: Isabella gropes through the cellars for a hidden passage and finds she is not alone in the dark.

696.label: A voice below the window
696.recap: Matilda and her chattering maid sit up through the night and overhear a stranger in the room beneath them.

696.label: The friar's errand
696.recap: A priest brings news of the missing lady and refuses to be bullied out of delivering it before the princess.

696.label: Sentence in the courtyard
696.recap: A young prisoner kneels for execution, and as he loosens his collar something on his shoulder is noticed.

696.label: The knight's procession
696.recap: A silent champion arrives with a huge sword, a long train, and a challenge to Manfred's right to rule.

696.label: An unbolted door
696.recap: Matilda slips away while the castle is empty to open a prisoner's cell and beg him to run.

696.label: In the oratory
696.recap: Frederic goes looking for Hippolita and finds a kneeling figure at the altar instead.

696.label: Night in the church
696.recap: Acting on a servant's report of a secret meeting, Manfred steals through the aisles toward Alfonso's tomb.

696.label: The castle answers
696.recap: Thunder breaks over the household and the walls give way, and the truth of Otranto is finally spoken aloud.

730.label: Born in the workhouse
730.recap: A child is born in a parish workhouse and his young mother dies within minutes of seeing him.

730.label: Asking for more
730.recap: Half-starved boys draw lots, and the one chosen walks up to the master with his empty basin.

730.label: Apprenticed to the undertaker
730.recap: Bound to a coffin-maker, Oliver walks in funeral processions and endures the spite of the household.

730.label: Goaded past endurance
730.recap: A fellow apprentice's mockery of Oliver's dead mother finally provokes the quiet boy into striking back.

730.label: The road to London
730.recap: Oliver runs away and sets out on foot for London with a crust of bread and a penny.

730.label: Before the magistrate
730.recap: Accused of picking a pocket, Oliver is shut in a filthy cell and hauled up before a police magistrate.

730.label: Led through the fog
730.recap: A brutal man and a young woman march Oliver across foggy London by night, a dog at his heels.

730.label: The house at Chertsey
730.recap: Two housebreakers scale a wall and push Oliver through a small window to open the door from inside.

730.label: Tea by the workhouse fire
730.recap: On a bitter night the workhouse matron settles down to her tea and receives an unexpected caller.

730.label: Midnight on the bridge
730.recap: A woman waits on London Bridge for a secret meeting while a man shadows her from the dark.

730.label: Hunted to Jacob's Island
730.recap: The hunt closes on a rotting riverside slum where what remains of the gang has gone to ground.

730.label: How it all ended
730.recap: The narrator gathers up, in a few plain words, what became of everyone in the story.

766.label: Born on a Friday night
766.recap: The narrator opens his own life story with the circumstances of his birth and the sale of the caul he was born with.

766.label: First sight of Yarmouth
766.recap: Peggotty takes the boy on a long cart ride to the seaside town where her relations live, and her nephew carries him home on his back.

766.label: A cane in the parlour
766.recap: His stepfather binds a cane while the morning lessons are heard, and the day ends with the boy locked in his room.

766.label: A stoutish stranger
766.recap: Put to washing bottles at a riverside warehouse, the boy is introduced to a shabby-genteel gentleman who has been asked to lodge him.

766.label: The coach pulls away
766.recap: His landlords leave London after a farewell full of advice, and the boy is left standing in the road with nobody at all.

766.label: At the garden gate
766.recap: Ragged and footsore after days on the road, the boy finds the cottage of the aunt he has never met and tries to introduce himself.

766.label: A most respectable servant
766.recap: Staying at a friend's house, David is waited on by a manservant whose faultless respectability makes him feel about six years old.

766.label: A weekend at Norwood
766.recap: His employer carries him off to the country house for a weekend, an invitation the office clerks regard as a glimpse of paradise.

766.label: On the beach at dawn
766.recap: A household's disgrace becomes the whole town's talk, and two men walking the shore tell David the course they have settled on.

766.label: A summons obeyed
766.recap: An old friend has insisted the whole household attend him on some undisclosed business, and there is a fond family argument about who will go.

766.label: Before the ship sails
766.recap: With the emigrant ship close to leaving, David writes a letter and is brought an answer he is asked to read and carry.

766.label: A last look back
766.recap: The narrator closes his book by calling up the faces of everyone still travelling the road of life beside him.

768.label: Lockwood's Visit
768.recap: The new tenant Lockwood calls on his sullen landlord Heathcliff at the bleak, windswept Wuthering Heights.

768.label: A Ghost at the Window
768.recap: Snowbound overnight, Lockwood is terrified by a dream of a ghost child at the window begging to be let in.

768.label: The Foundling
768.recap: Housekeeper Nelly tells how old Earnshaw's adopted foundling Heathcliff and his daughter Catherine grew inseparable, to Hindley's jealousy.

768.label: Catherine and the Lintons
768.recap: Catherine returns from the refined Lintons changed, torn between wild Heathcliff and gentle Edgar Linton.

768.label: Heathcliff Vanishes
768.recap: Overhearing Catherine say it would degrade her to marry him, Heathcliff disappears into the storm.

768.label: His Return
768.recap: Years later, with Catherine now married to Edgar, a hardened and wealthy Heathcliff suddenly returns.

768.label: Catherine's Decline
768.recap: Caught between the two men, Catherine sinks into a feverish decline as Heathcliff schemes against the Lintons.

768.label: Catherine's Death
768.recap: Catherine dies giving birth to a daughter, leaving Heathcliff wild with grief and a desperate vow.

768.label: The Next Generation
768.recap: Years on, Catherine's daughter Cathy is drawn toward the Heights and Heathcliff's sickly son Linton.

768.label: Trapped at the Heights
768.recap: Heathcliff imprisons young Cathy and forces her to marry Linton so he can seize both family estates.

768.label: Lockwood Returns
768.recap: A year later Lockwood comes back to find young Cathy and the rough Hareton quietly drawn together.

768.label: Heathcliff's End
768.recap: Worn out by his obsession, Heathcliff stops eating and dies, longing only to rejoin his Catherine at last.

829.label: A surgeon takes to sea
829.recap: Gulliver explains how a thin education and a failing London practice pushed him back to sea, until a storm splits his ship and leaves him swimming for an unknown shore.

829.label: Court games and rope dancers
829.recap: Having won some goodwill, Gulliver watches the tiny court award its high offices by dancing on a stretched thread and leaping over a stick.

829.label: A plan against the fleet
829.recap: Warned of an invasion from the island across the channel, Gulliver sounds the water himself and proposes an extraordinary use for his size.

829.label: Left on a giant shore
829.recap: A second voyage is driven far east by monsoon weather, and a landing party abandons Gulliver on a coast where everything is enormous.

829.label: Sold to the queen
829.recap: Worn to a skeleton by daily exhibition, Gulliver is summoned to court, where the queen takes an interest and asks his owner what he wants for him.

829.label: A box beside the sea
829.recap: Homesick and quietly scheming, Gulliver persuades a page to carry his travelling box down to the rocks, and falls asleep inside it.

829.label: The flying island
829.recap: Gulliver is received among a people so lost in thought that hired servants must strike them with bladders before they can speak or listen.

829.label: The grand academy
829.recap: A tour of a great research academy introduces men who have spent years extracting sunbeams from cucumbers, and colleagues with stranger projects still.

829.label: The immortals
829.recap: In Luggnagg, Gulliver hears of children born with a mark meaning they will never die, and bursts into a rapturous speech about their good fortune.

829.label: Mutiny and a strange shore
829.recap: Commanding his own ship at last, Gulliver is seized by his own crew and set ashore in a country of horses and foul, man-shaped beasts.

829.label: The great assembly
829.recap: The horse people gather for the one debate their country has ever held, and Gulliver's host reports the arguments made about the land's brutish inhabitants.

829.label: Setting out alone
829.recap: Gulliver launches a small craft of his own building, hoping to find an empty island rather than return to the company of his own kind.

831.label: The hunt for the White Stag
831.recap: Arthur revives an old custom against Gawain's advice, since whoever kills the stag must kiss the fairest maiden of the court.

831.label: A night with the vavasor
831.recap: Riding after an insult without armour, Erec is taken in by an impoverished old knight whose daughter is dressed in a garment full of holes.

831.label: The sparrow-hawk contest
831.recap: Erec escorts the ragged maiden through a crowded town to claim a prize another knight has carried off unchallenged for two years.

831.label: What Enide said
831.recap: Erec wakes to find his wife weeping over a rumour about him, forces the truth out of her, and calls at once for his arms.

831.label: The horn in the garden
831.recap: After a hard fight inside a walled garden, Erec is told to sound a horn that will release a man and end a long waiting.

831.label: A Greek prince sails west
831.recap: An emperor's son leaves Constantinople for Britain, determined that only King Arthur shall make him a knight.

831.label: The tower and the garden
831.recap: After a long confinement Fenice asks to see daylight again, and a servant opens a door so cleverly made that nobody knew it was there.

831.label: A tale told at Pentecost
831.recap: While the king sleeps, a knight begins telling the court a story about an adventure he went looking for seven years ago.

831.label: The lion and the serpent
831.recap: Riding through a wood, Yvain comes on a lion held fast by a fire-breathing serpent and has to decide which of them to help.

831.label: A challenge at Camelot
831.recap: An armed stranger walks into the hall, announces that he holds Arthur's people captive, and dares any knight to follow him into the woods.

831.label: The cart
831.recap: A knight on foot, having lost his horse, is offered a ride in the one vehicle no gentleman may be seen in.

831.label: The last combat
831.recap: The long-postponed battle is finally fought in the king's presence, and the court is jubilant when it ends.

834.label: A horse and a trainer
834.recap: Holmes sets off for Dartmoor, where the favourite for a great race has disappeared and its trainer has been found dead on the moor.

834.label: A parcel from Belfast
834.recap: In a sweltering London, Holmes demonstrates a small feat of thought-reading and then turns to a grim package posted to a quiet Croydon lady.

834.label: The cottage on the hill
834.recap: A restless client returns to Baker Street with a story about his wife's secret visits to a neighbouring cottage.

834.label: A very good offer
834.recap: Holmes calls at Watson's new practice and carries him off to hear a clerk describe a suspiciously generous job offer.

834.label: An enigmatic message
834.recap: Holmes produces a scrawled note that once struck a robust old man down, and begins the story of his very first case.

834.label: The tin box
834.recap: Made to tidy his papers, Holmes digs out relics from an early case that turned on an old family catechism.

834.label: A rest cure in Surrey
834.recap: Watson takes an exhausted Holmes to the country to recover, where a burglary and a shooting interrupt the quiet.

834.label: A late caller
834.recap: Holmes arrives on Watson's step near midnight with a locked-room death in a garrison town.

834.label: The nervous doctor
834.recap: A young physician explains the strange arrangement with the patient who set him up in practice, and the visitors who have unsettled the house.

834.label: The silent club
834.recap: Holmes astonishes Watson by mentioning a brother and takes him to a club where conversation is forbidden.

834.label: A missing document
834.recap: An old schoolfellow of Watson's writes in desperation after a confidential paper vanishes from his Foreign Office desk.

834.label: Shutters and warnings
834.recap: Holmes walks into Watson's consulting room looking ill, bolts the shutters, and asks him to leave the country at once.

844.label: Act I: Bunburying
844.recap: In his London flat Algernon needles his friend Jack about a double life, just as a marriage proposal sets a comic deception spinning.

844.label: Act II: The Country
844.recap: At the country manor two young women each believe themselves engaged to the same imaginary man named Ernest.

844.label: Act III: Earnest at Last
844.recap: The tangle of names and false identities is untangled, revealing the truth behind the name Ernest.

851.label: The attack on Lancaster
851.recap: At sunrise an armed party burns the town and besieges the garrison house where the author's family has taken shelter.

851.label: The first night
851.recap: Marched a mile from the burning town, she spends a sleepless night among her captors and their plunder.

851.label: Riding to Wenimesset
851.recap: Wounded and holding her wounded child, she is set on horseback for a long day's travel to an Indian town.

851.label: Nine days in a wigwam
851.recap: For over a week she sits with her small daughter in her lap, with almost nothing to give her but cold water.

851.label: Crossing Banquaug river
851.recap: The whole company hurries ahead of an English army and rafts across a river she could never have forded.

851.label: Gleaning the burned fields
851.recap: In deserted English fields the company scavenges frozen wheat, and she learns what hunger will let her eat.

851.label: Meeting King Philip
851.recap: Ferried across the Connecticut river, she is received civilly by the war's leader and earns small pay for sewing.

851.label: A stranger's kindness
851.recap: Turned away from one fire, she is taken in, warmed and fed by people she has never met before.

851.label: Turned back again
851.recap: Hoping at last to travel homeward, she is ordered back with her mistress and left to beg a place to sleep.

851.label: Word from the council
851.recap: After a freezing river crossing she is told a letter about redeeming captives has reached the sachems.

851.label: An Englishman rides in
851.recap: A messenger from the council reaches the camp, and bargaining over her price begins in earnest.

851.label: The road back
851.recap: She travels through her ruined town toward Boston, and afterwards pieces together what became of her family.

863.label: An invitation to Styles
863.recap: Invalided home from the war, Hastings runs into an old acquaintance who invites him down to his mother's place in Essex.

863.label: Tea on the lawn
863.recap: Over tea under a sycamore, Hastings is introduced to the household of Styles Court, including the mistress of the house and her much younger husband.

863.label: A companion walks out
