863.recap: The family's blunt companion announces she has spoken her mind to her employer and is leaving the house that same hour.

863.label: A friend in the village
863.recap: Outside the village post office Hastings collides with a Belgian refugee he knew years ago as a celebrated detective.

863.label: The night of the alarm
863.recap: The household is roused before dawn and has to break down a bedroom door bolted from the inside.

863.label: Searching the room
863.recap: Poirot goes over the sealed bedroom inch by inch, gathering small objects whose importance Hastings cannot see.

863.label: The inquest
863.recap: Witnesses give evidence before the coroner, and the medical testimony sharpens the question rather than settling it.

863.label: A drawing-room announcement
863.recap: With Scotland Yard men present, Poirot gathers the household together to make a statement nobody expects.

863.label: Bad news at the door
863.recap: Coming back from the village, they find the servants outside in tears over an arrest.

863.label: The case for the prosecution
863.recap: Two months on, the case comes to court and Hastings sits through the evidence with his sympathies torn.

863.label: Poirot explains
863.recap: Poirot assembles everyone once more and walks them back through what he found on his very first morning.

863.label: The last word
863.recap: Alone with Poirot at last, Hastings demands to know why he was kept in the dark throughout.

910.label: The trail of the meat
910.recap: Two men hauling a coffin by dog sled through the frozen North realise something is following them and quietly counting their dogs.

910.label: One Ear breaks away
910.recap: When the sled overturns on a bad piece of trail, one of the dogs slips loose and trots out across the snow toward the waiting she-wolf.

910.label: Running with the pack
910.recap: The story crosses over to the wolves themselves, where the she-wolf runs at the head of a starving pack among jealous suitors.

910.label: Looking for a lair
910.recap: Heavy and slow now, the she-wolf searches along a frozen stream for the place she needs while her mate hunts for them both.

910.label: The wall of the world
910.recap: A grey cub learns the law of the cave entrance, and learns fear, before daring the bright wall of light beyond it.

910.label: Five silent figures
910.recap: Going down to the stream to drink, the cub meets men for the first time and is flattened by an awe he cannot name.

910.label: Hiding from the camp
910.recap: As the village packs its tepees into canoes, White Fang hides his trail in the stream and lies still while the voices call his name.

910.label: Sport at the fort
910.recap: At Fort Yukon the old hands come down to the bank to watch newcomers' dogs come to grief, and one man takes a particular interest in White Fang.

910.label: A squat opponent
910.recap: Loosed into the ring, White Fang faces a short, unhurried bull-dog who seems in no hurry at all to fight him.

910.label: A god sits down
910.recap: Braced for punishment, White Fang finds this master carries no club and simply sits down a few feet away and talks to him.

910.label: Into the Southland
910.recap: Stepping off a steamer into a roaring city, White Fang is made small again by pavements, cable cars and the sheer number of men.

910.label: News from San Quentin
910.recap: The papers carry the story of a convict's escape, and the book pauses over the making of a man society has hammered into a beast.

940.label: A war fought through forest
940.recap: The narrator sets out the country between the Hudson and the lakes, where armies had to beat the wilderness before they could reach each other.

940.label: A shortcut through the woods
940.recap: Two sisters ride for their father's fort with a young officer, leaving the column behind for a private path and a silent native guide.

940.label: A hunter and a Mohican
940.recap: A white scout and his Mohican friend argue about whose fathers took the land, while they wait beside a stream for someone.

940.label: The guide bolts
940.recap: Their guide disappears into the trees and the travellers must decide, in gathering dark, where to shelter for the night.

940.label: Pinned on the rock
940.recap: Besieged on a rock above the falls, the little party trades fire with enemies on both banks while their powder runs low.

940.label: Camp on the hilltop
940.recap: The captives are halted on a bare hill, and Heyward tries to talk their captor into taking a ransom instead of revenge.

940.label: Help arrives at the hill
940.recap: A single shot breaks the standoff and a hand-to-hand fight sweeps across the little plain.

940.label: Outside the fort walls
940.recap: As the garrison marches out under terms, the plain dissolves into slaughter, and the sisters are carried away from their father.

940.label: Leaving by water
940.recap: Before dawn the scout leads the party into a canoe, taking pains to leave no print on the sand behind them.

940.label: A conjurer and a bear
940.recap: Inside a Huron cavern Heyward plays healer to a sick woman under the watchful eye of a strangely behaved bear.

940.label: Before the old sage
940.recap: A prisoner is led into the ring and questioned by the ancient Delaware patriarch about his tongue and his blood.

940.label: A nation in mourning
940.recap: With the fighting over, the whole tribe gathers in silence for the burial songs.

967.label: The Nickleby fortunes
967.recap: The narrator traces how the Nickleby money was won and then lost, leaving a widow and two grown children with nothing.

967.label: A schoolmaster in London
967.recap: At a Snow Hill coaching inn, a one-eyed Yorkshire schoolmaster waits for parents willing to hand over their boys.

967.label: Setting out for Yorkshire
967.recap: Nicholas takes leave of his mother and sister and boards the northern coach toward his new post.

967.label: Morning at Dotheboys Hall
967.recap: Nicholas wakes to his first working day and sees exactly how the school is run and what the boys are given to eat.

967.label: Someone is missing
967.recap: At first light Nicholas searches the crowded dormitory for a face he cannot find, while the schoolmaster shouts up the stairs.

967.label: Lodgings in London
967.recap: Back in the city with almost nothing, Nicholas hunts for a cheap room and for any work that will keep him.

967.label: Kate among strangers
967.recap: Kate endures the spite of the dressmaker's workroom and is summoned to dine at her uncle's house.

967.label: Falling in with players
967.recap: Down to his last twenty shillings, Nicholas quits London and falls in with a travelling theatrical manager.

967.label: Idle gentlemen at breakfast
967.recap: Two fashionable men idle away an afternoon over an untouched breakfast, and one turns the talk to a girl he has noticed.

967.label: A flight and a face
967.recap: A terrified runaway makes his way back on foot, while Nicholas finds his thoughts returning to a young woman he has glimpsed.

967.label: A rescue attempted
967.recap: Newman Noggs chases Nicholas down in the street with news that sets him hunting for some way to help Madeline Bray.

967.label: Back to Yorkshire
967.recap: Nicholas travels north again to share his news with a plain-spoken old friend, and the affairs of Dotheboys Hall are settled for good.

974.label: The shop in Soho
974.recap: A grimy back-street shop is introduced, along with the quiet household living behind the counter.

974.label: Summoned to the Embassy
974.recap: Verloc arrives unusually early at a foreign embassy and is handed from one official to another.

974.label: The First Secretary
974.recap: A new man at the embassy takes Verloc apart and informs him his pay will have to be earned.

974.label: Talk in the back parlour
974.recap: Three revolutionists argue theory in the room behind the shop while the household listens through the door.

974.label: The man in the beer hall
974.recap: In an underground restaurant Ossipon tries to press a small, unshakable acquaintance about the day's news.

974.label: Two men in an alley
974.recap: Walking home through the crowds, the little man comes face to face with a police inspector in a narrow alley.

974.label: What the explosion left
974.recap: Chief Inspector Heat views the remains brought in from Greenwich Park and quietly pockets a scrap of cloth.

974.label: Asking for a free hand
974.recap: The Assistant Commissioner talks his way in to see a tired and irritable Secretary of State.

974.label: The cab and the horse
974.recap: Outside the almshouse gate a night cabman, his worn-out horse and Stevie leave a lasting mark on the boy.

974.label: A husband comes home
974.recap: Verloc returns from abroad in low spirits and takes little notice of the household arranged around him.

974.label: After the inspector's visit
974.recap: With the police gone, Verloc tries to explain himself to a wife who will not uncover her face.

974.label: A sound in the parlour
974.recap: Alone in the quiet parlour, Winnie hunts for a ticking she cannot place and finds its source.

974.label: The padlocked cupboard
974.recap: Ossipon and the Professor talk over beer, and the book closes on a man walking unnoticed through the crowd.

996.label: A gentleman and his books
996.recap: An idle country gentleman reads so many chivalry romances that he loses his wits and resolves to become a knight.

996.label: The windmills
996.recap: Riding across the plain, the knight sees monstrous giants where his squire sees only mills, and charges.

996.label: The chained men
996.recap: A file of prisoners chained by the neck comes down the road, and the knight stops to ask each man his story.

996.label: Into the mountains
996.recap: Master and squire climb into the wild Sierra Morena, where the knight decides to perform a penance in imitation of his heroes.

996.label: Carried home in a cage
996.recap: Friends contrive to bring the knight back to his village on an ox cart, and he explains the arrangement to himself as enchantment.

996.label: An errand to El Toboso
996.recap: Sent to find the lady Dulcinea, Sancho hits on a device of his own to explain what his master will see.

996.label: Curds and a cart
996.recap: Sancho hides curds in his master's helmet just as a cart carrying caged lions comes along the road.

996.label: Tale of a deep cave
996.recap: Hauled up from a pit, the knight describes at length the crystal palace and enchanted company he says he found below.

996.label: Governor of Barataria
996.recap: Sancho arrives at the island promised him, is handed the keys with mock ceremony, and begins giving judgments.

996.label: A night alarm
996.recap: On the seventh night of his government Sancho is woken by bells, drums and armed men crying that the island is invaded.

996.label: A knight on the beach
996.recap: A stranger in armour bearing a white moon on his shield rides up and challenges the knight to combat.

996.label: The last chapter
996.recap: A fever keeps the knight in bed, and he wakes calm and clear headed, asking for his friends so that he may make his will.

1001.label: Lost in the wood
1001.recap: Halfway through life the poet finds himself off the path, blocked by three beasts, until a shade offers another road.

1001.label: Words on the gate
1001.recap: He reads the inscription carved above a gateway and asks his guide what it means.

1001.label: The ferryman
1001.recap: On the bank of a dark river an old boatman objects loudly to carrying a passenger who is still alive.

1001.label: The endless wind
1001.recap: In a lightless place a storm drives crowds of souls forever, and the guide names the famous among them.

1001.label: Two on the wind
1001.recap: Two spirits who travel together come at his call, and one of them tells him how it began with a book.

1001.label: The thorn wood
1001.recap: Entering a trackless wood of poisonous thorns, he snaps off a twig and something bleeds and speaks.

1001.label: The beast with a kind face
1001.recap: A creature with a just man's face, a serpent's body and a scorpion's tail hauls itself onto the stone brink.

1001.label: The boiling pitch
1001.recap: A ditch of black boiling pitch is patrolled by devils with hooks, and one arrives with a fresh burden.

1001.label: The last voyage
1001.recap: A voice inside a flame tells how it talked an old crew into sailing past the edge of the known world.

1001.label: Figures in the mist
1001.recap: What look like towers in the gloom turn out to be enormous chained bodies standing in the well of the pit.

1001.label: The tower of famine
1001.recap: A count frozen into ice interrupts his gnawing to tell why he hates the man beside him.

1001.label: The bottom and the climb
1001.recap: At the frozen floor stands the emperor of this kingdom, and the way out lies straight past him.

1023.label: Fog over the courts
1023.recap: Fog and mud swallow the city while an ancient lawsuit grinds on in the Court of Chancery.

1023.label: A girl and her doll
1023.recap: A shy girl raised by a stern godmother explains that she told her secrets only to a doll.

1023.label: Telescopic philanthropy
1023.recap: Three young wards are lodged for a night with a lady whose devotion to Africa has left her own house in chaos.

1023.label: The road to Bleak House
1023.recap: The travellers leave London for the country and are met on the road by notes from their unseen guardian.

1023.label: The law-writer's room
1023.recap: A lawyer and a rag-shop keeper find the lodger they came to see beyond waking, and a doctor is fetched.

1023.label: Tom-all-Alone's
1023.recap: A homeless crossing-sweeper who can neither read nor write goes home to a collapsing slum street.

1023.label: The appointed time
1023.recap: Night settles on Lincoln's Inn and the neighbours gossip over beer about the rag-shop keeper and his lodger.

1023.label: Weeks of illness
1023.recap: The narrator describes the strange telescoping of time and the fevered dreams of a long confinement in a sick-room.

1023.label: Nowhere to put a boy
1023.recap: A young doctor walks a sick street-boy through the morning city, trying to think where anyone will take him in.

1023.label: A detective's field-day
1023.recap: A police officer breakfasts heartily and goes calmly to the library to lay out what he has learned.

1023.label: A chaise through the night
1023.recap: While the detective sleeps, a carriage carries two old women out of Lincolnshire towards London through freezing roads.

1023.label: Seven happy years
1023.recap: The narrator closes her account years later, accounting for the friends who are married, working, and thriving around her.

1063.label: A vow of revenge
1063.recap: The narrator explains that an insult has decided him on revenge, and on taking it without ever being suspected.

1063.label: Carnival meeting
1063.recap: He runs into his warmly drunken friend in carnival motley and mentions a cask of wine he has doubts about.

1063.label: An empty house
1063.recap: The servants have all slipped away for the holiday, leaving the palazzo entirely to the two men.

1063.label: Down to the vaults
1063.recap: Torches in hand, the pair go down a long winding stair into the damp family catacombs.

1063.label: A drink among the bones
1063.recap: A bottle is broken open against the cold and the two men drink to each other among the dead.

1063.label: A sign exchanged
1063.recap: A second flagon leads to an odd gesture and a question about membership in a secret brotherhood.

1063.label: The inner crypt
1063.recap: Deeper still they reach a small interior recess in the wall where the piled bones have been thrown down.

1063.label: Stone and mortar
1063.recap: The narrator uncovers building stone and mortar among the bones and sets to work at the mouth of the niche.

1063.label: The last stone
1063.recap: Near midnight, with one stone left to fit, a voice comes out of the dark behind the new wall.

1079.label: Interrupted at the start
1079.recap: The narrator blames his entire character on an ill-timed question asked at the very moment he was begotten.

1079.label: A parson named Yorick
1079.recap: The village clergyman is introduced through a long teasing account of his supposedly Danish ancestry.

1079.label: The uncle's hobby-horse
1079.recap: Uncle Toby, mending from an old wound and impatient with his maps and instruments, quietly hires a chariot and removes to the country.

1079.label: The midwife is sent for
1079.recap: Upstairs the mistress goes into labour while the two brothers sit downstairs disputing which practitioner should be trusted.

1079.label: A curse read aloud
1079.recap: Dr Slop is manoeuvred into reading an enormous formal excommunication out loud while Uncle Toby whistles through it.

1079.label: The learning of noses
1079.recap: The father's lifelong obsession with noses is set up as preface to a long borrowed tale about a stranger's remarkable one.

1079.label: Trim in the kitchen
1079.recap: Sad news reaches the servants' hall and Corporal Trim turns it into an unforgettable piece of plain oratory.

1079.label: A stranger at the inn
1079.recap: Trim comes back from the village inn to report on a poor sick lieutenant and the boy lodging there with him.

1079.label: Toby defends himself
1079.recap: Uncle Toby makes a gentle speech explaining how an old soldier may wish for war without wishing any man harm.

1079.label: Posting through France
1079.recap: The narrator sets off across France grumbling about post-horses, and promises a story about an abbess and a novice.

1079.label: The stolen remarks
1079.recap: A traveller finds his pocketful of written observations has vanished and raises a magnificent fuss about it.

1079.label: The parish bull
1079.recap: A servant's complaint about a cow that will not calve becomes the family's last great fireside debate.

1112.label: A quarrel in the street
1112.recap: Two servingmen swagger and bait their rivals over nothing at all, until swords come out and the whole city has to be pulled apart.

1112.label: Masked on the way
1112.recap: Masked young men joke their way toward a rival family's party, and one of them spins a long dazzling fantasy about the fairy who brings dreams.

1112.label: Torchlight and dancing
1112.recap: The old host calls for music and more light, an uninvited guest is recognised across the hall, and two strangers speak to each other for the first time.

1112.label: Over the orchard wall
1112.recap: Slipping away from his friends, who mock him in the dark, a young man hides in a walled garden and overhears words never meant for him.

1112.label: Herbs at daybreak
1112.recap: A friar filling his basket at dawn muses on how the same plant can cure or kill, then receives a startling request from a sleepless visitor.

1112.label: Before the church door
1112.recap: The friar warns two impatient young people to love moderately, and then leads them off to be joined.

1112.label: Hot blood in the street
1112.recap: On a scorching afternoon one friend begs another to go indoors, and instead the quarrel they were avoiding comes looking for them.

1112.label: Waiting for night
1112.recap: Alone and impatient for darkness, a young bride is interrupted by her nurse arriving with news she can barely be made to say plainly.

1112.label: A father's ultimatum
1112.recap: A father who believed he was arranging a splendid match turns violent with rage when his daughter thanks him but refuses.

1112.label: A desperate remedy
1112.recap: Cornered by a wedding date she cannot accept, a young woman is offered a plan every bit as frightening as the thing it is meant to prevent.

1112.label: Morning at the bedside
1112.recap: On the wedding morning the nurse bustles upstairs to wake the bride, and within moments the whole house is wailing.

1112.label: Night in the churchyard
1112.recap: By torchlight in the graveyard, men arrive separately at the family vault, each unaware of the others, and everything the play has been building toward arrives at once.

1153.label: A princess at court
1153.recap: Tara of Helium bathes, dresses, and joins her father's garden reception, where she is introduced to a jewel-covered visitor from a distant kingdom.

1153.label: Caught by the tempest
1153.recap: Drawn by an unusual cloudy sky, she takes her small flier up alone and cannot bring it back against the wind.

1153.label: Cutting the moorings
1153.recap: A cruiser's crew choose to cut their cables and fly into the raging storm in search of the missing princess.

1153.label: The valley of towers
1153.recap: Stranded and thirsty, she creeps to a hilltop and looks down on a cultivated valley of walled towers and the unsettling creatures inside one enclosure.

1153.label: A night among banths
1153.recap: Treed by prowling predators, she endures a long cold night under two moons and refuses to give up hope.

1153.label: Inside the tower
1153.recap: Taken down into the tunnels, she discovers what her captors really are and what they keep the headless bodies for.

1153.label: A brain begins to doubt
1153.recap: One of the cold brains, unsettled by the prisoner's singing, starts questioning everything his kind believes.

1153.label: The strange city
1153.recap: A wandering warrior searches the walls of an unknown city for food and water, unaware he is being watched.

1153.label: The Jeddak's Games
1153.recap: The city's great living-chess tournament opens, and the second match of the day is announced as a game played to the death.

1153.label: The taxidermist's grudge
1153.recap: An ancient craftsman with a grievance tells the jeddak he has traced the fugitives' hiding place by their footprints in the dust.

1153.label: The dreaded chamber
1153.recap: The jeddak wakes alone in the chamber everyone fears and walks back to his court determined to hide what happened there.

1153.label: The throne room
1153.recap: Armed men from distant cities fill the throne room, and the fate of Manator and its ruler is settled in front of everyone.

1155.label: A stranger on deck
1155.recap: As a torpedoed liner settles, a frightened passenger picks out a young American girl and asks her to carry something for him.

1155.label: Tea and no money
1155.recap: Two friends who met in a wartime hospital run into each other in London and compare their equally empty pockets over tea and buns.

1155.label: The Esthonia offer
1155.recap: A sleek businessman offers Tuppence a large sum for an easy trip abroad, on condition that she asks no questions.

1155.label: Tommy tries shadowing
1155.recap: Tommy trails two men across London and discovers that following somebody is far harder than the novels make it look.

1155.label: Recruiting Albert
1155.recap: Left behind while Tommy gives chase, Tuppence wins over a lift-boy with a borrowed badge and a thrilling story.

1155.label: A long night's watch
1155.recap: A sudden collapse leaves the three of them helpless, able only to sit through the night beside a bed and wait for morning.

1155.label: Locked in and hungry
1155.recap: Shut in an upstairs room with no supper, Tommy works out an ambush behind the door and settles down to wait.

1155.label: The train north
1155.recap: A hurried council in the street sends two of the party off to catch a connection, with a warning from the man who cannot come.

1155.label: Watching Astley Priors
1155.recap: Tommy and Albert take rooms at a village inn and quietly collect gossip about a doctor's isolated house.

1155.label: Supper at the Savoy
1155.recap: A millionaire throws a lavish private supper for a small, select party, and a question left hanging is finally answered.

1155.label: The long way home
1155.recap: A late drive back from supper takes a deliberately roundabout route through the park.

1170.label: Two royal brothers
1170.recap: A dying Persian king leaves two sons, and the younger quietly begins collecting soldiers on a pretext.

1170.label: The true destination
1170.recap: At the Euphrates the Greek troops finally learn where they are really being led, and refuse to move without more money.

1170.label: Dust on the plain
1170.recap: The king's army comes into view behind a wall of dust, scythe-chariots along its front, and the Greek line advances to meet it.

1170.label: Morning after the battle
1170.recap: The commanders wake expecting orders and instead receive messengers with news that changes their whole situation.

1170.label: An invitation accepted
1170.recap: Five generals and twenty captains walk into the satrap's headquarters at his own friendly invitation, while their men wait outside.

1170.label: A thousand miles from home
1170.recap: Leaderless, guideless and ringed by enemies, the army passes a sleepless night until one man who holds no rank begins to think.

1170.label: Into the mountains
1170.recap: Before dawn the army climbs into the hills of a fierce independent people whose narrow passes it must force.

1170.label: Six feet of snow
1170.recap: On the frozen Armenian uplands men barter food for a place at the fire, and the rearguard argues with those who will not get up.

1170.label: The view from Theches
1170.recap: A hired guide brings the column to a summit, and a shout starts at the front and runs back down the line.

1170.label: Dances under arms
1170.recap: At a feast with Paphlagonian envoys, soldiers from every corner of Greece take turns performing their war dances.

1170.label: Ferried out of Asia
1170.recap: A satrap arranges to have the army shipped across the strait, and the promises of pay waiting on the other side start to look thin.

1170.label: One last march
1170.recap: A final night expedition in Asia Minor ends with the troops handed over to a newly arrived Spartan commander.

1184.label: Homecoming
1184.recap: The young sailor Edmond Dantès reaches Marseilles with everything before him: a captaincy promised and Mercédès to marry.

1184.label: The Conspiracy
1184.recap: Envious of his good fortune, Dantès's rivals plot to denounce him with an anonymous letter as a Bonapartist traitor.

1184.label: The Betrothal Feast
1184.recap: At his betrothal feast Dantès is seized by gendarmes and torn from Mercédès before they can wed.

1184.label: The Magistrate
1184.recap: To protect a secret that would ruin his own family, the magistrate Villefort condemns the innocent Dantès to a hidden cell.

1184.label: The Château d'If
1184.recap: Long years pass in the island fortress, where the forgotten Dantès sinks toward despair.

1184.label: The Abbé Faria
1184.recap: Dantès befriends a wise old prisoner, the Abbé Faria, who tunnels into his cell and becomes his teacher.

1184.label: The Hidden Treasure
1184.recap: The dying abbé entrusts Dantès with the secret of a vast fortune buried on the lonely isle of Monte Cristo.

1184.label: The Escape
1184.recap: Dantès makes a desperate bid for freedom, taking a dead man's place to escape the prison at last.

1184.label: Treasure of Monte Cristo
1184.recap: Free and alone, Dantès reaches the island and unearths the abbé's staggering hoard of gold and jewels.

1184.label: Tracing the Traitors
1184.recap: Disguised as a priest, Dantès quietly seeks out old acquaintances to learn exactly who betrayed him.

1184.label: The Count Appears
1184.recap: Years later in Italy a mysterious and fabulously rich Count of Monte Cristo dazzles two young Parisian travellers.

1184.label: Into Paris Society
1184.recap: The Count comes to Paris and is welcomed into the homes of the very men who once destroyed Edmond Dantès.

1184.label: Haydée
1184.recap: The Count's beautiful Greek ward, Haydée, carries a secret that ties her to one of his enemies.

1184.label: The Net Tightens
1184.recap: Moving through the salons of Paris, the Count patiently turns his enemies' own sins against them.

1184.label: A Public Disgrace
1184.recap: An old betrayal is dragged into the light, and one proud enemy of the Count faces public ruin.

1184.label: Mercédès
1184.recap: Mercédès knows Edmond at last, and pleads with him over the duel now threatening her son.

1184.label: Expiation
1184.recap: One of the Count's foes is overtaken by a ruin more terrible than anything he had feared.

1184.label: Danglars' Reckoning
1184.recap: The greedy banker Danglars meets a fitting and frightening reckoning far from home.

1184.label: Wait and Hope
1184.recap: His long vengeance complete, the Count takes his leave and gives the young lovers his parting wisdom: wait and hope.

1200.label: A giant is born
1200.recap: In the middle of a countryside drinking party a woman goes into labour and her enormous son arrives bellowing for a drink.

1200.label: The boy's great invention
1200.recap: A father comes home and questions his small son, who answers with an exhaustive account of his own cleverness.

1200.label: A quarrel over cakes
1200.recap: Shepherds ask some passing cake-bakers to sell them a few cakes, and the insults that follow turn into blows.

1200.label: The monk defends the vines
1200.recap: While his brethren chant prayers, one monk notices the enemy stripping the abbey's grapes and decides to deal with it himself.

1200.label: Six pilgrims in a salad
1200.recap: Pilgrims hiding among the lettuces are gathered up by a hungry giant, and spend an alarming time trying to keep their footing.

1200.label: An abbey with no rules
1200.recap: Offered an abbacy, the monk asks instead to found a house run on exactly the opposite principles to every other.

1200.label: A ragged stranger on the road
1200.recap: Walking outside the city, the young giant meets a wounded, tattered young man who answers his questions in one language after another.

1200.label: A giant captain's challenge
1200.recap: With their camp lost, the enemy giants withdraw and their captain insists on fighting the newcomer single-handed.

1200.label: Should he marry?
1200.recap: Panurge asks his master for advice about marrying, and gets an answer that flips with every objection he raises.

1200.label: Bargaining for a sheep
1200.recap: After a shipboard quarrel is patched up, Panurge quietly promises his friends some sport and starts haggling with a sheep merchant.

1200.label: A storm at sea
1200.recap: The fleet meets shiploads of friars, and then a gale that sends one passenger into magnificent, undignified panic.

1200.label: Leaving the oracle
1200.recap: The travellers write their names in a ritual book and are sent home with a long parting speech about what lies hidden underground.

1212.label: A faultless heroine
1212.recap: Laura begins the history of her misfortunes for a friend's daughter, pausing first to list her own many perfections.

1212.label: Someone at the door
1212.recap: A family debates at length whether the knocking at their cottage door really means that somebody wishes to come in.

1212.label: The beautiful stranger
1212.recap: The young man at the fireside explains how bravely he disobeyed his father, and how thoroughly he lost his way.

1212.label: A cold reception
1212.recap: At his aunt's house in Middlesex, Laura meets a sister-in-law who fails entirely to open her arms.

1212.label: Turned out of the Hall
1212.recap: A private drawer, an interrupted errand and a quarrel end with the two friends ordered out of the house within half an hour.

1212.label: A carriage on the road
1212.recap: A conversation neither friend can safely continue is broken off by an overturned phaeton on the turnpike behind them.

1212.label: How everyone ended up
1212.recap: Laura wraps up her correspondence with a brisk accounting of where all the survivors of her story finally settled.

1212.label: Letters from a castle
1212.recap: Two sisters shut up in a mouldering Scottish castle write to a friend about their brother's troubles and their own charms.

1212.label: A wedding dinner wasted
1212.recap: A cook-hostess describes a family disaster chiefly in terms of the vast quantity of meat now going spare.

1212.label: A prejudiced history
1212.recap: A frankly partial historian races through the English kings, promising very few dates and no attempt at fairness.

1212.label: Two girls come out
1212.recap: A proud mother prepares her daughters for their first week in the world, which begins with tea at a neighbour's.

1212.label: Scraps and a tale
1212.recap: The collection closes with odds and ends, including a gentleman who takes a cottage and solves the furniture problem with blankets.

1251.label: A king's unlawful want
1251.recap: King Uther makes war on the Duke of Cornwall over the duke's wife, and sends a knight to find Merlin.

1251.label: The sword in the stone
1251.recap: With the realm leaderless, a sword set in a stone appears in a London churchyard and every great lord tries and fails to draw it.

1251.label: The hand in the lake
1251.recap: Left swordless after a hard fight, Arthur is brought to a broad water where an arm in white samite holds a blade above the surface.

1251.label: The poorly clad knight
1251.recap: A damosel comes to court girded with a sword no man can loose, and a shabby former prisoner asks leave to try.

1251.label: A wedding and a table
1251.recap: Arthur tells Merlin he means to marry Guenever, and her father sends the Round Table and a hundred knights along with her.

1251.label: Merlin besotted
1251.recap: Merlin follows one of the ladies of the lake wherever she goes, teaching her everything he knows while warning the king of what is coming.

1251.label: A ship on dark water
1251.recap: Arthur and two companions chase a hart until their horses drop, and find a silk-hung ship lying empty at the shore.

1251.label: The giant on the mount
1251.recap: Campaigning abroad, Arthur hears of a monster holding a mountain and rides out at night with only two knights.

1251.label: Four queens ride by
1251.recap: Launcelot sleeps armed under an apple tree, and four queens who find him there each decide they want him for themselves.

1251.label: A nameless young man
1251.recap: A tall stranger arrives at Arthur's feast and asks only to be fed for a twelvemonth, and the steward gives him a mocking nickname.

1251.label: A sorrowful birth
1251.recap: A king is trapped by enchantment while his wife searches the forest for him and bears their child alone under a tree.

1251.label: A shield at the tourney
1251.recap: An unknown knight fights brilliantly in a great tournament behind a shield whose device unsettles both the king and the queen.

1257.label: A yellow pony at Meung
1257.recap: A young Gascon riding a ridiculous horse toward Paris picks a quarrel at an inn and loses something he badly needs.

1257.label: Three collisions, three appointments
1257.recap: Racing out of the captain's house in a temper, the newcomer manages to offend three musketeers in the space of a few minutes.

1257.label: Noon by the convent wall
1257.recap: He arrives alone for his first duel and finds that his opponent's two seconds are the other two men he has arranged to fight.

1257.label: The mousetrap downstairs
1257.recap: With the cardinal's men arresting everyone who knocks at his landlord's door, the young Gascon listens through a gap in his floor.

1257.label: The road to the coast
1257.recap: The four friends and their servants ride hard for the Channel, and find that every stop on the road has been prepared for them.

1257.label: A chapel full of candles
1257.recap: In London a great nobleman brings the messenger to a hidden chapel to fetch what the queen has asked him to return.

1257.label: The innkeeper's confession
1257.recap: Back at the inn where a friend went missing, the landlord is squeezed for the truth about what happened after that night's brawl.

1257.label: A dangerous flirtation
1257.recap: A reckless scheme puts the Gascon between a beautiful Englishwoman and her devoted maid, and he refuses to abandon it.

1257.label: Breakfast at the Parpaillot
1257.recap: Needing somewhere nobody can overhear them, the four friends look for a private corner in a camp inn crowded with soldiers.

1257.label: A prisoner works on her jailer
1257.recap: Held in an English castle with a day left before she is shipped away, a prisoner plays her last card on the officer guarding her.

1257.label: A road beside the Lys
1257.recap: By a river under a storm-red moon, a small grim procession walks its prisoner down to the water's edge.

1257.label: What became of everyone
1257.recap: With the siege ended, the narrator sets out where each of the friends, servants and enemies finished up in the years that followed.

1259.label: A Half-Pistole's Effects
1259.recap: Scraping by under the new minister Mazarin, d'Artagnan is glad to have his shrewd old servant Planchet back as Paris simmers toward revolt.

1259.label: Two Angelic Faces
1259.recap: Having won the good-natured Porthos back to adventure, d'Artagnan rides on toward his next old comrade.

1259.label: The Abbé Scarron
1259.recap: At the celebrated salon of the crippled wit Scarron, all fashionable Paris gathers amid the swirl of intrigue and discontent.

1259.label: The Ferry across the Oise
1259.recap: The young Raoul, Athos's ward, sets out for the wars, hiding the grief of leaving his beloved guardian behind.

1259.label: A Letter from Charles the First
1259.recap: At a Paris convent the exiled English queen prays for her husband Charles I, and a desperate appeal for help is set in motion.

1259.label: Another Queen in Want of Help
1259.recap: Athos quietly gathers his friends as yet another threatened sovereign turns to them for rescue.

1259.label: The Interview
1259.recap: Lodged together through the city's riots, d'Artagnan and Porthos are drawn deeper into Mazarin's dangerous games.

1259.label: The Avenger
1259.recap: In England the reunited friends stand by the betrayed King Charles as the net of treachery tightens around him.

1259.label: London
1259.recap: With their plans in ruins, the four comrades ride hard toward London, fearing the worst.

1259.label: A Cornered Foe
1259.recap: The vengeful Mordaunt, cornered by the four friends, coolly watches for any chance to slip free.

1259.label: The Ambassadors
1259.recap: Back in a rain-flooded Paris, the friends pick their way through the perils of the Fronde.

1259.label: Strength and Sagacity
1259.recap: Held captive, d'Artagnan and Porthos set their wits and their strength to engineering an escape.

1260.label: Gateshead
1260.recap: Orphaned Jane suffers under her cruel aunt and cousins at Gateshead, and is locked in terror inside the red-room.

1260.label: Lowood School
1260.recap: Jane is sent to grim, hungry Lowood charity school, where she befriends the gentle, saintly Helen Burns.

1260.label: Loss at Lowood
1260.recap: A fever sweeps Lowood, and Jane loses her beloved friend Helen to illness in the night.

1260.label: Thornfield
1260.recap: Grown and trained, Jane takes a post as governess at Thornfield Hall for the ward of its absent master.

1260.label: Mr. Rochester
1260.recap: Jane and the brooding Mr Rochester grow close, and she saves him from a mysterious fire set in his bed at night.

1260.label: The House Party
1260.recap: A glittering party fills the hall, and Jane quietly aches as Rochester seems to court the beautiful Blanche Ingram.

1260.label: The Proposal
1260.recap: In the moonlit garden Rochester declares he loves Jane, not Blanche, and asks her to be his wife.

1260.label: The Wedding Halted
1260.recap: At the altar the wedding is stopped: Rochester already has a living wife, the madwoman hidden in the attic.

1260.label: Jane Flees
1260.recap: Refusing to live as his mistress, Jane tears herself from Rochester and flees Thornfield into the dark.

1260.label: Moor House
1260.recap: Starving and penniless on the moors, Jane is taken in by the kind Rivers siblings at Moor House.

1260.label: An Inheritance
1260.recap: Jane discovers she has inherited a fortune and that the Rivers are her own cousins, whom she gladly shares it with.

1260.label: St. John's Demand
1260.recap: The cold, devout St John presses Jane to marry him for his mission, until she hears Rochester's voice call across the night.

1260.label: Reader, I Married Him
1260.recap: Jane returns to find Thornfield burned and Rochester blinded but free, and the two are reunited at last.

1268.label: Falling from the sky
1268.recap: A balloon caught in a hurricane sinks toward the Pacific while its passengers throw away everything they own to stay aloft.

1268.label: Who the castaways are
1268.recap: The story turns back to explain that the balloon's passengers were prisoners of war inside besieged Richmond who seized a desperate chance.

1268.label: Search along the shore
1268.recap: The four who reached the beach set off through fog and darkness to look for the companion the sea took.

1268.label: A shelter and no fire
1268.recap: They make a rough home out of a rock crevice, then discover that the only box of matches is gone.

1268.label: Fire out of nothing
1268.recap: The hunters return to a burning hearth and learn how a blaze was kindled without a single match.

1268.label: A bullet in the game
1268.recap: A lead ball found inside a young animal forces the settlers to accept that someone else has been on the island.

1268.label: The missing ladder
1268.recap: Coming home at night, the colonists find their way up has been taken away, and something above them seems to laugh.

1268.label: The abandoned hut
1268.recap: On a far islet the sailing party finds a long-deserted cabin with rusted kettles, damp bedding and a mouldering Bible.

1268.label: The silent stranger
1268.recap: A newcomer living among the colonists refuses to speak, though his grief becomes plain to everyone who watches him work.

1268.label: The brig offshore
1268.recap: With an armed ship anchored in the fog, the engineer divides his small company into posts and prepares to fight.

1268.label: The mountain smokes
1268.recap: Vapour begins rising from the crater above them while the settlers hurry to finish building a seagoing vessel.

1268.label: The last rock
1268.recap: The survivors are crowded onto a bare stone barely clear of the water, with their provisions almost gone.

1342.label: A Single Man of Fortune
1342.recap: Mrs Bennet is delighted that wealthy Mr Bingley has taken nearby Netherfield, and at once schemes to match him with a daughter.

1342.label: The Meryton Assembly
1342.recap: At the local ball Bingley is taken with Jane, while his proud friend Mr Darcy slights Elizabeth, who overhears him.

1342.label: At Netherfield
1342.recap: Nursing an ill Jane at Netherfield, Elizabeth trades sharp words with the scornful Miss Bingley and the watchful Mr Darcy.

1342.label: Mr. Collins Arrives
1342.recap: The pompous clergyman Mr Collins, heir to Longbourn, arrives meaning to marry one of the Bennet girls.

1342.label: The Netherfield Ball
1342.recap: At the Netherfield ball Elizabeth dances with Darcy amid mutual sparring, while her family embarrasses itself.

1342.label: Collins Proposes
1342.recap: Mr Collins proposes to Elizabeth, who refuses him flatly, to her mother's despair.

1342.label: Charlotte's Choice
1342.recap: To Elizabeth's shock, her sensible friend Charlotte accepts Mr Collins for the comfort and security he offers.

1342.label: Darcy's Proposal
1342.recap: Darcy stuns Elizabeth with a proud declaration of love; insulted, she refuses him and throws his faults in his face.

1342.label: The Letter
1342.recap: Darcy's long letter explains his hand in parting Bingley from Jane and the real truth about Wickham, shaking Elizabeth's certainties.

1342.label: Pemberley
1342.recap: Touring Darcy's grand estate, Elizabeth hears him warmly praised and meets him again, unexpectedly gentle.

1342.label: Lydia's Flight
1342.recap: Word arrives that her reckless sister Lydia has run off with Wickham, threatening the whole family's name.

1342.label: Darcy Speaks Again
1342.recap: His feelings unchanged, Darcy proposes a second time, and now Elizabeth gladly accepts him.

1342.label: Two Weddings
1342.recap: With Jane and Elizabeth both happily married, the Bennet household settles at last into contentment.

1399.label: A house in confusion
1399.recap: A Moscow household falls apart after the wife finds a letter, and her husband wakes on his study sofa remembering why.

1399.label: On the platform
1399.recap: A young officer meeting his mother's train notices the lady stepping down from her compartment.

1399.label: Before the mazurka
1399.recap: At a Moscow ball Kitty watches the evening she had counted on turn into something quite different.

1399.label: The officers' race
1399.recap: Seventeen riders take a three-mile course of nine obstacles while the court watches from the pavilion.

1399.label: A day with the scythe
1399.recap: Levin resolves to spend a whole day mowing beside his peasants, unsure whether his brother will laugh at him.

1399.label: Strangers at home
1399.recap: Three people wait for something to change while nothing does, and Vronsky is saddled with escorting a visiting prince.

1399.label: Letters in chalk
1399.recap: At a card table two people spell out whole sentences in initial letters and understand each other perfectly.

1399.label: A provincial hotel
1399.recap: Levin arrives with his wife at a filthy hotel where his brother is lying gravely ill.

1399.label: A full summer house
1399.recap: A crowded country household plans a mushroom hunt, and Kitty notices something passing between two of the guests.

1399.label: The long drive
1399.recap: Dolly travels a whole day by carriage to pay a visit, turning her own life over in her mind on the way.

1399.label: The evening train
1399.recap: Anna boards a train alone and finds every face, voice and pleasantry around her unbearable.

1399.label: Under the stars
1399.recap: Alone on the terrace between lightning flashes, Levin quietly settles something he has been struggling with for months.

1400.label: The Convict
1400.recap: In the marsh churchyard the orphan boy Pip is seized by an escaped convict and frightened into bringing him food and a file.

1400.label: Miss Havisham
1400.recap: Pip is summoned to the decaying Satis House to play for the strange Miss Havisham and her cold, lovely ward Estella.

1400.label: Apprenticed
1400.recap: Bound apprentice to the kind blacksmith Joe, Pip grows ashamed of his humble home and pines for Estella.

1400.label: Great Expectations
1400.recap: A lawyer brings astonishing news: Pip has a secret benefactor and great expectations, and must leave for London to become a gentleman.

1400.label: London
1400.recap: In London Pip meets the formidable lawyer Jaggers and lodges with his cheerful friend Herbert Pocket.

1400.label: Estella Returns
1400.recap: Sure that Miss Havisham means Estella for him, Pip falls deeper in love despite her warning that she has no heart.

1400.label: The Benefactor
1400.recap: On a stormy night Pip's true benefactor appears: not Miss Havisham, but the convict he once helped, Magwitch.

1400.label: Magwitch's Story
1400.recap: Magwitch tells his life, revealing a link to the man who once jilted Miss Havisham, as danger closes around him.

1400.label: Satis House Burns
1400.recap: Pip forgives a remorseful, broken Miss Havisham just before her decaying house goes up in flames.

1400.label: The Trap on the Marsh
1400.recap: Lured back to the marshes, Pip is nearly murdered by the vengeful Orlick before help arrives.

1400.label: The Escape Fails
1400.recap: The plan to smuggle Magwitch out of England collapses; he is captured and badly hurt in the struggle.

1400.label: Reunion
1400.recap: Years later, humbled and changed, Pip comes home and meets Estella once more among the ruins of Satis House.

1497.label: Down to the harbour
1497.recap: Walking home from a festival, Socrates is cheerfully outnumbered and talked into staying the evening.

1497.label: At the old man's house
1497.recap: In his host's front room he falls into conversation with an elderly man about wealth, old age, and what it means to owe something.

1497.label: An angry interruption
1497.recap: A furious guest can hold back no longer and insists that justice is nothing but whatever suits the stronger.

1497.label: The challenge revived
1497.recap: Unsatisfied with how the argument closed, Glaucon takes up the case against justice himself and pushes it as hard as he can.

1497.label: Stories for the young
1497.recap: With the rules about the gods settled, the talk turns to which tales, music and training will shape the city's guardians.

1497.label: Are the guardians happy?
1497.recap: Adeimantus objects that this imagined city makes its own protectors miserable, and the answer leads into the parts of the soul.

1497.label: Who should rule
1497.recap: Having separated real philosophers from imitations, Socrates argues that only they should govern, and must explain why they seem so useless.

1497.label: A den and a fire
1497.recap: Socrates describes prisoners chained underground who have never seen anything but shadows thrown on a wall.

1497.label: How cities decay
1497.recap: With the good city described, the talk turns to the ways it goes wrong, one form of government sliding into the next.

1497.label: The tyrant's soul
1497.recap: The last and worst character is examined, and the question becomes what such a life actually feels like from the inside.

1497.label: Poetry on trial
1497.recap: The case against imitative poetry is reopened, and the poets are measured against what is actually true.

1497.label: Choosing a life
1497.recap: A soldier's report from the other world describes souls stepping forward to choose the lives they will be born into.

1510.label: The three-year oath
1510.recap: The King of Navarre binds himself and three lords to three years of study, fasting and no women within a mile of the court.

1510.label: A flaw in the oath
1510.recap: Berowne points out that the French King's daughter is already coming on business, which breaks the no-women clause before it starts.

1510.label: Costard sentenced
1510.recap: A country fellow caught with a wench quibbles cheerfully over every word of the proclamation and is handed over to the Spaniard for keeping.

1510.label: Armado and his page
1510.recap: The grandiloquent Spanish visitor admits to his very quick little page that he has fallen for the same country girl.

1510.label: The Princess arrives
1510.recap: Halted outside the forbidden gates, the French Princess sends an ambassador ahead while her ladies describe the lords they already know.

1510.label: A letter to be carried
1510.recap: Armado calls for a song and sets his page to fetch the clown, meaning to employ him to deliver a love letter.

1510.label: The Princess goes hunting
1510.recap: Waiting on the King's answer, the Princess takes a bow to the deer stand and trades sharp jokes with a forester about her own looks.

1510.label: The schoolmaster's table talk
1510.recap: A pedant, a curate and a slow constable pick over Latin tags and disagree about what kind of deer was killed.

1510.label: All hid, all hid
1510.recap: One after another the sworn scholars steal into the park to read love poems aloud, each unaware that he is overheard.

1510.label: Masks and swapped favours
1510.recap: Warned that the lords mean to come disguised, the ladies mask themselves and exchange tokens so every man will woo the wrong woman.

1510.label: A messenger from France
1510.recap: In the middle of the afternoon's entertainment a messenger arrives from France and the whole mood of the day changes.

1510.label: Terms set for a year
1510.recap: The ladies answer the lords' suits not with acceptance but with conditions to be kept for a twelvemonth.

1513.label: A Street Brawl
1513.recap: The feuding Montagues and Capulets clash in Verona until the Prince warns that the next to break the peace will die; lovesick Romeo pines for another.

1513.label: The Capulet Feast
1513.recap: At the Capulets' masked ball Romeo and Juliet meet and fall in love at once, only to learn they are children of sworn enemies.

1513.label: The Balcony
1513.recap: Beneath Juliet's window the two pledge their love and resolve to marry in secret.

1513.label: Married in Secret
1513.recap: Friar Lawrence weds Romeo and Juliet, hoping their union might heal the families' feud.

1513.label: Mercutio and Tybalt
1513.recap: Tybalt kills Mercutio; a grief-stricken Romeo kills Tybalt in turn, and the Prince banishes Romeo from Verona.

1513.label: Parting at Dawn
1513.recap: Romeo flees to Mantua after their one night together, just as Juliet's father commands her to marry Paris.

1513.label: The Friar's Plan
1513.recap: Desperate, Juliet takes a potion from Friar Lawrence that will make her seem dead so she can slip away to Romeo.

1513.label: The Potion
1513.recap: Alone and afraid, Juliet drinks the potion and sinks into a deathlike sleep.

1513.label: The Tomb
1513.recap: Believing Juliet dead, Romeo drinks poison at her tomb; waking to find him gone, Juliet takes her own life, and the families at last make peace.

1514.label: A wedding and a complaint
1514.recap: A duke counts the days to his wedding, and an angry father arrives demanding the law be used on his daughter.

1514.label: A plan to run
1514.recap: Two lovers agree to slip out of the city by night and meet at a place in the wood.

1514.label: Casting the interlude
1514.recap: A company of Athenian workmen hand out parts for the play they hope to perform at court.

1514.label: Fairies in the wood
1514.recap: Two spirits meet by moonlight and speak of the quarrel that has set the fairy king and queen against each other.

1514.label: A flower with a use
1514.recap: The fairy king sends his servant off with a charmed flower and instructions concerning an Athenian.

1514.label: Lost, and asleep
1514.recap: Two travellers lose their way and lie down apart to rest, and a mistake is made over them in the dark.

1514.label: Rehearsal in the wood
1514.recap: The workmen worry that their play will frighten the ladies and invent elaborate ways to soften it.

1514.label: Waiting for news
1514.recap: The fairy king waits to hear what his charm has done, and learns his orders went astray.

1514.label: The night turns cruel
1514.recap: The four young Athenians turn on one another in a bruising quarrel that nearly comes to blows.

1514.label: Doted upon
1514.recap: The fairy queen lavishes attention on her strange new favourite while her husband watches unseen.

1514.label: Back in Athens
1514.recap: The players despair of their missing man until he bursts in with orders and no explanation.

1514.label: The play at court
1514.recap: The duke doubts the young people's story, and the workmen finally perform their tragedy for the wedding party.

1523.label: A brother's grievance
1523.recap: A young gentleman complains that his elder brother keeps him unschooled and idle, and the two come to blows.

1523.label: The wrestling match
1523.recap: The court gathers to watch a bout everyone expects to end badly for the newcomer.

1523.label: Two cousins flee
1523.recap: Facing banishment, two young women plan to escape in disguise and take a jester with them.

1523.label: Life in the forest
1523.recap: The banished duke praises the plain hardships of the greenwood over the flattery of the court.

1523.label: Arrival in Arden
1523.recap: The travellers reach the forest footsore and hungry and overhear a shepherd complaining of love.

1523.label: A fool in the forest
1523.recap: A melancholy courtier delights in a jester he has met and begs to be given a motley coat of his own.

1523.label: The seven ages
1523.recap: While a starving old servant is fed, the company hears a speech on the stages of a human life.

1523.label: Verses on the trees
1523.recap: Love poems start appearing pinned to the branches, and the forest sets about mocking them.

1523.label: A cure for love
1523.recap: In disguise, one of the travellers offers to cure a lovesick man by a distinctly odd arrangement.

1523.label: A scolding backfires
1523.recap: A proud shepherdess is bluntly told to be kinder to the man who worships her.

1523.label: A bloody handkerchief
1523.recap: A stranger arrives with a token and an account of something that happened under an oak tree.

1523.label: All accounts settled
1523.recap: The tangle of disguises and promises is undone and news arrives that changes everyone's fortunes.

1564.label: A bookseller's son
1564.recap: The subject of the book is born in a Staffordshire market town to a father who deals in books.

1564.label: Arrival at Oxford
1564.recap: He arrives at university better read than anyone expects, and startles the company by quoting an author nobody had raised.

1564.label: Trying London
1564.recap: He moves to the capital with his wife, hawks an unwanted tragedy round the theatres, and takes work on a magazine.

1564.label: The Dictionary appears
1564.recap: The great two-volume work is published at last, and its author answers criticism of his slips with cheerful bluntness.

1564.label: A book in a week
1564.recap: After his mother's death he writes a short philosophical tale in the evenings of a single week to pay for her funeral.

1564.label: A bookshop back parlour
1564.recap: A young Scot who has read everything the great man wrote finally contrives to be in the room when he walks in.

1564.label: Tavern arguments
1564.recap: Over supper at a tavern the two friends argue about savages, singularity and the pleasures of city life.

1564.label: A threatening letter
1564.recap: A furious author threatens him over a literary dispute and receives a reply that refuses to be frightened.

1564.label: An impossible dinner party
1564.recap: Boswell schemes to seat his hero at table with a political enemy he has never agreed to meet.

1564.label: A letter of comfort
1564.recap: Writing to a bereaved friend, he sets down what it is to outlive the person who shared your whole mind.

1564.label: Consulting the doctors
1564.recap: With his health failing, opinions on his case are gathered from physicians across two countries.

1564.label: Friends at the bedside
1564.recap: In his final weeks the house fills with visitors, and his old sharpness and courtesy keep breaking through.

1597.label: An emperor and two weavers
1597.recap: Two strangers offer to weave a cloth invisible to anyone unfit for his office, and the Emperor pays them handsomely to begin.

1597.label: A prince in disguise
1597.recap: Rejected along with his gifts of a rose and a nightingale, a poor prince blackens his face and takes work minding an emperor's pigs.

1597.label: A test for a princess
1597.recap: A prince who has searched the world for a genuine princess gets one last chance when a girl arrives out of a storm.

1597.label: Shoes that grant wishes
1597.recap: The narrator opens on a Copenhagen party and a pair of shoes that carry whoever wears them straight to whatever they wish for.

1597.label: The impatient fir tree
1597.recap: A small fir in the forest wishes away its own good days, longing only to grow tall and be carried off somewhere grand.

1597.label: A mirror in splinters
1597.recap: A malicious sprite's distorting mirror shatters, and the splinters scatter over the world into people's eyes and hearts.

1597.label: A jumping contest
1597.recap: Three jumpers boast of their breeding before a king who has offered his daughter to whichever of them leaps highest.

1597.label: Tea and a tall tale
1597.recap: A boy kept in bed with a cold is told a story that seems to rise out of the steam of his elderflower tea.

1597.label: A mother's bargain
1597.recap: A mother watching over her failing child answers a knock at the door, and then sets out after what she has lost.

1597.label: A learned man's shadow
1597.recap: A scholar from the cold north, shut indoors by the heat, grows curious about the balcony opposite and about his own shadow.

1597.label: New Year's Eve in the snow
1597.recap: A barefoot girl carrying unsold matches through a freezing city finally settles in a corner to strike one and warm herself.

1597.label: A pair of red shoes
1597.recap: A poor girl is given a pair of red shoes and finds she cannot stop thinking about them, even in church.

1600.label: A friend is asked
1600.recap: Apollodorus, stopped on the road, agrees to repeat second-hand the speeches made at a famous supper years before.

1600.label: An unbidden guest
1600.recap: Aristodemus meets Socrates unusually well turned out and is invited along, unasked, to a victory banquet.

1600.label: Socrates goes missing
1600.recap: Socrates stops in a neighbour's porch and stays there, leaving his companion to arrive at the party alone.

1600.label: A game is proposed
1600.recap: Still feeling the previous night's wine, the guests send the flute-girl away and agree that each will make a speech in praise of Love.

1600.label: Love the eldest god
1600.recap: Phaedrus opens the round by arguing that Love is the oldest of the gods and the surest source of courage and honour.

1600.label: A hiccough intervenes
1600.recap: A fit of hiccoughs forces the comic poet to swap turns, and the physician takes the floor with a theory drawn from medicine.

1600.label: The halved people
1600.recap: Aristophanes offers a comic myth about what the first human beings looked like and why people have been searching ever since.

1600.label: The host's showpiece
1600.recap: The young host delivers an ornate, highly polished encomium calling Love the youngest, tenderest and fairest of the gods.

1600.label: Questions after applause
1600.recap: Socrates admires the speech, then asks the host a short chain of questions about what Love actually wants.

1600.label: What the priestess said
1600.recap: Socrates reports a long conversation with a wise woman of Mantineia who taught him a very different account of desire.

1600.label: A loud arrival
1600.recap: A knocking at the door interrupts the evening as a garlanded, thoroughly drunk latecomer forces his way in and takes charge of the wine.

1600.label: Dawn at the table
1600.recap: A band of revellers spoils the order of the party, and by daybreak only a few are still awake and arguing.

1608.label: An emptied apartment
1608.recap: The narrator joins a crowd of curious visitors touring the luxurious rooms of a woman who has just died.

1608.label: The sale
1608.recap: At the packed auction he finds himself bidding stubbornly for a single inscribed book he did not come to buy.

1608.label: A caller in travelling dust
1608.recap: A distraught young stranger arrives at the narrator's door and asks a favour connected with that book.

1608.label: A feverish errand
1608.recap: Ill and grieving, Armand insists on carrying out a painful resolution and asks the narrator to come with him.

1608.label: Across the theatre
1608.recap: Armand watches Marguerite from the stalls and finds an acquaintance who might arrange an introduction.

1608.label: By a single candle
1608.recap: Alone with Marguerite after a coughing fit, Armand offers his devotion and is answered with unsparing honesty.

1608.label: A letter written in anger
1608.recap: Believing he has been made a fool of, Armand writes a cutting farewell and sends it before he can regret it.

1608.label: Summer in the country
1608.recap: The two settle into a quiet country life together, though Marguerite sometimes weeps without explaining why.

1608.label: His father calls
1608.recap: Armand's father arrives in Paris and opens a cold, deliberate conversation about the woman his son is living with.

1608.label: A night at cards
1608.recap: Armand gambles recklessly at a stranger's supper party and uses his winnings to make a deliberately cold proposition.

1608.label: Pages in her own hand
1608.recap: Marguerite's own writing takes over the story, explaining what happened after Armand's father came to Bougival.

1608.label: Last calls
1608.recap: The narrator and Armand pay their final visits, and Armand goes back to his family in the country.

1656.label: Opening the defence
1656.recap: The speaker asks the court to forgive his plain, unpractised way of talking and to judge only whether what he says is true.

1656.label: The old slander
1656.recap: He sums up the rumours that have followed him for years and denies studying the heavens or taking money for teaching.

1656.label: A question at Delphi
1656.recap: He tells how an impetuous friend once went to the oracle and came back with an answer that puzzled him.

1656.label: Testing the reputedly wise
1656.recap: He describes questioning poets and craftsmen about their own work and what he concluded from their replies.

1656.label: Why the young follow him
1656.recap: He explains that idle young men imitate his questioning, and that the anger this causes has landed on him.

1656.label: Questioning the accuser
1656.recap: He calls his prosecutor forward and begins asking who exactly improves the young people of Athens.

1656.label: On fearing death
1656.recap: Answering the charge that his way of life is reckless, he argues that no one knows whether death is an evil.

1656.label: The gadfly
1656.recap: He compares himself to a stinging fly set upon a large, sleepy horse, and says the city will not easily find another.

1656.label: Two dangerous orders
1656.recap: He recalls two occasions, under different governments, when he refused to take part in what he thought unlawful.

1656.label: Naming his own penalty
1656.recap: Asked what punishment he deserves, he considers the options with unsettling cheerfulness before his friends intervene.

1656.label: A word to the majority
1656.recap: He tells those who voted against him what he expects will follow, and why silencing critics rarely works.

1656.label: Two ideas of dying
1656.recap: Turning to the friends who supported him, he sets out two possibilities about death and takes comfort from both.

1658.label: A question at Phlius
1658.recap: Far from Athens, Echecrates finds a man who was there and presses him to tell, as exactly as he can, everything said on Socrates' last day.

1658.label: The prison door opens
1658.recap: The friends gather earlier than usual, are kept waiting outside, and find Socrates just released from his chains with his wife beside him.

1658.label: Why not simply depart
1658.recap: Asked why a man may not end his own life if death is a good, Socrates offers an old teaching that men are possessions of the gods.

1658.label: The practice of dying
1658.recap: Socrates argues that philosophy has always been a training in separating soul from body, so a philosopher of all men should not flinch at death.

1658.label: Learning as remembering
1658.recap: Cebes raises the idea that what we call learning is really remembering, and Simmias asks to hear the arguments for it laid out again.

1658.label: The lyre and the harmony
1658.recap: Simmias offers a picture that unsettles everyone: the soul as the harmony of a strung instrument, which cannot outlast the strings.

1658.label: The weaver and his coats
1658.recap: Cebes adds an image of an old weaver outliving his coats, and doubts that a long-lived soul must therefore be a deathless one.

1658.label: The argument falters
1658.recap: The telling pauses, and the listener confesses that these objections have shaken his confidence in argument itself.

1658.label: Socrates' own story
1658.recap: Socrates takes his time before answering, then begins to describe his own youthful hunger to know why anything comes to be at all.

1658.label: The true earth
1658.recap: Socrates describes the earth as it would look from far above, and the brighter country he believes lies beyond the hollows we live in.

1658.label: The bath
1658.recap: Socrates leaves the room to wash, speaks briefly with his family, and comes back to sit with his friends as the sun nears the hills.

1658.label: The cup is brought
1658.recap: The poison is carried in, Socrates asks the attendant how it should be taken, and the room can no longer hold back its grief.

1661.label: A Scandal in Bohemia
1661.recap: The King of Bohemia hires Holmes to recover a compromising photograph from Irene Adler, the one woman ever to outwit him.

1661.label: The Red-Headed League
1661.recap: A pawnbroker is paid generously to copy out an encyclopaedia for a bogus society, and Holmes senses a deeper scheme.

1661.label: A Case of Identity
1661.recap: A short-sighted typist begs Holmes to find the fiancé who vanished on the very morning of their wedding.

1661.label: The Boscombe Valley Mystery
1661.recap: A young man stands accused of murdering his father, and Holmes travels west to test the damning evidence.

1661.label: The Five Orange Pips
1661.recap: A frightened client whose relatives die soon after receiving envelopes of orange pips comes to Baker Street for help.

1661.label: The Man with the Twisted Lip
1661.recap: A respectable gentleman seems to vanish inside an opium den, and Holmes sets out to learn what became of him.

1661.label: The Blue Carbuncle
1661.recap: A precious jewel turns up inside a Christmas goose, sending Holmes on a festive chase to trace its journey.

1661.label: The Speckled Band
1661.recap: A terrified woman fears for her life after her sister died gasping of a speckled band, and Holmes eyes her sinister stepfather.

1661.label: The Engineer's Thumb
1661.recap: A hydraulic engineer arrives maimed and shaken after a nightmarish night's work for a mysterious client.

1661.label: The Noble Bachelor
1661.recap: A lord's bride disappears from the wedding breakfast, and Holmes is asked to explain her sudden flight.

1661.label: The Beryl Coronet
1661.recap: A banker entrusted with a priceless coronet finds it damaged and his own son seemingly to blame.

1661.label: The Copper Beeches
1661.recap: A governess offered a strange post, asked to cut her hair and sit at a window, asks Holmes whether she is in danger.

1685.label: News of a crime
1685.recap: Paris newspapers report that a famous scientist's daughter has been attacked in a room locked from the inside.

1685.label: Forcing the door
1685.recap: The old servant describes how the men finally broke into the chamber and what they found on the floor.

1685.label: The reporter appears
1685.recap: The narrator introduces his friend, a teenage journalist with a knack for finding what the police cannot.

1685.label: Train out from Paris
1685.recap: On the way to the crime scene the young reporter charms and needles the examining magistrate for details.

1685.label: Arrival at the château
1685.recap: They reach the guarded house, where the reporter greets the injured woman's fiancé with a strange demand.

1685.label: Inside the room
1685.recap: The reporter examines the scene of the attack inch by inch, including the floor beneath the bed.

1685.label: Breakfast at the inn
1685.recap: A hostile innkeeper turns obliging the moment the reporter says something that means nothing to the narrator.

1685.label: Bring revolvers
1685.recap: A telegram calls the narrator back to the château, where he is told that matters are going badly.

1685.label: Footprints in the gallery
1685.recap: Woken by a strange cry at night, the reporter finds muddy footprints in the corridor and lays a plan.

1685.label: The second vigil
1685.recap: The reporter posts his friend in a dark closet and explains that he wants to see a face, not make an arrest.

1685.label: At the assizes
1685.recap: The reporter arrives late at a packed courtroom and offers to name the murderer.

1685.label: Afterwards
1685.recap: Months later the narrator finds his friend low-spirited, brooding over something he will not explain.

1686.label: A stranger at the villa
1686.recap: The general's wife goes to look over the young Frenchman who has arrived at her heavily guarded house.

1686.label: Dinner with the general
1686.recap: The reporter is presented to the general's boisterous old friends over champagne and hunting stories.

1686.label: The garden at night
1686.recap: Matrena shuts the villa up for the night and discovers where the reporter has quietly stationed himself.

1686.label: The tick-tack
1686.recap: She confides her terror of hidden clockwork and describes how one earlier attempt on her husband was foiled.

1686.label: The sleeping general
1686.recap: They climb to the bedroom floor, where the sleeper talks aloud in a nightmare about Moscow.

1686.label: Voices in the wood
1686.recap: Following footprints into the ferns, the reporter overhears an argument he was never meant to hear.

1686.label: Watching the bolt
1686.recap: Reporter and wife keep a silent vigil on a locked door until, near dawn, something moves.

1686.label: Back to the river bank
1686.recap: He races from a night restaurant to the dark grounds of the villa, where police are already lying in the grass.

1686.label: The alchemist's shop
1686.recap: A chase across the city ends in a cluttered herbalist's den where a test can finally be made.

1686.label: After the explosions
1686.recap: The damage is counted at the wrecked villa while one member of the household is still missing.

1686.label: A blindfolded journey
1686.recap: Carried off in a shuttered carriage, the reporter is led into a bare room full of silent young men.

1686.label: A dash for the Tsar
1686.recap: He wakes the whole hotel, packs in a fury and sets off through the night countryside.

1695.label: The Two Poets
1695.recap: In a London suburb the poet of order, Gabriel Syme, clashes with the red-haired anarchist poet Lucian Gregory.

1695.label: The Secret of Gabriel Syme
1695.recap: Gregory secretly leads Syme to an underground anarchist meeting, never guessing Syme is an undercover detective.

1695.label: Elected Thursday
1695.recap: Syme boldly gets himself elected to the anarchist Central Council under the code name Thursday.

1695.label: The Tale of a Detective
1695.recap: Syme recalls how a man in a pitch-dark room recruited him into a secret philosophical police force.

1695.label: The Feast of Fear
1695.recap: Syme sits in dread at the Council's table beneath its vast, terrifying leader, the man called Sunday.

1695.label: The Exposure
1695.recap: Syme and the sinister Professor de Worms watch one another warily, each fearing the other has seen through him.

1695.label: The Professor Explains
1695.recap: The Professor reveals he too is an undercover detective, and the council's terror starts to come apart.

1695.label: The Duel
1695.recap: Syme fights a strange, almost unkillable duel with a council member who turns out to be yet another ally.

1695.label: The Earth in Anarchy
1695.recap: One by one the anarchists are unmasked as fellow detectives, all fleeing a mob that seems to be the whole world.

1695.label: The Pursuit of Sunday
1695.recap: The detectives give chase to the elusive, godlike Sunday across the country in an ever wilder pursuit.

1695.label: The Accuser
1695.recap: In a dreamlike finale Sunday reveals himself, and Syme faces the strange meaning behind the whole ordeal.

1719.label: The horse on the hill
1719.recap: The chalk horse cut into the downs is older than memory, and it has watched age after age go past.

1719.label: A king in the grass
1719.recap: With Rome sunk and the Northmen everywhere, Alfred is beaten back into hiding and holds on with nothing but hope.

1719.label: A vision by the river
1719.recap: Alone in the marshes Alfred sees a figure standing among the grass, and asks her whether his land will ever come home.

1719.label: At Eldred's farm
1719.recap: He comes to a ruined farm where a huge, drink-worn man would rather watch his plums ripen than fight again.

1719.label: Into the enemy camp
1719.recap: Carrying nothing but a harp, Alfred walks unarmed toward the Danish fires and is dragged in to play for them.

1719.label: Songs round the fire
1719.recap: The earls take the harp in turn, each singing out his own bleak creed to the men at the fire.

1719.label: The woman at the hut
1719.recap: A scarred woman looks at the ragged stranger and offers him a cake if he will watch her fire.

1719.label: The Danes take the field
1719.recap: Guthrum, who has swept the country, picks his ground at the parting of the ways and draws up his lines.

1719.label: The armies meet
1719.recap: The two hosts crash together on the field and the chiefs seek each other out in the press.

1719.label: A child on the down
1719.recap: Far from the fighting a child plays alone on the chalk, piling small stones that keep falling down.

1719.label: Peace and the orchard
1719.recap: In quiet years afterwards the King sits among his apple trees, gathering up the songs of ordinary men.

1719.label: Riding out at dawn
1719.recap: With the down scoured clean again the levies gather, and the King rides away on a tall grey horse.

1727.label: The Gods in Council
1727.recap: The poet calls on the Muse; the gods agree it is time for long-lost Ulysses to be freed from Calypso's island and brought home.

1727.label: Calypso
1727.recap: Released at last by the nymph Calypso, Ulysses builds a raft and sails, only to be wrecked by Poseidon's storm.

1727.label: Nausicaa
1727.recap: Cast ashore, Ulysses is discovered by the kind princess Nausicaa, who sends him on toward her father's palace.

1727.label: The Cyclops
1727.recap: Ulysses tells how he blinded the man-eating Cyclops Polyphemus to escape his cave, drawing down Poseidon's wrath.

1727.label: Circe
1727.recap: After the wind-god's bag and the cannibal Laestrygonians, Ulysses outwits the enchantress Circe, who turns men to swine.

1727.label: The Visit to the Dead
1727.recap: Ulysses sails to the edge of the underworld to question the prophet Tiresias and meet the shades of the dead.

1727.label: The Sirens and Scylla
1727.recap: Past the Sirens and the monsters Scylla and Charybdis, his starving crew doom themselves by eating the Sun-god's cattle.

1727.label: Return to Ithaca
1727.recap: The Phaeacians carry the sleeping Ulysses home to Ithaca, where Minerva hides him in the shape of an old beggar.

1727.label: The Swineherd
1727.recap: In disguise Ulysses is taken in by his faithful old swineherd Eumaeus, who does not know his master.

1727.label: Father and Son
1727.recap: Ulysses reveals himself to his son Telemachus, and together they plot against the suitors plaguing his house.

1727.label: The Trial of the Bow
1727.recap: Penelope sets the contest of the great bow, which none of the suitors can string, that only Ulysses can win.

1727.label: The Killing of the Suitors
1727.recap: Ulysses throws off his disguise and, with Telemachus, slays the suitors and reclaims his home and his queen.

1837.label: Two boys are born
1837.recap: On one autumn day two boys are born in London: one into a poor family that did not want him, and one whom all England has been praying for.

1837.label: At the palace gate
1837.recap: Tom drifts out to the palace gates hoping for a glimpse of royalty, is flung back by a guard, and is called inside by the prince himself.

1837.label: Alone in the cabinet
1837.recap: Left by himself among the prince's things, Tom plays at grandeur, then falls into terror when the prince does not come back.

1837.label: The first royal dinner
1837.recap: Dressed for dinner and attended by a small army of hereditary officials, Tom tries to get through a formal meal without disgracing himself.

1837.label: Inside Offal Court
1837.recap: Hauled into a squalid room by a violent man, the boy insists on his own name before a hostile household, and a frightened woman grieves over him.

1837.label: Across London Bridge
1837.recap: Escorted through the crowds by a ragged soldier, the boy hears the city shouting news of a death and a new reign.

1837.label: Ambassadors and councils
