1837.recap: Ceremony, audiences and state business wear on the boy in the palace, who dreads one small ordeal more than all the great ones.

1837.label: The children in the barn
1837.recap: Waking in a barn, the boy is found by two farm children who consider his claim about himself with perfect seriousness.

1837.label: The hermit's vigil
1837.recap: A soft-voiced old hermit sits beside his sleeping guest through the night, whetting a knife and murmuring to himself.

1837.label: The stocks
1837.recap: Miles is sentenced to the stocks as a vagabond, and when the boy protests on his behalf the officers reach for the lash instead.

1837.label: Coronation morning
1837.recap: Hours before dawn the galleries of Westminster Abbey fill, and the peeresses take their places under a sudden shaft of sunlight.

1837.label: Hunting the crowds
1837.recap: Robbed of his last farthing, Miles Hendon works out a soldier's plan for finding the boy: hunt not for him but for the crowd around him.

1849.label: A man alone in the house
1849.recap: A man sits motionless through a day and a night, then rings for his servant and gives orders to leave his home for good.

1849.label: Questions at the hotel
1849.recap: A luggage porter and a cabman are paid to say what they remember of a lady who changed her destination mid-journey.

1849.label: Hiring a fixer
1849.recap: Mr Sabin engages a loud New York operator who promises the facts he wants by nightfall.

1849.label: Dinner interrupted
1849.recap: The report is delivered over oysters and champagne, and so is the man who employs its author.

1849.label: A crowded restaurant
1849.recap: Amid a rowdy yacht-race celebration, Mr Sabin finally tells the friend he summoned from Paris what has happened.

1849.label: Landing in England
1849.recap: Felix finds Mr Sabin already waiting on the quay, and over lunch they agree how each will help.

1849.label: Taking a man's measure
1849.recap: At a London luncheon Mr Sabin studies a rising Cabinet minister and wonders where their paths will cross.

1849.label: An old story told
1849.recap: Over coffee in a winter garden he tells his niece about the woman he has loved since he was thirty-five.

1849.label: Cards and a reunion
1849.recap: He walks in on a country-house card party and calmly states his claim before the whole company.

1849.label: A Soho wine shop
1849.recap: He finds a shabby eating house where an old acquaintance, shaking with fear, begs him to leave at once.

1849.label: The detective's theory
1849.recap: Over breakfast a private detective sets out what he believes really happened to Mr Sabin's servant.

1849.label: An audience granted
1849.recap: Mr Sabin at last lays his charges before the one man with the power to settle them.

1872.label: A drowsy afternoon
1872.recap: In the housekeeper's room a parlour-maid and her aunt gossip about the brother expected from Australia.

1872.label: The visitor arrives
1872.recap: A rough-looking stranger is shown into the office, and the maid goes off to find her master.

1872.label: Who owns the house
1872.recap: A short history of the Red House's owner, his luck with money, and the silent cousin who runs his affairs.

1872.label: A stranger at Woodham
1872.recap: An idle, sharp-eyed traveller gets off at the wrong station and learns an old friend is staying nearby.

1872.label: In through the window
1872.recap: Two men give up on the locked door and force their way in from the lawn instead.

1872.label: The inspector's questions
1872.recap: A police inspector starts on the servants while the housekeeper's room trades rival versions of what it heard.

1872.label: The guests go home
1872.recap: With the house emptied, the two friends settle on a garden seat and go over the whole affair.

1872.label: Keys and theories
1872.recap: Dressing for dinner, Antony sets his friend to checking small physical details nobody else has bothered with.

1872.label: Dragging the pond
1872.recap: The inspector, pleased with himself, puts men into the pond while Antony doubts they will find much.

1872.label: Waiting in the dark
1872.recap: Bill lays out old clothes and a towel and lies awake, listening for the house to settle.

1872.label: The inquest
1872.recap: The coroner lays out the official account and the witnesses are walked carefully through their evidence.

1872.label: Over the last pipe
1872.recap: Antony finally explains to his friend how he reached his answer, and the two of them part.

1874.label: An ordinary villa
1874.recap: Three comfortable suburban children are introduced along with their perfect Father and their story-writing Mother.

1874.label: Two gentlemen call
1874.recap: Evening visitors keep Father talking far too long, and afterwards Mother comes in white-faced and sends the children straight to bed.

1874.label: Playing at being poor
1874.recap: The family packs only the useful things and leaves for a small white house in the country.

1874.label: Candles at Three Chimneys
1874.recap: Arriving late at a dark house with no supper laid, they prise open a packing case and light candles until the room looks cheerful.

1874.label: Caught at the coal heap
1874.recap: The station master waits in the dark for whoever has been helping themselves to the coal in his yard.

1874.label: Waving to the Green Dragon
1874.recap: The children begin waving every morning at a passing train, and one morning a hand waves back.

1874.label: A crowd on the platform
1874.recap: On a wet afternoon a knot of people forms around a bewildered stranger nobody can understand.

1874.label: The hillside comes down
1874.recap: A rockfall blocks the line minutes before a train is due, and the children improvise something red to wave.

1874.label: Smoke on the canal boat
1874.recap: While Peter fishes at dusk, smoke begins rising from the cabin of a moored barge with a baby asleep inside.

1874.label: Mother's workshop
1874.recap: Bobbie carries tea up to the bare writing room and Mother asks whether the younger two are forgetting their Father.

1874.label: Into the tunnel
1874.recap: A paperchase disappears into the dark tunnel mouth and the children climb the hill to watch for the runners coming out.

1874.label: Everyone is oddly kind
1874.recap: Villagers greet Bobbie with unexplained delight, and she goes down to wait on the platform for the late morning train.

1931.label: Tea and a Zeppelin
1931.recap: Over tea in a Norfolk country house, two officers and two young women compare notes on the airship that passed low in the night.

1931.label: Nora's trophy
1931.recap: A schoolgirl bursts in with a hat found near the fallen observation car and flatly refuses to hand it over.

1931.label: Lady Cranston comes home
1931.recap: Philippa returns from London with no news of her brother, a prisoner in Germany, and no comfort for her friend.

1931.label: A caller at the window
1931.recap: A mud-stained man climbs in through the French windows, locks the door behind him, and asks very politely for a hearing.

1931.label: The bargain
1931.recap: The visitor names the favour he wants in return for what he has done, and Philippa must decide whether to reach for the telephone.

1931.label: A quarrel by the fire
1931.recap: Philippa tells her comfortable, fishing-mad husband exactly what she thinks of his idleness, and makes him a hard promise.

1931.label: Home from the sea
1931.recap: Sir Henry comes back from days on the water looking anything but rested, and asks his butler to say nothing about it.

1931.label: A meeting in London
1931.recap: In a Dover Street hotel the visitor tells Philippa he has been ordered back to the little seaside town.

1931.label: Dinner in a gale
1931.recap: Three people dine gaily with danger over their heads, talking of far travels while the storm batters the windows.

1931.label: Waiting for news
1931.recap: With the house suddenly quiet, the two women argue mildly about a promise and whether it can possibly be kept.

1931.label: A car in the drive
1931.recap: With a car waiting and only hours of freedom left, Lessingham walks up to the house for his answer.

1931.label: Everyone in one room
1931.recap: The Commandant arrives with authority to make an arrest, and Sir Henry insists on finishing his conversation first.

1952.label: The ancestral hall
1952.recap: A woman describes the grand old house her husband has taken for the summer and admits she thinks something about it is queer.

1952.label: The room upstairs
1952.recap: She is settled into a barred top-floor nursery she did not choose, papered in a colour she cannot stand.

1952.label: Two weeks in
1952.recap: Writing in secret, she measures how little she can manage and how cheerfully her husband dismisses her account of it.

1952.label: Eyes in the pattern
1952.recap: She starts finding faces and expression in the wallpaper, and remembers being a child frightened by ordinary furniture.

1952.label: After the visitors
1952.recap: Company has come and gone, leaving her exhausted, tearful when alone, and oddly fonder of the room.

1952.label: Tracing the pattern
1952.recap: She spends hours trying to follow the paper's design to some kind of conclusion, and cannot.

1952.label: Something behind the paper
1952.recap: The dim shape in the sub-pattern resolves, for her, into a figure she cannot stop watching.

1952.label: Asking to leave
1952.recap: She tries once more, in the middle of the night, to persuade her husband to take her away from the house.

1952.label: The paper by moonlight
1952.recap: She notices the paper changes with the light, and that after dark the outside pattern turns into bars.

1952.label: Watching the watchers
1952.recap: She grows secretive, convinced her husband and his sister are studying the paper behind her back.

1952.label: A yellow smell
1952.recap: A week of damp weather draws an odour out of the paper that follows her through every room of the house.

1952.label: The last day
1952.recap: With the lease ending and the house nearly packed, she shuts herself in to finish with the paper once and for all.

2038.label: Ghosts of the bungalows
2038.recap: A narrator in India sets out the kinds of ghosts the country is said to keep, and the lonely roadside rest-houses where they turn up.

2038.label: The house at Taksali Gate
2038.recap: A very old man frets over daily news of his sick son while the other tenants of his house quietly calculate.

2038.label: The worm turns
2038.recap: A gentle young subaltern, teased raw by his regiment, wagers that he can pay his chief tormentor back in kind.

2038.label: The one woman
2038.recap: Watson, married and drifting from Baker Street, explains why a single woman stands apart in his friend's cold memory.

2038.label: A red-headed client
2038.recap: Holmes and Watson hear out a stout pawnbroker with flaming red hair and an unusually odd grievance.

2038.label: A stranger's hunting tale
2038.recap: A bloodless, bookish man promises a room of sportsmen a hunting story stranger than any of theirs, beginning with a Polish baron's invitation.

2038.label: The minister's small tale
2038.recap: An old French statesman begins a trifling story meant to prove how much his king really knew, starting with a horse that always cast a shoe.

2038.label: The lonely pavilion
2038.recap: A wandering misanthrope recalls the violent friend he broke with, and returns to the desolate seaside house they once shared.

2038.label: An empty inn yard
2038.recap: An English gentleman and his French wife stand stranded in a deserted yard with a lame horse and nobody to answer.

2038.label: The carriage comes back empty
2038.recap: A duke is told that his wife's carriage returned home without her, though the servants swear they saw her get in.

2038.label: A gift from a rival
2038.recap: A pipe collector opens a sandalwood box sent by his rival and finds a carving he cannot quite bring himself to like.

2038.label: Two stones on a table
2038.recap: A gem historian sets a celebrated jewel beside its double for comparison, and the lamp goes over in the dark.

2040.label: A boy and his Greek
2040.recap: Orphaned early and passed between schools and guardians, the writer becomes famous among his masters for his Greek.

2040.label: The last evening
2040.recap: On his final night at school he bows to the old head-master, certain he will never see the man again.

2040.label: The runaway trunk
2040.recap: A heavy trunk full of books has to be carried past the head-master's bedroom door, with almost catastrophic results.

2040.label: Hunger in London
2040.recap: He reaches London and endures sixteen weeks of real starvation, sleeping mostly in the open air.

2040.label: Kindness on the steps
2040.recap: Faint on a doorstep in Soho Square, he is saved by a young street companion who spends her own scant money on him.

2040.label: Night on the mail-coach
2040.recap: On the outside of a night mail he keeps falling against a stranger, whose manner changes completely once he explains himself.

2040.label: Searching the great city
2040.recap: Back in London he hunts everywhere for the friend who saved him, and finds that a single street can separate people forever.

2040.label: A rainy Sunday
2040.recap: Racked by twenty days of face pain, he is told to try opium and walks into a druggist's shop off Oxford Street.

2040.label: Opera nights
2040.recap: For years he allows himself a measured debauch of laudanum every few weeks, usually spent in the opera gallery for five shillings.

2040.label: A stranger at the door
2040.recap: A traveller in a turban appears at his mountain cottage, and the visit ends with a gift he immediately regrets giving.

2040.label: Dreams turn to water
2040.recap: The vast dream-architecture gives way to lakes, then to oceans, and finally to something far harder to bear.

2040.label: Breaking the chain
2040.recap: Facing a choice between two evils, he cuts his daily dose down step by step and describes what that cost him.

2087.label: The Darwin family
2087.recap: The editor traces the family from Lincolnshire yeomen down through Darwin's grandfather and his physician father.

2087.label: Looking back at a life
2087.recap: Darwin explains that he is writing these recollections for his children, as though he were a dead man reviewing his own life.

2087.label: Shrewsbury schooldays
2087.recap: Darwin remembers a purely classical schooling that taught him almost nothing, and a father who despaired of him aloud.

2087.label: Beetles at Cambridge
2087.recap: He describes the collecting mania that swallowed his university years, and one specimen he regretted holding in his mouth.

2087.label: A day in the household
2087.recap: Darwin's son sketches his father's appearance, manner and the shape of an ordinary day at home.

2087.label: The Beagle appointment
2087.recap: Letters and diary entries show how a friendship with a Cambridge professor led to the offer of a berth on a surveying ship.

2087.label: Five years at sea
2087.recap: The little ship is fitted out, and letters home describe the cramped cabin Darwin will live and work in.

2087.label: Back in London
2087.recap: After the voyage Darwin settles to scientific work in London while a persistent weakness of health begins to take hold.

2087.label: On belief
2087.recap: The editor gathers what his father wrote privately about religion, and explains why he kept nearly all of it out of print.

2087.label: Settling at Down
2087.recap: The family moves to a quiet Kent village that becomes the fixed centre of Darwin's working life.

2087.label: An essay from abroad
2087.recap: Letters follow the arrival of a young naturalist's essay and the joint paper and hurried book that came out of it.

2087.label: How it was received
2087.recap: Huxley closes the volume with his account of the storm that met the new theory, and of what it permanently changed.

2097.label: Baker Street, no case
2097.recap: With nothing to occupy him, the detective falls back on an old habit and his friend finally objects.

2097.label: A client with pearls
2097.recap: A young governess lays out the puzzle of her vanished father, a yearly gift she cannot explain, and a strange invitation.

2097.label: Night drive through fog
2097.recap: The three of them keep the stranger's appointment and are driven at speed across the river into unfamiliar streets.

2097.label: An oasis of art
2097.recap: A nervous, richly furnished host receives them and begins to explain why he sent for the young lady.

2097.label: Arrival at the lodge
2097.recap: The party reaches a walled house in darkness and finds the household badly frightened.

2097.label: Reading the dust
2097.recap: Holmes works over the sealed room and the space above it, drawing conclusions from marks nobody else noticed.

2097.label: Fetching a tracking dog
2097.recap: Watson sees Miss Morstan safely home, then goes to borrow a very particular dog from an old naturalist.

2097.label: The trail reaches water
2097.recap: The scent leads to a small wharf, where Holmes learns that a steam launch and its owner are missing.

2097.label: A provoking check
2097.recap: With no news of the launch, Holmes sinks into black impatience while Watson pays a call at Camberwell.

2097.label: Down the river
2097.recap: After a cheerful dinner the party boards a fast police launch and sets off along the Thames.

2097.label: The iron box
2097.recap: The prisoner speaks frankly to his captors about what the box has cost him.

2097.label: The long confession
2097.recap: Back at Baker Street the whole story is told from its beginning in India, and the business is wound up.

2130.label: A stranger in Antwerp
2130.recap: On an embassy to Flanders the narrator is introduced to a sunburnt, long-bearded traveller who has sailed to unknown countries and come back full of talk.

2130.label: Dinner with the Cardinal
2130.recap: The traveller recalls a dinner in England where a lawyer boasted about how briskly thieves were hanged, and he could not let the boast pass.

2130.label: Sheep eat the villages
2130.recap: He describes landlords enclosing fields for wool, turning farming families out with nothing to sell and nowhere to go.

2130.label: The fool and the friar
2130.recap: A household jester makes a joke about begging monks, and a thin-skinned friar takes the bait in front of the whole table.

2130.label: How councils really work
2130.recap: Asked why he will not serve a king, he imagines the schemes a royal council actually debates for squeezing money out of subjects.

2130.label: The argument about property
2130.recap: He states his central conviction plainly: while private property and money exist, no country can be governed either justly or happily.

2130.label: The island itself
2130.recap: After dinner he begins the long promised description, starting with the crescent-shaped island, its treacherous bay, and the man who cut it from the mainland.

2130.label: The city of Amaurot
2130.recap: He walks through a typical Utopian town, its streets, gardens and unlocked houses, having lived five years there himself.

2130.label: Slaves, sickness and marriage
2130.recap: He explains who becomes a bondsman among the Utopians, how the incurably ill are counselled, and the blunt customs surrounding courtship and marriage.

2130.label: How they fight
2130.recap: The Utopians claim to loathe war, yet drill constantly and prefer to win by bribes, assassins and hired foreign troops rather than their own blood.

2130.label: What they believe
2130.recap: Many faiths coexist on the island under a law of tolerance, and he describes their priests, their temples and their calm view of death.

2130.label: After the telling
2130.recap: The traveller finishes, and his host, privately unconvinced on several points but unwilling to argue with a tired man, takes him in to supper.

2147.label: A balloon over Rotterdam
2147.recap: A ludicrous patchwork balloon descends on a Dutch square and the pipe-smoking crowd below cannot make sense of it.

2147.label: A book at a bookstall
2147.recap: Hounded by creditors, a ruined bellows-mender stumbles on a treatise of astronomy and begins to form a plan.

2147.label: The recluse of Sullivan's Island
2147.recap: A narrator visits his solitary friend, who has caught a heavy gold-coloured beetle he insists is unknown to science.

2147.label: Digging by the tulip-tree
2147.recap: Following instructions that seem like lunacy, the party measures out a spot in the woods and sets to work with spades.

2147.label: A guided tour of Antioch
2147.recap: The reader is invited to stand in ancient Antioch and watch a crowd assemble for the arrival of its monstrous king.

2147.label: On the analytical mind
2147.recap: An essay on the pleasure of disentangling problems introduces a poor Parisian with unsettling powers of observation.

2147.label: News from the Rue Morgue
2147.recap: A newspaper account of two deaths in a locked fourth-floor room sends the pair hunting through every printed report.

2147.label: Coincidence and calculation
2147.recap: The same reasoner is drawn back to work by a young woman's disappearance, argued out from newspapers alone.

2147.label: The Atlantic crossed by air
2147.recap: A breathless dispatch announces that a steering balloon has crossed the ocean in seventy-five hours, with diaries offered as proof.

2147.label: A passenger out of Batavia
2147.recap: A determinedly unimaginative traveller sails from Java and notices a strange isolated cloud and an unnatural sea.

2147.label: A room in the Apennines
2147.recap: Wounded and feverish, a traveller shelters in an abandoned château hung with paintings and settles in to study them by candlelight.

2148.label: A visit in the dark
2148.recap: A police prefect calls on a reclusive Paris analyst about a stolen document he cannot find anywhere.

2148.label: The tale after the tales
2148.recap: A narrator claims an obscure manuscript corrects the familiar ending of the Arabian Nights, and begins retelling it.

2148.label: On the Norwegian cliff
2148.recap: On a cliff top above a strange stretch of ocean, an old guide offers to explain what once happened to him out there.

2148.label: An experiment proposed
2148.recap: A student of mesmerism decides to test whether a dying friend can be put under at the very edge of death.

2148.label: A household of pets
2148.recap: A condemned man sets down the household story of how a gentle, animal loving nature curdled under drink.

2148.label: Arrival at the house
2148.recap: A traveller answers a boyhood friend's desperate letter and arrives at a decaying mansion beside a black tarn.

2148.label: The sealed abbey
2148.recap: A prince shuts himself and a thousand courtiers inside a walled abbey while a plague empties the country outside.

2148.label: Carnival and a cask
2148.recap: A man nursing a private grievance meets his wine loving friend during carnival and mentions a cask he wants judged.

2148.label: The sentence and the dark
2148.recap: A prisoner hears his sentence pronounced, faints under the judges' white lips, and wakes in total blackness.

2148.label: A borrowed name
2148.recap: A man writing under a false name traces his ruin back to his schooldays and a boy who shared his name.

2148.label: Seven patient nights
2148.recap: A narrator insists on his sanity while explaining how an old man's pale eye came to occupy him night after night.

2148.label: The sealed valley
2148.recap: A dreamer recalls the hidden valley where he grew up with his cousin, and the summer their feeling for each other changed.

2160.label: The Hot Well
2160.recap: Gout-ridden and irritable, Matthew Bramble takes the waters at the Hot Well near Bristol.

2160.label: Bath
2160.recap: At Bath the family plunges into the whirl of the spa, to Bramble's disgust and the young people's delight.

2160.label: Humphry Clinker
2160.recap: A ragged postilion named Humphry Clinker is taken on as a servant, to Tabitha's mingled scandal and pity.

2160.label: Scarborough
2160.recap: At Scarborough, Bramble's sea-bathing turns to farce when Clinker, thinking him drowning, hauls him from the surf.

2160.label: Edinburgh
2160.recap: The party reaches Edinburgh and samples the bustle and learning of the Scottish capital.

2160.label: An Old Friend
2160.recap: On the journey home an old friend's recognition unravels the secret of Humphry's true parentage.

2199.label: A priest turned away
2199.recap: An old priest brings a great ransom to the Greek camp to buy back his captive daughter and is sent off with threats.

2199.label: The quarrel in council
2199.recap: Achilles comes close to drawing his sword on the commander who means to take his prize, and swears the army will miss him.

2199.label: A champion steps out
2199.recap: Paris swaggers out between the armies, flinches at the sight of the man he wronged, and is savaged by his own brother.

2199.label: One man's great day
2199.recap: A goddess sets fire glinting on Diomed's shield and sends him tearing through the Trojan line.

2199.label: Farewell at the gates
2199.recap: Hector finds his wife and baby son at the Scaean gates, and they argue about whether he must go back out to fight.

2199.label: A council in despair
2199.recap: With the Trojan watchfires burning near the ships, the Greek leaders meet in the dark and quarrel about sailing home.

2199.label: The wall and the ditch
2199.recap: The fighting closes on the trench and rampart the Greeks threw up around their ships without asking the gods' blessing.

2199.label: A friend's request
2199.recap: Patroclus comes to Achilles in tears and begs to be sent out wearing his armour, since Achilles will not go himself.

2199.label: News from the field
2199.recap: A runner brings word from the battle, and Achilles' cry of grief carries down to his mother and her sisters in the sea.

2199.label: New armour at dawn
2199.recap: Thetis lays god-forged armour before her son, and Achilles at last makes his peace with Agamemnon.

2199.label: Before the Scaean gates
2199.recap: The Trojans crowd behind their walls while one man refuses to come in, and his father cries out to him from the tower.

2199.label: A sleepless night
2199.recap: Achilles, unable to sleep for grief, drags Hector's body at dawn until the gods look down and decide they have seen enough.

2350.label: A grotesque telegram
2350.recap: On a bleak March day a telegram arrives at Baker Street and Holmes sets Watson arguing over the meaning of the word grotesque.

2350.label: The face at the window
2350.recap: Holmes, Watson and a country inspector reach a dark, isolated house where the constable left on duty has been badly frightened.

2350.label: Fog over Baker Street
2350.recap: Four days of yellow fog have left Holmes pacing and bored, until a telegram announces that his brother Mycroft is on his way.

2350.label: A quiet burglary
2350.recap: Holmes and Watson let themselves into the empty house of an absent man to look for papers the police could not lawfully seek.

2350.label: Rest cure in Cornwall
2350.recap: Ordered to rest, Holmes takes a cottage above a bleak Cornish bay and occupies himself with the ancient Cornish language.

2350.label: The lodger nobody sees
2350.recap: A landlady talks Holmes into looking at her new tenant, who pays generously and has not once been seen since the first night.

2350.label: Signals across the street
2350.recap: An interrupted signal sends Holmes and Watson across the road, where they run into a Scotland Yard man on the same errand.

2350.label: A lady goes missing
2350.recap: Holmes explains why a drifting, friendless woman is such an easy victim, and proposes that Watson go to Lausanne on her trail.

2350.label: News from Brixton
2350.recap: An agitated helper bursts in with an account of trailing a woman from an office to an undertaker's shop and on to a dark house.

2350.label: A landlady's alarm
2350.recap: Mrs Hudson fetches Watson in a panic, saying her lodger has taken to his bed and swallowed nothing for three days.

2350.label: Two Germans on a cliff
2350.recap: On a sultry August night two agents stand above the Channel and congratulate each other on four undisturbed years in England.

2350.label: A last quiet talk
2350.recap: With the night's work finished, two old friends pause on the terrace before the drive up to London.

2360.label: London in September
2360.recap: A fastidious young Foreign Office clerk, marooned in an empty city, opens a letter with a German postmark.

2360.label: Shopping for a voyage
2360.recap: He talks himself into going and spends a day buying nautical odds and ends he does not understand.

2360.label: Arrival at Flensburg
2360.recap: He meets his host on a dark platform and starts to suspect this holiday will not be what he pictured.

2360.label: Below decks
2360.recap: The yacht proves small, rough and crewless, and the newcomer takes gloomy stock of his quarters.

2360.label: Charts and cigars
2360.recap: Over cigars his host describes the cruise so far, but goes oddly vague about its final stage.

2360.label: A visitor in the fog
2360.recap: A kindly Dutch skipper appears out of the fog, and his affectionate hints force a confession.

2360.label: Making up his mind
2360.recap: Carruthers weighs what he has been told and settles the question of whether he stays aboard.

2360.label: First night in the islands
2360.recap: Left alone on the grounded yacht after dark, he hears a splashing footstep outside.

2360.label: The naval commander
2360.recap: A German naval officer invites them to talk at the village inn, and they hastily change their plan.

2360.label: Watching the packet
2360.recap: From behind the cabin windows they study the passengers coming ashore on the morning steamer.

2360.label: A night on foot
2360.recap: Carruthers shadows three men from a country station and cuts ahead of them towards the harbour.

2360.label: Back to the boat
2360.recap: He rows hard through wind and tide to reach the yacht with news that will not keep.

2376.label: A slave among slaves
2376.recap: He describes the cabin he was born in, the dirt floor, the flax shirt, and a childhood with no time in it for play.

2376.label: The day of freedom
2376.recap: Everyone on the plantation is called to the big house, a paper is read aloud, and the rejoicing gives way within hours to something heavier.

2376.label: The salt furnace
2376.recap: The family walks several hundred miles to a crowded West Virginia town, where the boy is put to work packing salt before dawn.

2376.label: An old blue-back speller
2376.recap: He teaches himself the alphabet from a battered spelling book, with no teacher anywhere near and his mother's whole encouragement behind him.

2376.label: Overheard in the mine
2376.recap: Two miners talk about a school where poor students can work their way through, and he decides on the spot where he is going.

2376.label: Setting out
2376.recap: With a cheap satchel, a half-hearted blessing and coins from old neighbours, he leaves home for a school five hundred miles away.

2376.label: A coat to sell
2376.recap: Stranded at school over the vacation with nowhere to go, he tries to sell his one spare coat and learns what the buyer means by paying.

2376.label: A telegram from Alabama
2376.recap: Gentlemen in a small Alabama town ask for a principal, expecting a white man, and a telegram arrives with four words that decide his life.

2376.label: Opening day
2376.recap: The school opens in a shanty and a church, watched hopefully by some neighbours and doubtfully by others.

2376.label: Making bricks
2376.recap: Determined that the students build their own buildings, he takes on brickmaking and finds out how many kilns can fail.

2376.label: Atlanta, on the platform
2376.recap: Facing thousands of upturned faces at a Southern exposition, he delivers the speech about casting down your bucket where you are.

2376.label: Back in Richmond
2376.recap: He finishes the book in the city where he once slept under a sidewalk, this time as the guest of its people.

2383.label: Company at the Tabard
2383.recap: In April a chance-gathered company of pilgrims falls into fellowship at a Southwark inn, and the narrator sets out to describe them all.

2383.label: The first tale drawn
2383.recap: The lot falls to the Knight, who begins with a conquering duke of Athens riding home in triumph.

2383.label: An Oxford household
2383.recap: The Miller answers with a story about a jealous carpenter, his very young wife and the clever scholar who lodges with them.

2383.label: Five husbands and counting
2383.recap: The Wife of Bath opens a long, wholly unabashed defence of marriage built on her own experience rather than on books.

2383.label: A promise in Brittany
2383.recap: A knight in Brittany wins his lady and swears he will never claim mastery over her.

2383.label: The Pardoner's confession
2383.recap: Before telling his tale, the Pardoner cheerfully explains to the company exactly how he works a congregation with relics and one text.

2383.label: Three drinkers and a bell
2383.recap: Three young revellers drinking before daybreak hear that a thief called Death has been carrying off people in the district.

2383.label: A widow's farmyard
2383.recap: A poor widow's small holding sets the scene for a beast fable about a splendid cock and his seven hens.

2383.label: The last pilgrim speaks
2383.recap: The Parson closes the ride not with a story but with a plain prose treatise on penitence.

2383.label: A prince of Troy
2383.recap: A separate long poem begins the history of a Trojan king's son and the sorrow that his loving brought him.

2383.label: A poet and his purse
2383.recap: A short late lyric addresses the poet's empty purse as though it were a cruel mistress.

2383.label: A closing prayer
2383.recap: The volume ends with a brief warning verse and a few lines of prayer.

2397.label: Lifting the veil
2397.recap: The narrator hesitates at the start of her own story, then begins with her birth in a small Alabama town.

2397.label: The fever
2397.recap: An illness at nineteen months leaves the baby alive but without sight or hearing.

2397.label: A journey for help
2397.recap: Her father takes her north to a famous eye doctor, who can do nothing but points the family toward a teacher.

2397.label: The teacher arrives
2397.recap: A young woman comes from Boston, and the child waiting on the porch feels a hand take hers.

2397.label: Caught in a tree
2397.recap: Left alone in the branches of a wild cherry tree, she feels a thunderstorm gather around her.

2397.label: First sight of the sea
2397.recap: A summer on Cape Cod gives her the ocean she had only read about in a book.

2397.label: Finding a voice
2397.recap: She hears of another deaf girl who learned to speak aloud, and asks to be taught the same.

2397.label: A story called into question
2397.recap: A little story she wrote and gave away turns out to resemble one that was read to her years before.

2397.label: Preparing for college
2397.recap: She enters a Cambridge school with her teacher beside her, spelling every lesson into her hand.

2397.label: First day at Radcliffe
2397.recap: College at last begins, and proves less of a romantic lyceum than she had imagined.

2397.label: The friends
2397.recap: She closes her own account with the writers and friends whose handshakes she remembers best.

2397.label: Dreamland
2397.recap: A later chapter turns to what she sees and hears when she is asleep.

2465.label: The Stranger
2465.recap: While roaming the Andalusian wilds in search of an ancient battlefield, the narrator befriends a hunted, dangerous stranger.

2465.label: Carmen
2465.recap: In Cordova the narrator meets a bewitching gypsy named Carmen, who reads his fortune.

2465.label: Don José's Tale
2465.recap: Condemned to die, the soldier Don José tells how his consuming love for Carmen led him to ruin.

2465.label: On the Roma
2465.recap: A closing essay reflects on the language and customs of the Romany people.

2489.label: Driving off the spleen
2489.recap: A man with empty pockets and a grim mood explains why, whenever life closes in, he goes to sea.

2489.label: The Spouter-Inn
2489.recap: He takes a bed at a smoky waterfront inn hung with a baffling painting and a wall of monstrous whaling gear.

2489.label: Down to the packet
2489.recap: He and his tattooed new friend wheel their gear to the Nantucket schooner, trading stories and drawing stares.

2489.label: A stranger on the wharf
2489.recap: A scarred, ragged man stops them in the street and asks unsettling questions about the ship they have just signed with.

2489.label: The captain appears
2489.recap: For days the ship runs under the mates alone, until one grey morning the captain is standing on his own quarter-deck.

2489.label: On the quarter-deck
2489.recap: The captain calls every hand aft and puts a run of simple questions to the crew that builds toward something else.

2489.label: The first lowering
2489.recap: At the first cry of whales the boats drop, and a fourth crew nobody knew was aboard pulls out from the ship's lee.

2489.label: A whale in a calm
2489.recap: Dozing at the masthead in a dead calm, he wakes to find a huge sperm whale rolling close under the lee.

2489.label: Through the straits
2489.recap: The ship makes for the narrows between Sumatra and Java, waters known for pirates and for whales alike.

2489.label: The ship-keeper's turn
2489.recap: A small, tender-hearted crewman who normally stays aboard is put into a boat's crew when another man is injured.

2489.label: Typhoon
2489.recap: Stripped of canvas, the ship rides out a Japanese-sea typhoon while the mates argue about courage in the dark.

2489.label: A scent on the wind
2489.recap: The captain smells whale on the night air, alters course, and at daybreak the mastheads are manned and every sail set.

2489.label: A fair third morning
2489.recap: A clear, lovely dawn finds the lookouts crowding the spars and the captain talking to himself about wind and thought.

2527.label: Glad to be gone
2527.recap: Werther writes to his friend Wilhelm from a village he has just moved to, relieved to be away from everything behind him.

2527.label: Grass and small insects
2527.recap: Lying by a stream in spring, he tries and fails to describe a happiness he can neither paint nor write down.

2527.label: Bread for the children
2527.recap: Sent to collect a young woman for a country ball, he finds her in a white dress cutting bread for a houseful of children.

2527.label: The waltz and the storm
2527.recap: The dancing begins, a name is dropped in passing, and a thunderstorm sends the whole party into another room.

2527.label: Borrowed pistols
2527.recap: Asking to borrow pistols for a journey turns into a long argument with Albert about what people may be forgiven for doing.

2527.label: A post in town
2527.recap: Werther takes a position with a fussy ambassador in a strange town and tries to talk himself into contentment.

2527.label: An evening at the count's
2527.recap: Dining with a friendly count, he stays past the hour when people of his rank are expected to have gone.

2527.label: Autumn in the valley
2527.recap: Back among familiar fields as the leaves turn, he meets a peasant lad he once wrote about and hears what became of him.

2527.label: Flowers out of season
2527.recap: Walking by the river in bad weather, he falls into conversation with a man searching the rocks for flowers in November.

2527.label: The editor steps in
2527.recap: The letters break off and an editor takes over, assembling the remaining account from people who knew all three of them.

2527.label: Written through the night
2527.recap: A letter written by candlelight sets out what he wants kept, what returned, and where he would like to lie.

2527.label: Six in the morning
2527.recap: A servant comes in with a candle at first light and the whole house is roused.

2542.label: Act I: Christmas Eve
2542.recap: On Christmas Eve, Nora Helmer hides the secret debt she once took on to save her husband's life.

2542.label: Act II: The Tarantella
2542.recap: As blackmail closes in, Nora desperately tries to keep her husband away from the letterbox.

2542.label: Act III: The Reckoning
2542.recap: The truth comes out at last, forcing Nora to confront what her marriage has really been.

2554.label: The Plan
2554.recap: In stifling Petersburg the destitute ex-student Raskolnikov nurses a monstrous idea and slips out to rehearse it at a pawnbroker's.

2554.label: The Family's Burden
2554.recap: A letter reveals his sister Dounia means to marry a smug benefactor to save the family, sharpening Raskolnikov's torment.

2554.label: The Murder
2554.recap: Raskolnikov kills the old pawnbroker with an axe, and then her meek sister Lizaveta, who walks in on him.

2554.label: Fever and Dread
2554.recap: Wracked by fever, Raskolnikov hides the stolen goods and lurches between terror and reckless self-betrayal.

2554.label: Marmeladov's Death
2554.recap: He sees the drunkard Marmeladov crushed by a carriage and helps the grieving family, meeting the gentle Sonia.

2554.label: First Duel with Porfiry
2554.recap: Raskolnikov fences warily with the sly investigator Porfiry, who seems to read his every nerve.

2554.label: Sonia and Lazarus
2554.recap: Drawn to Sonia's faith and suffering, Raskolnikov has her read aloud the raising of Lazarus.

2554.label: The Second Duel
2554.recap: A second, crueler interview tightens Porfiry's psychological net around Raskolnikov.

2554.label: Confession to Sonia
2554.recap: Unable to bear it alone, Raskolnikov confesses the murders to Sonia, who begs him to give himself up.

2554.label: Porfiry's Visit
2554.recap: Porfiry comes to Raskolnikov, quietly reveals he knows the truth, and urges him to confess for his own soul.

2554.label: Svidrigailov's End
2554.recap: The corrupt Svidrigailov, his last schemes collapsed, drifts through a grim final night to its end.

2554.label: Giving Himself Up
2554.recap: Taking Sonia's cross, Raskolnikov walks to the police and confesses to the murders.

2554.label: Siberia
2554.recap: In a Siberian prison camp, with Sonia faithfully beside him, Raskolnikov begins at last to find his way toward renewal.

2600.label: Anna Pávlovna's Soirée
2600.recap: At a glittering Petersburg soirée in 1805, society chatters about Napoleon as we meet the awkward, illegitimate Pierre.

2600.label: First Taste of War
2600.recap: In Austria the army marches, and young Nicholas Rostóv meets the chaos and thrill of his first battle.

2600.label: The Sky of Austerlitz
2600.recap: Fallen wounded at Austerlitz, Prince Andrew gazes up at the vast sky and sees how small his dreams of glory were.

2600.label: Home in Moscow
2600.recap: Nicholas comes home on leave to the warm, chaotic, loving Rostóv household in Moscow.

2600.label: A Search for Meaning
2600.recap: His marriage to Hélène in ruins, the restless Pierre seeks a purpose and is drawn into Freemasonry.

2600.label: Andrew Reawakened
2600.recap: A glimpse of the joyful young Natásha rouses Prince Andrew from his grief and back toward life.

2600.label: Natásha's First Ball
2600.recap: At her first grand ball Natásha is wretched with nerves until Prince Andrew chooses her to dance.

2600.label: Temptation
2600.recap: With Andrew away, the trusting Natásha is dazzled and nearly destroyed by the heartless Anatole.

2600.label: The Comet
2600.recap: Full of tender new feeling for Natásha, Pierre looks up into the night at the great comet of 1812.

2600.label: The Invasion
2600.recap: Napoleon's vast army crosses into Russia, and the whole country is swept toward war.

2600.label: Borodinó
2600.recap: On the great day of Borodinó, Pierre wanders out as a curious onlooker and finds himself caught in the thick of the slaughter at the Raévski redoubt.

2600.label: Moscow Abandoned
2600.recap: The people flee, and Moscow is left empty and silent to the advancing French.

2600.label: A Prisoner
2600.recap: A captive of the French, Pierre finds unexpected peace in the simple faith of the peasant Platón Karatáev.

2600.label: Seven Years On
2600.recap: Years later the survivors have built quieter lives, deeply changed by all they lived through.

2610.label: The sixth of January, 1482
2610.recap: All Paris wakes to bells and pours toward a bonfire, a maypole and a mystery play on the doubled feast of Epiphany and Fools.

2610.label: The grinning contest
2610.recap: The great hall abandons the play for a competition to pull the ugliest face through a broken rose window, and finally settles on a winner.

2610.label: Lost in the dark streets
2610.recap: Penniless and soaked, the poet blunders through the night city hunting a bed, then follows a reddish glow down a long muddy lane.

2610.label: Supper with a stranger
2610.recap: He finds himself warm, fed and alone with the young dancer and her goat, studying her as if she might dissolve at a blink.

2610.label: The scholar in the cloister
2610.recap: The archdeacon's boyhood is traced through theology, canon law, medicine and languages, up to the plague summer that interrupts him.

2610.label: The cell in the wall
2610.recap: A doorless cell hollowed into a house on the Place de Grève is described, left for centuries to grieving women who wish to bury themselves alive.

2610.label: An hour on the pillory
2610.recap: A prisoner is flogged and then left turning slowly on the wheel while the crowd jeers and throws things, until one person climbs the ladder to him.

2610.label: A month with no word
2610.recap: With the dancer missing for a month, the poet drifts past the criminal courts and hears that a woman is on trial for sorcery.

2610.label: Beneath the courthouse
2610.recap: Far under the Palais de Justice a prisoner lies chained on straw in a pool of seeping water, with a jug and a loaf beside her.

2610.label: Watch from the north tower
2610.recap: Keeping guard over the locked church at night, the bellringer sees the line of a distant quay begin to ripple like a crowd on the move.

2610.label: The church besieged
2610.recap: Woken by torches and shouting in the square below, she prays in terror in her cell until two men step in carrying a lantern.

2610.label: What the vault held
2610.recap: Years afterwards, searchers in a charnel cellar beneath an old gibbet turn up two skeletons locked in an embrace that crumbles when touched.

2638.label: A train into Petersburg
2638.recap: Two poorly dressed young men fall into conversation in a third-class carriage as the train nears the city.

2638.label: The general's household
2638.recap: The narrator lays out a wealthy general's comfortable life, his formidable wife and his three grown daughters.

2638.label: Lunch with the daughters
2638.recap: The newcomer is received by the women of the house and pressed to tell them stories about his years abroad.

2638.label: A parlour game
2638.recap: At an evening party the guests take turns confessing the worst thing they have ever done.

2638.label: An unexpected letter
2638.recap: A lawyer's letter is read aloud and changes the whole footing of the evening.

2638.label: The picture over the door
2638.recap: Walking through a gloomy merchant's house, two men stop before a harsh painting and fall to talking about belief.

2638.label: An unwelcome deputation
2638.recap: A group of angry young men arrive at the prince's villa to press a claim on him in front of his friends.

2638.label: A birthday on the verandah
2638.recap: He comes home to find his verandah full of guests and champagne on the night of his own forgotten birthday.

2638.label: Back from the park
2638.recap: A shaken mother brings the prince home at breakfast time and tries to work out what she has just witnessed.

2638.label: Rumours of a match
2638.recap: Half-formed gossip about an engagement hardens into conviction across two households.

2638.label: Ringing a closed door
2638.recap: The prince searches the city for a friend who is not answering, questioning servants and the porter.

2638.label: What was afterwards known
2638.recap: The narrator closes by reporting what became of the household and the people around it.

2641.label: The Bertolini
2641.recap: In a Florence pension Lucy and her fretful chaperon Charlotte are unhappy with their rooms, until the blunt Mr Emerson and his son offer to swap.

2641.label: In Santa Croce
2641.recap: Exploring a church without her guidebook, Lucy falls in with the kindly, unconventional Mr Emerson and his quiet son George.

2641.label: A Death in the Piazza
2641.recap: A sudden killing in the square sends Lucy fainting into George's arms, an encounter that quietly unsettles her.

2641.label: Among the Violets
2641.recap: On a country drive Lucy comes upon George on a hillside of violets, and he kisses her before Charlotte sweeps her away.

2641.label: They Return
2641.recap: Charlotte hurries Lucy out of Florence, and the two women bury the kiss in careful silence.

2641.label: Back at Windy Corner
2641.recap: Home in England, Lucy accepts a proposal from the polished, controlling Cecil Vyse.

2641.label: Cecil's Scheme
2641.recap: Amused by his country neighbours, Cecil mischievously arranges for two strangers to take a nearby villa.

2641.label: The Sacred Lake
2641.recap: George, it turns out, is the new neighbour; he joins Freddy and Mr Beebe for a wild, laughing bathe in the woodland pond.

2641.label: The Disaster Within
2641.recap: George kisses Lucy once more and declares his love; flustered, she orders him away as her engagement starts to feel wrong.

2641.label: Lying to George
2641.recap: Lucy sends George off for good, refusing to admit, even to herself, what she truly feels.

2641.label: Lying to Cecil
2641.recap: Seeing Cecil clearly at last, Lucy breaks off the engagement.

2641.label: Lying to Mr. Emerson
2641.recap: About to flee abroad to escape the muddle, Lucy meets old Mr Emerson, who gently makes her face the truth of her heart.

2641.label: A Room with a View
2641.recap: Lucy and George return to the Florence pension as newlyweds, the long muddle finally undone.

2701.label: Loomings
2701.recap: Restless and gloomy on land, Ishmael decides the cure is to go to sea, this time on a whaling voyage.

2701.label: The Spouter-Inn
2701.recap: At a crowded New Bedford inn Ishmael must share a bed with a fearsome, tattooed harpooneer, Queequeg.

2701.label: Bosom Friends
2701.recap: Ishmael and the noble cannibal Queequeg become fast friends and resolve to ship out together.

2701.label: The Pequod
2701.recap: In Nantucket the two sign aboard the Pequod, a weathered whaler whose captain, Ahab, stays strangely unseen.

2701.label: The Prophet
2701.recap: A ragged stranger, Elijah, darkly hints at the doom awaiting any crew that sails under Captain Ahab.

2701.label: Ahab
2701.recap: Days out to sea, Ahab at last appears on deck: grim, scarred, standing on a leg of carved whale ivory.

2701.label: The Quarter-Deck
2701.recap: Ahab nails a gold doubloon to the mast and binds the crew by oath to hunt one creature: the white whale, Moby Dick.

2701.label: The Whiteness of the Whale
2701.recap: Ishmael tells the legend of Moby Dick, the vast white whale that took Ahab's leg and now owns his soul.

2701.label: The First Lowering
2701.recap: At the first hunt Ahab unveils his own hidden boat-crew, and a squall nearly drowns Ishmael's whaleboat.

2701.label: The Castaway
2701.recap: The little cabin-boy Pip is left adrift in the sea; rescued at last, he is never the same, his wits set loose.

2701.label: The Try-Works
2701.recap: Rendering blubber by firelight at night, Ishmael is nearly hypnotized into steering the ship to ruin.

2701.label: Queequeg's Coffin
2701.recap: Gravely ill, Queequeg has a coffin built, then recovers; the box is later sealed into a spare life-buoy.

2701.label: The Chase, First Day
2701.recap: Moby Dick is sighted at last, and on the first day of the chase the white whale shatters Ahab's boat.

2701.label: The Chase, Second Day
2701.recap: The hunt rages on; the whale wrecks more boats and Ahab's shadowy harpooneer Fedallah is dragged under.

2701.label: The Chase, Third Day
2701.recap: On the third day Moby Dick staves in the Pequod itself; the ship goes down with all hands, Ahab among them.

2760.label: A deathbed at Careggi
2760.recap: Three famous scholars keep watch over the dying Lorenzo the Magnificent, who has sent for a severe friar to absolve him.

2760.label: A Roman gravestone
2760.recap: From a plain slab in a Roman church the narrator turns to Beatrice Cenci's father and the violent papal Rome that produced him.

2760.label: Two centuries at Nimes
2760.recap: The scene moves to the south of France, where the narrator traces religious hatred around Nimes back through generations of reprisals.

2760.label: An unlucky name
2760.recap: A roll-call of Stuart misfortunes opens the long and much-disputed story of Mary Queen of Scots.

2760.label: A student on the road
2760.recap: A young German student stops on a rise above Mannheim, notes the hour in his pocket-book, and walks on towards the town.

2760.label: A priest comes home
2760.recap: A small French town splits into rival camps over the announced return of a handsome and much-argued-about churchman.

2760.label: Schoolboys in the wood
2760.recap: Boys let out early from a religious school scatter into a wood to play, and one of them is caught trying to slip away.

2760.label: Bells over Naples
2760.recap: Church bells wake Naples at midnight, announcing that the old king is dying and that a very young queen must follow him.

2760.label: The nameless prisoner
2760.recap: The author lays out the riddle of a masked captive whose identity no historian has ever settled.

2760.label: An empire coming apart
2760.recap: The Ottoman provinces are shown falling to bold adventurers, among them the pasha whose history is about to be told.

2760.label: A visit by night
2760.recap: Two veiled women slip from an unmarked carriage into a Paris house whose sign advertises a midwife.

2760.label: What the town said after
2760.recap: The last of the histories closes with the gossip, the pay-offs and the quiet settlements that followed the scandal.

2806.label: How the papers came to me
2806.recap: A narrator explains how everyone in India knows everyone, and how a dying man's manuscript reached his hands.

2806.label: A shipboard attachment
2806.recap: The writer sets down without excuses how an affair began on a voyage out and how quickly it soured.

2806.label: Simla in April
2806.recap: A season of complete happiness in the hills, an engagement, and an ordinary errand to a jeweller's shop.

2806.label: A night in a rest-house
2806.recap: After years of sleeping in roadside bungalows, the narrator arrives at the one where he heard something.

2806.label: A feverish midnight gallop
2806.recap: Sick with fever and maddened by barking dogs, an engineer takes horse and hog-spear out into the moonlight.

2806.label: The crater described
2806.recap: He carefully measures the sand crater he has fallen into and counts the holes bored around its base.

2806.label: A message to carry
2806.recap: In a cheap carriage a stranger asks a fellow traveller to pass six words to a red-bearded man at a junction.

2806.label: Farewell at the caravanserai
2806.recap: Among camels and traders he goes down to see whether two acquaintances really mean to keep their word.

2806.label: Someone comes back
2806.recap: Two summers later, on another stifling night issue, a wrecked man crawls into the office begging for a drink.

2806.label: A bank clerk with ambitions
2806.recap: A young London clerk with literary hopes attaches himself to an older writer and reads him his poems.

2806.label: Details of a ship
2806.recap: Charlie describes with impossible confidence the food, the oars and the scratchings aboard a galley.

2806.label: A photograph on the paper
2806.recap: Charlie arrives glowing with news of a girl, and the older man's quiet plans rearrange themselves.

2813.label: A drink out of order
2813.recap: A guest orders an American cocktail in a hotel that does not serve them, and the head waiter takes offence.

2813.label: Dinner with a stranger
2813.recap: A young man attached to a German prince charms the table while the new owner quietly watches him.

2813.label: Small things that will not fit
2813.recap: A wink, a ribbon on a door-handle and a broken window keep the millionaire awake and rather pleased.

2813.label: A prince at the bureau
2813.recap: Royalty arrives leaning through the bureau window, and asks after an equerry who never met his train.

2813.label: The Gold Room ball
2813.recap: A thousand guests dance below a hidden little barred window from which the hotel keeps watch.

2813.label: A very particular guest
2813.recap: A plump old baroness asks for third-floor rooms and knows their numbers slightly too well.

2813.label: Waking on the water
2813.recap: Nella comes round to the roll of a deck and the beat of a screw, on a yacht she does not recognise.

2813.label: The room above the suite
2813.recap: Racksole finally works out why one particular bedroom mattered so much to somebody.

2813.label: A council in Ostend
2813.recap: Over dinner abroad, three people argue about whether to hand the whole affair to the police.

2813.label: Searching the launch
2813.recap: A customs officer boards a steam launch on the river on a pretext, and reports what he could and could not find.

2813.label: Two doctors confer
2813.recap: In the hotel's grandest bedroom, two physicians talk quietly about a patient who does not want to recover.

2813.label: A walk on the terrace
2813.recap: After dinner two men stroll the terrace and reopen an old piece of business about the hotel itself.

2825.label: The cottage on the tongue of land
2825.recap: A young knight rides out of a feared forest and asks shelter at an old fisherman's cottage by the lake.

2825.label: The wayward girl
2825.recap: The fisherman's adopted daughter bursts in, demands the knight's story, and runs out into the night when she is refused.

2825.label: How she came to them
2825.recap: The old man tells how he lost his own child and how a strange little girl appeared dripping at his door that same evening.

2825.label: Search in the flood
2825.recap: Huldbrand braves the swollen stream in the dark and finds the missing girl on a little island cut off by the water.

2825.label: Days on the island
2825.recap: Cut off by the flood, the knight settles happily into the little household and begins to think of himself as betrothed.

2825.label: After the wedding
2825.recap: Her wild spirits return the morning after the marriage, and a gentle rebuke from the priest draws a strange confession from her.

2825.label: Riding through the wood
2825.recap: The married pair and the priest set out through the haunted forest toward the knight's castle.

2825.label: A song at the feast
2825.recap: At a grand dinner Undine sings two ballads and then reveals what she has learned about a guest's parentage.

2825.label: Sealing the fountain
2825.recap: Undine has the castle's fountain covered with a great stone and will not fully explain her reasons.

2825.label: Down the Danube
2825.recap: A river voyage begins in high spirits but soon attracts unwelcome attention from the water itself.

2825.label: A dream of the sea
2825.recap: Half asleep, Huldbrand seems to be carried over the sea and to overhear a conversation far below the waves.

2825.label: The last procession
2825.recap: A funeral winds toward the churchyard, followed by a veiled figure that no one can turn away.

2833.label: Tea on the lawn
2833.recap: Three men take afternoon tea on the lawn of an old house above the Thames and talk idly about marriage and boredom.

2833.label: A cousin arrives
2833.recap: A young woman appears in the doorway, takes possession of the terrier, and announces that she is probably a relative.

2833.label: How she was found
2833.recap: The aunt's exacting habits are explained, along with the wet Albany afternoon on which she turned up and collected her niece.

2833.label: Ralph's history
2833.recap: The invalid son's upbringing, his shortened career and his deep fondness for his father are set out at leisure.

2833.label: A proposal on the grass
2833.recap: A rich neighbour walks her across the lawn and asks a question he has spent days thinking over.

2833.label: A caller in London
2833.recap: Alone in a hotel sitting room, she receives an unannounced visitor from home who has come for an answer.

2833.label: A remarkable new friend
2833.recap: Kept together in the house during an illness, she and an accomplished older woman fall into confidences.

2833.label: A house being emptied
2833.recap: A visitor calls at a London house that is being stripped and sold, and privately takes stock of who has gained by it.

2833.label: Free as a bird
2833.recap: Her aunt spells out exactly how much liberty she now has, and she decides all the same to go on travelling with her.

2833.label: The villa above Florence
2833.recap: In a shuttered hilltop villa outside Florence a collector entertains two nuns who have brought his young daughter home.

2833.label: A visit to the hilltop
2833.recap: She is driven up to the villa and meets a small girl fresh from her convent and a sister with a great deal of manner.

2833.label: Rome, and old faces
2833.recap: Wandering the Forum and Saint Peter's, she finds her friends and admirers converging on her at once, to her cousin's discomfort.

2848.label: The first six days
2848.recap: The historian opens by retelling the making of the world, the naming of day and night, and the forming of the first man and woman.

2848.label: A favoured son's dreams
2848.recap: Jacob's fortunes stand at their height when his best-loved son begins describing dreams that his brothers hear with growing resentment.

2848.label: Bitter water at Marah
2848.recap: Freed from Egypt, the crowd finds the desert waterless and the one well undrinkable, and Moses must answer their despair.

2848.label: Spies inside Jericho
2848.recap: Joshua takes command and sends scouts into a walled city, where an innkeeper hides them from the king's men.

2848.label: The captured ark
2848.recap: The Philistines set their prize beside their own god and find that whichever city houses it suffers strangely for the honour.

2848.label: A challenge in the valley
2848.recap: Two armies camp on facing hills while a huge champion comes out daily to demand that one man settle the war in single combat.

2848.label: A young king's first test
2848.recap: Solomon inherits the throne as a youth and at once faces a request from an elder brother that he reads as more than it seems.

2848.label: Assyria at the walls
2848.recap: Hezekiah buys off an invading king, only to find a general and a great force encamped before Jerusalem making speeches to frighten the city.

2848.label: After Alexander
2848.recap: The conqueror's generals divide the world between them, and one of them takes Jerusalem by walking in on a day when nobody expects a fight.

2848.label: Herod holds Jerusalem
2848.recap: With the city in his hands, Herod rewards the few who spoke for him and strips the wealth of everyone who did not.

2848.label: An emperor's madness
2848.recap: The narrative turns to Rome, where an emperor plunders temples, bridges a bay for his chariot, and demands to be honoured as a god.

2848.label: The last governor
2848.recap: A final Roman governor squeezes the province past bearing, and the author closes his twenty books by looking ahead to the war he has written of elsewhere.

2852.label: Mr. Sherlock Holmes
2852.recap: Holmes and Watson examine a walking-stick left by Dr Mortimer and deduce a great deal before the visitor returns.

2852.label: The Curse of the Baskervilles
2852.recap: Mortimer reads the old legend of a demonic hound said to haunt and hunt the Baskerville family.

2852.label: The Problem
2852.recap: Mortimer recounts Sir Charles Baskerville's mysterious death, with the footprints of a gigantic hound found nearby.

2852.label: Sir Henry Baskerville
2852.recap: The young heir Sir Henry arrives in London, already being shadowed and sent an anonymous warning to stay away.

2852.label: Baskerville Hall
2852.recap: Watson escorts Sir Henry to the gloomy hall on the moor, where an escaped convict is also at large.

2852.label: The Stapletons
2852.recap: Watson meets the naturalist Stapleton and his striking sister, who strangely begs Sir Henry to leave the moor.

2852.label: Watson's Watch
2852.recap: Settled at the hall, Watson tracks odd happenings: a sobbing in the night and the butler signalling across the dark.

2852.label: The Man on the Tor
2852.recap: Trailing a stranger to a stone hut on the moor, Watson discovers it is Holmes himself, secretly at work.

2852.label: Death on the Moor
2852.recap: A body is found on the rocks; to their relief it is the convict, and Holmes prepares to spring his trap.

2852.label: The Hound
2852.recap: Out of the fog the monstrous glowing hound attacks Sir Henry, and Holmes shoots it down and exposes the killer.

2852.label: A Retrospection
2852.recap: In London Holmes explains how Stapleton, a hidden Baskerville heir, used a painted hound to murder for the estate.

2868.label: The Lovers
2868.recap: The young lovers Lucy and Archie spar over a thousand-pound bargain tangled up with their hopes of marriage.

2868.label: The Unexpected
2868.recap: Archie frets that Professor Braddock's consent to the match was bought, uneasy at the old man's hunger for money.

2868.label: The Inquest
2868.recap: The sleepy village of Gartley wakes to sudden fame as police and reporters descend to inquire into a shocking crime.

2868.label: Mrs. Jasher's Luck
2868.recap: Weeks pass and interest in the unsolved murder of Braddock's assistant cools to idle village gossip.

2868.label: The Manuscript
2868.recap: Talk keeps returning to the vanished green mummy that the dead man had brought to England.

2868.label: The Unexpected Happens
2868.recap: Fresh rumours race through the village, and an unexpected development reopens the case.

2868.label: Circumstantial Evidence
2868.recap: Professor Braddock flings a fierce accusation at the young soldier Random, who is baffled by the charge.

2868.label: Nearer the Truth
2868.recap: A startling recognition of one of the men present brings the tangled mystery a step nearer its solution.

2868.label: Just in Time
2868.recap: One of the missing emeralds is returned anonymously, the strangest twist yet in the affair of the green mummy.

2868.label: A Confession
2868.recap: A night-time alarm and a terrified servant give way at last to a long-withheld confession.

2868.label: By the River
2868.recap: After a long day's manhunt the pursuers gather for a secret meeting down by the river.

3011.label: Canto I: The Chase
3011.recap: A royal stag-hunt in the Highlands leads a lost huntsman to a lovely maiden, Ellen, beside a lonely lake.

3011.label: Canto II: The Island
3011.recap: On Ellen's island we meet her father, the outlawed Douglas, and the fierce chieftain Roderick Dhu who loves her.

3011.label: Canto III: The Gathering
3011.recap: Roderick Dhu raises the clans for war, sending the Fiery Cross flaming across the glens.

3011.label: Canto IV: The Prophecy
3011.recap: A seer's grim prophecy hangs over the gathering, while Ellen's heart turns to the gallant stranger Fitz-James.

3011.label: Canto V: The Combat
3011.recap: Fitz-James and Roderick Dhu meet as foes, and a fierce single combat decides much.

3011.label: Canto VI: The Guard-Room
3011.recap: All paths lead at last to the king's court, where the true identity of Fitz-James is revealed.

3044.label: A Christmas in London
3044.recap: A young architect spends the holidays with a friend in Bloomsbury and loses his heart at first sight.

3044.label: The Shakespeare reading
3044.recap: His daughter sits through a dull public recitation, her attention wandering to workmen on a distant church spire.

3044.label: Leaving for the coast
3044.recap: Brother and sister travel to a seaside town to start again, and she advertises herself as a companion.

3044.label: A row on the bay
3044.recap: On the eve of a young man's departure for London the two of them take a boat out onto the water.

3044.label: Two letters in one post
3044.recap: An offer of employment and a love letter arrive together, and Cytherea sets off for a country mansion.

3044.label: Midnight in the dressing room
3044.recap: Attending her new mistress after a late dinner, she notices a locket the lady never removes.

3044.label: A misread timetable
3044.recap: The estate steward glances too quickly at a railway column, and his wife's train is due hours earlier than he believes.

3044.label: Fire in the village
3044.recap: Flames take hold of an old thatched inn and the whole parish turns out to get everyone clear of it.

3044.label: The night before the wedding
3044.recap: Lying awake, Cytherea counts over the sensible reasons she gave herself for agreeing to the match.

3044.label: A name in a prayer-book
3044.recap: Owen walks six miles to a country church to look at the writing inside a book left in a private pew.

3044.label: Following through the trees
3044.recap: Four figures move separately through a dark plantation, each shadowing the one in front.

3044.label: The ringers' gossip
3044.recap: Fifteen months on, the parish bell-ringers gather in the tower and talk over how everything turned out.

3070.label: The forgotten walking-stick
3070.recap: Holmes and Watson try to reconstruct the owner of a stick left behind by a caller they managed to miss.

3070.label: An old family paper
3070.recap: A visitor produces a manuscript dated 1742 and reads aloud the origin of a legend that runs in one family.

3070.label: Close questions about the ground
3070.recap: Holmes presses the doctor about the yew alley, the weather, and exactly what was found near the body.

3070.label: The heir at Baker Street
3070.recap: The young baronet arrives from overseas and produces an odd letter delivered to his London hotel.

3070.label: Down to Devonshire
3070.recap: Watson is briefed at the station, told to report facts rather than theories, and to keep his revolver near.

3070.label: First morning at the Hall
3070.recap: Sunlight improves the old house, but a question about a woman crying in the night unsettles the household.

3070.label: Watson writes to Baker Street
3070.recap: Watson begins reporting by letter on the moor, its prehistoric huts, and the neighbours around the Hall.

3070.label: A window facing the moor
3070.recap: Watson examines the room a servant crept to at night and works out what could possibly be seen from it.

3070.label: A visit to Coombe Tracey
3070.recap: Armed with two new facts, Watson drives out alone to question a lady about a letter she once wrote.

3070.label: A voice outside the hut
3070.recap: Alone among the stone huts on the moor, Watson hears a voice he knows extremely well.

3070.label: The night drive back
3070.recap: Kept in the dark about the plan as usual, Watson rides out after dark towards the final effort.

3070.label: By the Baker Street fire
3070.recap: Weeks later, before a November fire, Holmes takes the whole business apart point by point.

3146.label: The column in the firs
3146.recap: A restless lady keeps noticing an isolated tower on her husband's estate and at last drives out to see it.

3146.label: The youth at the telescope
3146.recap: At the top of the column she finds a young man so absorbed in the sun that he waves her away.

3146.label: Home in the dell
3146.recap: The young astronomer packs up at dusk and walks down to his grandmother's thatched farmhouse for supper.

3146.label: A promise kept
3146.recap: Sitting at her window under a bright planet, she finally throws on a cloak and walks out towards the tower.

3146.label: Watching for the post
3146.recap: She opens the post-bag anxiously while the young man is away on an errand she asked him to run.

3146.label: The new equatorial
3146.recap: A waggon of packing-cases crosses the field to the column, and a bill has to be settled without anyone knowing.

3146.label: A misgiving on the path
3146.recap: She recognises what she actually feels for the young astronomer and resolves to keep out of his sight.

3146.label: An errand in Bath
3146.recap: Alone in a strange city, she walks by the obscurest streets to keep a nerve-racking appointment.

3146.label: Dawn in the cabin
3146.recap: Swithin dresses before daylight in his hut under the trees and reads a letter on the road that alters his prospects.

3146.label: The Bishop at luncheon
3146.recap: Lady Constantine, her mind elsewhere, charms a visiting Bishop at a luncheon her brother has arranged.

3146.label: A picture in the paper
3146.recap: An illustrated newspaper arrives from an unknown hand with a lurid engraving she cannot stop looking at.

3146.label: Southern skies
3146.recap: Years on, Swithin is still at the Cape, turning a barrow-load of observations into work of real value.

3177.label: Envying the journey
3177.recap: A young man envies his brother's western appointment, then is offered the post of private secretary and packs within the hour.

3177.label: On top of the coach
3177.recap: The travellers ride atop the flying stage across the plains and meet their first prairie dogs, antelope and coyote.

3177.label: The desperado's legend
3177.recap: Stage talk turns to a division agent whose reputation for killing runs ahead of him along the whole line.

3177.label: Into the Rockies
3177.recap: The coach overtakes footsore emigrants and climbs past Devil's Gate, a dry soda lake and a natural ice house.

3177.label: The silver fever
3177.recap: Camped in a canyon of eleven cabins, he sneaks off alone certain he will pick silver up off the ground.

3177.label: Stranded at the inn
3177.recap: Flood-bound at a wayside inn, he suffers a tireless singer and a drunk who is desperate to pick a fight.

3177.label: Lost in the snow
3177.recap: Lost in a night snowstorm, the party tries to light a fire with pistols and manages to lose the horses instead.

3177.label: A rich strike
3177.recap: The camp goes wild over a spectacular new strike, while one partner keeps insisting the ore is not what everyone thinks.

3177.label: A representative citizen
3177.recap: A saloon-keeping notable is buried with full honours, and a rough is deputed to arrange things with a new eastern minister.

3177.label: The vanished camps
3177.recap: In California he looks at torn hillsides and silent meadows where roaring gold towns stood twenty years earlier.

3177.label: Down in the crater
3177.recap: By lantern light two men run across the hot floor of a volcano toward a distant lake of fire.

3177.label: Out on the divide
3177.recap: Walking home over a lonely ridge after a lecture, he is stopped in the dark by a masked man with a revolver.

3268.label: La Vallée
3268.recap: In a peaceful corner of Gascony, the gentle Emily St. Aubert grows up devoted to her parents and to nature.

3268.label: A Mother Lost
3268.recap: Emily's mother dies, and her grieving father takes her travelling through the mountains for his failing health.

3268.label: Valancourt
3268.recap: On the journey a tender attachment grows between Emily and the spirited young Valancourt.

3268.label: Alone in the World
3268.recap: Far from home, Emily's beloved father dies, leaving her an orphan.

3268.label: Madame Cheron
3268.recap: Emily is taken in by her cold and vain aunt, Madame Cheron.

3268.label: Montoni
3268.recap: Madame Cheron marries the sinister Italian Montoni, and the household is carried off toward Venice.

3268.label: The Castle of Udolpho
3268.recap: Montoni shuts them up in his brooding, half-ruined castle deep in the Apennines.

3268.label: Whispers in the Castle
3268.recap: Servants' tales of ghosts and a dreadful secret behind a black veil prey on Emily's mind.

3268.label: Under Siege
3268.recap: Montoni fills the castle with rough soldiers as his schemes turn openly violent.

3268.label: Montoni's Tyranny
3268.recap: Standing alone, Emily resists Montoni's threats and his demands that she sign away her estates.

3268.label: Château-le-Blanc
3268.recap: The scene shifts to a haunted château in Languedoc and its kindly new owner, the Count De Villefort.

3268.label: A New Refuge
3268.recap: Having escaped Udolpho, Emily finds shelter at the château among new friends.

3268.label: Montoni's Fate
3268.recap: Word arrives of the reckoning that has at last overtaken the tyrant Montoni.

3268.label: The North Apartments
3268.recap: Strange happenings in the château's shut-up north rooms revive old fears and buried secrets.

3268.label: All Explained
3268.recap: Every lingering mystery is unravelled at last, and Emily finds her long-delayed happiness.

3289.label: A cipher at breakfast
3289.recap: Holmes leaves his breakfast untouched to puzzle out a coded note from a nervous informant, and explains to Watson who stands behind the man.

3289.label: The moated manor house
3289.recap: Watson pauses to describe the old Sussex manor with its drawbridge and moat, and the popular American-made gentleman who leased it.

3289.label: Laughter behind the hedge
3289.recap: Walking in the manor garden, Watson comes upon two members of the household in a mood that badly unsettles him.

3289.label: Advice to abandon the case
3289.recap: Holmes startles the two detectives by telling them to drop their hunt entirely, promising a shorter route to the truth.

3289.label: A stranger reaches Vermissa
3289.recap: Years earlier and an ocean away, a young Irishman rides an evening train into a coal valley and picks a fight with two policemen.

3289.label: Facing the Bodymaster
3289.recap: McMurdo courts his landlord's daughter, makes a dangerous enemy, and walks into the saloon of the man who rules the valley.

3289.label: Lodge night
3289.recap: McMurdo moves lodgings, wins the gang's respect in a bar-room scrape, and is put through the lodge's initiation.

3289.label: A warning on Miller Hill
3289.recap: Nursing a branded arm, McMurdo answers an unsigned summons and hears a frightened brother describe what the valley has become.

3289.label: Ettie's doubt
3289.recap: McMurdo's standing among the brothers rises, while the girl he loves, startled by something she glimpses in him, begs him to break away.

3289.label: A detective on the trail
3289.recap: Word reaches the lodge that an outside agency has planted an investigator among them, and the brothers begin deciding how to answer.

3289.label: The trap is laid
3289.recap: The conspirators prepare a lonely house on the edge of town for the arrival of the man they intend to question.

3289.label: A cable from Cape Town
3289.recap: Months later a shaken visitor brings news from overseas, and Holmes names the hand he believes lies behind it.

3321.label: The attic studio
3321.recap: In a studio over a pawnshop a roaring red-haired painter finishes a portrait of a small-time crook while the crook's daughter waits her turn to sit.

3321.label: Waiting for Larry
3321.recap: The men praise an absent confidence man due out of prison, and float the idea of pairing the girl with him on jobs, which delights her.

3321.label: Home from Sing Sing
3321.recap: Fresh out of prison, Larry sees a detective inside the pawnshop, avoids him, and walks out to the end of the pier to breathe free air.

3321.label: The paintings are real
