3321.recap: Larry looks hard at the canvases everyone in the street laughs at, and turns on the painter demanding to know what he is really doing there.

3321.label: A duel of purposes
3321.recap: Larry urges Maggie to stay out of the crooked game, and she answers with all the certainty and scorn of eighteen.

3321.label: Maggie packs a suitcase
3321.recap: After days of cold silence Larry comes home to find Maggie in hat and coat with her baggage in the hall, leaving the street for good.

3321.label: Waking on Park Avenue
3321.recap: Larry wakes in a splendid unfamiliar bedroom with a valet at the bell, trying to make sense of the night that brought him there.

3321.label: A rainy night visit
3321.recap: Muffled in a raincoat and umbrella, Larry risks a call at his grandmother's pawnshop to find out where Maggie has gone.

3321.label: Playing the ingenue
3321.recap: Installed in a hotel suite with a hired chaperone, Maggie plays hostess to her fake relatives and the pleasant young man they are stalking.

3321.label: A dangerous invitation
3321.recap: Larry settles on a risky scheme to have Maggie welcomed as a guest by the very household she is plotting against.

3321.label: A proposal by the roadside
3321.recap: Driving her home, Dick pulls the car off the road and stammers out a proposal, and Maggie finds she cannot answer it easily.

3321.label: The morning after
3321.recap: With the storms past and the house quiet, Larry sits over his plans feeling restless and unsure of where he stands with anyone.

3530.label: A meeting in the hills
3530.recap: Six noblemen wait in a goatherd's hut on a mountainside for a soldier they mean to make an offer to.

3530.label: Betrayed on the path
3530.recap: Marching feet come up the mountain, and the conspirators decide the only way out is straight through them.

3530.label: A fool trips over a stranger
3530.recap: A jester running from an angry friar falls over a wounded man lying half hidden in the bracken.

3530.label: The lady at the brook
3530.recap: A young noblewoman finds the wounded man and tends him with water carried in his own hat.

3530.label: Heads above the gate
3530.recap: Riding into Babbiano, the Count sees what the failed plot has cost, then goes to dine with the Duke.

3530.label: A courtier's private scheme
3530.recap: Gonzaga finishes laying his plans and goes down to a filthy tavern to hire the men he needs.

3530.label: The Duke questions a jester
3530.recap: Halting for the night on his journey, Gian Maria has the fool brought to his bedchamber and interrogates him.

3530.label: Trouble in the courtyard
3530.recap: The hired soldiers turn on a newcomer's servant, and their captain discovers what the newcomer can do.

3530.label: The siege begins
3530.recap: Word comes that the Duke has camped in the plain below, and the household settles who will command its defence.

3530.label: A quiet week of siege
3530.recap: Nothing stirs outside the walls while inside a smiling courtier works patiently to win back everyone's trust.

3530.label: Mass at Corpus Christi
3530.recap: While the garrison kneels at Mass, one man excuses himself and climbs to the ramparts.

3530.label: Parley beneath the walls
3530.recap: The positions are reversed outside Roccaleone and terms are argued back and forth under the battlements.

3567.label: A Corsican at Brienne
3567.recap: The narrator sets out his friend's birth, poor family and schooldays at a French military college.

3567.label: Out of favour
3567.recap: Struck off the list of generals, the young officer hangs about Paris looking for any command that will have him.

3567.label: A marriage in ten days
3567.recap: The secretary watches his friend point out a young widow across the table and marry her days before leaving for Italy.

3567.label: Bargaining with Austria
3567.recap: Peace talks drag on in Italy while the general berates government envoys at dinner and threatens to resign.

3567.label: Up the Nile to Cairo
3567.recap: Sailing under fire from the riverbanks, the party learns a battle has been fought and follows the army into Cairo.

3567.label: Plague on the retreat
3567.recap: Falling back from Syria, the army halts at a ruined town where men are dying of plague and a decision must be made.

3567.label: The eighteenth Brumaire
3567.recap: With the Directory collapsing, the general goes in to face the two councils and the outcome hangs in doubt for hours.

3567.label: Over the Alps
3567.recap: Italy having been lost, the First Consul takes an army across the great pass to meet the Austrians in the plain.

3567.label: A prince is shot
3567.recap: A Bourbon prince is seized and executed, and the courts of Europe return their honours in disgust.

3567.label: Toward Russia
3567.recap: Two emperors negotiate while both privately want war, and Napoleon's remaining allies fall away.

3567.label: Paris falls
3567.recap: With the Allies fighting at the walls of Paris, the Emperor hurries back too late and must face his own marshals.

3567.label: The last island
3567.recap: The final years on a remote Atlantic rock are told through to the funeral procession.

3913.label: An unprecedented promise
3913.recap: The author announces that he will present one man in full honesty, and that the man will be himself.

3913.label: The broken comb
3913.recap: A comb is found damaged, a boy is accused, and he refuses to confess to something he says he never did.

3913.label: The gates close early
3913.recap: Racing back to the city after curfew, an apprentice arrives to find the drawbridge already up.

3913.label: A lady at Annecy
3913.recap: Carrying a priest's letter of introduction, the runaway meets the charitable lady he had pictured very differently.

3913.label: A pink and silver ribbon
3913.recap: A trifle goes missing from a dead woman's household, and when questioned the young servant names someone else.

3913.label: Monsieur de Villeneuve
3913.recap: Arriving broke in a strange town, he invents a new name, a Paris past, and a profession he cannot practise.

3913.label: The Charmettes
3913.recap: He describes a country interlude he remembers more exactly than any other stretch of his life.

3913.label: The road to Vincennes
3913.recap: Walking to visit an imprisoned friend, he reads a prize question in a journal and is changed by it.

3913.label: Into the Hermitage
3913.recap: Against the mockery of his Paris circle, he moves out of the city into a small house in the country.

3913.label: All Paris waits
3913.recap: His long-delayed novel finally appears and the reaction, especially among women, exceeds anything he expected.

3913.label: Stones on the road
3913.recap: Denounced from local pulpits, he walks through the countryside in his foreign dress amid jeers and thrown stones.

3913.label: A chaise at dawn
3913.recap: Ordered out of one more territory, he leaves before the official deputation arrives and before his companion can join him.

3922.label: An afternoon in Paris
3922.recap: A rich countess waits for callers in a drawing room she has made beautiful and finds nothing in it to want.

3922.label: How she came to this
3922.recap: Alone by the fire she looks back over her father, her marriage and the choices that were made for her.

3922.label: A hunting trip
3922.recap: A small disagreement about a planned absence turns quietly into something much colder.

3922.label: Leaving for Italy
3922.recap: She sets off for Florence with a placid companion and a ragged poet who nearly misses the train.

3922.label: A villa above Florence
3922.recap: The house at Fiesole waits for a late guest while its residents argue about doors and misfortune.

3922.label: The cobbler's basil plant
3922.recap: A morning of churches and a poor cobbler's contentment ends with an admission she does not answer aloud.

3922.label: A room by the cemetery
3922.recap: She keeps an appointment at a room that has been carefully prepared for her arrival.

3922.label: A note from a hotel
3922.recap: On a spring festival morning she slips away to answer two lines of writing delivered by post.

3922.label: Goodbye at the station
3922.recap: A last meeting on a railway platform is witnessed, she fears, by people who might recognise him.

3922.label: The sculptor's house
3922.recap: She visits a crowded, half-ruined studio house and imagines what she would change in its garden.

3922.label: A night at the opera
3922.recap: All of Paris turns its opera glasses on her box, her jewel, and the newly announced ministry.

3922.label: The last conversation
3922.recap: A final attempt to be believed settles everything between them.

4085.label: Born in Scotland
4085.recap: Disowned father, mother dead young: little Roderick Random is left to the mercy of a cold grandfather and cruel relations.

4085.label: Uncle Bowling
4085.recap: His rough but warm-hearted uncle, Lieutenant Tom Bowling, arrives to rescue the neglected boy.

4085.label: Apprenticed to Surgery
4085.recap: Penniless and shunned, Roderick learns surgery under the cynical Mr Crab, who at last stakes him to seek his fortune in London.

4085.label: The Road to London
4085.recap: Roderick and his devoted friend Strap set off for London, meeting a colourful and dangerous crew of fellow travellers.

4085.label: Green in the City
4085.recap: Reaching London as raw newcomers, the pair are gulled and fleeced at every turn.

4085.label: The Apothecary's House
4085.recap: Working for the French apothecary Lavement, Roderick is caught between a scheming mother and her daughter.

4085.label: Pressed to Sea
4085.recap: Forced aboard a man of war, Roderick endures the brutal squalor of the ship's surgery in the cockpit.

4085.label: Cartagena
4085.recap: His ship joins the disastrous British assault on Cartagena, amid disease, blunder and slaughter.

4085.label: Shipwrecked
4085.recap: Homeward bound under the brutal Crampley, Roderick is wrecked on the English coast and robbed of everything.

4085.label: The Poet Melopoyn
4085.recap: Thrown into a debtors' prison, Roderick befriends the luckless poet Melopoyn and hears his tale of literary misfortune.

4085.label: Father and Fortune
4085.recap: Reunited at last with his long-lost father and his fortune made, Roderick heads home to buy back the family estate.

4200.label: The first entry
4200.recap: Pepys opens his journal with a note on his health, his tiny household in Axe Yard, and the unsettled state of the nation.

4200.label: The King comes ashore
4200.recap: Sailing home with the returning King, Pepys goes ashore at Dover among enormous crowds and a great deal of shouting.

4200.label: Coronation day
4200.recap: He waits seven hours on a scaffold in the Abbey to see the crowning, then wanders the feast in Westminster Hall.

4200.label: An ordinary busy day
4200.recap: A typical working day of navy contracts, a new viol, tavern gossip and a sharp word with a neighbour.

4200.label: Plague summer
4200.recap: With sickness in town he ventures out in a new wig and wonders who will dare buy hair again.

4200.label: A day of two halves
4200.recap: He weighs good news and his own safety against a lengthening list of neighbours, servants and watermen dead.

4200.label: Fire in the City
4200.recap: Woken before dawn, Pepys watches the fire spread, carries word to the King, and finds the Lord Mayor overwhelmed.

4200.label: Burying the cheese
4200.recap: With flames close by he digs pits in the garden for wine and papers and sups in the office without napkins.

4200.label: The Dutch in the river
4200.recap: With enemy ships in the Thames he sends his wife away with gold, makes his will, and hears treason talked in the streets.

4200.label: A bad month at home
4200.recap: He closes a month shamed by the worst quarrel of his marriage and uneasy about the young woman at the centre of it.

4200.label: Laying down the pen
4200.recap: Failing eyesight forces Pepys to stop keeping the journal in his own hand.

4300.label: Morning on the tower
4300.recap: A loud medical student shaves on the roof of a seaside tower and needles his sullen young housemate.

4300.label: Walking on the strand
4300.recap: Alone on Sandymount strand, Stephen shuts his eyes and lets his thoughts run through sight, sound and memory.

4300.label: Breakfast in Eccles Street
4300.recap: Bloom feeds the cat, walks round the corner for a kidney, and carries his wife her tea and the morning post.

4300.label: An errand along the quays
4300.recap: Bloom drifts through the warm morning city, thinking of tea and far-off countries, a card hidden in his hatband.

4300.label: The funeral carriage
4300.recap: Four men ride across Dublin to a burial, making awkward talk while Bloom keeps most of his thoughts to himself.

4300.label: Lunchtime in the city
4300.recap: A handbill pressed into his hand sets Bloom thinking about blood, belief and where a man might eat.

4300.label: Argument in the library
4300.recap: A circle of literary men argue about poetry and Ireland while Stephen builds a case about Hamlet and its author.

4300.label: The city in pieces
4300.recap: A priest sets off across town and the afternoon is followed through dozens of separate Dubliners at once.

4300.label: In the pub, told sourly
4300.recap: An unnamed Dublin loafer narrates an afternoon's drinking in his own scornful voice, with grand parodies breaking in.

4300.label: Evening on the rocks
4300.recap: Three young women mind children on the shore at dusk while the prose turns to sugary magazine romance.

4300.label: Into nighttown
4300.recap: The book becomes a play script as Stephen and a friend walk into the brothel quarter after midnight.

4300.label: In the dark, unpunctuated
4300.recap: Molly Bloom lies awake and lets a lifetime of memory and appetite run through her without a single stop.

4367.label: An Ohio boyhood
4367.recap: Grant traces his family from a 1630 landing in Massachusetts to a tanner's household in Georgetown, and sketches the village schooling he barely tolerated.

4367.label: Sent to West Point
4367.recap: His father announces an appointment to the military academy that the seventeen-year-old has no wish to accept, and quietly assumes he will go anyway.

4367.label: The war begins
4367.recap: A young second lieutenant on the Texas coast hears the first guns of the Mexican War and admits, privately, that he was sorry he had enlisted.

4367.label: Farming and failing
4367.recap: Out of the army at thirty-two, Grant tries farming, hauling wood for sale, and a real estate office, and none of it holds.

4367.label: Given a regiment
4367.recap: He takes charge of an unruly volunteer regiment that has rejected its elected colonel, and sets about bringing it under discipline.

4367.label: The empty camp
4367.recap: Riding towards an enemy camp for the first time as a commander, Grant learns something about fear that he says he never afterwards forgot.

4367.label: Investing Fort Donelson
4367.recap: With Fort Henry taken, Grant rides close to the works at Donelson, studies the ground, and privately sizes up the generals holding it.

4367.label: Close call at Shiloh
4367.recap: Riding beyond his own left on the battle's second day, Grant and two officers come under sudden fire and stop afterwards to count the damage.

4367.label: After Vicksburg
4367.recap: With the Mississippi opened, Grant tallies the surrendered prisoners and guns and answers Washington's anxiety about the paroles he granted.

4367.label: Into the Wilderness
4367.recap: The Army of the Potomac crosses the Rapidan to begin a campaign Grant expects will cost more in a year than the three that came before.

4367.label: Towards Appomattox
4367.recap: Nursing a violent headache at a roadside farmhouse, Grant answers a letter from Lee and rides on to reach the head of his column.

4367.label: The armies go home
4367.recap: With armed resistance ended, the troops march to Washington for a grand review, and Grant sets down his estimates of the men he served with and against.

4488.label: Dame Gossip begins
4488.recap: A gossiping narrator introduces a famous countess, defends her against the scandalmongers, and names her children.

4488.label: Farewell to the mountains
4488.recap: On their last sleepless night in an emptied Alpine house, a brother and sister go out to call the morning one final time.

4488.label: The disabled walker
4488.recap: A lamed young wanderer is helped down a scree by two passing strangers, and repays them with his philosophy of the road.

4488.label: Two strange young men
4488.recap: Woodseer walks on alone, loses his notebook, and finds that the stranger who read it will not be shaken off.

4488.label: A pride in a word
4488.recap: Two fashionable women weigh up a rich young lord's pride in keeping his promises, and what it may be worth to them.

4488.label: News of the ball
4488.recap: In a long letter written at dawn, Henrietta describes the ducal ball and the astonishing thing that happened during a dance.

4488.label: The drive from the wedding
4488.recap: A silent bride rides beside her husband in perfect trust while his thoughts run in a very different direction.

4488.label: A taste of old England
4488.recap: The honeymoon coach turns into a Kentish meadow, where two backed champions are stripping for a bare-knuckle fight.

4488.label: Money and blame
4488.recap: Sudden poverty sharpens the fashionable ladies' judgements on Carinthia's refusal to submit to her husband.

4488.label: Wales with her child
4488.recap: Living plainly in Wales with her baby, Carinthia takes stock of a marriage that has become a state of war.

4488.label: The bitten child
4488.recap: A dog bite in a village cottage puts Carinthia in command, and her husband, for once, finds himself taking orders.

4488.label: The last word
4488.recap: Brother and sister prepare for a foreign expedition, and the Dame steps forward to close the account of the marriage.

4499.label: A rich merchant of Cologne
4499.recap: Old Cologne is introduced through its wealthiest citizen, a money-lender with a proverb for everything and a famous daughter.

4499.label: A wager at the door
4499.recap: Armed ruffians hammer at a merchant's house over a bet, and his daughter comes downstairs to face them herself.

4499.label: Night on the Drachenfels
4499.recap: Under a breaking thunderstorm a young man is led to the haunted rock by a monk who asks only his silence.

4499.label: After the storm
4499.recap: The Rhine tale closes with a legend spreading through the towns and a crowd of imitators springing up overnight.

4499.label: A gentlemanly residence
4499.recap: A retired general finds a half-acre home outside London and settles blissfully into small ownership, overlooked by one attic window.

4499.label: The general on display
4499.recap: Stung by an unflattering likeness of himself, he carries it round the neighbourhood showing it to everyone who will look.

4499.label: The duke and the dairymaid
4499.recap: A popular ballad about a nobleman who married a milkmaid opens the fashionable world of a spa town and its reigning wit.

4499.label: Meeting the young duchess
4499.recap: A famous beau rides out in state to escort a new duchess to the Wells, coaching his companion on her duties as they wait.

4499.label: The dignity of small men
4499.recap: A seaside town's leading citizen is introduced along with a warning about eccentricity in the eminent.

4499.label: The vicar in the river
4499.recap: A narrator finds his absent-minded friend and his portly wife standing fully clothed in the river, chatting quite equably.

4499.label: A Surrey garden
4499.recap: An unfinished comedy opens with a professor delivering an oration on womanly devotion to a strolling garden party.

4499.label: The fly in amber
4499.recap: The closing essay argues that comedy sharpens the wits and that readers could be taught a finer taste in laughter.

4599.label: The squire's two houses
4599.recap: The narrator lays out the Dale family, their unentailed acres, and the two houses that give the story its shape.

4599.label: Two sisters talking
4599.recap: Lily and Bell trade opinions about a London gentleman who has been visiting the neighbourhood.

4599.label: The hobbledehoy
4599.recap: John Eames is introduced, an awkward and unformed young clerk lodging in a London boarding house.

4599.label: A guest from town
4599.recap: Crosbie turns down grander invitations and travels down to Allington for a month in the country.

4599.label: Beautiful days
4599.recap: The narrator finally describes the two Dale sisters, in the middle of a golden Allington summer.

4599.label: The last day
4599.recap: A visit at Allington comes to an end, and a parting has to be got through with more talk than either party wants.

4599.label: A field near Guestwick
4599.recap: Walking home along the earl's pastures, John Eames hears shouting and the bellowing of a bull.

4599.label: Leaving the castle
4599.recap: Driven away from a grand country house, Crosbie takes stock of the promises he has made and thinks poorly of himself.

4599.label: A quiet Christmas
4599.recap: Christmas at Allington is subdued, and Lily carries a private hurt with a courage that alarms her family.

4599.label: Illness in the house
4599.recap: Scarlatina appears in the Small House and the doctor is sent for from Guestwick.

4599.label: Packing up
4599.recap: With the move underway, Mrs. Dale carries a note up through the gardens to the squire.

4599.label: Conclusion
4599.recap: In June Lily goes up to the Great House to plead the gardener's case in a long-running quarrel about manure.

4693.label: Antony and Cleopatra
4693.recap: The book opens with the Egyptian queen fighting to keep her throne and the Roman soldier who is sent to question her.

4693.label: Abelard and Heloise
4693.recap: A brilliant and combative teacher draws thousands of students to Paris and makes enemies as fast as disciples.

4693.label: Elizabeth and Leicester
4693.recap: The narrator turns to a queen whose entire life was spent in a courtship that led nowhere.

4693.label: Mary Stuart and Bothwell
4693.recap: A Scottish queen inherits a kingdom in disorder and a reputation for fascination she never asked for.

4693.label: Christina of Sweden
4693.recap: A warlike northern kingdom produces a strange, learned queen who is raised almost as a son.

4693.label: Charles II and Nell Gwyn
4693.recap: The narrator ranks England's kings before settling on the Stuarts and the affections they inspired.

4693.label: Aaron Burr
4693.recap: An American politician is set beside his famous rival, with the narrator arguing for a fairer verdict.

4693.label: Charlotte Corday
4693.recap: A young Norman woman of ruined noble stock is introduced, along with the part of her story usually left out.

4693.label: General Houston's wives
4693.recap: The narrator describes what going to Texas once meant, and the punishing journey it took to get there.

4693.label: The Carlyles
4693.recap: A famously mismatched literary couple are seen at their worst by embarrassed dinner guests.

4693.label: Charles Dickens
4693.recap: The most publicly visible writer of his age is introduced as a man everyone knew and nobody quite did.

4693.label: Reade and Laura Seymour
4693.recap: The closing chapter takes up a novelist and the woman who kept his house, and asks what they were to each other.

4712.label: A stranger on the road
4712.recap: A young vagabond strolls a June highway, talks his way past a constable, and stops to help a stranded motoring party.

4712.label: The coffin and the armour
4712.recap: At a run-down farmhouse an old Quaker takes an axe to a coffin he built for himself, and his son appears dressed for a crusade.

4712.label: Knight-errantry tested
4712.recap: The armoured pilgrim's first meeting with the travelling public goes very badly, and his companion says so plainly.

4712.label: A suit of clothes
4712.recap: An eccentric judge hangs good clothing on a fence-post for whoever needs it, and two very different men come upon the offer.

4712.label: The rack-tender
4712.recap: Trespassing on mill land for shade, the wanderer falls into talk with the old Frenchman who rakes rubbish from the canal.

4712.label: The girl from Tadousac
4712.recap: He is introduced to a mill-girl who has taken charge of the small child he has quietly made himself responsible for.

4712.label: A wicked summer
4712.recap: Heat settles over the tenements, undertakers' wagons come daily, and sickness reaches into the household he cares about.

4712.label: Toys on the graves
4712.recap: At the cemetery the old Frenchman lays out a child's toys and speaks of martyrs, and something hardens in the wanderer.

4712.label: The colonel at his mirror
4712.recap: The head of the state's water trust reassures his own reflection, then receives three country businessmen he has quietly ruined.

4712.label: A lawyer takes an interest
4712.recap: A famously reserved attorney hails the wanderer across the street and demands to know who he really is.

4712.label: Speaking to the convention
4712.recap: He takes the floor of a state convention, and the machine men on the platform begin to sweat.

4712.label: Back to the tenement yard
4712.recap: Searching for someone he has lost, he wanders down to the dark mills, where the old rack-tender is waiting with news.

5131.label: A jaded young lord
5131.recap: A youth worn out by his own revels finds his native land unbearable and resolves to travel.

5131.label: Good night to England
5131.recap: At sunset aboard ship he sings a farewell to the fading shore, and his page and yeoman answer with griefs of their own.

5131.label: Three armies on a plain
5131.recap: The poem turns to the Spanish war, where three nations meet on one field and the poet counts the cost rather than the glory.

5131.label: The maid of Saragoza
5131.recap: A woman who once flinched at the sight of a scar is described taking up arms at a battered tower.

5131.label: Sunday at the bullring
5131.recap: Cadiz packs the arena on the sabbath for horsemen, matadors and the bull.

5131.label: Athens in ruins
5131.recap: The second canto stands among Greek stones and asks what became of the people who raised them.

5131.label: Into Albania
5131.recap: Harold comes down at dusk on the minarets of Tepelene and enters the crowded court of a mountain despot.

5131.label: Standing on Waterloo
5131.recap: The third canto walks the field where an empire ended and refuses to join the victors' celebration.

5131.label: A ball in Brussels
5131.recap: A brilliant evening of music and dancing is interrupted by a sound nobody wants to name.

5131.label: Night on Lake Geneva
5131.recap: On the still lake at night the poet turns away from crowds toward stars, silence and the feeling of being least alone in solitude.

5131.label: Venice, dogeless
5131.recap: The fourth canto opens in a Venice whose power has drained away, leaving beauty and borrowed ghosts.

5131.label: In the Coliseum
5131.recap: Among the ruined seats the poem imagines a dying fighter whose thoughts are far away by the Danube.

5131.label: Farewell to the sea
5131.recap: The pilgrimage closes with a long address to the unchanging ocean and a leave-taking to the reader.

5200.label: The Transformation
5200.recap: Gregor Samsa wakes transformed into a monstrous insect, and his family recoils as he fails to leave for work.

5200.label: A Prisoner at Home
5200.recap: Shut in his room, Gregor adjusts to his strange body while his sister warily feeds him and the household strains.

5200.label: The End
5200.recap: Wounded and unwanted, Gregor wastes away, and his relieved family turns hopefully toward the future.

5225.label: A rant about the schools
5225.recap: The narrator holds forth in a portico on how the schools have rotted eloquence and stuffed young men with nonsense.

5225.label: Lost in the city
5225.recap: Absorbed in a professor's reply, the narrator loses his companion, then loses himself in streets he does not know.

5225.label: The helpful old woman
5225.recap: An obliging vegetable seller offers to show him the way home and leads him somewhere else entirely.

5225.label: The door bursts open
5225.recap: Back at the lodging a private reunion is interrupted by a jeering friend with a strap in his hand.

5225.label: Beware the dog
5225.recap: Arriving at a rich freedman's house, the guests edge along a hallway painted end to end with their host's own life story.

5225.label: The host arrives
5225.recap: The master of the house is carried in among cushions, loaded with rings and jewellery, and the dinner properly begins.

5225.label: Chalk marks in the dark
5225.recap: Drunk and lost at midnight, the friends find their way back by a trick of the boy's, and the night ends badly.

5225.label: Dividing the boy
5225.recap: A joke about splitting their belongings turns into drawn swords, and the boy at the centre of it makes an offer of his own.

5225.label: Aboard by night
5225.recap: Persuaded to leave town, the narrator packs in a hurry and boards a ship after dark with the boy and an old poet.

5225.label: A story about women
5225.recap: To keep the company amused, the old poet offers a tale he swears happened within his own memory.

5225.label: Living on credit
5225.recap: In a town full of legacy hunters the friends eat magnificently on a reputation they invented, and the narrator starts calculating the risk.

5225.label: The reading of the will
5225.recap: A will with a monstrous condition attached is read out to the heirs, and the townspeople begin watching their guests rather closely.

5921.label: A gentleman and his books
5921.recap: An aging country gentleman sells acres of farmland to buy books of chivalry and reads until he loses his wits.

5921.label: The first sally
5921.recap: Before dawn on a hot July morning he rides out alone in patched armour and takes a wayside inn for a castle.

5921.label: Righting a wrong
5921.recap: Heading home for money and a squire, he hears cries in a thicket and interrupts a farmer beating a servant boy.

5921.label: The library on trial
5921.recap: While he sleeps, the curate and the barber go through his books one by one, sparing a few and condemning the rest to the yard.

5921.label: Out on the plain
5921.recap: Riding with his new squire, he sees a row of monstrous giants where Sancho insists there are only windmills.

5921.label: A night at the inn
5921.recap: Battered and bedded down in a straw loft, he takes the inn for a castle and imagines the household in love with him.

5921.label: Two armies approaching
5921.recap: He names the knights and nations of two great armies advancing over the plain while Sancho hears only bleating.

5921.label: The chained men
5921.recap: A dozen convicts chained by the neck pass along the road, and he asks each in turn how he came to be there.

5921.label: Into the Sierra Morena
5921.recap: Deep in the mountains he lifts the ban on Sancho's tongue and resolves to imitate the mad penances of his favourite knights.

5921.label: A tale found in a trunk
5921.recap: A manuscript discovered at the inn is read aloud, telling of two inseparable Florentine friends and a newly married wife.

5921.label: Battle in the garret
5921.recap: Sancho bursts in shouting that his master has beheaded a giant upstairs, and the whole company runs up to look.

5921.label: A procession in the valley
5921.recap: A village walks in procession praying for rain, and the knight takes the veiled image they carry for a lady held captive.

6130.label: The quarrel in the camp
6130.recap: A priest is turned away, a plague falls on the Greek ships, and two commanders fall out over a captive woman.

6130.label: A dream and a muster
6130.recap: A dream sent from heaven moves the Greek king to test his army, and the whole host is drawn up and counted.

6130.label: A duel to end the war
6130.recap: The armies come face to face and a single combat is proposed to settle the whole quarrel at once.

6130.label: Two enemies, one old debt
6130.recap: The gods step back from the fighting, and two men meeting between the lines discover a tie between their houses.

6130.label: An embassy by night
6130.recap: After a bad day the Greek leaders sit up in council and send envoys to plead with the man who will not fight.

6130.label: The fiercest day
6130.recap: A new dawn brings the hardest fighting yet, and one after another the Greek captains are carried off wounded.

6130.label: A friend's request
6130.recap: Weeping, Patroclus begs to be allowed to take the field wearing his friend's armour.

6130.label: The messenger by the water
6130.recap: A young man waits by the sea with news, while Achilles sits among his ships turning over his fears.

6130.label: Armour from the forge
6130.recap: At daybreak a goddess brings her grieving son the arms made for him by the smith of the gods.

6130.label: One man outside the gate
6130.recap: The Trojans crowd back behind their walls, and a single defender stays out on the plain before the gate.

6130.label: Funeral games
6130.recap: Achilles gathers his men, lays out prizes, and holds contests of chariots, boxing, wrestling and archery.

6130.label: An old man's journey
6130.recap: With the games over Achilles cannot sleep, and in Troy an aged king prepares to set out on an errand of his own.

6133.label: The Arrest of Arsène Lupin
6133.recap: Aboard a transatlantic liner, word spreads that the master thief Arsène Lupin is among the passengers in disguise.

6133.label: Arsène Lupin in Prison
6133.recap: Even locked behind bars, Lupin contrives to rob a baron's riverside chateau entirely by post.

6133.label: The Escape of Arsène Lupin
6133.recap: Awaiting trial, Lupin cheerfully promises he will walk free, and sets about proving it.

6133.label: The Mysterious Traveller
6133.recap: A night train journey turns sinister when the narrator finds danger sharing his compartment.

6133.label: The Queen's Necklace
6133.recap: A famous diamond necklace vanishes from a locked room, baffling its owners for years.

6133.label: The Seven of Hearts
6133.recap: The narrator recounts the curious affair of a playing card that first drew him into Lupin's orbit.

6133.label: Madame Imbert's Safe
6133.recap: Lupin sets his sights on the fortune said to be locked away in Madame Imbert's safe.

6133.label: The Black Pearl
6133.recap: A priceless black pearl draws Lupin into a midnight burglary that does not go to plan.

6133.label: Sherlock Holmes Arrives Too Late
6133.recap: A great English detective is summoned to a country chateau, only to find Lupin a step ahead.

6400.label: A young man abroad
6400.recap: Caesar serves his first campaigns in Asia and Cilicia, and on a winter voyage to Rhodes falls into the hands of pirates.

6400.label: The little bridge
6400.recap: Halting at the small river that marks the edge of his province, he tells the men around him that crossing it leaves only one way out.

6400.label: Warnings before the ides
6400.recap: Omens, a soothsayer's caution and a note pressed into his hand all reach him on the morning the senate is due to meet.

6400.label: An obscure family
6400.recap: The account turns back to the small-town Octavii and to the sneers rivals aimed at the ancestry of the man who became Augustus.

6400.label: Asking for a mirror
6400.recap: On his last day the old emperor has his hair combed and asks the friends around him whether he played his part on the stage of life well.

6400.label: Withdrawal to the island
6400.recap: Tiberius retires to a cliff-ringed island he finds delightful, and the business of the empire is increasingly left to run itself.

6400.label: A campaign of sorts
6400.recap: Caligula assembles an enormous force for a northern expedition, then turns the whole thing into an elaborate piece of theatre.

6400.label: A watchword and a plan
6400.recap: Guards officers, weary of insult and frightened for themselves, settle on a time and a place, while prodigies pile up around the palace.

6400.label: Behind the hangings
6400.recap: Hiding on a balcony during the uproar in the palace, the family's overlooked laughing-stock is spotted by a passing soldier.

6400.label: Six days of fire
6400.recap: Fire runs through the old streets for six days and seven nights while the prince watches from a tower and sings about Troy.

6400.label: The line runs out
6400.recap: With the Julio-Claudian line ended, the narrative moves to the elderly, gouty, immensely rich Galba and the scramble that follows.

6400.label: A steward's bandaged arm
6400.recap: The common account of Domitian's last hour is set down in detail, down to what a boy in the bedchamber later reported.

6593.label: The Foundling
6593.recap: The good Squire Allworthy comes home to find a baby asleep in his bed, and resolves to raise the foundling as his own son.

6593.label: Tom and Blifil
6593.recap: Tom grows into a warm but reckless youth, while the demure Master Blifil quietly turns the household against him.

6593.label: Sophia Western
6593.recap: Tom and Sophia, the neighbouring squire's lovely daughter, fall in love.

6593.label: A Forbidden Match
6593.recap: Squire Western dreams of marrying Sophia to Blifil, never guessing that her heart already belongs to Tom.

6593.label: Cast Out
6593.recap: Turned out of doors through Blifil's scheming, Tom sets off to seek his fortune, while Sophia too flees her father's house.

6593.label: On the Road
6593.recap: On his wanderings Tom gains a faithful companion in the barber Partridge and hears the strange tale of the Man of the Hill.

6593.label: The Inn at Upton
6593.recap: At the inn at Upton a tangle of mistaken rooms and jealousies sends Tom and Sophia past each other in the night.

6593.label: Sophia's Flight
6593.recap: Sophia presses on toward London with her maid, nursing her hurt at Tom's wandering ways.

6593.label: London
6593.recap: In London Tom is drawn into the worldly Lady Bellaston's orbit, even as he longs only for Sophia.

6593.label: Sophia Confined
6593.recap: Sophia's father and a scheming lord press her toward a marriage she does not want.

6593.label: The Lowest Ebb
6593.recap: With Tom flung into prison and seemingly ruined, his few true friends despair of saving him.

6593.label: All Revealed
6593.recap: At the darkest hour the secret of Tom's birth comes to light, Blifil's villainy is exposed, and fortune turns at last.

6635.label: A julep interrupted
6635.recap: A Kentucky colonel is mixing his Sunday julep when his daughter announces she is riding out with a young man he dislikes.

6635.label: A race to the mill
6635.recap: The two riders race down the country road toward town, and the ride ends in a scramble at a railroad crossing.

6635.label: A reformed character
6635.recap: Riding home in love, Donald resolves to change his whole life, then falls into talk with a red-headed stranger at the Junction.

6635.label: The ash-barrel boy
6635.recap: The history of a speechless foundling from Bean Alley and the private revenge he has been planning for six weeks.

6635.label: A week of rain
6635.recap: Rain drowns the farm while Miss Lady waits for a letter that never comes and her father watches her, baffled.

6635.label: After the funeral
6635.recap: Grieving and unanswered, she is finally handed the letter she has been waiting for and must weigh it against a promise.

6635.label: A visitor from town
6635.recap: A fashionable cousin arrives on a duty call and is disarmed by the girl she meets in the hall.

6635.label: Rule of the kitchen
6635.recap: A formidable cook takes charge of a professor's household and briskly prunes the family of its hangers-on.

6635.label: The house-warming
6635.recap: A grand new house on the hilltop throws a Christmas ball, while the new furnace man causes trouble downstairs.

6635.label: Accounts overdrawn
6635.recap: The Doctor finds his affairs in disorder and refuses his wife's offer to sell off more of her old home.

6635.label: Worries in a pack
6635.recap: After a lost case and a bank failure, Donald walks the terrace alone and looks down at a familiar light below.

6635.label: Waiting on the jury
6635.recap: In a crowded court room the last speech is made, and Miss Lady finds she can no longer keep her seat.

6761.label: Sage Observations
6761.recap: The narrator opens with wry remarks on history before introducing his cold-hearted anti-hero, Ferdinand Fathom.

6761.label: The Patron's Daughter
6761.recap: Raised in the household of his benefactor Count de Melvil, the cunning young Fathom wins the favour of the Count's daughter.

6761.label: Into the World
6761.recap: Fathom and the trusting young Renaldo set off into the world, where Fathom turns their friendship to his own profit.

6761.label: A Blind Security
6761.recap: Grown bold on success, Fathom's intrigues with the ladies very nearly trap him in a scrape.

6761.label: Scylla and Charybdis
6761.recap: Ever wary of others' treachery, Fathom finds himself caught between two dangers at once.

6761.label: Foiled
6761.recap: Outwitted at his own game, Fathom takes his reverse philosophically and falls in with a remarkable new acquaintance.

6761.label: The Fair Elenor
6761.recap: His schemes carry him on to a fresh design upon the virtue of the fair Elenor.

6761.label: Bristol Spring
6761.recap: The adventurer arrives at the Bristol spa, where for a season he reigns as the king of fashion.

6761.label: Majesty in Eclipse
6761.recap: In a debtors' prison Fathom meets a colourful crew of fallen schemers and make-believe kings.

6768.label: The knocking upstairs
6768.recap: A young composer marches upstairs to confront the man who has been banging on her ceiling while she works.

6768.label: A London girl in exile
6768.recap: A cinema-loving London girl is banished to the sleepiest village in Hampshire and starts making her boredom felt over the garden fence.

6768.label: The swimmer at Marvis Bay
6768.recap: A first-time playwright escapes his rehearsals to a seaside resort and finds something on the pier far more absorbing than his play.

6768.label: The jealous barber
6768.recap: A manicurist finally tells her hairdresser fiance that his endless scowling at friendly customers is neither fair nor professional.

6768.label: The waiter's story
6768.recap: A sour, spineless waiter corners a silent diner and begins the tale of two tramps and the simple wealthy man who took them in.

6768.label: Why he hates cats
6768.recap: A melancholy Frenchman saves the narrator from a persistent fly and insists on repaying him with the story of his blighted life.

6768.label: The pawnbroker's clerk
6768.recap: A young Englishwoman who keeps the ledgers in a Riviera pawnshop walks out into the evening air weighed down by the life her father has arranged.

6768.label: The hopeless golfer
6768.recap: An enthusiastic and dreadful golfer, beloved of the least demanding club in New Jersey, is interrupted by a telephone call.

6768.label: Outfaced by a butler
6768.recap: A guest losing ground to a soulful poet at a country house is close to fleeing when the butler steps silently into his room.

6768.label: New York changes her
6768.recap: A girl from a small Canadian town finds New York indifferent to her, and takes work she would have refused two weeks earlier.

6768.label: The worst knight at Camelot
6768.recap: A knight who has never once won a joust picks himself out of the dust again, painfully aware he does not belong at Arthur's court.

6768.label: The hall-bedroom writer
6768.recap: In the cheapest room of a New York apartment house a bank clerk sits up late writing stories and listening to the building's night noises.

7184.label: A midnight boudoir
7184.recap: A wealthy widow keeps a handsome captain past midnight to press her feelings on him, and an angry intruder steps out from behind the curtains.

7184.label: Tableaux of the past
7184.recap: The narrator sketches a series of scenes from Haughton Hall's history, showing how the orphaned Vaura Vernon came to be raised there.

7184.label: A letter left behind
7184.recap: Trevalyon drives across London only to find his friends already departed, and reads the perfumed note they left for him.

7184.label: Breakfast at Eaton Square
7184.recap: Mrs. Tompkins packs her sharp-eyed stepdaughter off for the day so that she can receive a particular caller alone.

7184.label: Waiting at Dover
7184.recap: Lady Esmondet and Vaura wait at Dover for the newly married Colonel and his bride to land from America.

7184.label: Roses in Paris
7184.recap: In a Paris hotel Trevalyon brings Vaura a bouquet, and the three friends settle into easy company at dinner.

7184.label: A night at the theatre
7184.recap: The party draws every eye at the Theatre Francais, and Trevalyon startles himself with the drift of his own thoughts.

7184.label: A ballroom declaration
7184.recap: Between dances at a Paris ball a young baronet corners Vaura and pours out feelings she cannot return.

7184.label: A ride out of Rome
7184.recap: Troubled by the scandal hanging over his name, Trevalyon rides alone into the hills to think out what he must do.

7184.label: Christmas morning in Rome
7184.recap: Vaura wakes on Christmas Day to find a hurried farewell note among some crushed flowers, and small gifts left behind.

7184.label: The Twelfth-night dinner
7184.recap: At a glittering dinner a card is sent in to one guest, and Trevalyon arrives asking leave to address the whole company.

7184.label: Up to the north tower
7184.recap: Lionel finds Vaura singing to the crowd, and a scribbled note sends the pair climbing to the tower for the night's last surprises.

7326.label: Our Journey Commences
7326.recap: Oliver Wheatman, a Staffordshire yeoman, sets out from his family farm and into adventure.

7326.label: Losing My Virgil
7326.recap: In a town crowded with soldiers, a small mishap pitches Oliver into danger and intrigue.

7326.label: Sultan
7326.recap: Oliver and Mistress Waynflete press across country on foot, racing to reach an inn ahead of a rival.

7326.label: Pharaoh's Kine
7326.recap: The shrewd Master Freake and the Colonel trade tales of narrow escapes as Oliver learns the tricks of the game.

7326.label: In the Moorlands
7326.recap: Wounded and dazed, Oliver wakes to find himself carried to safety across the wild moorlands.

7326.label: The Double Six
7326.recap: After a stirring scrape Oliver presses on by moonlight, a little richer in luck and disguise.

7326.label: Master Freake Knows at Last
7326.recap: At the Prince's council the daring plan to march on hangs in the balance.

7326.label: Lord Brocton's Account
7326.recap: A prisoner of the villainous Lord Brocton, Oliver finds his first faint glimmer of hope.

7326.label: The Little Jack
7326.recap: Years on, happily settled at the Hanyards with Margaret, Oliver looks back with a smile.

7452.label: A Bengali childhood
7452.recap: The narrator introduces his household: an open-handed mother, a careful railway-official father, and eight children.

7452.label: The two kites
7452.recap: On a Lahore balcony a boy tests, in front of a scornful sister, whether a prayer at his little shrine will really be answered.

7452.label: A midnight warning
7452.recap: A figure at the mosquito netting sends the boy pleading with his father to catch the first train to Calcutta.

7452.label: Flight toward the Himalayas
7452.recap: Schoolboys buy English clothes as a disguise and board a train north, hoping to outwit a watchful elder brother.

7452.label: The Tiger Swami
7452.recap: Two schoolboys call on a monk famous for fighting tigers barehanded and ask him how it was done.

7452.label: Meeting the master
7452.recap: In a Benares lane he finally stands before the teacher whose face has been appearing in his visions for years.

7452.label: The cauliflower robbery
7452.recap: A gift of home-grown cauliflowers becomes the material for an unexpected lesson at the seaside hermitage.

7452.label: Taking the ochre cloth
7452.recap: His teacher dyes a length of silk and, without ceremony, receives him into the monastic order under a new name.

7452.label: A school for boys
7452.recap: Pressed to build rather than withdraw, he starts a school meant to train body, mind and spirit together.

7452.label: A tale of Babaji
7452.recap: A Sanskrit tutor recounts how a government accountant, posted to the hills, was called by name up a mountainside.

7452.label: The call to America
7452.recap: A vision of Western faces comes to him in a storeroom, and within a day an invitation to a congress in Boston arrives.

7452.label: A hermitage by the ocean
7452.recap: Returning to California he is shown a cliff-top retreat built for him while he was away, looking out over the Pacific.

7524.label: Where Germany begins
7524.recap: Tacitus fixes the country's boundaries by river and mountain and reports the ancient songs in which the tribes trace their descent from an earth-born god.

7524.label: Chiefs and companions
7524.recap: He describes the bond that ties a war-band to its leader, where the chiefs fight for victory and the companions fight for the chief.

7524.label: Marriage and household
7524.recap: He turns to marriage gifts, the raising of children, inherited feuds and the open-handed hospitality of German houses.

7524.label: Tribe by tribe
7524.recap: The survey moves along the Rhine from people to people, beginning with the disciplined Catti and their vow to go unshorn until they have killed a man.

7524.label: The edge of the north
7524.recap: Having reached the sluggish northern sea and the poorest tribes of all, Tacitus stops at the point where reports turn into fable.

7524.label: Books burned in the forum
7524.recap: Opening his second work, Tacitus recalls how praise of good men was once punished as a crime and their books burned, and explains his long silence.

7524.label: A provincial upbringing
7524.recap: Agricola's birth, his mother's steadying influence on his taste for philosophy, and his first experience of soldiering in Britain.

7524.label: The island described
7524.recap: A description of Britain's shape, climate, metals and cloudy pearls, and of the earlier Roman attempts on the island.

7524.label: The province rises
7524.recap: With the governor away, grievances harden into revolt under a leader of royal descent, and the province is only just held.

7524.label: A new governor lands
7524.recap: Agricola arrives in midsummer when the campaigning season is thought over, and marches out at once rather than wait.

7524.label: Honours and a cold welcome
7524.recap: Honours are voted at Rome while the emperor broods, and Agricola slips into the city by night to a brief, wordless reception.

7524.label: Mourning and memory
7524.recap: His death is mourned across the city amid whispers of poison, and Tacitus closes by urging that the man be remembered in the conduct of those he left.

7700.label: Waiting in the street
7700.recap: Lysistrata waits impatiently outside the Acropolis for the women she has summoned, and only her neighbour turns up.

7700.label: The proposal
7700.recap: With women gathered from several cities at last, Lysistrata asks what they would give up to stop the war, then names her price.

7700.label: An oath over wine
7700.recap: The women squabble over what to swear on before taking their vow over a great bowl of unwatered wine.

7700.label: Old men with firewood
7700.recap: A chorus of old men drags logs and fire up the hill, meaning to smoke the occupiers out.

7700.label: Water against fire
7700.recap: A chorus of women hurries up with water pitchers and answers the old men threat for threat.

7700.label: The magistrate at the gate
7700.recap: A city official arrives for treasury money, finds the doors barred, and orders his archers to make arrests.

7700.label: Years of silence
7700.recap: Lysistrata sets out what the wives endured at home while the men ran the war, and what changed her mind.

7700.label: Deserters at the postern
7700.recap: Lysistrata catches women inventing increasingly desperate excuses to slip home, and argues them back inside.

7700.label: A husband at the wall
7700.recap: A husband arrives pleading for his wife, who is coached to lead him on and give him nothing.

7700.label: A herald from Sparta
7700.recap: A Spartan messenger turns up with news that the same trouble has broken out in his own city.

7700.label: Arbitration
7700.recap: Delegates from both sides are brought before Lysistrata, who reminds them what each once owed the other.

7700.label: After the feast
7700.recap: The banqueters come out warm with wine and the evening closes in singing and dancing.

7735.label: Thames Court in the rain
7735.recap: A shabby errand-runner brings a book to a dying woman in a riverside alehouse, and a small boy is left in the landlady's keeping.

7735.label: A name and an education
7735.recap: Grown to twelve and christened Paul, the boy amuses the alehouse with pickpocket pranks until his guardian resolves to buy him some Latin.

7735.label: Lessons in criticism
7735.recap: Paul calls on his tutor and asks to become a reviewer, and receives a solemn lecture on the three great branches of the critic's art.

7735.label: The House of Correction
7735.recap: Locked up for a theft he did not commit, Paul finds an old acquaintance among the prisoners and waits in vain to be cleared.

7735.label: A philosopher in prison
7735.recap: A polished fellow prisoner, now styling himself a philosopher and a moderate Whig, begins telling Paul the story of his own life.

7735.label: Warlock Manor-house
7735.recap: The story turns to a quiet country house, its idle squire, his brilliant lawyer brother, and the squire's lovely daughter Lucy.

7735.label: Three riders and a hedge
7735.recap: Three masked horsemen wait on a moonlit common for a nobleman's carriage, and their captain conducts the business with startling courtesy.

7735.label: Captain Clifford at Bath
7735.recap: A dashing stranger becomes the most admired man in Bath and devotes himself entirely to Lucy Brandon, to the annoyance of a rival.

7735.label: The new judge
7735.recap: Raised to the bench and briefly freed from pain, Brandon grows thrifty and receives a ragged visitor with information to sell.

7735.label: Riding for the prisoners
7735.recap: Clifford learns that comrades taken in his place are being moved to a county jail, and sets off in disguise to intercept them.

7735.label: A night alone
7735.recap: Alone in a panelled country chamber, Brandon broods over his career and over the son he has never stopped trying to find.

7735.label: Twenty years later
7735.recap: The tale closes far from England, with a respected citizen and his wife whose earlier lives their neighbours never learn.

8486.label: The nervous sacristan
8486.recap: An English collector spends a day photographing a Pyrenean church and notices that its guardian behaves like a hunted man.

8486.label: Orphan at Aswarby Hall
8486.recap: A newly orphaned boy arrives to live with an elderly recluse who asks his exact age twice in two minutes.

8486.label: A print on approval
8486.recap: A museum curator orders an unremarkable engraving of a manor house from a London dealer's catalogue.

8486.label: The witch and the ash
8486.recap: In 1690 a Suffolk squire testifies that he watched a village woman cutting twigs from the ash-tree by his house at full moon.

8486.label: A room in Viborg
8486.recap: An English researcher settles on a long first-floor room at an old Danish inn to work through church papers.

8486.label: A traveller in Sweden
8486.recap: A solitary, over-curious Englishman goes to a Swedish manor to research an old family for a book of travels.

8486.label: The landlord's story
8486.recap: Pressed for what he knows, an innkeeper reluctantly tells of two men who went poaching in the Count's wood one summer night.

8486.label: A golfing holiday
8486.recap: At a college dinner a precise young professor plans a week on the East Coast and is teased about ghosts by a blunt colleague.

8486.label: The abbot's hidden gold
8486.recap: An antiquary translates a Latin passage about an abbot who hid a fortune and left only a riddling clue to it.

8486.label: Down into the well
8486.recap: By full moonlight two men fit a rope over the well wheel and climb down the stones inside, counting the steps.

8492.label: The Repairer of Reputations
8492.recap: In a strange near-future New York, a man unhinged by a forbidden play nurses a secret claim to a throne.

8492.label: The Mask
8492.recap: A sculptor discovers a fluid that turns living things to marble, amid a love triangle shadowed by the cursed play.

8492.label: In the Court of the Dragon
8492.recap: Having read the dreaded play, a man feels himself pursued through a Paris church by a sinister organist.

8492.label: The Yellow Sign
8492.recap: A painter and his model are drawn toward horror by a corpse-like churchyard watchman and a fatal symbol.

8492.label: The Demoiselle d'Ys
8492.recap: A hunter lost on the lonely moors slips into a vanished world of falconry and a lady out of the past.

8492.label: The Prophets' Paradise
8492.recap: A series of brief, dreamlike prose-poems forms a haunting interlude.

8492.label: The Street of the Four Winds
8492.recap: A stray cat leads a painter to a quiet, sorrowful discovery in a garret across the way.

8492.label: The Street of the First Shell
8492.recap: Amid the Prussian siege and bombardment of Paris, lovers cling together as the shells fall.

8492.label: The Street of Our Lady of the Fields
8492.recap: An American art student finds love in the Latin Quarter of Paris.

8492.label: Rue Barrée
8492.recap: The art students of the Quarter vie over an unattainable young woman known to them only as Rue Barrée.

8800.label: Lost in the dark wood
8800.recap: A traveller strays from his road at the midpoint of life, is turned back by three beasts, and meets a shade who offers another way.

8800.label: The gate and its warning
8800.recap: They pass beneath an inscription that promises no hope, and find first the souls who lived without praise or blame.

8800.label: Blown on the black wind
8800.recap: In a place where the light is silent, a ceaseless storm drives the souls of lovers, and one of them agrees to tell her story.

8800.label: A voice in the flame
8800.recap: From inside a tongue of fire an old Greek captain describes how he talked his crew into sailing past the last landmark of the known world.

8800.label: The count in the ice
8800.recap: Frozen into the lowest region, a gnawing sinner lifts his head to recount how he and his sons were shut up in a tower.

8800.label: The emperor of the pit
8800.recap: At the very bottom the travellers come face to face with the three-faced giant whose beating wings keep the whole depth frozen.

8800.label: Under open sky again
8800.recap: Out of the darkness at last, the poet sees dawn colours and four unfamiliar stars, and an old guardian appears at his side.

8800.label: A dream of the eagle
8800.recap: Asleep near dawn on the mountainside, the poet dreams an eagle snatches him upward into fire, and wakes somewhere he did not lie down.

8800.label: A shower of flowers
8800.recap: Amid singing and scattered blossoms a veiled woman appears on the car, and the poet turns to speak to his guide and finds him gone.

8800.label: Beginning the ascent
8800.recap: The poet warns that what he saw above is beyond retelling, calls on Apollo for help, and begins the last stage of his song.

8800.label: The last looking
8800.recap: A prayer made on the traveller's behalf is answered, and he lifts his eyes into a light that outruns memory and speech.

8954.label: Audley Court
8954.recap: An old rambling manor house in Essex is described, down to the disused well hidden away in its shrubbery.

8954.label: The baronet proposes
8954.recap: Sir Michael offers his hand to the young governess, and she answers with a vehemence that unsettles him.

8954.label: Aboard the Argus
8954.recap: A young passenger sailing home from Australia counts the days, while a fellow traveller confesses her dread of what may wait ashore.

8954.label: The lady's maid
8954.recap: Phoebe Marks slips out to meet her cousin by the old well, then takes him through her mistress's rooms.

8954.label: A barrister without briefs
8954.recap: Idle Robert Audley is introduced, and on an errand in the city he is almost knocked down by an old school friend.

8954.label: A week in the country
8954.recap: A year on, Robert coaxes his low-spirited friend down to the village of Audley for a week's fishing.

8954.label: Storm at the inn
8954.recap: A thunderstorm breaks over the inn, and a teasing remark sends one of the friends out into the rain.

8954.label: Nobody by the stream
8954.recap: Robert wakes on the riverbank to find his companion gone, and nobody in the village can say where.

8954.label: Southampton in the snow
8954.recap: Robert travels through winter weather to look in on his friend's small son and finds a stranger keeping the house.

8954.label: Back to the Court
8954.recap: A letter about his uncle's illness brings Robert walking up the darkening lane to Audley Court.

8954.label: A letter burned
8954.recap: My lady throws a threatening letter into the fire and paces her room, thinking hard about the man who wrote it.

8954.label: A cottage by the river
8954.recap: Two years later the story closes at a riverside cottage, with the household that has gathered there.

9473.label: An inn at Tyniec
9473.recap: A travelling knight and his young nephew drink with merchants and tell them where the wars have taken them.

9473.label: A song at the inn
9473.recap: The princess's court arrives and a small girl sings on a bench, and the young knight cannot stop looking at her.

9473.label: A giant on the road
9473.recap: On the road to Krakow the party sees an enormous horseman motionless on a hill, and the courtiers begin to pray.

9473.label: Alone in the tower
9473.recap: Shut in a castle cell while the city mourns its queen, Zbyszko waits for an uncle who does not come back.

9473.label: The market square
9473.recap: Krakow fills at dawn for a beheading, the crowd's mood turns ugly, and the prisoner is walked out to the scaffold.

9473.label: Home to Bogdaniec
9473.recap: Back on their own ruined land, uncle and nephew count the fields, the cattle and the debts they have inherited.

9473.label: The neighbour's daughter
9473.recap: Macko rides to Zgorzelice to patch up a quarrel and finds Jagienka alone and unusually quiet.

9473.label: A challenge postponed
9473.recap: A foreign knight and Zbyszko are made to swear they will not fight without permission, and ride off through wolf country.

9473.label: Deep winter
9473.recap: The court leaves the forest lodge for Ciechanow and Zbyszko, still too weak to ride, is left behind to mend and to miss his wife.

9473.label: Inside the castle gates
9473.recap: Jurand of Spychow walks alone into a Teutonic castle yard, jeered by the soldiers, and is shown to a door.

9473.label: Storm in the wilderness
9473.recap: Macko's train pushes into the forest at daybreak as gales tear at the pines and the daylight keeps going out.

9473.label: The road to Spychow
9473.recap: Zbyszko carries the rescued Danusia the last miles home through country where every door opens to help them.

9911.label: A drawer of old letters
9911.recap: A weary man past fifty sits alone by his hearth after a brilliant evening, rummaging through old papers, and finds a small forgotten box.

9911.label: An idle day in Frankfort
9911.recap: A young Russian with hours to kill before his coach leaves wanders into a quiet Italian confectionery shop for a glass of lemonade.

9911.label: Quick, quick, save him
9911.recap: A frantic girl drags the stranger into a back room where her young brother lies senseless, and he improvises what help he can.

9911.label: The outing to Soden
9911.recap: A pleasure party's country dinner is spoiled when a drunken officer at the next table helps himself to a toast and to a rose.

9911.label: Sorting cherries
9911.recap: In the evening garden Sanin finds Gemma picking over fruit, and neither of them manages to say quite what they mean.

9911.label: Walking as in a dream
9911.recap: Two people walk home barely able to speak, and one of them recounts the scene that ended an engagement.

9911.label: The rich lady's questions
9911.recap: In Wiesbaden a blunt, wealthy woman cross-examines Sanin about his marriage plans and pronounces them delightful.

9911.label: Off the road
9911.recap: A morning ride leaves the path for bogs, streams and fences, and turns into a headlong race toward the mountains.

9911.label: Frankfort thirty years on
9911.recap: Returning to a city he no longer recognises, Sanin hunts for anyone who still remembers a family that once lived there.

9911.label: The summer I was sixteen
9911.recap: A second story begins as a boy at a Moscow country house drifts through a golden summer, until new neighbours take the empty lodge.

9911.label: The porter Gerasim
9911.recap: A third story opens in the household of a miserly old widow, whose most remarkable servant is a deaf and mute giant of enormous strength.

9911.label: The road home
9911.recap: A huge man walks out of Moscow by night along the highroad, bound for the village he was taken from.

10002.label: A fishing holiday
10002.recap: Two friends camp beside an unmapped river in a bare corner of Ireland and go looking for good water.

10002.label: The diary begins
10002.recap: An elderly recluse explains that he lives alone with his sister and his dog in a house the locals will not go near.

10002.label: The candles change colour
10002.recap: Reading late in his study, the old man watches the light turn green and then red, and finds himself somewhere else entirely.

10002.label: The arena of shapes
10002.recap: Carried through a gorge, he comes out above a vast ring of mountains with something enormous standing at its centre.

10002.label: Something in the ravine
10002.recap: Stones fall from the cliff of the pit behind the house, the dog will not stop barking, and the man goes down to look.

10002.label: A run for the door
10002.recap: A landslip in the pit sends the old man and his sister racing back across the garden with company behind them.

10002.label: Shoring the door
10002.recap: He props the weakest door with timber, then climbs to the roof to see what can be done from above.

10002.label: Down among the vaults
10002.recap: Candle in hand, he works through the enormous cellars he has never properly explored in all his years there.

10002.label: The rope and the hole
10002.recap: Curiosity beats fear at last, and he lowers himself down the rift to listen at the dark opening in its wall.

10002.label: The quiet sea
10002.recap: A soft mist takes the study away and leaves him standing on the shore of an enormous, silent ocean.

10002.label: The light goes out
10002.recap: Watching from the window, he sees the racing sun darken from copper to a heavy, blood-tinged purple.

10002.label: Back in the chair
10002.recap: He comes to himself in his own study with the sun rising, and goes looking for his dog.

10002.label: Closing the book
10002.recap: The reader of the manuscript sets it down and asks his friend the one question that matters to him.

10102.label: Standing in at the consulate
10102.recap: An Englishman minding a consulate in a sweltering Italian port receives a yacht owner who wants a small favour written in Italian.

10102.label: A tour of the yacht
10102.recap: Shown round his host's floating palace after dinner, the narrator sees two things he was clearly not meant to see.

10102.label: Police at the consulate
10102.recap: Detectives puzzle over a break-in while the narrator works out how thoroughly he was used, and the yacht slips away.

10102.label: A room over the water
10102.recap: A former servant met by chance in London leads the narrator to a top-floor room in a grim Lambeth street.

10102.label: A face at a Scottish house
10102.recap: At a shooting-lodge house party the narrator comes face to face with the yacht owner, introduced under an entirely different name.

10102.label: Something in Rannoch Wood
10102.recap: A cry in the dark brings him to a figure lying across a path, and to someone moving quietly among the trees.

10102.label: A visitor asks for help
10102.recap: The daughter of the house comes to him alone and, with great difficulty, begins to ask a favour she is ashamed of.

10102.label: A man who should be dead
10102.recap: In a London restaurant he confronts a man he had already seen laid out in a mortuary.

10102.label: North to find the truth
10102.recap: Unable to let one question rest, the narrator resolves to travel to Finland and learn about the Baron and his niece for himself.

10102.label: The castle on the lake
10102.recap: A night boat carries him down a lonely river to an old fortress where a lantern signal is waiting for him.

10102.label: Shaking off a shadow
10102.recap: Followed through the Russian capital, he doubles back through dark streets and reaches the door of a powerful stranger.

10102.label: Two years afterwards
10102.recap: Looking back from a quiet distance, the narrator settles the accounts of everyone whose path crossed his.

10148.label: A wager in the greenwood
10148.recap: An eighteen-year-old Robin sets out for an archery match and is taunted by a party of foresters feasting under an oak.

10148.label: The stranger on the bridge
10148.recap: Hunting for adventure, Robin meets a very tall stranger at a narrow log bridge and neither will stand aside.

10148.label: A warrant nobody wants
10148.recap: The Sheriff's messenger rides to Lincoln and stops at an inn where a loud, thirsty tinker is drinking with foresters.

10148.label: Shooting for the golden arrow
10148.recap: The best bowmen in England gather at Nottingham for the Sheriff's grand match and its glittering prize.

10148.label: A cart and a halter
10148.recap: One of Robin's men is brought out of Nottingham castle in a cart with a rope about his neck while the town looks on.

10148.label: Robin turns butcher
10148.recap: Restless after a quiet year in the forest, Robin walks out to the highroad and falls in with a young butcher bound for market.

10148.label: Seeking the curtal friar
10148.recap: Robin arms himself in mail beneath his Lincoln green and rides out with four men to find a famously stout riverside friar.

10148.label: A page from London
10148.recap: A richly dressed boy on a white horse rides down into Nottinghamshire carrying the Queen's business with him.

10148.label: The King comes to town
10148.recap: Nottingham throws up arches and banners and builds a throne in the Guild Hall for a royal visit.

10148.label: Parting on the path
10148.recap: Robin and Little John split up to seek separate adventures, and Robin walks on alone down a shaded forest road.

10148.label: The teller draws back
10148.recap: The storyteller pauses to warn that the merry days are over, then turns to Robin's last return to Sherwood.

10441.label: A ruined young gentleman
10441.recap: A young man wiped out by a market crash takes stock of his useless accomplishments and decides his conjuring may be his only living.

10441.label: On the bridle path
10441.recap: A bolting horse throws its rider in the park, and the man on the bench steps out of the thicket to catch it.

10441.label: The green mouse
10441.recap: A neighbour knocks at his door to ask whether pea-green mice exist, and gets a far more startling answer than she expected.

10441.label: The company is founded
10441.recap: Three founders vote a small company into being and hear how a watch-sized machine claims to connect anyone to their destined match.

10441.label: The stuck elevator
10441.recap: A maid fetches entirely the wrong man, and the household's temperamental elevator jams halfway up the shaft with him inside.

10441.label: A card with a mouse
10441.recap: On the way to a weekend party one friend describes the odd young woman who called at his office and asked to experiment on him.

10441.label: The cross-town car
10441.recap: One friend is seized by the conviction that everything happening has happened before, and starts announcing what will come next.

10441.label: Trouble in the cellar
10441.recap: A cry from the dark cellar of a shut-up summer house sends him running downstairs with a match and a shovel.

10441.label: Confession in the gymnasium
10441.recap: A furious father interrogates his identical triplet daughters about which of them meddled with the instrument in his locked laboratory.

10441.label: The paper hanger
10441.recap: A girl stranded on a workbench tries desperately to keep the young workman talking so he will not need the table.

10441.label: A palace of marble
10441.recap: The company is capitalised, a vast headquarters rises on Madison Avenue, and circulars promise happy marriage by machinery for twenty-five dollars.

10441.label: The last holdout
10441.recap: The one remaining unmarried sister refuses the machine, sews herself a mermaid costume, and paddles off alone to rehearse.

10636.label: An address to all readers
10636.recap: The book opens by summoning every rank of reader and promising to set down things seen as seen and things heard as heard.

10636.label: Out of Constantinople
10636.recap: Two Venetian brothers lay in a store of jewels and cross the Black Sea on a trading venture.

10636.label: An errand to the Pope
10636.recap: Pleased by what the brothers tell him of the Latins, the Great Kaan makes them envoys and dictates a letter westward.

10636.label: Asking leave to go
10636.recap: After long service the Venetians begin angling for permission to leave, and an unexpected errand changes their prospects.

10636.label: A challenge in Baudas
10636.recap: A ruler seizes on a line of scripture and gives the Christians of his city ten days to make good on it.

10636.label: Riders in the dark
10636.recap: A hot plain is described where mud-walled towns guard against raiders said to travel inside a darkness they conjure themselves.

10636.label: A garden between mountains
10636.recap: A mountain chief walls off a valley and fills it with fruit, music and running honey, admitting only those he chooses.

10636.label: A king is chosen
10636.recap: Chinghis is raised up by the Tartars, takes province after province, and sends an embassy that receives a furious answer.

10636.label: Battle on the plain
10636.recap: Two vast armies form up at dawn, and the Tartar custom of singing and playing before the drums sound is described.

10636.label: Inside the winter palace
10636.recap: The walls, gates and eight armouries of the Kaan's palace at Cambaluc are paced out enclosure by enclosure.

10636.label: Money made from bark
10636.recap: The imperial mint turns mulberry bark into sealed paper notes that nobody in the empire dares refuse.

10636.label: Household gods and souls
10636.recap: The volume closes on the daily worship, the ideas about the soul, and the courteous manners of the people of Cathay.

11030.label: Six happy years
11030.recap: The narrator describes a sheltered early childhood, her skilled father and her formidable grandmother, and the day she learned what she was.

11030.label: Hiring day
11030.recap: New Year's in the South is described as the day people are hired out or sold, and families are broken apart on the auction ground.

11030.label: Benjamin's farewell
11030.recap: A young uncle who fought back against his owner comes secretly to say goodbye before making for the north.

11030.label: Fifteen years old
11030.recap: At fifteen the narrator becomes the target of her master's relentless pressure, with no law and no mistress to shelter her.

11030.label: A desperate choice
11030.recap: To defeat her master's newest scheme the narrator makes a decision she tells the reader plainly she is ashamed of.

11030.label: The flight
11030.recap: Learning her children are to be taken to the plantation, she works through the evening, waits until midnight, and climbs out of a window.

11030.label: The garret
11030.recap: She is hidden in a crawl space above a shed, too low to stand in, and bores a small hole to let in air and see the street.

11030.label: Letters from the north
11030.recap: From her hiding place she arranges for letters postmarked hundreds of miles away to reach her master, then listens to him read one aloud.

11030.label: Seven years in the dark
11030.recap: After years in the crawl space her limbs and health are failing and the roof is leaking, and she begins to plan a way out.

11030.label: Aboard the boat
11030.recap: She reaches a waiting vessel at night, parts from the friends who risked everything for her, and finds an unexpected companion in the cabin.

11030.label: Still not safe
11030.recap: Settled in the North with a kind employer, she still cannot step outside without fear, and news arrives from home.

11030.label: How the story ends
11030.recap: The narrator sums up plainly what freedom has and has not given her, and closes on the memory of her grandmother.

11339.label: Grapes out of reach
11339.recap: A fox jumps and jumps for fruit he cannot reach, then decides aloud that he never wanted it.

11339.label: The mice hold council
11339.recap: The mice debate a brilliant scheme for staying safe from the cat until one old member asks who will carry it out.

11339.label: A wolf finds a grievance
11339.recap: A wolf hunts for a respectable excuse to justify what he has already decided to do to a stray lamb.

11339.label: A small promise repaid
11339.recap: A lion spares a mouse who has woken him, amused by its promise that it will one day return the favour.

11339.label: The boy who cried wolf
11339.recap: A bored shepherd boy discovers how entertaining it is to raise a false alarm, and repeats the joke.

11339.label: Frogs ask for a king
11339.recap: Discontented frogs petition Jupiter for a ruler, and find the first one he sends far too quiet for their liking.

11339.label: The body on strike
11339.recap: The parts of the body decide they will no longer work to feed a belly they consider idle.

11339.label: A guest with a story
11339.recap: A thief loitering at an inn spots something he wants and starts telling the innkeeper about a strange affliction of his.

11339.label: Shelter from the storm
11339.recap: Three animals given warmth and food by a stranger decide to repay him by each contributing something to human life.

11339.label: Asleep beside the well
11339.recap: An exhausted traveller falls asleep on the edge of a deep well and is woken by an unexpected visitor.

11982.label: Born in Johnstown
11982.recap: She sets down her arrival in 1815 into a lawyer's household and sketches the reserved father, self-possessed mother and Revolutionary grandfather she grew up among.

11982.label: The darkened parlour
11982.recap: Sitting on her grieving father's knee after her only brother's death, she resolves to become everything the son had been to him.

11982.label: Boarding school at Troy
11982.recap: Sent to a famous girls' seminary instead of the college she wanted, she takes up French, music and dancing among a hundred other girls.

11982.label: A secret upstairs
11982.recap: At her cousin's house a group of girls is led to a third-floor room and asked to listen to a young woman's account of her life in slavery.

11982.label: A wedding on a Friday
11982.recap: After breaking and renewing her engagement she marries with the word obey struck out of the service, and sails for England within days.

11982.label: Lodgings in Queen Street
