25344.recap: On the colony's one holiday Hester and Pearl come into a market-place crowded with countryfolk, sailors and the whole town.

25344.label: After the sermon
25344.recap: The Election Sermon ends and the congregation pours into the street, still full of what they have heard, as the procession re-forms.

25344.label: What the town remembered
25344.recap: Afterwards the townspeople argue over what they saw and what it meant, and the later lives of everyone concerned are set down.

25440.label: A note on the road
25440.recap: Two young cavalry officers riding home on furlough are met by the family overseer carrying an urgent written plea for help.

25440.label: Scouting the mansion
25440.recap: Deck creeps up to the neighbouring plantation house alone and finds the situation there is not at all what the note described.

25440.label: The sentry at the bridge
25440.recap: Approaching his own family's creek bridge, Deck spots a guard and decides to try taking him single-handed.

25440.label: A cry from the porch
25440.recap: A scream from the house sends Deck sprinting across open ground toward the women held there.

25440.label: Hunting the missing silver
25440.recap: After the fighting, the family combs the ground for stolen household valuables and pieces together who took what.

25440.label: Voices in the dark woods
25440.recap: Overhearing three Confederates at night, Deck decides to follow rather than seize them, hoping to find what they are guarding.

25440.label: The army swings wide
25440.recap: The narrative pulls back to the wider campaign as Rosecrans feints at the centre while moving his weight around the enemy's flank.

25440.label: Out through the floor
25440.recap: Held at a hostile plantation, Artie digs his way clear and sets about recovering his horse without waking the house.

25440.label: The vanishing horsemen
25440.recap: An entire enemy detachment seems to evaporate behind a hedge, and Deck spreads his regiment out to find where it went.

25440.label: Blocked on the mountain trail
25440.recap: A landslide seals a narrow mountain path at both ends, leaving a platoon and its horses stranded on a ledge.

25440.label: A very calm captor
25440.recap: Deck loses his pistol to a coolly spoken stranger who marches him into the creek at gunpoint.

25440.label: Running for the timber
25440.recap: With three horses and a sudden opening, Deck rides hard for the shelter of the woods as the alarm goes up behind him.

25440.label: Reunions afterward
25440.recap: With the war over, the regiment keeps meeting each year, and its old commander offers the same toast every time.

25502.label: A king from the sea
25502.recap: A child drifts to the Danish shore in a treasure-laden boat and grows up to found a royal line.

25502.label: The night watch in Heorot
25502.recap: A visiting champion lies weaponless among his sleeping men while the creature that empties the hall comes for it again.

25502.label: An emperor falls asleep
25502.recap: A beloved Roman emperor rests during a hunt and returns to the city in a silence nobody can explain.

25502.label: An oath at a deathbed
25502.recap: A dying Danish king binds a trusted friend by fearful oaths to guard his three young children.

25502.label: Envoys in the orchard
25502.recap: Messengers bearing olive branches find Charlemagne enthroned beneath a pine and offer him submission and gifts.

25502.label: The Isle of Saints
25502.recap: The tale opens on a newly Christian Ireland, rich in abbeys and hermits but still troubled by war.

25502.label: The boy who took arms
25502.recap: A king's nephew claims a warrior's weapons at seven years old, choosing great fame over a long life.

25502.label: Christmas at Carlisle
25502.recap: Restless among his feasting knights, King Arthur vows not to rise from the table until some adventure offers itself.

25502.label: Twelve chosen companions
25502.recap: A boy prince grows up among twelve close companions, one of them devoted and one hiding envy behind affection.

25502.label: A guest for dinner
25502.recap: Robin refuses to eat until his three closest men find him a wealthy traveller to pay for the hospitality.

25502.label: An ungovernable son
25502.recap: A pious mother tries and fails to steer her wild, golden-haired second son toward a life in the cloister.

25502.label: A minstrel at the feast
25502.recap: To reach a bride pledged against her will, the young Saxon enters her wedding hall disguised as a singer.

25551.label: Under the beech tree
25551.recap: Two sisters idle away a hot afternoon on the lawn, one sewing steadily and one acting out balcony scenes and dreaming of the stage.

25551.label: Twilight on the porch
25551.recap: Olive broods alone on the steps until her lame youngest sister coaxes her into saying what is really troubling her.

25551.label: News of a nutting party
25551.recap: The twins burst in with news of a school outing, and by suppertime one of them is trying to sneak into the house soaking wet.

25551.label: A stranger at the door
25551.recap: Grief settles over the household, and that same evening an imperious old gentleman arrives from three hundred miles away and refuses to be turned out.

25551.label: Midnight by the fire
25551.recap: Mother and daughter sit up long past midnight, and each finally tells the other what she has been keeping back.

25551.label: An empty place at supper
25551.recap: One sister does not come to supper, and the girls spend a frightened night alone in the house waiting for her.

25551.label: A mother's long-kept story
25551.recap: Mrs. Dering tells the story of two Virginia households, a pitying engagement, and a friend who vanished on the eve of a wedding.

25551.label: A year later
25551.recap: A year on, the twins grumble in the yard about the young boarder who is coming to stay and how he will spoil their fun.

25551.label: Arrival at Congreve Hall
25551.recap: Olive travels south and is met at the depot by her small sister, who has been sent ahead to grow strong.

25551.label: An evening at the opera
25551.recap: A quiet afternoon of sketching leads to an evening at the opera that turns out very differently from the one Olive expected.

25551.label: The absent sister's account
25551.recap: Nursed at home and changed by it, Ernestine finally tells her sisters what happened to her during the months away.

25551.label: Christmas, five years later
25551.recap: Five years on, the old house is lit from attic to basement for Christmas Eve, with small children turning somersaults in the hall.

25695.label: Two shocks in one day
25695.recap: A wealthy town reads in its newspaper of an enormous jewel robbery and, hours later, of a leading family's daughter eloping with a man far beneath her.

25695.label: The heiress keeps her head
25695.recap: While her household runs wild over the burglary, the robbed young mistress calmly drinks her coffee and waits for the officials to arrive.

25695.label: The Lamottes come calling
25695.recap: A prominent mill owner and his handsome son arrive to commiserate and to offer their services in hunting the missing jewels.

25695.label: A letter kept sealed
25695.recap: Alone at her window, the heiress turns over a puzzling note from her closest friend that she has promised not to open before sunset.

25695.label: A detective from the tree
25695.recap: A shabby stranger who has been listening from a branch introduces himself in the drawing room and explains what really brought him to town.

25695.label: Lunch at Mapleton
25695.recap: A proud family sits at table with the coarse new son-in-law they cannot be rid of, until a visitor is announced at the door.

25695.label: Dismissing the detective
25695.recap: The heiress orders her hired investigator to drop the case, and discovers that he has terms of his own to propose.

25695.label: A night at the saloon
25695.recap: Hangers-on at a riverside bar ply a boastful, well-dressed man with drink and steer him toward mischief.

25695.label: What the dog found
25695.recap: On a rainy morning a doctor's bulldog refuses to come away from something half buried in the cellar of a burnt-out house next door.

25695.label: The inquest in the mud
25695.recap: Jurors, officials and reluctant witnesses gather ankle-deep in a flooded cellar, and a weapon is lifted out of the shallow grave.

25695.label: The trial opens
25695.recap: The courtroom is packed, a fair-haired stranger sits beside the prisoner, and the defence's chief counsel is unaccountably missing.

25695.label: After the drama ended
25695.recap: Beside a winter fire the whole tangled business is talked through at last, and the survivors' futures are quietly settled.

25789.label: Where the gift came from
25789.recap: The biographer weighs up the Brontë parents and argues about what the children inherited from each of them.

25789.label: A motherless nursery
25789.recap: Left largely to themselves in a remote parsonage, six small children become each other's only company.

25789.label: The clergy daughters' school
25789.recap: The charity school at Cowan's Bridge is described from its damp stone rooms to its proud, well-meaning founder.

25789.label: Back on the moors
25789.recap: Home again at Haworth, the surviving children invent kingdoms and magazines by the kitchen fire.

25789.label: Sent away to school
25789.recap: At sixteen Emily is sent to Roe Head, and her fierce attachment to her own moors is put to the test.

25789.label: Alone at Haworth
25789.recap: While her sisters earn their bread away from home, Emily keeps house, and a surviving letter shows what her brother values.

25789.label: Brussels
25789.recap: The two sisters enter a Brussels boarding school, where Charlotte sees beauty and Emily sees only exile.

25789.label: Called home
25789.recap: A death in the family brings the sisters back to Haworth, and Emily volunteers to be the one who stays.

25789.label: Waiting for bad news
25789.recap: Anxiety settles over the parsonage as the father's sight fails and the brother's conduct grows harder to ignore.

25789.label: The hidden poems
25789.recap: Emily writes verse in stolen minutes between chores, and her sister comes upon the manuscript book by accident.

25789.label: The heaviest months
25789.recap: Debts, blindness and her brother's collapse crowd the house during the very months Wuthering Heights is being written.

25789.label: The last illness
25789.recap: A cough takes hold after a family bereavement, and the strongest of the household refuses every remedy and every question.

25810.label: Noon at the Cross-roads
25810.recap: A drowsing post-office porch in blazing heat, presided over by an enormous and immovable storekeeper.

25810.label: The silent stranger
25810.recap: The mysterious newcomer from a mountain hollow buys a few supplies and leaves without offering a word.

25810.label: The cabin on the hillside
25810.recap: Help reaches the lonely cabin, and the storekeeper sits by the bed doing what little he knows how to do.

25810.label: The county talks
25810.recap: Word of what Tom has decided to do next spreads through the mountains and nobody quite believes it.

25810.label: New rooms
25810.recap: Tom offers the little girl brighter rooms and finds she would rather keep the plain ones she knows.

25810.label: The mountain acres
25810.recap: How a distant branch of the family came by thousands of worthless acres, and what was found under them.

25810.label: Growing up in Hamlin
25810.recap: Seasons of blossom, chestnuts and firelight as the child grows up beside the man who took her in.

25810.label: A New England mill town
25810.recap: Far to the north, a portrait of a narrow, church-going factory village and the lives lived inside it.

25810.label: Supper in Washington
25810.recap: In a small rented room in the capital the claimants gather over hot biscuits to plan their campaign.

25810.label: On the marble corridors
25810.recap: Tom becomes a familiar figure at the Capitol and learns how hard the proof he needs is to come by.

25810.label: A claim of his own
25810.recap: The small mountain man pursues his own claim in Washington, growing shabbier and hungrier by the week.

25810.label: Spring at the Cross-roads
25810.recap: In apple-blossom weather the whole county crowds the post-office to welcome travellers home again.

25868.label: A fishing trip spoiled
25868.recap: Sheltering from rain in an old cabin, a station agent's son overhears a plot against a train.

25868.label: First post alone
25868.recap: Sent to take charge of a small station at night, Alex meets fog, a landslide and a silent wire.

25868.label: The tinkering friend
25868.recap: Alex's telegraph chum Jack takes an instrument apart, earns a scolding, and is soon woken by a fire.

25868.label: The missing cash-box
25868.recap: Trusted with a safe combination, Jack finds himself suspected when money and then the box disappear.

25868.label: Woods on fire
25868.recap: The two boys picnic at the old cabin and find the forest burning between them and home.

25868.label: A storm and a runaway
25868.recap: On a night of rain and broken wires, an urgent call from up the line reaches Alex's station.

25868.label: The ghost at the junction
25868.recap: Promoted to the despatching office, Alex hears from an operator convinced something walks his platform.

25868.label: Thumbs on a train
25868.recap: Travelling on holiday, the boys notice two soldiers holding a silent conversation across the aisle.

25868.label: The dude operator
25868.recap: A dandified new operator is laughed at in the office and posted to the roughest station on the wire.

25868.label: Out with the graders
25868.recap: Alex takes a telegraph car on the prairie as two railroads race for a mountain pass.

25868.label: Twenty miles by pony
25868.recap: Alex rides alone across the prairie to a bridge camp where trouble is said to be brewing.

25868.label: Night at the viaduct
25868.recap: Alone at a box-car station, Wilson finds the wire cut and two strangers moving in the dark.

25911.label: Where the quarrel begins
25911.recap: The author traces the dispute back past the war itself to eighteenth-century ideas about trade, colonies and navies.

25911.label: Two irreconcilable claims
25911.recap: One nation insists a subject can never change allegiance; the other insists the flag covers every man beneath it.

25911.label: After the connection breaks
25911.recap: Independence leaves both sides guessing what commercial relation should replace an empire that no longer exists.

25911.label: An envoy sent to London
25911.recap: Seizures of American ships bound for France and her colonies send a special mission across the Atlantic for redress.

25911.label: A paper handed across the table
25911.recap: At the moment of signature the British negotiators produce a reservation, and a French decree turns a treaty into waste paper.

25911.label: A frigate stopped at sea
25911.recap: An American warship leaving Hampton Roads is hailed with a despatch, refuses a demand, and is fired into.

25911.label: A night meeting off Cape Henry
25911.recap: With orders written in the language of injured honour, two ships of very unequal force meet in the dark.

25911.label: Arguing over a navy
25911.recap: Congress debates whether ships or privateers should defend the coast, and narrowly declines to build the frigates.

25911.label: Weighing the board
25911.recap: Before the fighting starts, the author lays out what each side can and cannot do by sea and by land.

25911.label: Five ships put to sea
25911.recap: A squadron sails within an hour of the news, chases a convoy across the Atlantic, and finds fog instead.

25911.label: A duel of manoeuvre
25911.recap: Two frigates circle each other for three quarters of an hour, each refusing to be raked, before closing to pistol shot.

25911.label: An audacious crossing
25911.recap: A general with a small column and captured correspondence gambles on assault, and finds the gates opened to him.

25911.label: The cheapest victory
25911.recap: The author closes by defending a captain who fought at a distance, and by noting how loosely the coast was watched.

25919.label: The strategic window
25919.recap: Miss Mapp takes up her post at the garden-room window, from which nothing in her small town escapes her.

25919.label: Two bachelors observed
25919.recap: She catalogues the morning habits of the two retired officers opposite and puzzles over their late-burning lamps.

25919.label: Sketchers on the steps
25919.recap: Summer brings artists to every corner of Tilling, and Miss Mapp arranges to be beautifully visible among them.

25919.label: Roses from the curtains
25919.recap: Diva secretly cuts flowers out of her old chintz curtains to trim a dress nobody could possibly guess the origin of.

25919.label: A rival costume
25919.recap: Diva's finished dress arrives just as she catches sight of something alarmingly similar going down the street.

25919.label: Whisky and Roman roads
25919.recap: On a squally October evening the two friends settle down with their separate bottles and their separate grievances.

25919.label: Waiting for the tram
25919.recap: All Tilling gathers to watch the returning tram after three men leave for the sand dunes.

25919.label: A sermon on the seasons
25919.recap: A pointed sermon reopens the town's long quarrel about whether summer-time is to be recognised at all.

25919.label: The united services
25919.recap: The two officers, chastened, agree to keep their disagreements safely below challenge-pitch.

25919.label: A problem of ten
25919.recap: An evening bridge party threatens to leave two players cut out, and Miss Mapp calculates who it will not be.

25919.label: Fog and a visitor
25919.recap: Tilling shops all morning in the rain hoping for a glimpse of a much-discussed foreign guest.

25919.label: Christmas in church
25919.recap: Miss Mapp sings her Christmas hymn radiantly and takes stock of everyone else's shortcomings.

25948.label: A new girl arrives
25948.recap: A homesick girl reaches her boarding school after dark and hears a beautiful voice singing somewhere inside the house.

25948.label: Accident at the concert
25948.recap: At a charity ballad concert the schoolgirls watch their music mistress sing, until her dress catches fire at the footlights.

25948.label: Seventeen and starting school
25948.recap: A country girl who never loved books is sent at seventeen to a London high school and dreads the entrance examination.

25948.label: The wrong carriage
25948.recap: In the holiday crush at Paddington a fourteen-year-old scrambles into any seat she can find and does not check where it is going.

25948.label: A seaside holiday
25948.recap: On a hot August afternoon a boy waits impatiently under a window for his friend to come out and play by the sea.

25948.label: A plan in Mogador
25948.recap: A young illustrator on a cheap cruise decides to slip away from the ship's party and spend a day sketching an African town alone.

25948.label: Something wrong aboard
25948.recap: Two sisters sailing home from Sydney sense that the crew and the ship's surgeon are keeping something from them.

25948.label: Summoned to France
25948.recap: A telegram brings word that the girls' father has fallen ill abroad, and one daughter is chosen to travel with her mother.

25948.label: The bark humpy
25948.recap: Deep in the Australian scrub a flowering bark hut shelters a digger's family and the daughter everyone calls by a nickname.

25948.label: The tiny folk
25948.recap: In an old village a very small married couple live neatly and happily under a fairy's sentence that they shall never grow.

25948.label: A visitor in the tollbooth
25948.recap: A condemned Scottish gentleman, forbidding his sons to come until the eve of his execution, hears his prison door unlocked.

25948.label: The buried papers
25948.recap: Having hidden the family papers underground, a lady risks a secret journey north to recover them before damp or the magistrates find them.

25971.label: A dinner among celebrities
25971.recap: George Tanqueray sits through a dinner at Jane Holland's, sour about her new fame, and stays behind when the guests go.

25971.label: A voice by the sideboard
25971.recap: Alone and unable to work in his Hampstead lodgings, Tanqueray finally notices the young servant who has been quietly looking after him.

25971.label: The drive to the Heath
25971.recap: Sent out for an afternoon she never expected, Rose is taken driving, and the day ends with a question she is not ready for.

25971.label: Before the wedding
25971.recap: Arrangements are made and a date fixed, while Tanqueray realises he has told none of his friends.

25971.label: A white road at twilight
25971.recap: Walking ahead of the others on a birthday outing, Jane and Tanqueray talk, and he hunts for a way to tell her his news.

25971.label: An empty August
25971.recap: Jane stays on in a deserted London, hardening her heart against everyone until a child runs into her in the Gardens.

25971.label: The editor's ordered house
25971.recap: An editor's immaculate house is introduced, along with the quiet woman who has made herself its mistress in everything but name.

25971.label: A top floor in Camden Town
25971.recap: Laura writes in a bare room with her ailing father dozing beside her, and receives a visitor who is unwilling to come.

25971.label: Made indispensable
25971.recap: Gertrude Collett's rise from unwanted poor relation to the woman who anticipates everything her employer wants.

25971.label: The tide begins to turn
25971.recap: Tanqueray's new book is met, unexpectedly, with praise, and he finds he minds the reviewers less than he expected to.

25971.label: Walking the moor
25971.recap: Working near each other in Devon, Jane and Tanqueray set out across the moor and talk about her husband.

25971.label: A garden in spring
25971.recap: In a friend's quiet garden two women talk about what they will do next, while two others walk the paths and wonder whether they are happy.

26009.label: Out before dawn
26009.recap: Four travellers slip out of a sleeping town at four in the morning to begin a long collecting expedition.

26009.label: A dog invites himself
26009.recap: A greyhound raised by hand catches up with the party and wins his place in it before the town gates are open.

26009.label: At the sugar mill
26009.recap: A hospitable estate feeds them, and the boy gets a lesson in how cane is crushed and boiled into sugar.

26009.label: The difficult ascent
26009.recap: A path too steep to climb forces them to haul themselves up on a staked rope, load by load, to general laughter.

26009.label: Into the great forest
26009.recap: Higher and colder, the party reaches trees so enormous the boy doubts what he is seeing.

26009.label: Morning after the storm
26009.recap: A bright morning and a rabbit for breakfast restore everyone's spirits after a frightening night of wind.

26009.label: Lamps for the cave
26009.recap: They render fat and cut resinous branches for torches, then take a first cautious look inside a cave.

26009.label: The torrent at dawn
26009.recap: A flood wakes the camp at first light, and the loss of their hats leads to some improvised remedies.

26009.label: Onto the cold plateau
26009.recap: On the frosty high plain they discuss dew and fog, and hopes of an easy stage are disappointed.

26009.label: Cutting into the jungle
26009.recap: After a broken night they hack through a wall of creepers and step into the green half-dark of the forest.

26009.label: A crowded riverbank
26009.recap: A herd of peccaries drives them onto the raft, and the night that follows brings a heavier visitor still.

26009.label: Thirst and the last miles
26009.recap: Exhausted and desperately thirsty, they carry the boy by turns and press on through the night toward home.

26240.label: Victory reaches the ward
26240.recap: News of Lee's surrender sweeps through Washington while a young Northern nurse tends a wounded Confederate officer lying among his enemies.

26240.label: A mother is told
26240.recap: Elsie must break to the boy's mother the news that he has been condemned by court-martial, and the two set out for the White House.

26240.label: The Secretary of War
26240.recap: Carrying the President's order, Mrs. Cameron meets Secretary Stanton and receives an answer she did not expect.

26240.label: A nation in mourning
26240.recap: Celebration collapses into national grief after the assassination, and the Camerons fear what it means for the South.

26240.label: The uncrowned king
26240.recap: Austin Stoneman's modest brick house on Capitol Hill becomes the real seat of power, with senators and cabinet officers filing through it.

26240.label: Across the chasm
26240.recap: Recovered at last, Ben realises he is in love with Elsie and sets about winning her against her determined coolness.

26240.label: Return to Piedmont
26240.recap: The Stonemans take rooms in a ruined South Carolina village, renting the Lenoir cottage from a family on the edge of foreclosure.

26240.label: Arrested without warrant
26240.recap: Ben is seized by the military commandant and carried off to Columbia, and Phil travels there to fight for his release.

26240.label: A ball on election night
26240.recap: Marion Lenoir is brought out into society at a village ball held in deliberate indifference to the election being counted outside.

26240.label: At the dawn of day
26240.recap: In the small hours a mother and daughter, after a night of violence, agree together on a terrible course.

26240.label: Council in the cave
26240.recap: Hooded riders bring a prisoner to a great river cave where the Klan's den convenes in full ceremonial order.

26240.label: The last night
26240.recap: Stoneman returns to Piedmont on the night of the decisive election, makes a confession to his old enemy, and waits in the hotel parlour.

26416.label: Boarded in the dark
26416.recap: A tiny American cutter in the York River is rushed at night by a far larger boarding party, and defends herself in a way her enemy remembers.

26416.label: The guns at Craney Island
26416.recap: A column of British boats rows in against an earthwork battery guarding the approach to Norfolk.

26416.label: Raids along New England
26416.recap: Landing parties begin burning shipping and surprising small coastal towns from Connecticut up into Massachusetts.

26416.label: One hour to leave town
26416.recap: A British squadron gives a small Connecticut village an hour to clear out, and the villagers send back an answer instead.

26416.label: Gathering in the Gulf
26416.recap: British naval forces collect in the Gulf of Mexico and open fire on the fort guarding Mobile Bay.

26416.label: The privateers fit out
26416.recap: Shipyards from Maine to Savannah race to arm fast schooners for private war on British commerce.

26416.label: The navy at peace
26416.recap: With no war to fight, naval officers survey the Dead Sea, chase slavers off Africa, and push north into Arctic ice.

26416.label: An unready navy
26416.recap: As the Union splits, the fleet is found scattered across the world, half of it laid up or under sail.

26416.label: Stopping a neutral packet
26416.recap: An American captain, confident in his reading of international law, decides to intercept a British mail steamer.

26416.label: Raising a burnt frigate
26416.recap: A sunken frigate abandoned at Norfolk is lifted from the mud and rebuilt into something no one has seen before.

26416.label: A cruiser built in secret
26416.recap: A suspiciously sturdy merchantman is fitted out on the Mersey while customs officers are kept comfortably entertained.

26416.label: Facing Mobile Bay
26416.recap: Farragut gathers wooden ships and monitors before the strongest harbour defences a fleet has yet been asked to enter.

26416.label: Out of Santiago harbour
26416.recap: Trapped between an army ashore and a squadron outside, a Spanish admiral gambles everything on a run for open sea.

26429.label: A rainy-day supper
26429.recap: Rain keeps the old man indoors, and a child's question about geese starts the first story of the night.

26429.label: The fiddler in the new-ground
26429.recap: The tale begins of an old fiddler whose playing was wanted at every frolic, and who once set out in bad weather.

26429.label: Dozing by the fire
26429.recap: The boy finds the old man asleep, and a bat circling the rafters sets him off on a new tale.

26429.label: News from Jack Frost
26429.recap: A hickory nut cracking on the roof startles the boy and delights the old man into another story.

26429.label: A very sharp knife
26429.recap: The boy wants to try the leather knife, and is told instead why one creature copies another at his peril.

26429.label: A visitor by the hearth
26429.recap: The boy meets an old African visitor whose strange manner and long silence unsettle everyone in the cabin.

26429.label: Talk of haunts
26429.recap: The house-girl joins the circle and offers a ghost story about a woman, a man, and two silver dollars.

26429.label: Telling it straight
26429.recap: The old African objects that a tale has been twisted, and is invited to untwist it in his own words.

26429.label: A story from Virginia
26429.recap: Another listener is stirred to remember a tale she heard as a small girl, and is coaxed into telling it.

26429.label: No lions in Georgia
26429.recap: The boy reports that his mother says there are no lions here, which prompts an explanation of how the water came between.

26429.label: Christmas at the quarters
26429.recap: Holiday preparations, a wedding, and bonfires of lightwood fill the plantation the night before Christmas.

26429.label: Carried home singing
26429.recap: The boy falls asleep at the dance and is carried to the house while the singing follows him into his dreams.

26482.label: A suitor in the wood
26482.recap: A city gentleman presses a lonely young woman to leave her home with him that very night.

26482.label: Overheard from a branch
26482.recap: Hidden in her favourite tree, she hears her step-father and a visitor discuss her future in terms she was never meant to know.

26482.label: The old nurse's story
26482.recap: She demands from her old nurse the truth about her mother's life and death.

26482.label: Night train from Bellair
26482.recap: A traveller waits sourly on a dark platform, uncertain whether he leaves the village alone.

26482.label: A veiled visitor
26482.recap: A stranger calls at the hotel room with an unwelcome warning about the man she trusts.

26482.label: Blocking the doorway
26482.recap: She plans to slip away before her host returns, and finds him already standing on the threshold.

26482.label: Four months later
26482.recap: Recovered and sheltered by new friends, she watches an autumn road and keeps her own counsel.

26482.label: The new French maid
26482.recap: A quiet lady's maid settles into the country house and takes careful note of everyone in it.

26482.label: A message on the drive
26482.recap: A guest leaving the manor at night is stopped on the avenue and led toward a private meeting.

26482.label: Winter drawing-room
26482.recap: The household gathers by the fire, bored and bickering, until the door is opened for an announcement.

26482.label: Crossing the snow
26482.recap: A silent party enters the house by night for a long-planned reckoning.

26482.label: And then comes rest
26482.recap: With the house quiet again, two friends talk over all that has happened and what each will do next.

26524.label: A signature at Versailles
26524.recap: Louis XIV revokes the toleration his predecessor granted, to the loud satisfaction of the court and the French church.

26524.label: Civil death
26524.recap: The new decrees strip Protestants of worship, trades, property and children, and thousands begin trying to slip out of the country.

26524.label: The advocate
26524.recap: A Protestant lawyer of Nismes defends congregations in the courts until defending them there becomes impossible.

26524.label: Into the Cevennes
26524.recap: He returns secretly from exile to the mountains, reading scripture to hidden households while soldiers hunt the preachers.

26524.label: Languedoc stirs
26524.recap: The old liberty-loving province of Languedoc, long a stronghold of dissent, reaches the edge of open resistance.

26524.label: Peasants take arms
26524.recap: After fifteen years of passive endurance the mountain peasantry finally rise, and the Camisard war begins.

26524.label: Walking the battlefields
26524.recap: The author travels the modern countryside around Nismes, matching stations and villages to the young leader Cavalier's campaigns.

26524.label: Versailles takes notice
26524.recap: With France at war abroad, the rising becomes a real danger, foreign help is sought, and a new marshal is sent south.

26524.label: The quiet after
26524.recap: Resistance collapses, the king strikes medals proclaiming heresy extinct, and those who will not conform go to the galleys.

26524.label: A young man's idea
26524.recap: As the old king dies, an obscure youth resolves to rebuild the outlawed Protestant church from nothing.

26524.label: The case that carried
26524.recap: A judicial killing at Toulouse finally catches the attention of Voltaire, and public opinion turns against the persecutions.

26524.label: The exiles come back
26524.recap: The banished Vaudois of the Alpine valleys set out to march home and repossess the country they were driven from.

26563.label: A shipboard argument
26563.recap: On a steamer nearing the Irish coast, a traveller falls into conversation with a brilliant, chilly young scientist who declares the universe a mistake.

26563.label: The society's guest night
26563.recap: In London the narrator is taken to a meeting of Brande's private society, where the talk unsettles him and a strange instrument is demonstrated.

26563.label: An invitation to the coast
26563.recap: A letter brings an invitation to the Brandes' country house, and the narrator meets a second young woman with startlingly modern opinions.

26563.label: A name and an address
26563.recap: Pressed about what happens to members who leave, Brande answers with an address that stops the narrator cold, and he joins anyway.

26563.label: Read like a telegram
26563.recap: Shaken by proof that these men can read his thoughts, the narrator flees to London and receives a message he cannot explain away.

26563.label: A question by the sea
26563.recap: Returning to the coast, the narrator finally asks the woman he loves how much she knows about her brother's society.

26563.label: The public lecture
26563.recap: Brande addresses a packed hall, laying out a bleak philosophy of nature and suffering that leaves his audience deeply uneasy.

26563.label: An experiment at sea
26563.recap: Aboard a chartered steamer bound east, Brande stages a demonstration of his discovery on a scale nobody aboard has seen before.

26563.label: A night in the corridor
26563.recap: Armed and desperate, the narrator moves through the sleeping ship to sabotage Brande's plan, and pays a heavy price for the attempt.

26563.label: The last address
26563.recap: On a remote island Brande announces from a rock above the camp that his life's work is finished and the hour has come.

26563.label: Flight to the shore
26563.recap: With the camp collapsing into panic, the narrator gets the two women onto horses and fights his way toward the waiting steamer.

26563.label: Lashed to the deck
26563.recap: As a vast wave races after the ship, the narrator ties himself and Natalie down and she speaks to him for the last time.

26593.label: At the stage door
26593.recap: A tense American listens to a prima donna at the Paris Opera, then waits outside the stage entrance to see her leave.

26593.label: The woman in the tavern
26593.recap: A poised young stranger sits down at his table in a late-night restaurant and refuses to explain who sent her.

26593.label: The beautiful tigress
26593.recap: A portrait of a rival singer who collects admirers, keeps her heart out of every affair, and enjoys making mischief.

26593.label: A clumsy scheme
26593.recap: Stung by a wasted visit, he chases the singer across Paris and tries a plan that goes badly wrong.

26593.label: A newspaper in the gardens
26593.recap: A young painter reads that the singer he adores has vanished, and the police account raises more questions than it answers.

26593.label: Behind bars
26593.recap: A woman wakes to her fifth dawn behind a barred window, rehearsing everything she means to say to whoever put her there.

26593.label: The terrace above Como
26593.recap: On a famous lakeside terrace we meet a retired prizefighter enjoying his three good appetites a day.

26593.label: A dog and a collar
26593.recap: Hunting for someone in the village, he stops to quiet a squabbling puppy and reads the name on its collar.

26593.label: Two errands in the village
26593.recap: Slipping away from a tea party, the old fighter buys cigars and a book, and falls into talk with a stranger who knew his father.

26593.label: An unwelcome caller
26593.recap: A visiting card chills the whole drawing room, and the guest who follows it makes no effort to be polite to anyone but one person.

26593.label: An awkward errand
26593.recap: He calls on his painter friend to argue him out of a quarrel that has escalated further than the painter realizes.

26593.label: Journey's end
26593.recap: He takes a train away from the lake, tips the guard for privacy, and finds he has a veiled fellow passenger.

26704.label: Four men, one fire
26704.recap: Four rough-looking tramps share a meal at a hidden fire in the woods beside a railway, talking a slang outsiders cannot follow.

26704.label: Surrounded at the fire
26704.recap: Eight strangers ring the campfire and demand to know who these men are and which of them leads, and the silence has to be broken somehow.

26704.label: Into the swamp
26704.recap: One of the campers is blindfolded and taken by foot and boat far into an impassable swamp to be looked over by the gang's chief.

26704.label: Questioned by the chief
26704.recap: A tall, fierce young woman interrogates the newcomer about where he comes from and why he went hunting for the Hobo King.

26704.label: A machine off the rails
26704.recap: A strange vehicle is lifted off the railway track in pieces, rebuilt as an automobile and driven away toward a night's work in a village.

26704.label: Soap and scrubbing brushes
26704.recap: The outlaws test their new recruits by washing them, and not every disguise survives the treatment.

26704.label: A note from the railroad
26704.recap: A brief message calls the detective back to the railway president's office with news that undoes much of his work.

26704.label: The lumberman at Calamont
26704.recap: Disguised as a French Canadian timber measurer, he steps off the train into rough hill country where the gang is said to be hiding.

26704.label: Trial by campfire
26704.recap: The outlaws stage a mock trial of a prisoner tied to a stake, the queen presiding and the verdict decided before it begins.

26704.label: A room in Rivington Street
26704.recap: In a lamplit East Side room a table of new recruits is questioned one at a time and their answers written down.

26704.label: Lights out
26704.recap: A table goes over in a crowded dive, the lamps die at once, and everyone in the room scrambles in the dark.

26704.label: Facing the room
26704.recap: The detective walks in among twenty or thirty armed criminals and tells them exactly what he has come for and what will happen if they interfere.

26742.label: Back from Chautauqua
26742.recap: Four friends attend their city church for the first Sunday since a summer camp meeting and find the familiar building feels entirely different.

26742.label: Flossy's first class
26742.recap: Flossy takes the roughest class of older boys in the Sunday school and tries to win them by admitting she knows nothing.

26742.label: A gray Monday
26742.recap: Marion returns to teaching in pouring rain and finds the resolve that felt easy on Sunday very hard to feel at all.

26742.label: Col. Baker walks her home
26742.recap: Flossy's easiest friendship becomes an awkward test when she declines an invitation she would once have accepted without thinking.

26742.label: Eurie keeps house
26742.recap: With her mother away, Eurie juggles a crying baby, burning bread and an unexpected caller in one chaotic morning.

26742.label: Calling on the pastor
26742.recap: Eurie proposes the four go straight to Dr. Dennis's study and ask outright for a place in his church work.

26742.label: The card question
26742.recap: A careless remark sets Flossy puzzling over whether an amusement she never questioned is one she ought to give up.

26742.label: The half-year letter
26742.recap: Marion prepares her regular remittance to the aunt and uncle who raised her, and changes one word in her usual curt note.

26742.label: An unexpected guest
26742.recap: Flossy arrives at the midweek prayer meeting with a companion nobody expected, and the story doubles back to explain how.

26742.label: A sleepless library
26742.recap: Judge Erskine paces alone at night, pressed by a sermon that seemed written for him and by something he has never told.

26742.label: Flossy plans a party
26742.recap: Flossy announces an entertainment designed to bring her Sunday-school boys into company that will actually be kind to them.

26742.label: A parting glance
26742.recap: Two ministers compare notes on the changed young women, and the story looks in on each of the four one last time.

26951.label: Rails reach the range
26951.recap: A rancher rides toward a brand-new railroad town and takes the measure of what the coming tracks will mean for open cattle country.

26951.label: A view from the private car
26951.recap: A young easterner wakes in her father's railway car, falls for the raw country, and notices a horseman riding past her window.

26951.label: A word in the street
26951.recap: A trick-riding display in the main street is spoiled by a remark from an onlooker, and two men square off in front of the whole town.

26951.label: The back room
26951.recap: Two men throw off their hats in a locked room behind the bank and settle their quarrel with bare fists.

26951.label: The railroad king arrives
26951.recap: The line's president tours his booming town and holds a long private conference about who really owns the land around it.

26951.label: A caller at the Bar B
26951.recap: The promoter pays court on a ranch porch and explains, very reasonably, why many local land titles may not be worth the paper they are on.

26951.label: The courthouse safe
26951.recap: After a night intrusion, a frightened judge is made to open his safe while a suspicious visitor watches everything come out.

26951.label: Wreckage on the butte
26951.recap: A rancher looks down on a scene of ruin below the butte and rides into town to find opinion running strongly his way.

26951.label: Prison in a pueblo
26951.recap: The judge wakes in a deserted cliff dwelling and learns the price of his release from the man guarding the entrance.

26951.label: Fire in the night
26951.recap: A chaperon at her bedroom window sees the sky glowing over town, and a hard-ridden horse comes thundering up to the ranch door.

26951.label: After the storm
26951.recap: With the street gone silent, a woman sits alone in the private car working through what the town has done, until a visitor appears in the doorway.

26992.label: Herding in the drought
26992.recap: A fourteen-year-old girl minding cattle on the baking prairie is joined by a neighbour boy come to say goodbye.

26992.label: The mortgage
26992.recap: With the crop sown, a debt collector's visit leads to papers that must be signed against the family farm.

26992.label: Called home from school
26992.recap: Elizabeth packs up her books and says a private goodbye to the classrooms she has to leave.

26992.label: Planting potatoes
26992.recap: Working the rows with her mother, Elizabeth announces that this year she means to keep her own wages.

26992.label: At Aunt Susan's
26992.recap: Elizabeth arrives at the one house where she is simply welcome, and finds her plans warmly taken seriously.

26992.label: The first quarrel
26992.recap: Impatient about the house he is building, John picks an argument with Elizabeth about where she may walk.

26992.label: A neighbour keeps watch
26992.recap: An old farmer who has been sitting out in his barn all night creeps back to bed and says nothing about why.

26992.label: A day in town
26992.recap: A trip to Colebyville shows Elizabeth exactly how far she has drifted from her neighbours' good opinion.

26992.label: Snowbound chores
26992.recap: Cut off by a blizzard, Elizabeth wraps up in borrowed clothes and fights her way out to feed the stock alone.

26992.label: A bargain team
26992.recap: John brings home horses bought against agreement, and is warned about both the animals and the money.

26992.label: A letter at the post office
26992.recap: A letter in a familiar hand is waiting for Elizabeth, and she carries it all the way home unopened.

26992.label: The answer she writes
26992.recap: Elizabeth sets down plainly, hiding nothing, the terms on which a life together could begin again.

27151.label: News reaches England
27151.recap: Word of the squadron's unexpected victory arrives home, and a delighted family letter describes the toasts, promotions and rejoicing that follow.

27151.label: Superseded at Cadiz
27151.recap: After seven anxious weeks without letters, the despatches finally arrive and bring word that a senior officer is being sent to take the chief command.

27151.label: Knight of the Bath
27151.recap: With peace preliminaries signed, the Gibraltar garrison stages an elaborate procession to invest the admiral with a rare order of knighthood.

27151.label: Command at Guernsey
27151.recap: War resumes and he takes charge of the Channel Islands, testing the cliffs the enemy might climb and watching the ports opposite.

27151.label: Bombarding Granville
27151.recap: He takes a small squadron against the invasion craft gathered in the harbour, and his frigate grounds under fire from enemy gunboats.

27151.label: Sent to the Baltic
27151.recap: With Sweden the last friendly power in the north, he is chosen to command a large fleet sent to protect her.

27151.label: A general detained
27151.recap: The British general summoned to Stockholm is forbidden to leave, and has to contrive his own quiet way back to the fleet.

27151.label: Rescuing an army
27151.recap: Spanish troops stranded among the Danish islands are lifted off by boat, and the flagship is driven through a difficult channel by night to join them.

27151.label: Riot in Stockholm
27151.recap: A rumour about the crown prince's death turns a city crowd murderous, and Swedish politics grow harder for the fleet to navigate.

27151.label: The homeward gale
27151.recap: The fleet sails for England late in the season, and a captain's hour-by-hour log records a rising winter gale around a crippled ship of the line.

27151.label: Passed over at home
27151.recap: With the Baltic quiet he comes ashore for good, takes up charitable work in Guernsey, and finds his name missing when peacetime honours are handed out.

27151.label: Last years in Guernsey
27151.recap: In old age he attends Parliament, bears a bereavement and a robbery with great composure, and his final illness is set down by those who kept watch.

27288.label: A boy and the money
27288.recap: An excise collector's son in Prussia describes helping himself to his father's government money and being caught out by a simple trap.

27288.label: Jail at sixteen
27288.recap: After running up hotel bills he cannot pay, the boy is arrested, examined, and held for weeks until his father sends money.

27288.label: A Saturday evening meeting
27288.recap: A friend takes him to a small house gathering where people read, sing, and kneel to pray, and the evening leaves him quietly happy.

27288.label: Preaching in Devon
27288.recap: Newly settled in England and awkward in the language, he preaches in small chapels and is eventually asked to stay on as pastor.

27288.label: The call to Bristol
27288.recap: An invitation from a fellow minister sets him weighing, day by day, whether his work in Teignmouth is finished.

27288.label: An orphan house imagined
27288.recap: Reading about an earlier charitable work, he begins praying about whether to attempt something similar himself.

27288.label: Nobody applies
27288.recap: The house is rented and furnished, but no child is offered, and he uses the silence to re-examine his own motives.

27288.label: A day with nothing in hand
27288.recap: With three houses needing bread and only pennies available, he records hour by hour exactly what arrives and when.

27288.label: Why he takes no credit
27288.recap: In a lean stretch he sets out, point by point, his refusal to buy anything on credit however tight things become.

27288.label: A polite complaint
27288.recap: A neighbour's courteous letter about the noise of children sends him listing reasons for and against moving the whole work.

27288.label: The doors open
27288.recap: After years of praying and building, a new house stands ready and children begin to be received into it.

27288.label: A last look back
27288.recap: He closes with an account of a stirring among the children in his care, deliberately withholding details for their sake.

27365.label: The shop near Seven Dials
27365.recap: Two customers try to buy a polished crystal egg from a nervous dealer whose wife wants the sale.

27365.label: A light in the dark
27365.recap: Wandering his shop at three in the morning, the dealer notices the crystal glowing in a way optics cannot explain.

27365.label: Shutters on the street
27365.recap: After a busy fortnight the investigator returns to Seven Dials and finds the shop closed.

27365.label: An erratic planet
27365.recap: Astronomers report that Neptune is moving strangely, and a new speck of light appears beyond it.

27365.label: After the passing
27365.recap: Survivors creep back to flooded cities and find the world's weather and seasons permanently altered.

27365.label: Spring on the Wey
27365.recap: A small tribe camps by the river, ruled by a cunning old man whose attention frightens a young woman.

27365.label: The lord of the gorge
27365.recap: A cave bear sees firelight on a cliff ledge for the first time and grows curious about the creatures making it.

27365.label: The lion comes nightly
27365.recap: A stumpy-toothed old lion takes someone from the camp night after night, and the tribe cannot agree how to answer it.

27365.label: A very sensible man
27365.recap: A thoroughly correct Victorian gentleman is described, then his descendants are followed into a mechanised future.

27365.label: Down in the underways
27365.recap: A refined couple reduced to labour service must learn to live and speak among the workers of the lower city.

27365.label: An argument in the bar
27365.recap: A stubborn clerk arguing that miracles cannot happen discovers, mid-demonstration, that he can perform one.

27365.label: A wind over everything
27365.recap: The consequences of one careless command are laid out, and the man responsible tries to think clearly in the gale.

27430.label: A ministry falls
27430.recap: Lord North's government collapses in London, and the Whig politicians who had openly cheered the American cause find themselves suddenly near power.

27430.label: The war ends
27430.recap: Word of the peace treaty reaches America, hostilities formally cease, and furloughed soldiers walk home to farms they have not seen in years.

27430.label: Washington gives up command
27430.recap: Washington says goodbye to his officers, hands in an itemised account of his own expenses, resigns before Congress, and goes home to Mount Vernon.

27430.label: A widow sues
27430.recap: A New York widow sues for her confiscated house, and the young lawyer who takes the unpopular other side sets off a pamphlet war.

27430.label: The paper money craze
27430.recap: State after state prints its own currency, and each attempt to force people to accept it at face value drives the value down faster.

27430.label: Who owns the west
27430.recap: Old royal charters leave four states claiming the same enormous wilderness beyond the mountains, and the claims cannot all be true.

27430.label: Debt in the countryside
27430.recap: Massachusetts farmers, crushed by taxes and lawsuits and losing homesteads to foreclosure, begin turning their anger on lawyers, judges and merchants.

27430.label: Behind closed doors
27430.recap: The Philadelphia convention shuts its doors, rumours of monarchy fly through the country, and Washington rises to warn the delegates against half measures.

27430.label: A hair's breadth compromise
27430.recap: With the convention close to breaking up over how states should be counted, two Connecticut delegates float a compromise that nobody much likes.

27430.label: Sent to the states
27430.recap: The finished draft goes to Congress amid determined opposition, and is passed on to the states, splitting the country into two new parties.

27430.label: Essays for a hostile state
27430.recap: Facing a convention packed with opponents in New York, Hamilton enlists two collaborators to explain the new plan in a run of newspaper essays.

27430.label: The journey to New York
27430.recap: Washington leaves Mount Vernon again, is met with flowers and arches along the road, and takes the oath of office before a packed street.

27432.label: A letter to Rome
27432.recap: In a damp cellar room the King orders his frightened Archbishop to write a letter of submission to the Pope.

27432.label: The terrace at Pontefract
27432.recap: The Queen walks a carpeted castle terrace above empty country, planning how she will alter the realm.

27432.label: Bargaining with the King
27432.recap: Katharine teases her husband into granting a small favour before he will tell her the large one he has already done.

27432.label: The scholar and the child
27432.recap: The King's grim elder daughter works among her books while her small brother carries a message to her in Latin.

27432.label: Ruling in his absence
27432.recap: With the King gone north, the Queen governs the castle, teaches her ladies Latin, and labours over the wording of his letter.

27432.label: A gentleman shaves his beard
27432.recap: The Archbishop's smooth secretary asks leave to carry the letter himself and refuses to explain the scheme behind it.

27432.label: The forgotten chapel
27432.recap: High in the castle roof the Queen and the Lady Mary pray each night in a small chapel that escaped the visitors.

27432.label: The northern progress
27432.recap: The King rides to the Scottish border to meet a nephew who never comes, and returns through country he has marked.

27432.label: Late in the bedchamber
27432.recap: Katharine dismisses her maid, jokes at the old Lady Rochford's fearfulness, and is interrupted by blows on the door.

27432.label: Prayers and a whisper
27432.recap: Kneeling before a weeping ivory Christ, the Archbishop cannot pray, and his gentleman offers to sit up and talk instead.

27432.label: Rain at Hampton Court
27432.recap: Netting a purse in a grey gallery, the Queen is interrupted by a weeping servingwoman begging to be kept from her own brother.

27432.label: The council in black
27432.recap: The lords sit silent in black while the King, in tears on his throne, begs his Archbishop to save her for him.

27475.label: A Suspicion
27475.recap: Gossip swirls through the new West about a pretty girl suspected in the death of a renegade.

27475.label: Dan's Ward
27475.recap: The easygoing Max Lyster grows curious about the mysterious young ward of Dan Overton.

27475.label: The Stranger's Warning
27475.recap: It is decided that the wild girl 'Tana should be sent away to school.

27475.label: The Track in the Forest
27475.recap: The party camps in the wilderness by the Kootenai, where a strange spring hides a secret.

27475.label: Gold
27475.recap: A rich gold strike turns the little party's fortunes upside down.

27475.label: 'Tana's Engagement
27475.recap: Changed since her fever, 'Tana makes a puzzling demand and a surprising engagement.

27475.label: On Manhattan Island
27475.recap: A winter on in New York, 'Tana resists the polished society her new fortune has lifted her into.

27587.label: Wagers at the Isthmus
27587.recap: A crier takes bets on the pentathlon while the crowd argues over a handsome young Athenian, and a small elderly man fights his way forward to stake his money.

27587.label: The inn on the dark road
27587.recap: An Athenian orator slips away from the festival to a squalid inn where a Spartan wrestler asks him for a pledge before showing him a visitor.

27587.label: The fivefold contest
27587.recap: The Athenian champion is called out to face five rivals in leaping, discus, javelin, running and wrestling before twenty thousand spectators.

27587.label: Homecoming at Eleusis
27587.recap: At a seaside village the athlete's wife and her family wait by the gate with musicians while runners bring word that he is close.

27587.label: Full market time
27587.recap: The story moves to Athens itself, from the rock of the Acropolis down into the noise and bargaining of the Agora.

27587.label: A debt coming due
27587.recap: The orator realises that money he quietly took from the public chest will be discovered within days unless he can replace it.

27587.label: The letter in the boot
27587.recap: A search of a frightened messenger produces a sealed papyrus, and everyone in the room recognises the seal stamped upon it.

27587.label: Storm in the Aegean
27587.recap: A ship is driven helplessly past island after island until her captain gives up trying to make harbour.

27587.label: Waking among cushions
27587.recap: A man wakes weak and bewildered on soft pillows in a scented room, too feeble at first to wonder where he is.

27587.label: The Hot Gates
27587.recap: The narrative turns to the narrow pass the Persian king must force, where the Greeks have thrown a wall across the road.

27587.label: The march on Athens
27587.recap: After a costly victory the Persian army moves south, burning the cities that refused to submit while the Greek fleets wait.

27587.label: The last battle line
27587.recap: On a windy morning the Persian cavalry, archers and lancers form up, and their general rides out to the cheers of his captains.

27587.label: Above the ruins
27587.recap: Survivors climb the burnt Acropolis, look out over the sea and hills, and speak about what should be rebuilt.

27609.label: A survivor's preface
27609.recap: The narrator introduces himself as the only person to walk away from the Undersea Tube disaster and promises to explain how it happened.

27609.label: Digging the great tunnel
27609.recap: He sketches the building of the world's longest tunnel, dug from Liverpool and New York toward each other far beneath the ocean floor.

27609.label: The sealed cavern
27609.recap: Workers break into a glittering sealed cave beneath the sea and find something inside it that scientists cannot explain.

27609.label: A trickle of seawater
27609.recap: A small newspaper item reports that the sea has begun seeping through a single crack, and the engineers quietly worry while the public forgets.

27609.label: Ordered to France
27609.recap: The narrator is sent abroad on company business and decides to make the crossing by Tube.

27609.label: The engineer's warning
27609.recap: Over dinner his old college roommate, now one of the Tube's designers, urges him to travel by air instead.

27609.label: How the Tube works
27609.recap: The engineer draws the plan and explains the wind-propulsion system, the pumps, the pressures and the speeds involved.

27609.label: A reckless decision
27609.recap: Told plainly what his friend fears is under the tunnel, the narrator announces that he is now more determined than ever to go.

27609.label: Boarding the Flier
27609.recap: He reaches the terminus, is ticketed and processed, and is shown to the front car of the glowing train.

27609.label: A stranger asks a favour
27609.recap: An elderly man with a mass of silver hair asks to share the private car, and the narrator agrees before falling asleep.

27609.label: Red light through the port-hole
27609.recap: A violent shock throws him from his berth, and through the window he sees something no one has ever seen before.

27609.label: Waking in a hospital
27609.recap: He comes back to himself in an English hospital and learns what remains of the Tube and its passengers.

27673.label: The suppliants' plea
27673.recap: A priest kneels at the palace steps with a crowd of suppliants and begs the king to save a city dying of plague.

27673.label: The word from Delphi
27673.recap: Creon returns with the oracle's demand that something unclean be cast out of the land.

27673.label: Summoning the blind seer
27673.recap: Oedipus welcomes the blind prophet with great courtesy and asks him to name the old king's killer.

27673.label: Creon defends himself
27673.recap: Stung by an accusation, Creon comes to the palace and asks the elders exactly what was said of him.

27673.label: The queen asks questions
27673.recap: Jocasta calms the quarrel and presses her husband to explain plainly what he has been told.

27673.label: A stranger from Corinth
27673.recap: A traveller arrives at the palace asking for the king, with news from the city where he grew up.

27673.label: The old shepherd
27673.recap: The herdsman they have been waiting for is led in, frightened, and set before the king.

27673.label: A question pressed home
27673.recap: Under threat the old servant is driven step by step toward an answer he does not want to give.

27673.label: News from within the house
27673.recap: A messenger comes out to tell the elders what happened behind the palace doors.

27673.label: Answering the elders
27673.recap: Oedipus refuses to be argued out of what he has done, and speaks of what he could not bear to look upon.

27673.label: The chorus' last word
27673.recap: The elders turn to the city with a closing warning about fortune and the end of things.

27743.label: Sailing into Helsingfors
27743.recap: After four and a half days from Hull the writer's ship threads a maze of marked channels and islands into the Finnish capital.

27743.label: A country house welcome
27743.recap: The party travels on to Wiborg and is carried by ferry and pine wood to a wooden island house where the hostess laughs at their fur coats.

27743.label: The Finnish bath
27743.recap: A servant leads the writer to the little bath house to be steamed, scrubbed and beaten in the national manner.

27743.label: A night in a monastery
27743.recap: On the longest day of the year they sail for a Russian monastery on Lake Ladoga, crewed by long-haired monks and provisioned against a strict fast.

27743.label: A crowded festival town
27743.recap: Ten thousand visitors descend on a town of thirteen hundred for a music festival, and even getting on the train proves a scrimmage.

27743.label: An old-fashioned wedding
27743.recap: A staged wedding of a century earlier shows a bashful proposal by proxy, a hired weeping woman, and the undoing of the bride's maiden plait.

27743.label: Lodging in a ruined castle
27743.recap: With every room in town taken, an obliging friend explains how he talked the mayor into letting two Englishwomen sleep inside a fifteenth-century castle.

27743.label: Setting out through Savolax
27743.recap: A planned two hundred mile drive nearly collapses when their escort is delayed, and a governor offers his son instead.

27743.label: Three little carts
27743.recap: Springless two-wheeled karra arrive for the next stage, and the coachmen spend an hour arguing over three bags and a bundle of rugs.

27743.label: Up the river by tar-boat
27743.recap: To learn what the boatmen endure, the party goes a mile and a half upstream in a tar-boat, through two deep black locks and four bouts of towing.

27743.label: Descending the rapids
27743.recap: The long run down to the coast takes twenty-nine sleepless hours, with the pilot flinging his weight on the steering pole at every cataract.

27743.label: Farewell to Suomi
27743.recap: Three months after landing, the writer sums up what English eyes could and could not learn of a little-known country.

27761.label: The midnight watch
27761.recap: Two sentries bring a sceptical friend onto the cold castle platform to see for himself the shape that has visited them twice already.

27761.label: The new king's court
27761.recap: The new king addresses his court about his brother's death and his own marriage, then asks his nephew why he is still in black.

27761.label: Farewells at Polonius's house
27761.recap: Laertes leaves for France after warning his sister about the prince's attentions, and their father presses the same point harder.

27761.label: Hamlet keeps the watch
27761.recap: Hamlet waits out on the platform in the bitter cold and speaks to the figure when it appears, over his friends' objections.

27761.label: Alone with the ghost
27761.recap: Drawn away from the others to a remote part of the platform, Hamlet finally hears what the apparition has come to say.

27761.label: Ophelia's fright
27761.recap: Ophelia describes a wordless and unsettling visit from the prince, and her father decides the king must be told at once.

27761.label: A staged encounter
27761.recap: The king and his counsellor place Ophelia where Hamlet will come upon her, and hide themselves to judge what passes between them.

27761.label: The recorder lesson
27761.recap: Hamlet hands a musician's pipe to his old schoolfellow and uses it to accuse them both of trying to play upon him.

27761.label: The queen's chamber
27761.recap: With a listener concealed behind the hangings, the queen confronts her son, and the interview goes violently wrong.

27761.label: Flowers and songs
27761.recap: Ophelia comes into the hall singing snatches of ballads and handing out herbs, while her brother looks on unable to reach her.

27761.label: The gravediggers
27761.recap: Two grave-diggers argue coroner's law over a fresh grave, and Hamlet stops to talk with them about the bones they turn up.

27761.label: The wager
27761.recap: The court assembles for a fencing match between Hamlet and Laertes, with foils chosen, wine set out and a wager laid.

27794.label: A name by the fire
27794.recap: At a country dinner party a retired magistrate teases his hosts with talk of a criminal nobody can identify.

27794.label: The slow train south
27794.recap: An elderly traveller takes unusual care choosing his carriage on the night train out of Paris.

27794.label: The magistrate arrives
27794.recap: An ambitious young magistrate reaches the chateau and has the steward walk him to the room where the killing happened.

27794.label: Beside the tunnel
27794.recap: A shabby stranger loiters among navvies at a railway cutting, asking oddly precise questions about the morning trains.

27794.label: The absent tenant
27794.recap: A well-dressed caller talks his way up five flights to the rooms of a lodger who has been away three weeks.

27794.label: The Cahors assizes
27794.recap: Gentry crowd a small provincial courtroom for a trial in which a well-liked neighbour sits as the defendant.

27794.label: The Royal Palace Hotel
27794.recap: A Russian princess returns late to her grand hotel suite and orders a bath before bed.

27794.label: Inside the asylum
27794.recap: Two underpaid house doctors grumble over breakfast at the private madhouse where they do all the work.

27794.label: The widow's charities
27794.recap: A widowed lady withdraws from society into hospital wards and poor streets, administering her late husband's estates.

27794.label: On remand
27794.recap: A prisoner settles with unnerving composure into the routine of the Sante after his money for outside meals runs out.

27794.label: The court of assize
27794.recap: All Paris schemes for a seat at a murder trial that has excited public opinion for months.

27794.label: Before dawn on the boulevard
27794.recap: A singing, drinking crowd of the very rich and the very poor streams through the dark toward one destination.

27997.label: St. James's Square
27997.recap: On a blustery October afternoon in 1869, the story opens before an earl's town house in fashionable London.

27997.label: Sara's Letter
27997.recap: Torn by indecision, Sara weeps over her letter to the Duke of Marshire and tries to banish Robert Orange from her heart.

27997.label: The Duke's Suit
27997.recap: Sara keeps the lovelorn Duke waiting, unable to give him a true answer.

27997.label: Political Duty
27997.recap: Even in the shadow of grief, party politics presses on, and the unambitious Orange is drawn toward its leadership.

27997.label: A Long Retreat
27997.recap: With circumstances suddenly changed, Robert turns away from the world toward the Jesuits and a long Retreat.

28054.label: The Karamazov Family
28054.recap: We meet the dissolute landowner Fyodor Pavlovitch Karamazov and his three very different sons.

28054.label: At the Monastery
28054.recap: The quarrelling family gathers at the monastery for the saintly elder Zossima to settle a dispute over money.

28054.label: Father and Son
28054.recap: Hot-tempered Dmitri arrives late, and his bitter feud with his father erupts before the elder.

28054.label: The Servants
28054.recap: Attention turns to the Karamazov household and its sly, resentful servant, the foundling Smerdyakov.

28054.label: Sent into the World
28054.recap: The dying elder blesses Alyosha and sends him out of the monastery to live among ordinary men.

28054.label: Rebellion
28054.recap: Ivan pours out his heart to Alyosha, rebelling against a God who allows the suffering of innocent children.

28054.label: The Grand Inquisitor
28054.recap: Ivan recites his poem in which Christ returns to earth and is confronted by the Grand Inquisitor.

28054.label: An Odour of Corruption
28054.recap: After the elder's death the monastery is shaken when his body decays, sorely testing Alyosha's faith.

28054.label: Mitya's Torment
28054.recap: Frantic for money and wild with jealousy over Grushenka, Dmitri rushes desperately about the town.

28054.label: At Mokroe
28054.recap: Dmitri chases Grushenka to a wild night of feasting at the village of Mokroe.

28054.label: The Investigation
28054.recap: A sudden crime brings the authorities down on Dmitri, and a long night of questioning begins.

28054.label: The Boys
28054.recap: The story pauses to follow a band of schoolboys and the proud, sickly little Ilusha.

28054.label: Ivan and Smerdyakov
28054.recap: Tormented by doubt, Ivan returns again and again to Smerdyakov, circling a terrible suspicion.

28054.label: The Trial
28054.recap: The whole district crowds into the courthouse for Dmitri's long-awaited trial.

28152.label: A New England line
28152.recap: The book opens with the family's American beginnings, tracing an ancestor who served at Bunker Hill.

28152.label: The bleak Davis place
28152.recap: After his father's business collapses, the boy's family moves to a gaunt, half-ruined farmhouse under the rocks.

28152.label: Ore on the bridge road
28152.recap: A boy drives a heavy ox-team along a hill road toward a high bridge on a scorching August day.

28152.label: Taming Chestnut Bess
28152.recap: Determined to impress his uncle, the boy saddles the one mare in the county nobody will ride.

28152.label: Into the Union blue
28152.recap: The war fever of 1861 sweeps the young schoolmaster into a New York cavalry regiment.

28152.label: Libby Prison
28152.recap: Captured and shut up in a Richmond prison, he tries to school himself into patience while other men plan escapes.

28152.label: Voices in the dark
28152.recap: Two escaped prisoners moving through the night must guess, from speech alone, whether the strangers behind them are friends.

28152.label: A Georgia county jail
28152.recap: Held as curiosities in a small-town jail, the prisoners are examined by a board of officers and sent on under guard.

28152.label: Boston to San Francisco
28152.recap: Years after the war he sets out from Boston on a lecture tour made on horseback, aiming for the Pacific.

28152.label: Near the Skull Rocks
28152.recap: Riding west with two herders, he meets a mounted band on the Laramie plains whose signals leave no doubt of their intent.

28152.label: Beyond Lake Itasca
28152.recap: On short rations, the canoe party pushes past the accepted source of the Mississippi to test a guide's claim of another lake.

28152.label: Greetings of the voyage
28152.recap: The book closes with an album of tributes and autographs gathered along the whole route from the river's head to the Gulf.

28203.label: A betrothal in question
28203.recap: In a hot southern city a restless man leans from a window for a breath of sea wind, and the woman he is engaged to comes in behind him.

28203.label: Refusing to get up
28203.recap: A young woman stays in bed out of sheer weariness with everything, batting away every cure and diversion her brisk elder sister proposes.

28203.label: An eighteenth birthday
28203.recap: On her birthday Sylvia is joined on the piazza by her brother and his two friends, and hears of a trip she badly wants to be part of.

28203.label: A day on the river
28203.recap: The second day of the voyage brings basket-making, berry-picking, water lilies, and the smoke of a burning wood on the horizon.

28203.label: By the autumn fire
28203.recap: Dreaming over the summer just past, Sylvia is startled out of her thoughts by a visitor who has come with something to ask her.

28203.label: A Christmas basket
28203.recap: An anonymous basket of holly arrives on Christmas morning, and Sylvia keeps her guess about the sender to herself.

28203.label: Wedding morning
28203.recap: Prue wakes her sister in tears, and the two say things to each other that nineteen years together had never drawn out.

28203.label: The wedding journey
28203.recap: The married pair wander through summer country, stopping at old inns and picnicking in green corners of the road.

28203.label: Asleep and awake
28203.recap: Writing late in the library, Moor looks up to find his wife standing in the doorway with open, unseeing eyes.

28203.label: Six months of gossip
28203.recap: Alone and much talked about, Sylvia fills a long half year with duties while the neighbourhood makes up its mind about her.

28203.label: A search in Italy
28203.recap: A traveller looking for a countryman is told by excited villagers about a recent battle and one stranger's part in it.

28203.label: Snow-drops in April
28203.recap: On an April birthday the household gathers round Sylvia's couch and she tells each of them what her life has taught her.

28329.label: Arriving in St. Petersburg
28329.recap: He lands with a hundred dollars and a knapsack and walks a vast, scattered city that leaves him feeling utterly alone.

28329.label: The emperor's bear-hunt
28329.recap: He describes, with straight-faced amusement, the machinery of officials set in motion whenever a bear is sighted near the railway.

28329.label: Too much Russian tea
28329.recap: Hospitable American railway men in Moscow insist he drink glass after glass of tea, and he cannot bring himself to refuse.

28329.label: Night walk by the Kremlin
28329.recap: Sleepless, he wanders the moonlit streets past gilded domes and painted churches, then turns to find his way back.

28329.label: Inside the traktir
28329.recap: He watches the keeper of a low tavern reckon up accounts on a little frame of beads.

28329.label: Manners and bowing
28329.recap: He turns from anecdote to observation on the gravity, courtesy, and contradictions of Russian daily life.

28329.label: Walks about Stockholm
28329.recap: Warning the reader to expect nothing brilliant, he rambles through the museums and streets of the Swedish capital.

28329.label: Up the Gudbrandsdal
28329.recap: He leaves Lillehammer by cariole and drives up a long valley of waterfalls, sawmills, and hillside farms.

28329.label: Letters for Iceland
28329.recap: In Copenhagen he collects introductions, advice, and hospitality in preparation for a voyage further north.

28329.label: Riding into the lava
28329.recap: He rides out of Reykjavik through fog across a wilderness of lava and bog loud with startled water birds.

28329.label: First sight of the Geysers
28329.recap: His guide points out a distant column of vapour and names it with no ceremony whatever.

28329.label: A night at the farm
28329.recap: He stops at an Icelandic farmhouse for supper and a bed, and finds the family's kindness hard to navigate.

28621.label: The song begins
28621.recap: The poet asks the gods for help and sets out to sing of bodies changed into new shapes, starting from chaos.

28621.label: The palace of the Sun
28621.recap: A palace of gold and gems opens the second book, where a father receives a visitor with an alarming request.

28621.label: A brother sent to search
28621.recap: A prince ordered to find his stolen sister asks an oracle instead where he should build a city.

28621.label: A face in the water
28621.recap: A proud young hunter stops at a still pool and is caught by the reflection he finds looking back.

28621.label: Lovers and a wall
28621.recap: Two neighbours forbidden to marry discover a crack in the wall between their houses and plan to slip out at night.

28621.label: Uproar at the wedding
28621.recap: A hero is telling his story at his own wedding feast when armed men burst into the hall.

28621.label: A contest of weavers
28621.recap: The goddess of craft, freshly praised by the Muses, turns her attention to a mortal who boasts of her own skill.

28621.label: Two gods knocking
28621.recap: Two gods walk through a Phrygian village in human shape, trying a thousand doors before one opens.

28621.label: An ill-omened wedding
28621.recap: The god of marriage answers a famous singer's call, and every omen at the ceremony is wrong.

28621.label: The singer in the woods
28621.recap: The Thracian singer holds the trees and beasts spellbound until frenzied women catch sight of him.

28621.label: The claim to the armour
28621.recap: Greek captains assemble to hear two rivals argue over which of them deserves a dead hero's arms.

28621.label: The poet's last word
28621.recap: The poem closes with its maker claiming a name that no fire, sword or age can put out.

28780.label: Handing in his key
28780.recap: A star wireless operator walks into his chief's office and stuns the room by resigning from the China run.

28780.label: An errand in Chinatown
28780.recap: Delivering a message to a hidden room, he catches the eye of a woman at an upstairs window.

28780.label: The junk alongside
28780.recap: The liner stops in a dark river and a junk drifts silently against her side.

28780.label: Up the Yangtze
28780.recap: The story shifts to a small, ferociously strong river steamer and the courtship going on aboard her.

28780.label: Alone on the road
28780.recap: Footsore and hungry, he walks inland through the mud and stumbles on a caravan camped at dusk.

28780.label: Watching the drawbridge
28780.recap: From a rooftop he keeps a sleepless watch over a mining city's gate, waiting for a captive to arrive.

28780.label: A warning in Batavia
